f: Why do the Jurists begin their books with the rules of Taharah?
b: Taharah is amongst the conditions for the validity of Salah. Salah is the second of the Five Pillars of Islaam. They therefore begin with the rules of Taharah, followed by Salah.

f: What is the meaning of Taharah linguistically and in Shari'ah?
b: Taharah is linguistically cleanliness. In Shari'ah it is the removal of al-Hadath al-Asghar [minor impurity] and al-Hadath al-Akbar [major impurity], and filth from clothing, body and places of Salah.

f: What is al-Hadath al-Akbar?
b: When a bath of the whole body becomes obligatory upon a man or a woman the state is called al-Hadath al-Akbar. After the bath the Hadath is removed. The bath is called Ghusl or Ightisal.

f: What is al-Hadath al-Asghar?
b: When the washing of certain organs and wiping some becomes obligatory upon a man or a woman in order to perform Salah it is called al-Hadath al-Asghar. This washing is called Ghasl or Wudu. The person in a state of wudu is called mutawaddi.

f: List those organs which must be washed or wiped during wudu
b:
The face from the hairline to bottom of the chin; and from the right ear-lobe to the left ear-lobe.
The hands from the fingertips to the elbows.
The feet from the tips of the toes till the ankles - these three organs must be washed completely or the wudu is invalid. Even if the space of a hair is not washed he will not be mutawaddi until water reaches that place.
The part which must be wiped is the head. It is Sunnah to wipe the entire head, but if a quarter of the head is wiped the Fard amount is sufficed.

f: Are the elbows and ankles included in the washing?
b: Yes, they are included in the Fard of wudu.

f: From where have you learnt that it is Fard to wash the three organs and to wipe the head during wudu?
b:
Allaah Ta'ala has mentioned them in His Kitab:
O you who believe, when you stand for Salah wash your faces and your hands till the elbows and wipe your heads and [wash] your feet till the ankles. [al-Maidah:6]

f: What is the proof that it is Fard to wipe at least a quarter of the head?
b: The proof is the Hadith of al-Mughirah bin Shu'bah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, He said "Verily the Nabi ﷺ performed wudu and wiped his forelocks." [Muslim, Chapter of wiping the leather socks]

f: What are the Sunnahs of Wudu?
b:
They are:
Intention - he intends removing Hadath or making permissible that which is not permitted except with wudu.
Washing the hands till the wrists thrice at the beginning of wudu. He should wash properly if he has arisen from sleep. He should therefore wash them before placing them in the water vessel.
Mentioning the Name of Allaah before beginning wudu.
Using Miswak [toothstick].
Rinsing the mouth thrice.
Placing water in the nostrils and blowing it thrice.
Wiping the entire head.

Wiping the ears.
To interlace the fingers through each other.
To pass the fingers through the beard.
Washing each part thrice.
Following the order as mentioned in the Noble Quran. He thus washes his face first; then the hands till the elbows; then wipes the head; then washes the feet till the ankles.
To begin each time with the right. He thus washes his right hand then the left hand. In the same way he begins with the right foot then the left.
To wash the next part without break.
To wipe the neck.1
1 Al-Quduri has listed washing the hands before putting them in the vessel; and saying, the Bismillaah, Siwah, rinsing the nostrils, wiping the nose, takhlil of the beard and fingers, and washing each part thrice as Sunnah. He then says, "It is recommended for the person making Wudu to intend Taharah, to wipe the entire head, to wash right before left, to make the wudu with continuity and to wipe the neck. He thus made these Sunan Mustahab. On the other hand, the author of al-Hidayah has made Bismillaah Mustahab and intention and order of washing Sunnah. Because of this difference, we have mentioned them all under Sunnah so that the beginner might not be confused. The teacher should explain that Mustahab is less emphasised than Sunnah.

f: When a man or a woman has been purified of al-Hadath al-Asghar by means of wudu, when does that Taharah terminate?
b:
This Taharah is terminated by any of the following factors.
They are called nullifiers of wudu:
Emergence of excreta.
Conviction that one has passed wind through the anus, whether with sound or not.
Emergence of urine, "wady" (pre-semen fluid) or semen.
Emergence of blood, pus or pus tinged with blood. If any of these three emerge from any place to another place it terminates the ruling of purity.
Vomit if it fills the mouth.
Sleeping in a lying position.
To sleep while leaning or reclining against something, that if that object is removed the sleeper would fall.
Where one's intelligence has been overpowered with unconsciousness.
Insanity.
Loud laughter whilst in a Salah which has Ruku and Sujud.
If any of these afflict someone, he may not perform Salah till he has repeated his wudu.

f: What brings about al-Hadath al-Akbar? What makes Ghusl Wajib?
b:
Al-Hadath al-Akbar is brought about by one of the following:
Nocturnal emission of a male or female when sperm is ejaculated.
When a man enters his penis in the vagina of a woman or her anus or the anus of another man, whether sperm is ejaculated or not. The Ghusl in these cases is Fard upon both the perpetrator and the one who is penetrated. The jurists call vaginal penetration, "iltiqa al-khatanayn".
Ejaculation with a gush and lust, of sperm, whether from male or female. If any of these three occur to someone, that persion is called "jub" whether male or female.
At the end of the menstrual period.
At the end of the childbirth period.
Through these factors Ghusl becomes Fard, i.e. washing of the whole body, not even leaving the space of a hair except that it has been washed with water.

f: Is there Ghusl for emitting semen or wady?
b: Ghusl is not compulsory by emitting these liquids. They only nullify wudu as we had mentioned.

f: Are there occassions for Ghusl besides the Fard Ghusl in the Enlightened Shari'ah?
b:
Yes. Rasulullaah ﷺ has made it Sunnah to perform Ghusl the Day of Jumu'ah, the two 'Ids, Ihram and staying at 'Arafah.2 

2 Samurah bin Jundub رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrated that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "He who performed wudu for the Day of Jumu'ah, then it is good and acceptable, but he who performs Ghusl has done better." (at-Tirmizi: Chapter on Jumu'ah. "Hadith Hasan")
Ibn 'Abbas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Verily Allaah has made this day an 'Id for the Muslims. He who comes for Jumu'ah should perform a Ghusl. If he has fragrance, let him apply it. You should use Miswak." [Ibn Majah:Chapter on Beatification on the Day of Jumu'ah]
Al-Munziri said in at-Targhib, "Its chain is Hasan."
At-Tahawi quotes Zadan in Sharh Ma'ani al-Athar:Chapter on Ghusl on the Day of Jumu'ah: I asked 'Ali رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ about Ghusl. He said, "Make Ghusl when you want to." I asked, "I am asking you about the Ghusl which is important." He said, "The Days of Jumu'ah, 'Arafah, Fitr and an-Nahr.
In al-Mustadrak (447/1) al-Hakim narrates from Bakr bin 'Abdillah from Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا. It is Sunnah to make Ghusl when one intends entering Ihram and when one intends entering Makkah.
Al-Hakim said, "Sahih according to the conditions of Muslim and al-Bukhari."
Az-Zahabi agrees.

f: What are the Fard requirements of Ghusl?
b:
The following are Fard in a Fard Ghusl:
Gargling the full mouth till the throat.
Entering water into the nose till its soft part.
Wash the entire body once.3 
3 As opposed to three.

f: What is the Sunnah method of Ghusl?
b:
The Sunnah method is to begin by washing the hands. Then perform Istinja i.e. wash the front and back private parts. He should be at ease however much possible during Istinja. Remove all filth which might be on the body. Perform the Wudu which is performed for Salah. Pour water over the head and the rest of the body thrice. Pay attention to the insides of the ears, the armpits, the navel and other parts where water does not reach except with care.

Note: If the Ghusl is performed on a wooden surface, stone or tiled floor whereby the used water does not gather, he should wash his feet at the end of the Wudu as is usual. If however the used water remains in the place of Ghusl, he should delay the washing of the feet till the end of the Ghusl, after having moved to a different ground.

f: Is this method of Ghusl special for one upon whom Ghusl is Fard, or for all who perform Ghusl?
b: It is general for all who perform Ghusl, whether the Ghusl is Fard or Sunnah.

f: Is there exemption for a woman regarding moistening her hair in the Fard Ghusl? Or is it Wajib for her to tie her braids?
b: It is not necessary for a woman to tie her braids, nor is it Wajib to wet the hair as long as water reaches the roots. This exemption is only for her whose hair is braided. If her hair is not tied like that, it is Wajib for her to wet her hair together with making the water reach the roots. In the same way it is necessary for a man to wet all his hair in Fard Ghusl, even if he has much hair.

f: Explain the rules regarding the two Hadaths.
b: When Ghusl becomes Fard upon a man or a woman, it is not permissible for them to perform Salah in that condition. They may not enter the Masjid, read the Quran, touch its manuscript [Mushaf] - except with a detached covering, or perform Tawaf. It is permissible for them to remember Allah Ta'ala but not to recite the Quran. The person in al-Hadath al-Asghar may not perform Salah until he has performed Wudu. In the same way, he may not perform Tawaf of the Ka'bah. He may read Quran, remember Allaah ﷻ and enter the Mashid. He may not however touch the Mushaf of the Quran except with a detached covering.

f: Through what are al-Hadath al-Akbar and al-Hadath al-Asghar removed?
b: Purification from the two Hadaths are permissible by means of water from the sky, water of valleys, water of rivers, water of springs, and wells and sea water even if it is salty. Purification of the two Hadaths is permissible with water mixed with a pure substance and one of the qualities of the water changes e.g. flowing water mixed with sand, or water mixed with soap or saffron.

f: Are there waters which cannot be used to remove the two Hadaths?
b: Wudu and Ghusl are not allowed with water squeezed from a tree or fruit or water which is overcome by another substance so that the nature is no longer water, e.g. drinks, vinegar and broth etc.

f: What do you say about used water [ma musta'mal] which was used to remove a Hadath or used on the body to attain closeness to Allaah [Qurbah] such as when a man already has Wudu but renews it to gain reward?
b: Neither Wudu nor Ghusl are permissible with it.

f: We know that used water cannot remove a Hadath, but we want to know if it is pure or not?
b: It is pure if Hadath alone was removed with it, i.e it was not used to remove real Najasah. It is however ghayr mutahhir (cannot make pure), meaning that it cannot be used a second time to remove a Hadath. Thus if some drops of used water falls on clothing, water, or vessels, they do not become impure.

f: Can water become impure by something falling in it?
b:
Allaah has created water as pure and purifying [Mutahir]. However, it becomes inpure if any impurity falls in it, be it a little or a lot. The Nabi ﷺ ordered that water be protected from impurities. He said, "None of you should urinate in standing water which does not flow and then wash in it." [al-Bukhari from Abu Hurayrah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ in Kitabul Wudu]

He also said, "When one of you aries from his sleep, he should not put his hands in the vessel till he has washed it thrice. For verily he does not know where his hand spent the night." [Muslim from Abu Hurayrah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, Chapter on the dislike of a some making wudu inserting .....]

Thus if impurity falls in the water, neither Wudu nor Ghusl may be performed with it.

f: What do the Jurists say about Wudu made from a body of water in which impurity fell?
b: If the body is so large that its one side does not vibrate through the shaking of the other side, Wudu is permissible from the other side when impurity falls in one side. That is because it is apparent that the impurity does not reach the other side due to its distance from the side where the impurity fell.

f: What is the ruling of flowing water in which impurity fell?
b: Wudu and Ghusl are permissible with it as long as the traces of the impurity are not visible because the impurity does not remain with the flowing of water.

f: Does the death of animals in water pollute the water?
b: Yes, the death of an animal with flowing blood - bird or beast - pollute the water i.e. make it impure. The death of an animal which normally lives in the water does not make it impure, e.g. fish, frogs, crabs, just as it does not become impure through the death of that which does not have flowing blood e.g. bedbugs, flies, hornets and scorpions.

f: You have mentioned that well-water is pure. It is possible that impurity falls in it. How then is it purified?
b:
As follows:
If an impurity falls in a well, or a human, dog, sheep, or what resembles these in body dies in the well, then all the water is removed. The well is then purified.
If a dove, chicken, cat or what resembles them dies in the well, it is Wajib to remove 40 buckets of water and 50 is Mustahab.
If a rat, sparrow or what resembles them dies in the well, it is Wajib to remove 20 buckets of water and 30 is Mustahab.
This is when the corpse did not puff or disintegrate. If it is puffed or disintegrated, it is Wajib to remove all the water, whether the animal was big or small.

f: What size of bucket is considered when taking the water out?
b: A medium sized bucket which is used in wells.

f: What calculation is made when the bucket is big?
b:
If the bucket is big that it is equivalent to ten medium sized buckets, the removal of two or three buckets will suffice when a rat or the like has died. The same calculation will be made when forty medium sized buckets had to be removed when a dove and the like died.

NOTE: The meaning of removing all the water, is that there should only be so much water that half the bucket cannot be filled.

f: Some wells have a strong spring (outflow). As soon as water is taken out, it refills from the bottom. How should it be purified?
b:
When the amount which was in it has been extracted, it is purified. The word of two just men who have insight in water will be regarded as to the amount.

It is narrated from Imaam Muhammed bin al-Hasan رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى, the companion of Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى, may Allaah's mercy be upon them both, that 200-300 buckets should be taken from such as well.4 

NOTE: When a well has been declared purified, whether some or all the water had to be removed, the bucket, rope, hand of the extractor, the walls and earth of the well are all considered pure. There is no need to rewash any of these things.

NOTE: The extraction of the water is only valid after the impurity has first been removed. Even if all the water has been removed but the impurity was still there, it is not pure.

4 Ad-Durr al-Mukthar states. "This [Muhammad's narration] is easier and that [the word of two just men] is more cautious.
Ibn 'Abidin said, "his saying that is more cautious in the text is to avoid a difference of opinion and because there are narrations to that effect." (143/1)
Al-Hidayah states: There are two ways to calculate the amount of a spring-well narrated from Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ. The first is to dig a hole with the same breadth, width and depth as the well. The water must be taken from the well and thrown into the hole. When the hole is full the well is purified. The second method is to drop a bamboo or dry rope into the well and mark where the water reaches on it. Then extract twenty buckets for example. Put the bamboo back and see how much the water has dropped. The proportionate to that, extract buckets in twenties and continue that procedure.

f: Sometimes a rat is found and it was not known when it died. People have used its water for Wudu for Salah, washing clothing, vessels and other items. What should they now do?
b: If the rat has not become puffed or disintegrated, they should repeat the Salah of a day and night and rewash anything which was washed with that water. If the rat has puffed or disintegrated, then according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى they should repeat the Salah of three days and nights. Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى say that they do not have to repeat anything until it is established when the rat fell. This is easier. Imaam Abu Hanifa's رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى opinion is safer, Allaah's mercy be on them all.

f: What is the ruling of a man's or animal's Sur [leftover food or drink]?
b: The leftovers of every human are pure, male or female, junubi (one who is in need of ghusl), menstruating, Muslim or Kafir. Similarly the leftovers of an animal whose flesh can be eaten are pure. The leftovers of dogs, pigs, and hunting animals are impure. The leftovers of cats, free chickens, hunting birds like falcons and hawks are Makruh (detested), as are the leftovers of animals which live in the home like rats and snakes.

f: What is the ruling of Makruh leftovers?
b: When there is something else, it will be Makruh to use it, e.g, a man has pure water from which a cat drank and pure water from which a man drank. He wants to make Wudu. It will be better for him to use the leftover water of the man instead of the cat's leftover.

f: If he does not have any water besides the leftover of the cat, should he make Wudu with it or make Tayammum?
b: He should make Wudu with it, not Tayammum. The water is still pure, even though it is Makruh if there is other water.

f: Are there any doubtful leftovers?
b: Yes, the leftovers of donkeys and mules are doubtful because of different proofs.

f: If there is water from which a donkey or mule drank from, should Wudu or Tayammum be made?
b: Both Wudu and Tayammum should be made to remove the doubt.

f: Should Wudu or Tayammum be done first?
b:
Any one of the two is fine.

NOTE: The leftover of a man is pure as long as he did not drink wine, or no blood flowed from his gums, or he did not vomit a mouth-full. In these cases his leftovers are impure until he rinses his mouth thrice or he swallows his saliva so many times that no impurity remains in his mouth and lips.5 The leftover of a cat is impure if it ate a rat and immediately put its mouth in the water. If it does it after a while and cleaned its mouth with its saliva and the traces of the impurity are gone, then it is pure although Makruh.6 

5 Hashiyah Ibn 'Abidin 'ala ad-Darr al-Mukthar (149/1) gives this preference.
6 Al-Hidayah states, "if it ate a rat then immediately drank the water, it is impure, unless it waited a while to wash its mouth with its saliva. The exception is according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. If there is a need for the water, the requirement is to pour out the water falls away.
Ibnul Humam says that this is not according to Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى because according to him impurity is not removed except with water."

f: What is Tayammum linguistically and in Shari'ah?
b: Tayammum linguistically means to intend or aim. In Shari'ah it is to use sand and what is of the earth to in a special manner to remove the two Hadath with the intention of Taharah. The origin of this is Allaah's Words, "If you do not find water then make Tayammum with pure earth. Then wipe your face and your arms with it." [al-Maidah:6]

f: When is Tayammum permissible for the Muhdith?
b: If the Muhdith does not find water and he is travelling or outside a city; and the nearest water is a mile or more away, then he may perform Tayammum to remove the Hadath.

f: Is Tayammum allowed if there is water but one is sick?
b: Yes, if a sick person fears that by using water the sickness will worsen. If a Janub fears that bathing with cold water will kill him or sicken him and he does not have the means to warm the water, then he may perform Tayammum.

f: What is the method of Tayammum?
b: Firstly to intend the removal of al-Hadath al-Akbar or al-Asghar, whichever one it is, or to intend to make Salah permissible. Strike the hands on the earth and then wipe them over the entire face so that not even the space of a hair remains which has not been wiped by the hands. Strike the earth a second time with the hands. Wipe the right arms with the left hand, from the tips of the fingers until the upper end of the elbow. Then wipe the left arm with the right hand from the finger tips until the upper end of the elbow.

f: Is that Tayammum for al-Hadath al-Akbar or al-Asghar?
b: There is no difference in Tayammum for al-Hadath al-Akbar or al-Asghar. The methods we just described encompass both.

f: With what is Tayammum made?
b: Tayammum is permitted with pure dust and whatever is of the earth such as sand, plaster of Paris, lime, antimony and stone even if it is smooth without any dust. It is a condition for all these substances to be pure. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is not permitted except with dust and sand and they must be pure. May Allaah's mercy be on them all.

f: If a house collapses and the wind blows the dust in such a way that someone's face and arms are completely covered, is the Tayammum complete? May he perform Salah like that?
b: That is not Tayammum. The required Taharah has not been obtained, because intention is a Fard of Tayammum. On the other hand, if someone is submerged in water without an intention of Ghusl, the Ghusl is made. In the same way, if the rain wets all the organs required to be wet for Wudu and the water flows over them and he passes his hand over his head, the Wudu is made even though he had no intention of Wudu. That is because intention is Sunnah in Ghusl and Wudu, not Fard.

f: When someone makes Tayammum, can he make Nafl Salah with it?
b: He may perform whatever Fard and Nafl he wishes with Tayammum. He may do whatever one can do after Ghusl and Wudu. There is no difference between the Taharah acquired from Wudu and Ghusl and the Taharah from Tayammum. With Tayammum one can touch the Mus-haf of the Quran, read Quran and make Tawaf.

f: Is it possible for a healthy resident [Muqim] to make Tayammum in any situation?
b: A person may be healthy and resident and have water and be able to use it, but when the Janazah [funeral] has come and the Wali [guardian] is someone else, and this person fears that he will miss the Janazah if he makes Wudu, then he may make Tayammum and join in the Janazah Salah.

f: If the same situation befalls someone at the 'Id Salah and he needs Wudu?
b: In the same way, the person who fears missing the 'Id Salah if he makes Wudu, may make Tayammum and join the Imam for the 'Id Salah.

f: A man does not have Wudu and fears he will miss the Jumu'ah Salah if he makes Wudu. Can he make Tayammum?
b: He may not make Tayammum. He must make Wudu. If he catches with the Imam he should pray two Rak'at of Jumu'ah. If he misses him he should pray four Rak'at of Zhuhr.

f: Someone is short of time, for example, he awoke just before sunrise. He does not have time to perform Wudu and Salah. May he make Tayammum?
b: He must not. He must make Wudu. If he is Junub he must make Ghusl. He must then pray Qada [compensate after valid time] after the sun has arisen the height of a spear. Lack of time is not a valid excuse for Tayammum.

f: Someone does not have water and is looking for water. Is it Wajib to delay his Salah until the end of that Salah's time [Waqt?]
b: It is not Wajib on him. It is Mustahab for him to delay it to the end of the Waqt. If he finds water he must make Wudu, or else he must make Tayammum and pray.

f: A traveller forgot he had water in his baggage. He had put it there himself or had ordered someone to put it there. He made Tayammum and prayed. He then remembers the water during the Qat. Must he repeat the Salah?
b: He does not repeat according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى said, "He repeats the Salah in this situation." May Allaah's mercy be on them all.

f: Is it Wajib on a traveller who does not have water to search for water?
b: It is not Wajib unless his overwhelming thought is that there is water nearby. If he feels like that, he cannot make Tayammum until he searches for water.

f: If his travelling-companion has water, must he ask him before making Tayammum?
b:
Yes, and if the companion sells it at a price people will pay or gives it for free then he must make Wudu. If he refuses him he must make Tayammum and pray.8  

8 Al-'Iyanah states: There are three scenarios. He either sells it at a price of a place where water is scarce, or at a low price or at an excessive price. In the first two scenarios Tayammum is not allowed. In the third situation it is allowed because of harm to him. There is a difference in the definition of excessive price. An-Nawadir says it is the doubling of the price whilst others say it is a price price-settlers would not accept.

f: What nullifies Tayammum?
b: Whatever nullifies Wudu nullifies Tayammum when the Tayammum is to substitute Wudu. The Tayammum of a Junub is nullified by what makes Ghusl Wajib. Also when one fnds water or is now able to use it, both forms of Tayammum are nullified.

f: Is there a replacement for washing the feet in Wudu?
b:
Yes, many authentic Hadith prove that wiping the leather socks is a substitute for washing the feet.9

9 Ibnul Munzir said: We narrated from al-Hasan, "Seventy Companions of the Nabi ﷺ narrate that Rasulullaah ﷺ wiped his leather socks." - Nasbur Rayah (162/1)

f: Are there preconditions to wipe? [i.e. the Khuff]
b: Yes, the Khuff must be worn when already in a state of Taharah.

f: Is there a time limit to wiping? [i.e. the khuff]
b: When someone wears the Khuff in a state of purity, then becomes Muhdith, he may wipe on them from that point for a day and night if he is a resident and three days and a night if he is travelling. Whenever he makes Wudu in the allowed period, he just has to wipe the Khuffs whether resident or travelling.

f: Does the period of a day and night or three days and nights begin when wearing the Khuff or upon Hadath?
b: The period begins upon Hadath after wearing them in a state of Taharah, e.g. he made a complete Wudu at Zawal and wore the Khuffs while still pure. He then became Muhdith at travelling.

f: Can one upon whom Ghusl is Fard wipe his Khuff?
b: He may not. It is Fard upon him to wash his feet like the rest of his body.

f: Can a Khuff with holes be used?
b: If the holes are many, to the extent that thrice the size of the small toe is visible, the Khuff cannot be used for wiping on. It is allowed if the extent is less than that.

f: Is this amount in one Khuff or both? [i.e. permitted amount of hole(s)]
b: The holes of one Khuff are added, not both. If the holes of both combined equals the size of three toes, one may wipe over them. If that amount is in each or one of them, then it will not be allowed.

f: What is the method of wiping the Khuff?
b:
Use the fingers to wipe a line over the top. The fingers must first be moistened and then placed in its entirety.10 Wipe the fingers from the toes to the calf. At least three fingers must compulsorily be used on each Khuff.

10 Meaning that the fingertips will not suffice. The whole finger must be used.

f: What will nullify this wiping? [i.e. of the Khuff]
b: Whatever nullifies Wudu will nullify the wiping; as will removing the Khuff and the expiry of the period.

f: If the period has expired or one or both Khuff have been removed, but otherwise nothing has nullified the Wudu, what should he do?
b: He must wash both feet and may then pray. He need not repeat the rest of the Wudu.

f: You said that a resident can wipe for a day and a night and a traveller for three days and nights. What do you say about a traveller who comes home or a resident who then travels?
b: He who began wiping during travel and reaches home after having wiped for a day and night or more, must remove the Khuff. If less than that he may complete the period of a day and night. He who begins wiping at home and then travels, before completion of the period of a day and night then he can make 'masah' for a complete 3 days and 3 nights.

f: Can one wipe on a sock worn over the Khuff?
b: Yes, he may if he wore it before Hadath.

f: What is the ruling of wiping on socks?
b:
It is not allowed unless it is Mujallad11 or Muna''al as per Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى say that it is permisible if they are thick, not thin. May Allaah's mercy be upon them all.

11 Muallid: has leather on the top and bottom. Muna''al: has leather at the bottom like a sandal for the foot.

f: Is there wiping on something besides the Khuff?
b: A bandage can be wiped if the wound is severe; or on an organ that is broken and must be healed; or a bandage on a broken limb like an arm or leg.

f: Is it a condition for wiping on the bandage that it be put on while in a state of Taharah?
b: No, it is not. If one ties it without Wudu and then wants to make Wudu he may do so.

f: If he loosens and takes off the bandage after the wound has healed, is the wiping on it still valid?
b: In this scenario the wiping is nullified. If he was in the state of Wudu and then removed the bandage and nothing else nullifies the Wudu then he needs only wash the organ which the bandage has covered and may then pray.

f: Is wiping on the turban, headgear, Burqa' or gloves allowed?
b: No.

f: What is Hayd [Menstruation]?
b: Allaah has decreed that blood flows from the wombs of the daughters of Banu Adam. Most women have this blood flow every month. This flow is called menstruation. Its opposite is Tuhr.

f: Are there laws in Shari'ah pertaining to these two states? [i.e. Hayd (menstruation) and Tuhr]
b: Yes, there are laws mentioned in the Fiqh books.

f: What laws are applicable to a menstruating woman?
b:
There are five laws applicable to her:
She may neither perform Salah nor fast during the days of her menses. Neither Fard nor Nafl.
She may neither enter a Masjid nor make Tawaf.
She may not read the Quran.
She may not touch the Mus-haf of the Quran except with a detachable barrier.
Her husband may not have intercourse with her.

f: When she becomes purified, does she have to compensate any Salah or fast? [i.e. when menstruation ends]
b: She does not have to compensate for any Salah. That has been removed from he responsibility, except that which had to be compensated anyway from before. As for the fasts of Ramadan, that has to be kept when she becomes purified.

f: Are there minimum and maximum periods for the menses?
b: Yes, the minimum menstruation is three days and nights and the maximum is ten days and nights.

f: Is there a specific colour to the menses blood?
b: Whatever she sees of red, yellow, brown during the days of menses is menstrual blood, until she sees only white.

f: When the menstrual blood ends and she sees only white, when may she have sex?
b:
If the menses ended before ten days, she may not have intercourse until she has a Ghusl12 or the Waqt of a complete Salah passes.13 If it ends after ten days have ended, she may have intercourse without Ghusl.

12 This is when it ended in less than ten days and is her normal cycle. If however it is less than her normal cycle she may not have intercourse even if she makes Ghusl, until her normal period is completed. It is most probable that her normal period will recommence and hence it is safer to avoid sex. Al-Hidayah states so.
13 "Complete Salah" is to exclude Salah like ad-Duha and 'Id. If it happens in such times, then she must wait until the time of azh-Zhuhr passes.

f: If there is a period of purity between two bleedings, does that fall under the rule of menses or purity?
b: The "purity" which might occur during the menstrual period is still menses. All laws of menstruation still apply.

f: Are there minimum and maximum periods of purity?
b: The minimum period of purity is 15 days. This means that if there is bleeding after ten days, and before 15 days, it will not be considered menses because the minimum period of purity has not passed. There is no maximum period of purity. If she does not menstruate for years, she will still be pure until she bleeds.

f: What is Nifas?
b: It is the bleeding from a woman's womb after childbirth.

f: What is its period? (i.e. Nifas)
b: Maximum is 40 days. There is no minimum

f: What law applies to Nifas?
b: The same rules as menses. She may not make Salah, fast, sex, enter the Masjid, make Tawaf, read the Quran, touch the Mus-haf except with a detachable cover. She must compensate for missed fasts of Ramadan but not Salah as we mentioned under the laws of menses.

f: When twins have been born from the same womb, from which does the period of Nifas begin?
b: It begins with the first according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى . Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Zufar رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى says that it begins with the second. May Allaah's mercy be upon them both.

f: If a woman has a Caesarean Section, do the laws of Nifas apply?
b: The laws of Nifas will apply if blood flowed from her womb via the normal passage. If no blood flows from the womb it will be regarded as a wound with all the normal applicable laws of wounds.

f: Do the laws of Nifas apply when she gave birth the normal way but no blood flowed from the womb?
b: Yes, she must take a Ghusl and pray and fast without delay.

f: Is a woman in a state of Nifas when she has a miscarriage?
b: If some part of the foetus was completely created and is seen, such as a hand, leg, nail, hair or finger, then she is in Nifas. If no organ can be seen then it is treated as blood, flowing from the womb. If it lasts three days and nights preceded by a purity period, then that is menses, otherwise Istihadah. [see ad-Durr al-Mukthar]

f: What is the ruling of a period of purity during Nifas?
b: The purity between two bleedings within a 40 day period is still Nifas.

f: What is Istihadah?
b:
It occurs in several forms:
If she bleeds and it stops before three days it is Istihadah.
What goes over her normal period or over ten days is Istihadah.
If she bleeds for the first time and it goes over 10 days, then the ten days are menses and the rest Istihadah. If this bleeding of a beginner goes on for years, then her menses is ten days of every month, the rest Istihadah.
The bleeding of a pregnant woman is Istihadah.
The bleeding of a pregnant woman before giving birth is Istihadah.
If a woman in Nifas has a set known period, and her Nifas bleeding exceeds 40 days, then what exceeds her period is Istihadah.
If however, a woman gave birth for the first time and she bleeds for more than 40 days, then the 40 days is Nifas and the rest Istihadah.
If he has a miscarriage and no organ of the foetus is completed and this period cannot be her menses, then it is Istihadah.

f: What are the laws of Istihadah?
b: She is the same as a pure woman regarding reading the Quran, entering the Masjid, fasting Fard and Nafl and relations with the husband. If however, there is no time except that the blood is flowing then she is Ma'zur [excused]. She must make Wudu for every Waqt of Salah. With that Wudu she may perform any amount of Fard and Nafl she wishes. The Wudu ends with the end of that Waqt. When she has made wudu she may pray, make Tawaf and touch the Mus-haf.

f: What should someone with continuous nosebleed, or a wound which does not stop flowing, or continuous urine or passing of wind do?
b: They have to make a fresh Wudu for the Waqt of each Salah. With that wudu they may perform any amount of Fard and Nafl they wish. Their continuous ailment does not nullify the Wudu. The Wudu is nullified by the end of the Waqt.

f: If some other nullification arises besides their continuous ailment, is the Wudu nullified?
b: Yes, e.g. he suffers from continuous wind and then urinates, so the Wudu is nullified with the urine and does not continue until the end of the Waqt.

f: What are impurities and what kinds are there?
b:
There are two kinds: Ghalizhah and Khaififah [severe and light].

Ghalizhah includes whatever the human body emits which necessitates Wudu or Ghusl, such as excreta, urine, semen, wadi, bile, bile with blood, vomit when it is a mouth-full; blood of menses, Nifas and Istihadah; urine of a baby boy or girl whether they ate food or not; wine; flowing blood; and the flesh, fat and skin of carrion.

Also, the urine of that whose flesh may not be eaten; excreta of a cow, dog, chicken, duck, goose, hunting animals - all these are Najasah Ghalizhah, as are all parts of the pig.

Khafifah includes the urine of an animal which can be eaten, horse urine and excreta of a bird which cannot be eaten.14

14 The specification is made because the excreta of birds which can be eaten such as doves and swallows are pure according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى.

f: When does the difference between severe and light impurity arise?
b: It arises when soiled by them. If someone's body or clothes was soiled with Ghalizhah to the amount of a dirham or less, then the Salah is allowed but Makruh. If soiled with Khafifah then Salah is allowed as long as the dirt does not reach a quarter of the clothing. If the Ghalizhah is over a dirham or the Khafifah reaches the amount of a quarter of the clothing, then Salah would not be allowed.

f: If the body or clothing is soiled, what is the method of purification?
b: If the dirt is visible, then the body or clothing must be washed until the body of the dirt is removed. Pure water or liquid such as vinegar or rose water must be used. If it cannot be seen, such as urine or filthy water, then it must be washed until the person's overwhelming feeling is that it has been purified.

f: What is the ruling when visible dirt has been removed but its trace remains?
b: When the body has been removed, then the traces which are difficult to remove such as smell and colour do not matter.

f: Are there other methods to purify?
b:
Yes, the Fuqaha have expounded many, some of which we mention here:
If one tramps with one's leather socks on dirt which has a body one may scrape it on the earth when it dries. If the dirth has been removed one may pray in it.
If sperm soiled the clothing, it cannot be cleaned except with washing. If it has dried, one may scrape it off on condition that it was not mixed with urine.15 
It is enough to wipe clean a mirror or sword which has been soiled with Najasah.
If there was any Najasah on the earth and it dried and its traces removed, one may pray on that place. Tayammum may not be made with that earth. If the earth was washed and the traces of dirt removed, then both (matters) are allowed.
When a hide of carrion has been tanned, it is purified and Salah on it is allowed. Wudu from a vessel made from it is allowed. The hide of a pig can never be purified. The skin of a human may not be used out of respect.

f: What is the ruling of Istinja?
b: It is Sunnah fulfilled by wiping the place with a stone, mud or other substitute until the place is clean. To do so in odd numbers is better, not Wajib. Washing with water is better. If the Najasah extends beyond the place of emission, then stone and the like will not suffice. To use water or liquid will be Wajib.

f: What cannot be used for Istinja?
b: Do not make Istinja with the right hand. Do not use bones, excreta, food or anything which should be respected.

f: What do you say about facing the Qiblah or turning one's back to it when urinating or defecating in a building or in the open?
b: It is Makruh to face or turn one's back to Qiblah when urinating or defecating whether in a building or in the open.

f: Where is it forbidden to urinate or defecate?
b: It is forbidden to urinate or defecate in water, places of water, beneath fruit-trees, in a shade people use, in the path of people, in blowing wind, on rocks and to urinate standing.

f: What is the ruling of Salah in Islaam?
b: Salah is the greatest basic principle of Islaam after La ilaha illallaah Muhammedur Rasulullaah ﷺ. It is a pillar of Islaam which in the Quran Allaah has repeatedly commanded to be upheld. It is Fard upon every man and woman who has attained maturity and is sane. He who denies it being Fard is outside the pale of Islaam.

f: When should children be ordered to make Salah?
b:
The Nabi ﷺ has said, "Order your children to make Salah when they are seven years old. Hit them when they reach ten and separate them in their beds."16 Another narration states, "Teach the child of seven and hit them about it when they are ten."17

It is Wajib on the parent to pay attention in ordering the child for Salah. Allaah says, "And I have chosen you so listen carefully to what is being revealed.' [Taha: 132]

16 Sunan Abi Dawud: Chapter when a child must be ordered for Salah.
17 Jami' at-Tirmizi: Chapter when a child must be ordered for Salah.

f: How many times is Salah Fard in a day and night?
b: It is Fard five times in a day and night, at five specified times. Each time [Waqt] has a beginning and end.

f: Explain the beginning and end of these times [i.e. the Fard Salah].
b:
The First is Salat azh-Zuhr. Its beginning is after Zawal of the sun [after it descends from its high point]. Its end is when the shadow of each thing is double its heights plus the "fay"18 of Zawal according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى say that the time is from after Zawal until when the shadow of each thing equals its height plus the "fay" of Zawal.
The Second is al-'Asr. It begins when azh-Zhuhr ends as per the above different opinions. It ends when the sun rises.
The Third is al-Maghrib. It begins when the sun has set and lasts as long as the Shafaq has not disappeared.
The Fourth is al-'Isha. It begins when Shafaq disappears. It lasts as long as the second [true] dawn has not arisen.
The Fifth is al-Fajr. It begins when at second dawn and ends at sunrise.

18 Fay is the shadow when the sun reaches its high point at midday. Ad-Durr al-Mukthar states: Fay of Zwal is just before Zawal. It changes with different times and places.
'Umdah ar-Ri'ayah states: Associating Fay with Zawal is for the nearest association.

f: What is Shafaq?
b:
If you look to the west after sunset you will find a reddishness in the horizon which lasts 40 minutes and more. The reddishness gradually disappears and is replaced with a whiteness in the horizon. Both the redness and whiteness are called Shafaq. Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى said that Shafaq applies to the white. When the white disappears Maghrib ends and 'Isha begins.19 Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى said that the red is the Shafaq. When the red disappears Maghrib ends and 'Isha begins.

19 Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى has prefered that Shafaq refers to the white. This is according to Abu Bakr رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, Mu'az رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, and 'Aishah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا.
In Suhih Ibn Khuzaymah: When the red disappears and the white still remains, the time of al-'Isha is doubtful and not certain, because the 'Ulama have differed about the Shafaq. Some say it is the red, others the white. It is not established with knowledge from the Nabi ﷺ that it is the red. (184/1).

f: What is second dawn?
b: When night is nearly over you will find a vertical line like a pillar in the eastern horizon. That is the first or false or vertical dawn. Thereafter darkness covers the horizon. After the darkness a horizontal line of light arises in the eastern horizon and gradually increases. The horizontal light is the second or true dawn. It is also called the enlightening dawn and the horizontal dawn.

f: What are the number of Rak'at in each Fard Salah?
b: The Fard Rak'at for azh-Zhuhr, al-'Asr and al-'Isha are four. In al-Maghrib there are three and in al-Fajr there are two.

f: Are there any additional Rak'at with those?
b: Yes, there are other in Shari'ah, but they are not Fard. Amongst these are Witr which is Wajib. Then there are Sunan [Sunnahs] whose virtues are mentioned in a Hadith. We shall discuss themm InshaAllaah.

f: What is the Waqt of Salah al-Witr?
b: The Waqt of Witr is exactly that of 'Isha, except that it cannot be performed before the Fard of 'Isha, because that sequence is Wajib. The final time for Witr is as long as second dawn has not risen.

f: Are there within the times any preferred times?
b:
Yes, there are preferred times:
Isfar [yellowing of the sky] is preferred for Fajr. Begin the Salah at that time and recite the Sunnah Qira'ah in such a way that upon completion, if any nullification of the Salah is discovered, it can be repeated inclusive of the Wudu with Masnun Qira'ah. It should not be delayed so much that there is doubt if the sun might have risen.
It is Mustahab to delay azh-Zhuhr in summer and to perform it early in winter.
It is Mustahab to delay al-'Asr both in summer and winter as long as the sun has not changed i.e. it has not becomes so weak that there is no difficulty to directly stare at it.
It is Mustahab to perform al-Maghrib early both in winter and in summer.
It is Mustahab to delay al-'Isha when a third of the night has passed. These are the general rules, it is however preferred to hasten with al-'Asr and al-'Isha when the day is cloudy and to delay the others.
He who loves Tahajjud should delay Witr to the end of the night if he is certain that he will awake. He who is uncertain and fears that he might not awake should perform Witr before he sleeps.

f: Are there times in the day and night when Salah is forbidden?
b:
Yes, there are three times when Salah is forbidden:
Sunrise
Sunset
At midday when the sun is at the peak
Salah may not be performed at these times, neither Fard, nor Sunnah, nor Nafl. Also, Salatul Janazah [Funeral] and Sajdah of Tilawah may not be made.

f: Are there any exceptions to that rule? [i.e. the times when Salah is forbidden]
b: Yes, a Salah may be performed at sunset although it is Makruh. It is for a person who has not prayed al-'Asr of that day. He cannot leave out the Salah just because it is Makruh. He should ask Allaah for forgiveness for his delay. No other Salah may be performed at that time.

f: Are there any other times when Salah is disliked?
b:
Yes, there are two times when Nafl is Makruh:
After Salatul Fajr until the sun has risen to the height of a spear.
After Salatul 'Asr until the sun has set.

f: If one has made Tawaf after Fajr or 'Asr may one pray the two Rak'at of Tawaf?
b:
The Salah of Taway may also not be performed in these two times. He should wait until the sun has adequately risen or set as per the time.20

20 Al-Bukhari made a chapter in his as-Sahih called, "At-Tawaf after Fajr and Asr". He mentioned that 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ made Tawaf after Fajr and then rode off and made the two Rak'at at Zu Tuwa. Al-Imam Malik also mentions it in his al-Muwatta. Al-Imam at-Tahawi mentions it with his own chain in Sharh Ma'ani al-Athar. He then says, "'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ did not immediately make two Rak'at because it was not a time of Salah. He waited until the time of Salah arrived and then prayed the two Rak'at. This was in the presence of the rest of the Sahabah of Rasulullaah ﷺ and none of them objected against him. If he could have made the two Rak'at at that time he would have. Why else would he have delayed it, when it is inappropriate for some who has made Tawaf to delay to two Rak'at, except with an excuse."

f: Can someone pray his missed Salah after Fajr or 'Asr?
b: Yes, except that he must complete the Salah he makes after 'Asr before the sun turns yellow.

f: Can he pray Janazah or Sajdah al-Tilawah in these two times? [i.e. after Fajr or 'Asr]
b: Yes, it is permissible.

f: What do you say about Nafl after dawn and before Salatul Fajr?
b:
Beyond the two Sunnah Rak'at any Nafl before Fajr is Makruh.21

21 Nafl means extra and is applied here to anything besides Fard because it is extra to Fard, hence it encompasses Sunnah Muakkadah [emphasised] and others.

f: What do you say about Nafl after sunset and before Salatul Maghrub?
b:
One should not make Nafl after sunset, but should hasten to perform al-Maghrib.22

22 The Nabi ﷺ said thrice, "Pray before Salatul Maghrib." At the third time he added, "whoever wants to." He disliked that the people should regard it as Sunnah. Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Kitabut Tahajjud under the Chapter of Salah before Maghrib. The Hadith is clear that there is a Shar'i basis for Nafl before Maghrib but that it is not Sunnah Muakkadah. Ibn Qudamah said in al-Mughni (766/1), "The apparant opinion of Ahmad is that the two Rak'at are allowed but not Sunnah."

f: What is the ruling of Azan in Shari'ah?
b: Azan is Sunnah Muakkadah for the five Slah and Jumu'ah and for no other Salah. It has no Shar'i basis for the two 'Id, Sunan, Nafl, Istisqa [Drought Prayer] or Eclipse Prayer.

f: What are the words of Azan?
b:
Allahu Akbar [Allaah is the greatest]
Allahu Akbar [Allaah is the greatest]
Allahu Akbar [Allaah is the greatest]
Allahu Akbar [Allaah is the greatest]
Ashaddu an la illaha illAllah [I testify that there is no Illah but Allaah]
Ashaddu an la illaha illAllah [I testify that there is no Illah but Allaah]
Ashaddu an Muhammad RasoolAllah [I testify that Muhammad ﷺ is the Rasul of Allaah]
Ashaddu an Muhammad RasoolAllah [I testify that Muhammad ﷺ is the Rasul of Allaah]
Hayya 'ala as-Salaah [Come to Prayer]
Hayya 'ala as-Salaah [Come to Prayer]
Hayya 'ala al-Falaah [Come to success]
Hayya 'ala al-Falaah [Come to success]
Allahu Akbar [Allaah is the greatest]
Allahu Akbar [Allaah is the greatest]
La illaha illAllah [There is no Illah but Allaah].

f: Are any other words added at times? [i.e. to the Azan]
b: Yes, in the Azan of Fajr, as-Salaatu ghayru min an-nawm [Prayer is better than sleep] is added after Hayya 'ala al-Falaah.

f: Is there Tarji' in Azan?
b:
There is no Tarji' according to the Ahnaf.23

23 Tarji'is to silently say the two Shahadah and then repeat it loudly. It is Sunnah according to the Shawafi'.

f: Explain the words and time of the Iqamah.
b: When the people stand for Jama'ah [congegrational] Salah, the Muazzin will repeat the words of the Azan. After Hayya 'Ala al-Falaah he will add Qad Qamaati as-Salaah [Salah is established] twice. The people present in the Masjid should be able to hear him. This is the iqamah.

f: Is there a difference in the way the Azan and Iqamah are rendered?
b: Yes, the Azan is lengthened out and the Iqamah is recited hastily.

f: What is the ruling on facing the Qibla during the two? [i.e. during Azan and Iqamah]
b: It is established from the Nabi ﷺ until our present day to face the Qiblah while calling Azan and Iqamah.

f: Should the face be turned when reciting any words?
b: It is Mustahab for the Muazzin to turn to the right when saying Hayya 'alas Salah and to the left when saying Hayya 'alal falah.

f: What is the ruling of putting the fingers in the ears during the two calls?
b: It is Sunnah during Azan only. The Nabi ﷺ ordered Bilal رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ to do so. He said, "It will raise your voice." [narrated by Ibn Majah].

f: What is the ruling of Azan and Iqaamah for missed Salah?
b: Both should be called. If he wishes to perform several missed Salah at the same time, both should be recited for the first. Thereafter he may recite both for each Salah or suffice with the Iqamah.

f: Can Azan and Iqamah be called without Wudu?
b: It is only appropriate that the Muazzin has Wudu. It is permissible to call the Azan without Wudu but Makruh to call Iqamah like that. It is also Makruh for a junub to call the Azan.

f: What is the ruling of a junub having called the Azan and Iqamah?
b:
The Azan should be repeated, not the Iqamah.24

24 This is the more authentic view as stated in al-Hidayah and al-Mujtaba.

f: Is the Azan of a child allowed?
b: Yes, if the child is intelligent ['aqil] and can distinguish [Mumayyiz]. His Azan needs not be repeated.

f: What is the ruling of Azan before the Waqt?
b: It is not valid and must be repeated. Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى however has permitted the Azan of Fajr before its time.

f: Describe the preconditions of Salah by which Salah is not valid.
b:
The following is necessary upon the Musalli:
Pure from both Hadath from the beginning of the Salah until the end.
His body must be pure from Najasah.
That the place of Salah be pure.
That he wear pure clothing which cover the 'awrah [private region]. The Salah with clothing which reveals the 'awrah is invalid as is Salah with clothing soiled with Najasah.
The Salah should be in its Waqt. It may not be before the entry of its time.
He must face the Qiblah.
He should have an intention in his heart which Salah he is performing. There should be no blockage (gap) between the intention and the Tahrimah. The Muqtadi [follower] should in addition intend that he is following the Imam.

f: What should someone who neither has pure clothing nor has the means of removing the Najasah do?
b:
He should perform the Salah in that Najis clothing. The Salah will be valid and need not be repeated.25 

25 That is in the concise words of al-Quduri. Al-Hidayah expands on it thus, "There are two scenarios. If a quarter or more of the clothing is pure then he should pray in it. If he prays naked it will not be valid. A quarter of a thing can represent a full. If it is less than a quarter is pure then the ruling remains the same according to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and one of two views of Ash-Shafii. They say that Salah in the dirty clothing is leaving one Fard, but Salah naked is leaving several. According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he has a choice between the two, but praying in the clothing is better because covering the private region is not specified to Salah, whereas purity is.

f: How should one pray who does not have clothing to cover his 'Awrah?
b:
If he prays and stands and makes Ruku' and Sujud it will be correct. It will be better if he sits and does Ruku' and Sujud by way of indication only. In either case he should hide from the people.26

26 There are four scenarios: 1. Salah sitting with indications; 2. or with full Ruku' and Sujud. 3. standing with indications; 4. or with full Ruku'and Sujud. According to ad-Durr al-Mukthar all four are permissible but the first is best. See its chapter on preconditions of Salah.

f: What are the limits of a man's 'Awrah which must be covered for the Slaah to be valid?
b: A man's 'Awrah is from below the navel to the knee. The knee is included but not the navel.

f: What is a woman's 'awrah?
b:
If she is a free woman then her 'awrah for the validity of Salah is her entire body. The only exception is her face, hands and feet. This is only for the validity of Salah. It does not mean that she is allowed to show her face to non-Mahrams.27 A slave-girl's 'awrah is the same as a man's, except that she will cover her stomach and back. The rest of her body is not 'awrah.

27 Ad-Durr al-Mukthar warns about this saying, "A young woman is forbidden from showing her face to men, not because it is 'awrah, but because of fear of temptation, just as even if there is no desire, touching is worse."

f: What should one do who is unable to face Qiblah due to fear of animals or some other reason?
b: He should face whichever direction he is able to.

f: If one is confused about the Qiblah and there is none to ask about it, what is the ruling?
b: He should make an effort to ascertain and then face wherever he thinks the Qiblah most probably is.

f: If after the effort he prayed and then learnt that his Qiblah was wrong, should he repeat the Salah?
b: No.

f: What should he do if he learns whilst already in Salah that his Qiblah is wrong?
b:
He should turn to the Qiblah and continue his Salah. He need not start anew.

NOTE: When one is in al-Masjid al-Haram, it is necessary that one faces the Ka'bah exactly. As for one outside, even in Makkah, it is sufficient to face the direction of the Ka'bah.

f: List the Fard acts of Salah.
b:
There are six Faraid:
at-Tahrimah [the first Allaahu Akbar]
Qiyam [standing]
Qira'ah [recitation of the Quran] even if it be an Aayah.
Ruku'
Sujud
The final sitting for the duration of Tashshahud.

f: What is the ruling of the Faraid?
b: It is necessary to do them. The Salah is not valid if even one is omitted, whether intentionally or forgetfully. The salah must be repeated and Sujudus Sahw will not suffice.

f: What are the Wajibat of Salah?
b:
They are as follows:
Recitation of Surah al-Fatihah.
To join a Surah or three Aayat with it.
To read al-Fatihah before the Surah.
To recite in the first two Rak'at of the Faraid.
Coming to a standstill in each posture [Itminan].
The first sitting.
Tashshahud in the first and second sitting.
The word, "Salam," when intending to end the Salah.
Qunut in Witr.
The extra Takbirs of 'Id.
For the Imam to read Qira-ah aloud in Fajr, Jumu'ah, the two 'Ids, Tarawih, Witr of Ramadan and the first two Rak'at of Maghrib and 'Isha.
For the Imam to read Qira-ah softly in Zhuhr and 'Asr and after the first two Rak'at of Maghrib and 'Isha.

f: What is the ruling of Wajib?
b: If a Wajib is omitted deliberately, it is Wajib to repeat the Salah. If it was forgotten then Sujudus Sahw suffices.

f: What are the Sunan of Salah?
b:
They are as follows:
Lifting the hands at the time of Tahrimah in line with the ears if a man and with the shoulders for a woman. Men will then place their right hands on their left below the navel.
Thana after Tahrimah.
Ta'awwuz [A'uzu billah minash Shaytanir Rajim].
Tasmiyah.
To say, "Amin" after al-Fatihah.
Tasbih.
Tahmid.
Takbir of Ruku', Sujud, Qiyam [standing] and when rising from Ruku'.
Tasbih of Ruku' and Sujud.
Holding the knees with the hands during Ruku' with the fingers spread out.
During the two sittings and between the two Sajdah to sit on the left foot flat under the buttocks with the right foot raised at the side.
To point the finger at Tashshahud.
Placing the hands on the thighs during the sittings.
Qira-ah after the first Rak'at in the Faraid. In non-Faraid Qira-ah is necessary in each Rak'ah. The Imam's Takbir, "Sami'Allaahu liman hamidah," and Salam.
Salat 'alan Nabi ﷺ in the final Tashshahud.
Du'a after that which resemble those of the Quran and Hadith.
To turn right and left during the two Salam.
For the Imam to intend greeting the men, guardian angels and pious Jinn when making both Salam.
The follower should intend greeting the Imam when turning in the direction the Imam is. If he is directly in line, he should intend both times.
The follower should intend greeting the other followers, guardian angels and pious Jinn in both directions.
One praying alone should intend the angels only.

f: What are the etiquettes of Salah?
b:
They are as follows:
A man should remove his hands from his sleeves at the time of Takbir.
To look at the place of Sujud when standing, at the top of his feet when in Ruku', at the nose when in Sujud, at the lap when sitting and at the shoulders when making Salam.
Avoid coughing as far as possible.
Closing the mouth when yawning.

f: Explain the method of Salah from beginning to end.
b:
When intending to start Salah, recite Takbir to begin without voewel elongation, whilst standing and raise the hands until the ears. Afer Takbir place the right hands over the left below the navel. Then recite Thana سُبْحَانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ وَبِحَمْدِكَ، وَتَبَارَكَ اسْمُكَ، وَتَعَالَى جَدُّكَ، وَلَا إِلَهَ غَيْرُكَ "Pure is You O Allaah with Your praises. Blessed is Your Name and high is Your station. There is no illah but You." Then recite Ta'awwuz and then Tasmiyah. These three are silent. A follower does not recite the last two because there is no Qira-ah for him. Thereafter al-Fatihah is recited. Then Amin is said softly even when it is a loud Salah. Thereafter a Surah or any three Aayat are read. After Qira-ah read Takbir and go into Ruku' without raising the hands. Then grip the knees with the hands. The fingers should be spread out and the calves straight. The back must be stretched out straight in line with the buttocks. The head should neither be raised nor dropped. In Ruku' he will say at least thrice, سُبْحَانَ رَبِّي الْعَظِيمِ "Pure is my Rabb Most Magnificent." He will then raise his head from Ruku', saying "Allaah has heard he who has praised Him." He will then say immediately سَمِعَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَهُ "Praise be to You my Rabb," if he is praying alone. In congegration the Imam will suffice with the first sentence and the follower with the second. He will stand up straight. He will then say Takbir رَبَّنَا لَكَ الْحَمْدُ and go into Sujud by first lowering his knees, then his arms then his hands. He will stretch his fingers to the Qiblah, making Sujud with his nose and forehead, his armpits open. His stomach must be away from his thighs. His toes should face the Qiblah. Recite at least سُبْحَانَ رَبِّي الْأَعْلَى "Pure is my Rabb Most High." Then raise the head, reciting Takbir. Sit up straight, coming to a standstill, hands on the thighs. Recite Takbir and go into Sajdah, reciting the same at least thrice. Then say Takbir to stand again without leaning on the hands or sitting in between. First the head should be raised, then the hands, then the knees and stand for second Rak'ah. There will be no Thana or Ta'awwuz this time. When the second Sajdah of the second Rak'ah is completed, place the left foot flat under the buttocks and raise the right foot, toes facing the Qiblah. Place the right hand on the right thigh and the left on the left. Fingers are spread out on them. Recite the tashshahud of Ibn Mas'ud رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ 
التَّحِيَّاتُ لِلَّهِ وَالصَّلَوَاتُ وَالطَّيِّبَاتُ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى عِبَادِ اللَّهِ الصَّالِحِينَ، أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ
"Greetings, salutations and purity be to Allaah. Salam to you O Nabi and Allaah's mercy and blessings. Salam be on us and Allaah's pious slaves. I testify that there is no illah but Allaah and I testify that Muhammad ﷺ is His slave and Rasul (messenger)."
He will indicate with his right index finger at the time of the Shahadah, making a circle with the thumb and middle finger and closing the small and next finger. If he intended two Rak'at, Salah 'alan Nabi ﷺ is recited after Tashshahud. Du'a from Quran and Hadith is then recited, but not what resembles the words of people. Salam is then made to the right saying, "As-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah." The same is done to the left. He should turn so much that someone looking behind at his shoulders will see his cheeks. He will intend that he is greeting the Imam, the guardian angels and the fellow Musallis as we have mentioned before.
If he intented four Rak'at at the time of Tahrimah he will stand up from Tashshahud for the third Rak'ah. He will not raise his hands, nor recite Ta'awwuza and Thana. After the two Sajdah he will stand for the fourth Rak'ah. The third and the fourth is completed with standing, Qira-ah, Ruku' and Sujud as we discussed with the first two. He will sit after the second Sajdah of the fourth Rak'ah just as he sat for the first two Rak'at. He will recite the Tashshahud and Salat 'alan Nabi ﷺ offer du'a and make Salam to the right and left as discussed.

If he intended three Rak'at at the time of Tahrimah, he will sit after the second Sajdah of the third Rak'ah. He will recite the Tashahud and Salat 'alan Nabi ﷺ, offer du'a and make Salam.
التَّحِيَّاتُ لِلَّهِ وَالصَّلَوَاتُ وَالطَّيِّبَاتُ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى عِبَادِ اللَّهِ الصَّالِحِينَ، أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ [1, 2]
التَّحِيَّاتُ لِلَّهِ وَالصَّلَوَاتُ وَالطَّيِّبَاتُ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى عِبَادِ اللَّهِ الصَّالِحِينَ، أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ [1, 2]

f: What is the ruling of Sajdah on the tail of the turban or the extra part of the clothing?
b:
If it is on the forehead and he makes Sajdah it is valid but Makruh. If done with an excuse then it is not Makruh.28

28 Ad-Darr al-Mukthar states, "It is Makruh Tanzihi to makes Sajdah on the turban tail except for a reason although it remains valid as long as it is completely or partly on the forehead as has been discusses. If it is only on his head and he makes Sajdah like that deficiently then it is invalid because Sujud was not made on its place. It is also a condition that the place of Sajdah be clean and that the bulk of forehead touches the ground. People are neglectful of that." [Description of Salah]

f: Is the descriptin you have given the Salah of a man only, or a man and woman? [i.e. question 149)
b:
It is for both. A woman however differs with a man as follows:
She will place her hands on her chest.
She will not take her hands out of her sleeces at the time of Takbir.
She will raise her hands to the height of her shoulders.
She will not spread out her fingers during Ruku'. She will keep them closed and place them on her knees.
She will lower herself slightly for Ruku' to the extent that she almost reaches the full extent but she will proceed beyond that.
She will keep her elbows in during Ruku'.
She will keep her stomach close to her thighs during Sajdah.

She will sit in the tawarruk position in every sitting. i.e. She will extend her legs to the right side. Right calf on the left calf. [Buttock] sitting on the ground.
She will place her arms on the ground during Sajdah.

f: Explain the laws of Qira-ah for the Imam, Muqtadi [follower] and Mufrid [solitary Musalli].
b:
The Masail are as follows:
Qira-ah in general is Fard in every Salah.
Qira-ah of al-Fatihah is Wajib.
To read a Surah or three Aayat thereafter is also Wajib. Qira-ah in itself by fulfilling one of these two is Wajib.
The third and fourth Rak'at of Fard Salah is exempted from the above rule. Here al-Fatihah is Sunnah, not Fard or Wajib.
It is Wajib to specify Qira-ah in the first two Rak'at of Fard [i.e. it cannot be substituted into other Rak'at]
It is Wajib to read al-Fatihah before the rest of the Qira-ah.
One has a choice if one wishes to read al-Fatihah after the first two Rak'at of the Fard. To do so is better. If he wants he can recite Tasbih. If one added any Qira-ah to al-Fatihah after the first two Rak'at Sadatus Sahw is not required.
The follower will not read behind the Imam, whether in audible or in-audible Salah.29 
It is Wajib upon the Imam to read aloud in the two Rak'at of Fajr, Jumu'ah, the two 'Ids and the first two Rak'at of Maghrib and 'Isha.
Both the Imam and Munfarid reads in-audibly in all Rak'at of Zhuhr and 'Asr, the third Rak'ah of Maghrib and the last two Rak'at of 'Isha.
A Munfarid may choose to read loud or soft those Qira-ah which the Imam must read aloud [Maghrib, Esha and Fajr].
It is Sunnah for the Imam and Munfarid to read Tiwal al-Mufassal [long surah] in Fajr and Zhuhr30 Awsat [medium length]31 in 'Asr and 'Isha and Qisar32 in Maghrib. This is for residents. Travellers should read what they may.
29 Muslim narrates that Abu Musa al-Ash'ari رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrated that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "And when he reads, then you keep silent." [Chapter on Tashshahud in Salah]

30 From Suratul Hujarat to al-Buruj.

31 From Suratul Tariq until al-Bayyinah.

32 From Suratuz Zilzal till the end of the Quran.

f: Should the Imam or Munfarid read Bismilaah or Ta'awwuz aloud when the Qira-ah is loud?
b: No, they must be read softly.

f: Should the Imam or Munfarid read Amin aloud after al-Fatihah?
b: No.

f: Does a woman read aloud when praying a loud Salah on her own?
b: No.

f: Can Qira-ah be specified in certain Salah?
b: Qira-ah should not be specified when it be construed that no other Qira-ah is allowed in that Salah. It is in fact Makruh to specifiy a certain Surah for all Salah or some Salah and never read anything else.

f: If there is no Wajib specification, is there anything from the Sunnah about reading certain Surahs in some Salah, which if the Musalli chooses to read then he will be rewarded?
b:
Yes, there do appear such Surahs which will be rewarded. Some are:
It is Sunnah to read Alif Lam Min Tanzil in the first Rak'ah of Fajr of the Day of Jumu'ah, "Hal ata 'aalal Insan" in the second Rak'ah. [al-Bukhari and Muslim from Abu Hurayrah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ]
It is Sunnah to read Suratul Jumu'ah in the first Rak'ah of Salatul Jumu'ah and "Iza ja akal Munafiqun" in the second. [Muslim from Abu Hurayrah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ]
It is Sunnah to read "Sabbihisma Rabbikal A'la" in the first Rak'ah of Salatul Jumu'ah and "Hal ataka Hadithul Ghasiyah" in the second. [Muslim from Nu'man bin Bashir رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ".
It is Sunnah to read "Sahhibisma Rabbikal A'la" in the first Rak'ah of both 'Ids and "Hal ataka Hadithul Ghashiyah" in the second. [Muslim from Nu'man bin Bashir رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ]

f: How is Witr performed? How many Rak'at does it consist of?
b:
Witr is three Rak'at prayer after 'Isha. It is not permissible before it. The method is recite Takbir for beginning then Thana, Ta'awwuz, Bismillaah, al-Fatihah and the Surah thereafter. Then make Ruku' and two Sujud and then stand and pray the second Raka'ah as in any other Salah. At the end of it sit and read Tashshahud. Then stand for the third Rak'ah, read al-Fatihah and then a Surah. Then read Takbir33, raising the hands to the ears34. Read the Qunut35 and upon completion36 read Takbir and make Ruku'. Complete the Rak'ah like any other Salah's.

33 Ibn Abi Shaybah narrates from Shu'bah, "I have heard al-Hakam, Hammad Abu Ishaq saying that after completion of Qira-ah, read Takbir and then Qunut."
34 'Abdurrahman bin al-Aswad narrated from his father who narrates that 'Abdullaah bin Mas'ud رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ used to raise his hands in Qunut of Witr. [Ibn Abi Shaybah (390/3) Madinah edition; al-Imam al-Bukhari in Juz Raf'il Yadayn. In it he verifies that 'Abdullaah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ used to read al-Ikhlas in the last Rak'ah of Witr then raise his hands and read Qunut before Ruku']
35 Ibrahim عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ said, "Read in Qunut of Witr: Allaahumma inna nasta'inuka wa nastaghfiruka." [Ibn Abi Shaybah (381/3)]. Abu 'Abdirrahman said, "Abdullaah bin Mas'ud tau of Rasght us how to read in Witr: Allaahumma inna nasta'inuka wa nastaghriuka wa numinu bika wa nuthni 'alaykal khayr." [Ibn Abi Shaybah]
36 'Alqamah narrates that Ibn Masud رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ and the Sahabah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ of Rasulullaah ﷺ used to read Qunut in Witr before Ruku'. [Ibn Abi Shaybah (383/3)] 'Abdurrahman bin al-Aswad narrates from his father that when Ibn Mas'ud رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ completed his Qira-ah, he read Takbir and then Qunut. Thereafter he made Takbir and Ruku'. [Ibn Abi Shaybah (383/3)]

f: Are al-Fatihah and a Surah read in all Rak'at of Witr?
b: Yes, in all.

f: Is there Masnun Qira-ah in Witr?
b:
Yes, it is Sunnah to recite in the first Rak'ah after al-Fatihah Surah al-A'la; al-Kafirun in the second an al-Ikhlas in the third. Other narrations add al-Falaq and an-Nas with al-Ikhlas to the third Rak'ah.37

37 At-Tirmizi narrates it from 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا and an-Nasai from 'Abdurrahman bin Abzi. Ahmad narrates from Ubayy bin Ka'b رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ and ad-Darami from Ibn 'Abbas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا. These two do not mention al-Falaq and an-Nas. [See Mishkatul Masabih, Chapter on Witr].

f: Is Qunut read loud or soft?
b: It is soft, swhether one is Imam, Munfarid or Muqtadi.

f: Can Witr be performed in congegration?
b: Yes, it is Sunnah to perform it in congregation every night of Ramadan after Tarawih.

f: Does the Imam read Qira-ah aloud in Witr?
b: Yes, in all three Rak'at.

f: Is there Qunut in any Salah besides Witr?
b: No, unless it is recited due to a disaster which aflicts the Muslims. In that case Qunut is read whilst standing after Ruku'. The Imam will make du'a for the Muslims and against their enemies.

f: How many Rak'at of Sunnah are made before and after the Fard?
b:
12 Rak'at of Sunnah are emphasised. They are called Sunnah Muakkadah [emphasized]. Ummul Muminin 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا narrated that the Nabi ﷺ said, "Allaah will build a house in Jannah for he who is constant on twelve Rak'at of Sunnah - 4 before Zhuhr, 2 after, 2 after Maghrib, 2 after 'Isha and 2 before Fajr."38

Shurayh narrates that 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ never prayed 'Isha, except that he would then come by me and pray 4 or 6 Rak'at."39

38 This is the words of al-Timirzi, similarly narrated by an-Nasai. At-Tirmizi adds, "In the chapter there are also narrations from Umm Habibah, Abu Hurayrah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, Abu Musa and Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا." He then narrates the narration of Umm Habibah and declares it authentic. Muslim also narrates the Hadith of Umm Habibah and in the end says that she said, "I then always prayed these."
39 Whoever practices upon these four or six mentioned does well. However, only two are emphasised because of the narration encouraging consistency on it. Abu Dawud narrates the Hadith of Shurayh.

f: Are some of these [i.e. 12 Rak'at of Sunnah] more emphasised than the others?
b:
Yes, the most emphasised are the two before Fajr, then the four before Zhuhr. 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا said, "the Nabi ﷺ did not emphasise any Nafl as much as he placed importance on two Rak'at before Fajr."

She also said that Nabi ﷺ,  "Never left the 4 before Zhuhr and 2 before early morning." [al-Bukhari and others have narrated both narrations]

f: Are there Sunan before and after Jumu'ah?
b:
Yes, there are 4 Rak'at before and 4 after.40

That is according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the Sunnah is 6 after Jumu'ah.

40 The 4 afterwards are based on Muslim's narration from Abu Hurayrah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ who narrated that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "When you pray after Jumu'ah, pray 4." A group other than al-Bukhari narrate that Rasulullah ﷺ said, "When one of you prays Jumu'ah he must pray four afterwards." The first indicates Istihbab and the second Wujub. We have therefore combined the two as Sunnah Muakkadah. As for the four before, it is due to the consistency of Rasulullaah ﷺ on the four after Zawal which includes Jumu'ah as well.

f: Is there Sunnah before 'Asr?
b:
Yes, there is a Hadith which encourages 4 Rak'at before 'Asr. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "May Allaah have mercy on a man who prays four before 'Asr." [Abu Dawud]
'Ali رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to pray two Rak'at before 'Asr. [Abu Dawud]

f: Is there Sunnah before 'Isha?41
b:
Four Rak'at before 'Isha is Mustahab.

41 Al-Halabi says in his commentary on Munyatul Musalli, 'The four before are not mentioned specifically in a Hadith. Proof is taken from the Hadith of 'Abdullaah bin Mughaffal رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ that Rasulullaah ﷺ said twice, "Between Azan and Iqamah there is Salah." Then he said after the third time, "For who wants to." This is when there is no obstacle to praying before the Fard and is regarded as Mustahab. Four specifically is based on the view of Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى that the word, "Salah" in its complete form and quality indicates 4.'

f: What is the ruling of these Sunan? [i.e. the Sunan before 'Asr and 'Isha]
b: The Sunan before 'Asr and before 'Isha are not Muakkadah.

f: Is there Sunnah Qira-ah in any of these Sunan?
b:
Yes, at-Tirmizi narrates that 'Abdullaah bin Mas'ud رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ said, "I cannot count the amount of times I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ read in the two Rak'at after Maghrib and the two Rak'at before Fajr, 'Qul ya ayyuhal Kafirun...' and 'Qul HuwAllaahu Ahad.'"
Muslim narrates from Abu Hurayrah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to read in the first Rak'ah before Fajr, "Qulu amanna billahi wa ma unzila ilayna..."[al-Baqarah] and in the last Rak'ah, "Amanna billahi wash-had bi-anna Muslimum..." [Al-'Imran]
Muslim also narrates from Ibn 'Abbas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to readi in the Rak'at before Fajr, "... amanna billahi wa ma unzila ilayna..."42 and from al 'Imran, "... Ta'alaw ila kalimatin sawaim baynana wa baynakum"

42 It means he read in the first Rak'ah, "Qulu ammanna billahi..." until the end of the Aayah. It is clarified in al-Bayhaqi that he read until, "wa nahnu lahu Muslimun." In the second Rak'ah he read the complete Aayah from Al 'Imran from, "Qul ya Ahlal Kitabi ta'alaw ila kalimatin..."

f: Besides Fardh, Witr and the above Sunan [i.e. 'Asr and 'Isha] are there any other Salaats prescribed?
b:
Yes, Shari'ah allows one to perform whatever Nafl one is capable of day and night. There is great virtue43 in that. The Makruh times we have mentioned should however be avoided.

43 Abu Hurayrah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates that he heard Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "The first thing the slave will be questioned about concerning his deeds on the Day of Qiyamah is his Salah. If it is in order he succesful and victorious. If it is unsound then he has failed and lost. If there is a deficiency in his Fard, then the Rabb Most Blessed and High says, 'See if My slave has any Nafl to make up for the deficiency in his Fard.' Then all of the rest of his deeds are treated in the-like that.

f: Is the Nafl you mentioned for all times and conditions? Is there narrated anything about extra virtues at special times?
b:
Yes, the virtue of Nafl at the end of the night has been narrated.44 It is called Salatul Tahajjud. Also narrated is ad-Duha [early morning]45; the nights of Ramadan especially Laylatul Qadr [Night of Power]46; after Wudu47, when entering the Masjid before one sits48, when a matter befalls him49, when repenting [Tawbah]50, when in need [Hajah]51 and when seeking guidance [Istikharah]52.

44 Abu Umamah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "you should perform the Salah of the night. It is the way of the pious before you and draws you closer to your Rabb. It compensates for evil and erases sins."[at-Tirmizi].
45 Abu Hurayrah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "He who guards the two Rak'at of Duha will have his sins forgiven even if they are equal to the foam of the sea." [Ahmad, at-Tirmizi and Ibn Majah]
Mu'azah asked 'Aishah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا, How many Rak'at of Duha did Rasulullaah ﷺ pray? " 'Aishah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا used to pray 8 Rak'at of Duha and used to say, "I would never leave it even if my parents were to be resurrected for me." [Malik]
46 Abu Hurayrah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "He who fasts Ramadan with Iman and hoping for reward has his passed sins forgiven.
