He who prays the Salah of Ramadan with Iman and hoping for forgiveness has his passed sins forgiven. He who prays on the Night of Power with Iman and hoping for forgiveness has his passed sins forgiven." [al-Bukhari and Muslim]
47 Abu Hurayrah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said to Bilal رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ at the time of Fajr, "O Bilal! Tell me what deed you have done in Islaam which you have most hope in? Indeed I have heard the stepping of your sandals before me in Jannah." Bilal said, "I have no greater hope in any deed other than whenever I make Wudu at any time of the day or night I pray with that Wudu however much Salah has been written for me." [al-Bukhari and Muslim]
48 Abu Qatada رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "When one of you enters the Masjid he should pray two Rak'at before sitting." [al-Bukhari and Muslim]
49 Huzayfah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates, "When any difficulty befell the Nabi ﷺ he would resort to Salah." [Abu Dawud]
50 'Ali رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates: Abu Bakr رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrated to me and Abu Bakr رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ was truthful. He said, I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, 'There is no man who sins and then arises to make Wudu, pray Salah and seek Allaah's forgiveness except that Allaah forgives him.'" [Ibn Majah]
51 'Abdullaah bin Abi Awfa رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said: He who has a need from Allaah or any son of Adam عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ should perform Wudu and it should be a proper Wudu. Let him pray two Rak'at, praise Allaah and offer salutations upon His Nabi ﷺ. Let him then recite, "There is no illah but Allaah the Most Clement and Generous. Pure is Allaah the Rabb of the Magnificent Throne. All praise be to Allaah Rabb of all the worlds. I ask of You that which necessitates Your mercy, resolve which earns Your forgiveness, bounty of all good and safety from all wrong. Do not leave me with any sin except that You have forgiven it, no worry except that You ease it and no need with which You are pleased with except that You fulfil it, O Most Merciful of those who show mercy." [at-Tirmizi and Ibn Majah]
52 Jabir رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates: Rasulullaah ﷺ used to teach us Istikharah in all matters just as he taught us a Surah of the Quran. He said, "When a matter worries one of you, he should pray two Rak'at outside of the Fard and then say, .... [the famous Istikharah du'a]" [al-Bukhari]

f: How many Nafl Rak'at should be prayed with a single Salam?
b: In the day one may pray two or four Rak'at of Nafl with a single salam. More than that will be Makruh. At night one may pray up to 8 Rak'at with a single Salam according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the limit at night is two.

f: What do you say about someone who has started Nafl Salah and then broke it off?
b: Nafl becomes compulsory to complete once it has commenced. It should therefore be repeated.

f: If he intended four, sat in the second and broke off during the last two Rak'at, how many should he repeat? [i.e. Nafl Salah]
b: He should repeat two because the first pair was completed. Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى says that he should repeat all four.

f: Is it allowed to pray Nafl sitting when one is able to stand?
b: Yes, but the reward is halved.

f: What do you say about starting Nafl Salah standing and then sitting?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is allowed. His two companions say that it is only allowed with an excuse.

f: Is it allowed to pray Nafl on a beast?
b: Yes, one may pray riding on a beast, facing whatever direction the animal is facing and making the postures by indication. This is only allowed travelling out of the city.

f: When should one fulfil a missed Salah?
b: As soon as one remembers, except during the three times Salah is forbidden.

f: When a Salah has been missed, how does one fulfil it?
b: He should perform them in the ame order as they would originally have been prayed. This is Wajib on one who is Sahibut Tartib [one with sequence].

f: What does "One with sequence" mean?
b:
In the terminology of the Fuqaha one with less than six omitted Salah is called, "One with sequence." It is Wajib on him to fulfil the Salah which are on time as well as the missed ones in their correct sequence. It is Wajib on him to pray the omitted Salah in their correct order. He may not pray the "on time" Salah before the missed ones. If he does the opposite then he must repeat what he prayed.

For example, one of sequence prayed a missed 'Asr but he still has the missed Zhuhr to fulfil. It is Wajib on him to then pray the missed Zhuhr and repeat the missed 'Asr.

An example of "on-time" versus missed - a man of sequence remembered a missed Salah at the time of Zhuhr. He then prayed the Zhuhr before the missed Salah. It is Wajib for him to pray the missed Salah then repeat the Zhuhr.

f: Is sequence Wajib between Witr and Fard?
b: Yes. If he does pray the Witr before the 'Isha, then it is Wajib to repeat the Witr after praying 'Isha. If he fell asleep without having prayed Witr and dawn has set in, it is Wajib for him to pray Witr before he prays Fajr. If he does the opposite he must repeat Fajr.

f: Does the Wajib nature of sequence drop under any circumstances?
b:
Yes, it does in any of the following circumstances:
When the number of missed Salah reaches 6, excluding Witr.53 
Forgetting a missed Salah.
When running out of time.
When the missed Salah reaches 6, he may pray first whichever one he wishes to. He may pray the Salah which is "on time" even if he remembers that he has missed Salah.

When he forgets that he has a missed Salah and prays a Salah in its correct time that Salah is valid and need not be repeated.

If he awakens just before sunrise and he remembers that he has missed 'Isha or Witr, he should pray Fajr then and the 'Isha and Witr after the sun has sufficiently risen. He need not repeat Fajr, becaise sequence was dropped due to lack of time.

53 Ad-Durr al-Mukthar (488/1) states sequence is not necessary when time is short or when the missed Salah is forgotten. These are excuses. When they reach six according to belief they will be difficult to fulfil in sequence.

Ibn 'Abidin sayd in his Hashiyah that "according to belief" to exclude that which is Fard in practice, i.e. Witr. Even though sequence is Wajib between Witr and the others which are Fard, Witr will not be added to the missed ones in this instance because Witr is a completion of the deeds of the day and night. The numbers increase through the increase of times, and Witr does not have an independent time of its own.

f: What actions and words nullify Salah?
b:
The actions are:
Eating or drinking, even if forgetfully.

Performing many actions not of Salah.
Deliberately talking.
Walking three or more steps continuously.
Turning the chest away from the Qiblah.
Unconsciousness.
Insanity.
Hadath Akbar, whether through looking or nocturnal emission.
Standing in line with a woman who may be sexually desired in a general Salah in which she has joined from the Tahrimah and she is in the same place without any obstacle.
Fulfilling a Rukn [essential deed of Salah] with an exposed 'awrah or Najasah which prevents Salah.
Laughing so loud that you can hear your laugh.
The words are:
To speak a word, be it deliberately, forgetfully or by mistake.
Making Salam to someone.
Returning Salam verbally.
To sigh.
To groan.
To moan.
To verbally cry due to pain or calamity, but not due to remembering Jannah or Hell.
Replying to a sneezer, "May Allaah have mercy on you."
Replying "La ilaha illAllaah," to one asking about Allaah having a partner.
Saying "Inna lillah wa inna ilayhi raji'un," when hearing bad news.
Saying "Alhamdullilah," when hearing good news.
Saying "La ilaha illAllaah" or "SubhanAllaah" out of surprise.
Anything which is a reply or addressing someone, e.g. saying as speech, : Ya Yahya khuzil Kitaba biquwah - O Yahya take the Book with strength."
Rectifying someone who is not your Imam.
Such a mistake in Qira-ah or Takbir which corrupts the meaning, such as extending [madd] the Hamzah of Allaahu Akbar.54 
Twelve points of difference 

If one who performed Tayammum sees water whilst in Salah and he is able to use it.
He had wiped his Khuff and the time of wiping expired whilst in Salah.
He removed both his Khuff with minimal action.
He was unable to read Quran and then learnt an Aayah.
He was naked and found clothing.
He had to pray by indication and suddenly was able to make Ruku' and Sujud.
He remembered that he still had to pray the Salah which was before the one he was engaged in, and he was a man of sequence.
The Imam who could Qira-ah lost his Wudu and appointed one unable to read to continue the Salah.
The sun rose during Fajr.
The Waqt of 'Asr came during Jumu'ah.
He had wiped his bandage. It fell of and it proved to be healed.
A Mustahadah's bleeding stopped [woman who bleeds outside menses].
According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the Salah is void even if it occurs in the final sitting after sitting the duration of Tashshahud.

According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the Salah is complete if any of these scenarios occurred after sitting in the final sitting for the duration of Tashshahud.

54 It becomes a question, "is Allaah the greatest?"

f: List those Makruh acts which should not be done in Salah
b:
It is Makruh for the Musalli to:
To play with his body or clothing.
To move pebbles, unless they prevent him from Sujud. In that case he may level them once.
To pop or intertwine his fingers.
To place his hands at his waist.
To let his clothes hang down or pull them up.
To plait his hair.
To turn left or right by the movement of the neck.
To sit like a dog.
To spread one's arms on the ground in Sajdah.
To reply Salam with the hand.55 
To sit cross-legged, except with an excuse.
To wipe the dust off his forehead and nose.
To put something in his mouth which will prevent Qira-ah.
Anything which distracts one nad prevents concentration and humility is Makruh.
55 If he returns it verbally the Salah is nullified.

f: Explain the virtue of Jama'ah [congegration] and its status in Shari'ah.
b:
Jama'ah is Sunnah Muakkadah for men and has great reward. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Salah with jam'ah is 27 times greater than Salah alone." [al-Bukhari and Muslim from Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ]
Abud Darda رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "There are never three people in a town or countryside who do not establish Salah together except that the devil overpowers them. So uphold Jama'ah for the wolf eats the far off sheep." [Ahmad, Abu Dawud and an-Nasai].
Abu Hurayrah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrated that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "By He who hold my life in His Hand! I feel like ordering firewood to be gathered. I shall then order Azan for Salah to be called and I'll order someone a man to lead the people while I go and burn the houses of those men who are still at home." [al-Bukhari]

f: Who is most entitled to be Imam?
b: The most entitled is he who has most knowledge of the Sunnah and Shari'ah, especially the rules of Salah. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى says that he who is most versed in reading Allah's Kitab is more entitled. If they are equal, then the most pious. If they are equal, then the eldest.

f: Are there people whom it is Makruh to make Imam?
b: Yes, it is Makruh to make Imam a slave, a Bedouin, an open sinner, a blind man who is not careful with purity and illegitimate offspring. Nevertheless, if they lead the Salah remains valid.

f: May women attend Jama'ah in the Masjid?
b: It is Makruh. Their homes are better for them. Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى said that an old woman who does not display beauty may attend Fajr, Maghrib and 'Isha. Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى said that she may attend all Salah.

f: What do you say about a Jama'ah of women?
b: It is Makruh. If however it is done, then the Imam will stand in their centre just as when there is a Jama'ah of naked people.

f: Where does the follower stand if he is alone with the Imam?
b: The Imam will place him at his right. If more join in he will move forward.

f: If there is only one woman follower, where does she stand with the male Imam?
b: Behind him.

f: If the followers ar emen, women and children, how do they stand?
b: The men will first form their rows behind the Imam, then the children, then hermaphrodites then women.

f: What are the rules of following the Imam?
b:
The details are as follows:
One praying Fard can pray behind an Imam praying Fard, if both are praying the same Fard. When they differ, it is not allowed to follow, e.g. one prays Zhuhr and the other 'Asr; or one prays the Zhuhr of today and the other the Zhuhr of yesterday.
One with Tayammum can lead those with Wudu.
One who has wiped his Khuff can lead those who washed their feet.
One praying sitting due to illness can lead those praying standing.
One who must perform full Ruku' and Sajdah cannot follow one who makes by indication.

One praying Nafl can follow one praying Fard.
The opposite is not allowed.
A non-excused cannot follow an excused, e.g. a man with continous urine or passing wind or a wound which is not stopping cannot lead a man who is healthy and has proper purity.
A pure woman cannot follow a Mustahadah.
One able to recite Qira-ah cannot follow one who is unable to read the minimum Fard Qira-ah.
A clothed person cannot follow a naked person.

f: What should a follower do when he learns that Imam did not have Taharah?
b: He must repeat the Salah.

f: 56 What should a Munfarid do if he completed a Rak'ah of Zhuhr or 'Isha with the Sujud and congegrational Salah commences?57
b:
He adds another Rak'ah and joins the Jama'ah.58

56 This part is not in al-Quduri. The author of this book added it from Fat-hul Qadir and al-Fatawa al-Hindiyah.
57 i.e. actual Salah of the Imam commences, not merely Iqamah. In that case if the Munfarid did not complete the Rak'ah with Sujud, he completes the two Rak'at. There is no difference amongst our 'Ulama about this. [an-Nihayah] [Refer to al-Fatawa al-Hindiyah (119/1)]
58 What does he do if he was sitting in Tashshahud of the second Rak'ah of Zhuhr or 'Isha and Jama'ah commences? He will make Salam after the Tashahud and join the Imam.

f: If he did not yet make Sajdah? [i.e. a Munfarid when congregational Salah commences]
b: He will break off his Salah and begin with the Imam.

f: What is the ruling if he completed the Sajdah of the third Rak'ah of Zhuhr or Asr and Jama'ah commences?
b: He will complete his Salah and follow the Imam as Nafl.

f: If he did not yet make Sajdah of the third Rak'ah? [i.e. the Munfarid when congegrational Salah commences]
b: He will break off his Salah and join the Imam.

f: How does he break off? [i.e. the Munfarid when congegrational Salah commences]
b: He has a choice. If he wishes he can sit and make one Salam; or he recite Takbir standing and intend joining the Salah of the Imam. In that way both the breaking off the Salah he was praying as well as the joining with the Imam's Salah is achieved.

f: Explain what happens in 'Asr [i.e. the Munfarid when congegrational Salah commences].
b: If the Munfarid performed one or three Rak'at and the Jama'ah commenced then the ruling is the same as we mentioned in breaking off or completing in Zhuhr and 'Isha. The difference is that he will not join the Imam after completing 4 Rak'at because Nafl after 'Asr is Makruh.

f: What does a Munfarid do if he has prayed a Rak'ah or two of the Fard of Fajr or Maghrib and the Jama'ah commences.
b: If he has prayed a Rak'ah of Maghrib or Fajr he must break off his Salah whether he made Sajdah or not. He will also break off if he did not complete the Sajdah of the second Rak'ah. He will then join the Imam in these three scenarios. If he has made Sajdah of the second Rak'ah he will complete the Salah and not break it.

f: Will he [i.e. the Munfarid: see question 203] then join the Imam after completing as above?
b:
He will not join the Imam in this case.59

59 The author of al-Kanz says, "If he prayed a Rak'ah of Fajr or Maghrib and Jama'ah begins, he should break off and join the Imam."

f: What should a man do who has begun his Sunnah before Zhuhr or Jumu'ah and the Jama'ah or Khutbah begins?
b:
He makes Salam at the end of two Rak'at and then joins the Imam in Zhuhr or listens to the Khutbah as the case may be.60 

60 That has been narrated from Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ. It is also said that he should complete it. [al-Hidayah]. Ibn Humam says in Fathul Qadir that completing Salam upon two Rakat is better because he can complete it after the Fard and the two Rak'at are not null by making the Salam. He thus neither omits the Fard of listening nor misses his Salah without excuse.

f: If he began Nafl and the Jama'ah began?
b: He should complete the pair he is engaged in and not increase upon it.

f: A man reaches the Imam who is praying Fajr, and the man did not yet pray the two Sunnah before. What should he do?
b:
If he fears that he will miss a Rak'ah but will at least gain the second Rak'ah, he should pray the two Rak'at Sunnah at the Masjid entrace and then join the Imam. If he fears that he will miss both, then he should leave the Sunnah and join the Imam.61

61 That is per al-Hidayah. Al-Kafiyah states, "The book does not mention what he should do if he thinks he will at least get the final sitting, but it is obvious from the statement that if he fears missing both Rak'at he should join the Imam, hence in this situation he should also join the Imam. The Faqih Abu Ja'far narrates a view of Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى that he should pray the Sunnah, because according to them attaining the Tashshahud is like attaining the Rak'ah."
Al-Hidayah states, "The stipulation of praying at the entrance of the Masjid is due to it being Makruh to pray whilst the Imam is in Salah."

f: Someone missed Fajr and intends to pray it after sunrise. Should he pray the Sunnah as well or is the Fard sufficient?
b:
He should pray the Sunnah as subsidiary to the Fard if he fulfils it before Zawal. If after Zawal then he should only pray the Fard.62

62 Al-Hidayah states that there is a difference amongst the Mashaikh regarding after Zawal.

f: If he did not pray the Sunnahs of Fajr due to joining the Imam or due to lack of time, when should he make it up?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is not made up, whether before or after sunrise. Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى said, "I prefer that it be made between sunrise and Zawal."

f: If he misses the Sunnah before Zhuhr, when should he make it up?
b: He should pray it after the Fard of Zhuhr in its time. If the time passes then it is not performed.

f: If he is intending to pray the Sunnah which he missed before the Fard, after the Fard, must he pray four missed Rak'at first or the two which come after the Fard?
b:
He should first pray the two Rak'at then the missed four.63

63 There is a difference on what is preferred. Al-Kanz states that the four are performed before the two.
Ibnul Hamam said in Fatahul Qadir, "Praying the two first is better because that is its Sunnah time. The Sunnah time of the four has been lost. The Sunnah time of the two should not now also be lost without necessity.

f: If one misses the Sunnah before Jumu'ah should one pray it after Jumu'ah?
b: Yes, and its rules are the same as the four Rak'at before Zhuhr.

f: What should a Musalli do if afflicted with Hadath during Salah?
b: He should leave the Salah, renew his Wudu and continue his Salah where he left off. To start anew is better.

f: If he is the Imam [i.e. when afflicted with Hadath during Salah], what should he do with the followers?
b: He appoints one of the followers as Imam and the new Imam completes the remainder of the Salah.

f: What if the appointed one is a Masbuq [did not join the Salah from the beginning] [i.e. if the Imam is afflicted with Hadath during Salah]?
b: He will lead the others for the rest of the Salah and then appoint a Mudrik (one who had joined the Salah from the beginning) and the Mudrik will complete the Salam as the Imam.

f: What should the Musalli do if Hadath afflicts him after he sat for the duration of Tashshahud in a sitting when he must make Salam?
b: He should leave the Salah, make Wudu and complete the Salam.

f: What is the ruling if he spoke after the Hadath?
b: His Salah is void and he cannot continue it, whether he spoke deliberately, forgetfully or by mistake.

f: If that Musalli needs to walk to some place for Wudu or turns away from Qiblah for that purpose does his Salah break?
b: No, that is overlooked even if he walks three steps or more.

f: If Hadath Akbar afflicts the Musalli, can he continue with the Salah [after purity]?
b: He who sleeps in Salah and has Ihtilam, or becomes mad, or becomes unconscious, or laughs loudly in Salah, then the Salah is nullified. He cannot continue it. He should start his Salah anew after Ghusl in the first case and after Wudu in the remaining three cases.

f: What should a Musalli do when forgetful in Salah?
b:
If he adds an action which is an act of Salah, e.g. he repeated the Ruku' or added a Rak'ah, or he forgets a Wajib, e.g. he forgot al-Fatihah or the Sunan after it, or the first sitting or one of the two Tashshahud, or Qunut in Witr, or the Takbirs of 'Id, or the Imam read aloud in a soft Salah or soft in a loud Salah; then Sujudus Sahw must be made. It is two Sajdahs after the final Tashshahud then one Salam is made then another Tashshahud and then Salam is made.65

65 The preferred view is that he recite Salat 'alan Nabi ﷺ and du'a in the final sitting. It is also said that he should recite in both sittings as a precaution.

f: Is Sujudus Sahw Wajib on the followers if the Imam makes a mistake?
b: Yes, it is Wajib on the Imam and the followers.

f: If the Imam does not make the Sujud what does the follower do?
b: Then the follower will also not make Sujud.

f: If the follower forgets, does he have to make Sujud [Sahw]?
b: Neither he nor the Imam will make Sujud.

f: What should someone do if he forgets the first sitting in a three or four Rak'ah Salah?
b: He should examine his state. If he is closer to sitting, he should return to the sitting, recite Tashshahud and complete the rest of the Salah. There is no Sujudus Sahw. If however he is closer to standing then he should not return to sitting but continue to the standing position and complete his Salah. After the final Tashshahud he should make Sujudus Sahw and make Salam.

f: What must he do if he forgot the final sitting?
b: If he forgot to sit in a 4 Rak'at Salah and stood for the fifth Rak'ah without having yet made Sajdah, then he should abandon the fifth Rak'ah and return to the sitting. He should make Sujudus Sahw.

f: What must he do if he made the Sajdah of the fifth Rak'ah [i.e. if he forgot the final sitting]?
b:
The Fard status of the Salah is nullified because the Fard of the final sitting has been omitted. It now becomes Nafl and he should add a sixt Rak'ah.66 

NOTE: Deduce from the above rule what to do when one forgets the final sitting in a two or three Rak'at Salah.

66 If he does not add the extra Rak'ah, there is nothing against him as per al-Hidayah. Does he make Sujudus Sahw? Fathul Qadir states, "There is no Sajdah because the deficiency of nullification is not repaired with Sajdah."

f: What should he do if he sat in the Tashshahud of the fourth Rak'ah then rose thinking that it was the second Rak'ah and remembered the correct number?
b: He should return and sit if he did not make Sajdah for the fith Rak'ah. He should make Sujudus Sahw and his Salah is valid.

f: And if he did make Sajdah of the fifth Rak'ah? [i.e. if he sat in Tashshahud of the fourth Rak'ah then rose thinking that it was the second Rak'ah]
b: He will continue with a sixth Rak'ah and make Sujudus Sahw. The first four Rak'at are those he intended at Tahrimah and extra two are Nafl.

f: What is the ruling of one who is doubting in his Salah if he prayed three or four Rak'at?
b:
If that is the first time that happened in his life he must start the Salah anew. If it happened often then he should continue with what he thinks to be most probable and sit at every possibility of sitting.67 If he does not have a probable thought then he should continue with what he is certain of, i.e. the least amount and make Sujudus Sahw in both situations.68 

67 Al-'Inayah gives an example: If the doubt arose in a 4 Rak'at Salah whether it is the first or second Rak'ah he should act upon whatever his self-examination says. If there is no conclusion then, he should make it the least, i.e. the first Rak'ah. Yet he should sit on the possibility that it is the second for the sitting is Wajib. Then in his next Rak'ah he must sit again because he has acted on it being the second. In his next Rak'ah he must sit on the possibility that it is the fourth Rak'ah. In the Rak'ah thereafter he must sit because he has acted on it being the fourth in which sitting is Fard. Deduce the same rule on a three Rak'at Salah.
68 Al-Quduri does not mention Sujudus Sahw when continuing on the least or on the most probable. 
Ad-Durr al-Mukthar mentions that Sujudus Sahw is Wajib in all scenarios of doubt, whether it be self-examinatio nor continuing on the least.
As-Siraj states that Sujudus Sahw is made when one continues on the least; and when he acts on the most probable thought after thinking for the duration of a Rukn.
The text of al-Fath is as follows, "If his examination reveals something he will complete his Salah upon that and make Sujudus Sahw. Similarly in all scenarios of examination or continuing on the least Sujudus Sahw will be made... if his examination does not reveal anything then he will continue on the least.
Ibn 'Abidin ash-Shami supports this in as-Siraj, "When he ponders and his thought reaches a probability, then it is compulsary for him to act upon it. There is no cause for Sujud to be Wajib on him except if he takes long to think as has been explained."
I say that what is in al-Fath is correct because it is supported by an authentic Hadith of al-Bukhari and Muslim. 'Abdullaah bin Mas'ud رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates from Rasulullaah ﷺ, "When one of you doubts in his Salah let him ponder what is correct and complete upon that. Then he should make Salam and two Sajdah."
There is no Nass [explicit text] in the clause of Sajdah becoming Wajib when thinking long. It is however a cause for Sajdah according to the Ahnaf when one pauses for the duration of a Rukn without Qira-ah.

f: What is the reality of a single Sajdah we see readers of the Quran performing during their Tilawah [recitation]?
b: That Sajdah is callled Sajdatut Tilawah. It is Wajib upon one who recites or hears an Aayah of Sajdah, whether he intended to hear the Aayah or not.

f: What are the numbers of these Aayat [i.e. for Sajda Tilawah] and in which Surahs do they occur?
b:
They occur in the following 14 Surahs:
al-A'raf
ar-Ra'd
an-Nakhl
al-Isra
Maryam
al-Hajj
al-Furqan
an-Naml
Alif Lam Mim Sajdah
Sad
Ha Mim Sajdah
an-Najm
al-Inshiqaq
al-'Alaq
The Aayat of Sajdah are well known amongst those who memorise the Quran, and signs are indicated in the Mus-haf as well.

f: When the Imam recites an Aayah of Sajdah, is it Wajib upon the followes to make Sajdah as well?
b: Whether the Imam reads it softly or loudly and makes Sajdah, the followers will make Sajdah with him.

f: If the follower recites the Aayah of Sajdah, is the Sajdah necessary upon him and the Imam?
b: It is not compulsory upon either one of them.

f: Is the Sajdah [Tilawah] Wajib upon people who are in Salah, and they hear a man who is not with them in Salah reciting a Sajdah Aayah?
b: It is Wajib, but they should make it after Salah, not during it.

f: If they perform it in Salah [i.e. people who are in Salah and they hear a man who is not with them in Salah reciting a Sajdah Aayah], will it suffice?
b: No.

f: Will that extra Sajdah nullify their Salah?
b: No.

f: A man read an Aayah of Sajdah outside of Salah. He does not make the Sajdah. He then performs Salah and recites the same Aayah in it. If he performs a Sajdah for it, will it suffice for both recitations?
b: Yes, if both recitations were in the same Majlis [place and time].

f: What do you say about a man who read a Sajdah Aayah outside of Salah and made the Sajdah; then he commenced Salah and read the same Aayah in it. Does his first Sajdah suffice?
b: It does not suffice. He must make another Sajdah for that recitation.

f: Does one Sajdah suffice for repeating the same Sajdah Aayah?
b: One Sajdah will suffice if he repeats the same Aayah in the same Majlis. If he changes Majlis, the Sajdah equal to the number of Majlis is Wajib upon him. If he reads several Aayat of Sajdah, he must make Sajdah for each Aayah, even if it be in the same Majlis.

f: How should Sajdatul Tilawah be made?
b: Recite Takbir without raising the hands. Make a Sajdah then say Takbir and arise. There is no Tashshahud or Salam.

f: How should a sick person who cannot stand pray?
b: A sick person who is unable to stand in Salah, should sit and make Ruku' and Sujud.

f: If he is unable to make Sajdah and Ruku'? [i.e. the sick person]
b: He should indicate Ruku' and Sujud. The Sujud should be lower than the Ruku'. He should not raise anything to his head to prostrate thereon.

f: If he is unable to sit? [i.e. the sick person]
b: He should lie on his back with his legs towards the Qiblah with something below his head to raise it. He should face the Qiblah and pray like that, lying down and doing Ruku' and Sujud by indication.

f: What do you say about one who prays, laying on his side?
b: It is permissible if he lies on his side, praying with his face to the Qiblah and indicating his Ruku' and Sujud.

f: If he is unable to indicate with his head [i.e. the sick person], can he indicate with his eyes, eyebrows or heart?
b: He cannot indicate with anything besides his head. If he is unable to, then he should delay his Salah until he can.

f: How should one who can stand but cannot make Ruku' or Sujud pray?
b: Standing in not obligatory in that situation. It is best for him to pray sitting and by indications. If he stands and indicates then it is also permissible.

f: If someone was healthy and praying his Salah standing, then he became sick, how should he complete his Salah?
b: He should sit and make Ruku' and Sujud. If he cannot make Ruku' and Sujud he must make them by indication. If he cannot sit then he must lie down and indicate.

f: If someone was praying whilst sitting due to sickness and made Ruku' and Sujud, then became healthy during the Salah, does he begin his Salah anew?
b: No, he continues and stands.

f: If he prayed part of the Salah with indications and then became able to make Ruku' and Sujud, must he continue the Salah?
b: He must not continue. He must begin anew.

f: What is the ruling of Salah missed due to unconsciousness?
b: He who is unconscious for five or less Salah must pray them when he gains consciousness. When he misses more than that, he does not pray.

f: Are there separate laws in Shari'ah pertaining to travellers?
b: Yes, there are separate laws mentioned in the relevant chapters of the books of Fiqh.

f: Explain those laws relating to Salah.
b: When he intends travelling the distance covered in three day's travelling by camel or foot and will leave his city or town, he will reduce [Qasr] his four Rak'at Salah i.e. he will only pray two Rak'at for Zhuhr, 'Asr and 'Isha. There is no reduction in Maghrib, Fajr, Witr, Sunan and Nafl.

f: Will he be rewarded for praying four Rak'at when he should have made Qasr?
b: His extra two Rak'at are Makruh. Qasr is emphasised.

f: Although Makruh, if he prayed four Rak'at, has his Fard obligation been fulfilled?
b: If he prayed four and sat in the second Rak'ah for the duration of Tashshahud then the first two suffice for his Fard and the next two are Nafl.

f: What is the ruling if he did not sit in the second Rak'ah the duration of Tashshahud?
b: The Fard status of the Salah is void and becomes becomes Nafl. He must pray his Fard again.

f: Are there situations where a traveller prays four Rak'at?
b: Yes, if he is following a resident Imam or he has intended to stay at a town for 15 days or more.

f: If he intends staying less than 15 days?
b: He will continue Qasr, not complete [4].

f: A traveller enters a town and does not intend staying 15 days, but says, "I might go tomorrow or the day thereafter." What is the ruling?
b: He will continue Qasr even if it goes on for years.

f: The Muslim army enters the land of the enemy and intends staying 15 days. Do they pray the complete four?
b: They will continue Qasr because their intention is not definite.

f: A traveller leads residents in a four Rak'at Salah. Does he make Qasr?
b: Yes. The residents will complete their four Rak'at when the travelling Imam makes his Salam upon the second Rak'at.

f: Does the travelling Imam make any announcement to the followers?
b: Yes, it is Mustahab for the Imam to announce after Salam, "Complete your Salah for verily we are a travelling people."

f: If a traveller intends staying at Makkah and Mina for fifteen days is he a traveller or resident?
b: He is still a traveller because the intention of residence is based on a single habitation.

f: A traveller has returned to his town and did not intend to stay for 15 days. Does he complete or shorten his Salah?
b: He will complete four Rak'at when entering his town, however short the period. There is no condition of having to intend to stay.

f: A man was born in a town and lived there for years. He then made another town his hometown. He then enters the first town for some need. Does he complete or shorten his Salah?
b: He will make Qasr if the first town is the distance of three days journey or more from his new town. The Nabi ﷺ made Hijrah from Makkah to al-Madinah and made Qasr when he went to Makkah.

f: A traveller missed a Salah and upon entering his town wishes to pray it; or a resident missed a Salah and now wishes to pray while on travel. What do they do?
b: The principle behind it is that Qada [compensation Salah] is like Ada [original]. One who missed a Salah in travel makes it up as two Rak'at even when already at home. A Salah missed at home is fulfilled as four even when done during travel.

f: Is Qasr for an obedient traveller only or for sinners as well?
b: Both.

f: In this era people travel by car and plane and do not feel difficulty in it. Do they make Qasr despite that?
b: If they leave their hometowns intending a journey of three days distance then they will make Qasr. They journey in itself is in a place of the difficulty of journey.

f: Is a traveller allowed to join between two Salah, such as Zhuhr and 'Asr and Maghrib and 'Isha?
b: It is allowed in practice when the two times join, but not in each others' times. Allaah says, "Verily Salah is prescribed upon the believers at set times."

f: What do you mean it is allowed in practice but not in each other's times? [i.e. combining between two Salah]
b: A joining in practice is to delay Zhuhr and hasten 'Asr. Zhuhr is prayed right at the end of its Waqt and 'Asr right at the beginning of its Waqt. Similarly Maghrib is prayed at the end of its Waqt and 'Isha at its beginning. This is joining in practice and is called "Jam' Suwari" [Joining in Form] in the terminology of the Fuqaha. According to us a Salah in the time of the other is not allowed, whether delaying or bringing ahead. That is joining in a Waqt which the Fuqaha call, "Jam' Haqiqi" [Real Joining].

f: What is the ruling of Salatul Jumu'ah?
b: It is Fard 'Ayn [obligatory on each individual] on male who is free, mature, intelligent, and healthy, can see and is resident.

f: Are there conditions to establish it? [i.e. Salatul Jumu'ah]
b:
Yes, they are as follows:
That it be in a city or the prayer grounds of a city. It is not allowed in villages.
That the Sultan or one whom he orders establishes it. Or that the Muslims agree on it and appoint an Imam to lead them in Jumu'ah.70 
It has to be in the Waqt of Zhuhr. It is not valid before or after that.
A Khutbah [lecture] before the Salah. According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى a concise mention of Allaah will suffice. According to the other two Imams a lengthy discourse which can be called a lecture is necessary.
A congregration. The minimum according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى is three, excluding the Imam. Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى said that the minimum is two, excluding the Imam.71
70 Al-Quduri only said, "That the Sultan or one whom he orders establishes it." The author added, "Or that the Muslims agree on it and appoint an Imam to lead them in Jumu'ah." Al-Fatawa al-Hindiyah quotes Ma 'arijud Dirayah, "In lands where the rulers are Kuffar the Muslims may establish Jumu'ah and a judge may be appointed with their consent. It is Wajib upon them to seek a Muslim ruler." (146/1 - Egyptian Edition)
Ibn 'Abidin ash-Shami has also quoted it like that from Ma'araijud Dirayah in Raddul Muhtar (540/1).

71 Neither al-Quduri nor al-Hidayah mentions general permission to attend as a condition for the validity for Jumu'ah. It is however mentioned in the books of the Ahnaf. It means that the doors of the Masjid should be open and all people allowed to enter. If a group enters and then locks the door upon themselves, then it is not valid as per al-Fatawa al-Hindiyah quoting al-Muhit. Ash-Shami mentions in his commentary on ad-Durr al-Muhtar, "This condition is not mentioned in the Zhahirur Riwayah nor in al-Hidayah. It is mentioned in an-Nawadir. Al-Kanz, al-Wiqayah, an-Niqayah, al-Multaqi and other reliable texts rule according to it."

f: List those reasons which excuse one from attending Jumu'ah
b:
They are as follows:
One who travelled the distance of Qasr.
Women are excused.
Sickness.
Blindness.
One is a slave.
It is thus not obligatory upon a traveller, woman, ill, blind or slave.

f: If these people [i.e. those who are excused, see question 272) attend Jumu'ah have they fulfilled the Fard of that Waqt?
b: Yes.

f: Is the Salah of the Imam and followers valid if a slave, sick man, traveller or blind man leads freemen, healthy men and residents for Jumu'ah?
b: Yes, it is allowed and the Jumu'ah is valid.

f: What should one who has missed Jumu'ah for a reason do?
b: He should pray Zhuhr as should one who did not attend Jumu'ah without a valid reason. If he did not have a valid reason he has sinned.

f: Is it allowed to pray Zhuhr at home without any reason, before the Imam prays Jumu'ah?
b: He has committed a sin.

f: If he did that anyway [i.e. pray Zhuhr at home without any reason before the Imam prays Jumu'ah] and the Waqt of Zhuhr passes, has his Salah fulled fthe Fard of that Waqt?
b: Yes.

f: What is the ruling if he goes to join the Imam for Jumu'ah after having prayed his own Zhuhr?
b: The Jumu'ah is valid. According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the Zhuhr is void as soon as he sets off for Jumu'ah. According to his two companions it is void when he joins the Imam in the Salah of Jumu'ah.

f: Should those who are excused and prisoners pray Zhuhr in congegration on the Day of Jumu'ah?
b: It is Makruh. They should pray individually.

f: What should one who has missed a Rak'ah of Jumu'ah do?
b: Continue and then pray what was missed.

f: What should he do [one who has missed a Rak'ah of Jumu'ah] if he gains the Salah when the Imam is in Tashshahud or Sujudus Sahw?
b: He should continue the missed Rak'at of Jumu'ah according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. According to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى, if he attained most of the second Rak'ah, he should continue with Jumu'ah. If less, then he will continue with Zhuhr, i.e. he will pray four Rak'at with that Tahrimah.

f: What is the ruling of buying and selling after the Azan of Jumu'ah?
b: "When the call is made for the Salah of Jumu'ah then hasten to the remembrance of Allaah and leave of trade." [Quran]

f: What is the ruling of Salah and talking after the Imam emerges?
b: When the Imam emerges, the people should not pray Salah or talk until he completes his Khutbah according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. According to his two companions there is no harm in talking as long as he did not begin the Khutbah.

f: How many times is Azan called for Jumu'ah?
b:
Twice:
When the sun drops from its zenith then they should turn their attention to Jumu'ah. They must leave trade and hasten to the remembrance of Allah.
When the Imam ascends the Mimbar [pulpit] and sits on it. Azan is then called in front of him. The Imam then gives two Khutbah after which the Salah commences.

f: Describe the Sunnah Khutbah.
b: The Imam will stand and give two Khutbahs, sitting a while in between them.

f: Does the Imam read a loud or soft Qira-ah during Jumu'ah?
b: Loud.

f: What is the ruling of listening carefully to the Khutbah if one is far?
b: The far one is like the near one. Listening carefully and maintaining silence is Wajib whether one is near or far, whether one can hear the Imam or not.

f: What is the status of the Salah of the two 'Id?
b: It is Wajib upon whomever Jumu'ah is Wajib upon.

f: What are the beginning and end times for it?
b: The beginning time is when Salah becomes permissible when the sun is high enough. The end time is when the sun drops from its high point. It is Mustahab to hasten the Salah on 'Idul Adha because the sacrifices follow the Salah. It is Mustahab to delay it on 'Idul Fitr.

f: What are the Sunan of the two days of 'Id?
b: It is Mustahab on the two days to use Miswak, make Ghusl, apply fragrance and wear one's best clothes. On the Day of Fitr eat an odd number of dates or something sweet and pay the Sadaqatul Fitr before going to the Musalla. On the Day of Adha delay eating until the return from the Musalla when Udhiyah is made and eat from it.

f: Is Takbir proclaimed on the way when going to the Salah of the two 'Id?
b:
Takbir is reciting loudly on the way to the Musalla on the Day of Adha according to our three Imams. On the Day of Fitr Takbir is recited according to the two besides Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى.72

72 That is according to al-Quduri. According to al-Fatawa al-Hindiyah Takbir is recited loudly on the way on al-Adha and stops when one reaches the Musalla. On the Day of Fitr the preferred view is that it is not recited loudly. It is Mustahad to recite softly as per al-Jawharah an-Nayirah (150/1). This shows that the difference regarding Takbir on Fitr is regarding method and not the Takbir itself. See Ibn 'Abidin's commentary on ad-Durr al-Mukthar (558/1).

f: Is there a known Sunnah regarding going to the Musalla?
b: It is Mustahab when going for either 'Id Salah or take one route and to return on another,

f: Can one pray Nafl in the Musalla before Salatul 'Id?
b: No Nafl is prayed in the Musalla before 'Id Salah or afterwards.

f: Describe the method of 'Id Salah.
b: The Imam and the people will come out of their habitations to the outskirts of the city. The Imam will lead the people in two Rak'at. He will commence with Takbiratul Ihram, then Thana, then three loud Takbir, raising his hands with each Takbir. He will then recite Ta'awuz and Bismillah softly. He will then recite al-Fatihah and a Surah loudly. He will then complete the remainder of the Rak'ah like any other Rak'ah. He will rise for the second Rak'ah, recite Bismillah softly and al-Fatihah and a Surah loudly. After the Qira-ah he will loudly recite Takbir thrice, raisign the hands of each time. He will then recite Takbir for a fourth time to go into Ruku'. He will not raise his hands this fourth time. The Rak'ah will then be completed as in any other Salah. He will make Salam after Tashshahud, Salah 'alan Nabi ﷺ and du'a.

f: Are the hands left hanging at the sides or placed below the navel between the extra Takbirs?
b: They are left hanging after all extra Takbirs except for the third Takbir in the first Rak'ah after which he will place his hands under the navel.

f: Those are the actions of the Imam [i.e. regarding leaving the hands during the Takbirs of 'Id]. What do the followers do?
b: The followers will imitate him in all acts except three things which they do not do - Ta'awwuz, Bismillah and Qira-ah. They will not make Takbir loudly but softly.

f: Is there Khutbah in the Salah of the two 'Ids?
b: Yes, two Khutbahs in each Salah is Sunnah. The Imam will deliver the Khutbah, teaching the people the laws of 'Id such as Sadaqatul Fitr in the Khutbah of 'Idul Fitr; and the laws of Udhiyah and Takbir of Tashriq in the Khutbah of al-Adha.

f: What is the status of the Khutbahs of the two 'Ids?
b: They are Sunnah and are delivered after Salah.

f: What is the ruling for those present to listen carefully?
b: Listening carefully and keeping silent is Wajib in every Khutbah, be it that of Jumu'ah or 'Id.

f: A man was delayed and missed the 'Id Salah. Does he pray it afterwards [Qada]?
b: There is no Qada of 'Id Salah.

f: If the new moon was covered by clouds and the Imam received testimony of the moon's sighting after Zawal, when will 'Id Salah be prayed?
b: The next day.

f: When will it [i.e. 'Id Salah] be prayed if something prevents the people from praying it the next day?
b: It will not be prayed after the second day.

f: When will the Salah be prayed if some obstacle arises on the Day of al-Adha?
b: It will be prayed the next day or the day thereafter, but not after that.

f: What is the Takbir of Tashriq?
b:
To recite after every Fard Salah73, "Allaahu Akbar! Allaahu Akbar! La ilaha illAllaah. WAllaahu Akbar, Allaahu Akbar, wa lillahil hamd."

73 There is no harm to recite it after 'Id because it has been the constant practice of the Muslims. To follow them is Wajib. The 'Ulama of Balk have ruled accordingly. [ad-Durr al-Mukthar]. The meaning of no harm here means it is recommended [ad-Durr al-Mukthar (564/1)].

f: What are the beginning and final times of this Takbir [i.e. of Tashriq]?
b: It begins after the Fajr of the Day of 'Arafah. The last is after 'Asr of the Day of Nahr. This is according to Imaam ABu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. According to his two companions it ends after 'Asr of the final day of Tashriq. The Fatwa is according to them.

f: Is this Takbir [i.e. of Tashriq] loud or soft?
b: The Imam and followers will recite aloud, women soft.

f: If the Imam forgets the Takbir of Tashriq, will the follower recite it?
b: Yes.

f: What is the Status of this Takbir? [i.e. of Tashriq]
b:
It is Wajib upon one who has prayed any of the five Fard or Jumu'ah. It is read immediately after Salam.75

75 The meaning of immediately is to recite it without such a pause which prevents one from continuing Slah. Thus if he leaves the Masjid, talks deliberately or accidentally, or breaks his Wudu deliberately then the Takbir falls away. There are two views regarding turning one's back to the Qiblah. As for falling into Hadath unintentionally after Salam then the more correct opinion is to read Takbir and not to go and renew Wudu. [Raddul Muhtar (562/1)]

f: What are the Muslims commanded to do when the sun eclipses?
b: The Imam will lead the Muslims in two Rak'at without any Azan or Iqamah. It will be prayed in the form of Nafl i.e. 1 Ruku'and 2 Sajdah per Rak'ah. The Imam will lengthen the Qira-ah and then offer du'a until the sun appears.

f: Is the Qira-ah in it [i.e. in Salatul Kusuf (Eclipse prayer)] loud or soft?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is soft and according to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is loud.

f: Which Imam will lead the people in this Salah [i.e. in Salatul Kusuf (Eclipse prayer)]?
b: The Imam who leads them in Jumu'ah.

f: If the Jumu'ah Imam is not present [i.e. in Salatul Kusuf (Eclipse prayer)]?
b: The people will pray individually.

f: Is there a Khutbah in this Salah [i.e. in Salatul Kusuf (Eclipse prayer)]?
b: No.

f: What do the Muslims do when the moon exclipses?
b: Pray individually.

f: Is there any other action besides Salah in the two eclipses?
b:
'Aishah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا narrated that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Verily the sun and the moon are signs from amongst Allaah's signs. They do not eclipse due to the death or life of anyone. When you see that, make du'a to Allaah, Salah and Sadaqah."76 
Asma رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا narrated, "The Nabi ﷺ commanded that we set slaves free during solar eclipse."77 

76 Al-Bukhari, Chapter on charity during eclipse.
77 Al-Hidayah states, "Rasulullaah ﷺ did it once and did not do it the next tiem, so it is not Sunnah."
Ash-Shami states in Raddul Muhtar, "That is because a Sunnah is what he constantly acted upon. Doing it once and then leaving it means that it is recommended."

f: What is the meaning of Istisqa?
b: Seeking rain when afflicted by drought.

f: What is done in Salatul Istisqa?
b: There is a Shar'i basis for the Salah but it is not Wajib. It is allowed to suffice on du'a and seeking forgiveness. Sometimes Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed Istisqa and sometimes he did not pray it, but made du'a for rain whilst on the Mimbar for Jumu'ah. All that is established from him ﷺ.

f: What is the meaning of the words of Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى found in the books of Fiqh, "There is no Sunnah Salah for Istisqa."?
b: It means that Salah is not specified in Istisqa, it is not Sunnah Muakkadah that Istisqa is not valid without the Salah (e.g. du'a).

f: How will the Imam lead the people in the Salah? [i.e. Istisqa]
b: The Imam and the people will walk to the outskirts of the city with humility. They will display meekness to Allaah and lower their heads. The Imam will pray two Rak'at with loud Qira-ah. He will face the people and deliver two Khutbahs. He will invert his cloak during the Khutbah. He will make the top bottom and the bottom on top. He will bring the right edge to his left shoulder and vice-versa. The people will not invert their cloaks. He will then face the Qiblah after the Khutbah and engage in du'a. The people will sit facing the Qiblah, making du'a, seeking forgiveness and repenting. It is appropriate that Istisqa be made with the presence of the weak ones, old men, old ladies and children.

f: Is there any other act besides what you have mentioned [i.e. see answer to question #319 regarding Salatul Istisqa]
b: Yes, they should give charity before going to the Salah.

f: Is there an extra Salah in the month of Ramadan besides the Fard and usual Sunan?
b: Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "He who keeps the fast of Ramadan with Iman and hoping for reward has his past sins forgiven. He who stands in worship in Ramadan with Iman and hoping for reward has his passed sins forgiven." [al-Bukhari and Muslim] It is obvious from the Hadith that there is a Salah in the nights of Ramadan, over and above that which is prayed in the other nights.

f: How is this Salah [i.e. Tarawih] prayed in the nights of Ramadan?
b: The Imam leads the people in 20 Rak'at after 'Isha. He will make Salah upon every two Rak'at with a total of 5 rests in between.

f: What is the meaning of 5 rests? [i.e. in Tarawih]
b: A rest [Tarwihah] after every 4 Rak'at. That is why it is called Salatul Tarawih. The Imam will rest with the people the duration of the 4 Rak'at.

f: Is this Salah [i.e. Tarawih] Sunnah for women as well?
b: Yes, it is Sunnah Muakkadah for men and women. The men will pray in congegration in the Masajid and for women their homes are best,

f: What is the status of congegration for men in Tarawih?
b: It is Sunnah Muakkadah with Kifayah [collective] status. If all the people of the Masjid abandon it they have sinned.

f: Is Witr prayed in congegration during Ramadan?
b: Yes, after the five rests, the Imam will lead them in Witr in congegration. He will read the Qira-ah aloud in all five Rak'at. He and the followers will read the Qunut softly.

f: Is Witr prayed in congegration out of Ramadan?
b: No.

f: How will the Imam lead the people when the enemy is attacking and there is much fear?
b: The Imam will divide the people in two groups. One group to confront the enemy, and the other to pray behind them. He will pray a complete Rak'ah with that group. When he raises his head from the second Sajdah, that group will go face the enemy. The next group will come and the Imam will lead them in a Rak'ah. He will make Tashshahud and Salam but they will not make Salam. Upon his Salam they will go to face the enemy while the first group will complete their second Rak'ah without Qira-ah. They will make Tashshahud and Salam. They will go back to the enemy. The second group will come, and pray their remaining Rak'ah with Qira-ah. They will make Tashshahud and Salam.

f: What will the Imam do if he is resident? [i.e. during Salatul Khawf (Congegration Prayer during fear)]
b: He will pray the four Rak'at Fard, two Rak'at with each group.

f: How will he pray Maghrib with them? [i.e. during Salatul Khawf if the Imam is a resident]
b: He will pray two Rak'at with the first group and one with the second.

f: If the fear is so intense that they cannot meet for congegration nor can they dismount? [i.e. for Salatul Khawf when facing the enemy]
b: They will pray individually on their mounts, doing Ruku' and Sujud by indication.

f: What if they are unable to face the Qiblah? [i.e. when the fear is so intense whilst facing the enemy and people have to pray individually]
b: They should pray wherever they can.

f: If some of them are dismounted on the ground, how should they pray? [i.e. whilst facing the enemy]
b:
They will pray without walking and must fulfil the Ruku' and Sujud. If they are unable to fulfil them then they should do so by indication.78

78 "The infantryman will indicate when he is unable to make Ruku' or Sujud. [al-Fatawa al-Hindiyah (156/1)]

f: If they were forced to start fighting while they were engaged in Salah, what is the status of the Salah?
b: If they fought or walked, it is void because of many actions.

f: What should they do if the enemy attacks and they are unable to perform Salah with Ruku' or Sujud, not even by indication, whether individually or following the Imam?
b:
They should delay the Salah as Rasulullaah ﷺ did at the Battle of Khandaq,79 and pray it when they can even if Qada.

79 Al-Bukhari narrates just before the Book of Azan that Jabir bin 'Adbillah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates that 'Umar bin al-Khattab رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ came after sunset and cursed the Kuffar of the Quraysh. He said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ, I was only able to pray 'Asr when the sun was about to set." Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "By Allaah, I was unable to pray it." We then went to Bat-han. He made Wudu for Salah and we did likewise. He prayed 'Asr after sunset and then prayed Maghrib.

f: Allaah has made the Ka'bah the Qibla which the Muslim must face in Salah. Is Salah valid if prayed inside it?
b: Yes, both Fard and Nafl will be valid.

f: If the Imam prays in the Ka'bah and a follower's back faces the back of the Imam, is his Salah valid?
b: Yes.

f: And if a follower has his face to the face of the Imam? [i.e. when the Imam is inside the Ka'bah]
b: It is valid but Makruh.

f: And one whose back faces the Imam's face? [i.e. is his Salah valid whilst the Imam is inside the Ka'bah]
b: His Salah is not valid because he stood in front of the Imam.

f: When the Imam stands outside the Ka'bah in al-Masjid al-Haram and the people circle the Ka'bah and follow him, is their Salah valid?
b: Yes.

f: Is that a general rule [i.e. when the Imam stands outside the Ka'bah in al-Masjid al-Haram and the people circle the Ka'bah and follow him] or are certain followers excluded?
b: The follower who is closer to the Ka'bah on the side that the Imam is facing is excluded. His following is incorrect for being ahead of the Imam. The Salah is valid of one who is closer to the Ka'bah than the Imam if he is at a side different to the Imam's.

f: Is Salah on the roof of the Ka'bah valid?
b: It is valid but Makruh for not showing honour to the Ka'bah.

f: What should those who are present by someone is dying do?
b: When someone is about to die, he should be laid to on his right side and face the Qiblah. He should be encouraged to recite the Shahadatayn. When he dies his jaws should be tied and his eyes closed. The laws of a woman are like that as well.

f: How is a corpse washed?
b:
The corpse should be laid on a platform perfumed an odd number of times80. A cloth should be placed over his private region and his clothing removed. Wudu is then made for him, excluding washing his mouth and nose. His head and beard is washed with Khitmi81. He will then be laid on his left side. He will be washed until it is seen that the water reaches the platform beneath him. [Then do the same with the corpse on the right side.] The washer will then make him sit and lean against him. He will gently wipe the stomach. If something comes out of the corpse he will wash it there. He will not repeat the full Ghusl. He will then let the corpse lie on its left side and wash it, pouring camphor water over it. That is the third and final wash.

80 The corpse shoud be laid on a platform perfumed an odd number of times, up to a maximum of seven times just like when he is put in coffin cloth and when he dies, i.e. on three occasions. [ad-Durr al-Mukthar].
Ash-Shami said, "That the perfume should be taken around the platform one, thrice, five times or seven times, nothing more. This is in al-Fath, al-Kafi and an-Nihayah. At-Tabyin sets the maximum at five. 'On three...' means that the corpse is perfumed on three occasions i.e. when the soul departs to remove the bad odour when he is washed; and when he is dressed..."(574/1)
81 A plant with a pleasant aroma.

f: Is anything besides water used for cleaning? [i.e. the deceased]
b: Yes, the water can be boiled with lotus or potash and used to wash the corpse. Soap is also allowed.

f: If these things are not available? (i.e. lotus, potash or soap for cleaning the deceased)
b: Then with plain water.

f: Explain the number of Kafan [shrouds] and method of shrouding for men and women.
b:
There are details in this matter as follows:
The Sunnah kafan of a man is Izar [lower cloth]; Qamis ["shirt"] and lifafah [covering]. The minimum is Izar and lifafah. Under necessity, whatever can be found. To use only one cloth without an excuse is Makruh.
The izar is from head to feet. The lifafah is the same. The Qamis is from below the neck to the feet without pockets, attachments or sleeves.
The shrouds are perfumed in odd numbers. The lifafah is laid out, then the izar over it. After drying the corpse so that it does not wet the shrouds, it is placed on the izar. Hanut perfume is applied to his head and beard. Camphor is applied to his places of Sajdah i.e. forehead, nose, palms, knees and feet. He is first dressed in the Qamis82. Then the izar is folded over the corpse from his left side then from his right hand side. The same is then done with the lifafah. The right folds must be over the left folds.
If it is feared that the shrouds will open, the sides may be tied with something.
The Sunnah kafan of a woman is a Dir' ["armour"], izar, khimar ["headscarf"], lifafah and khirqah ["cloth"]. The khirqah is used to tie her breasts and Dir' refers to Qamis. The minimum kafan is izar, lifafah and khimar. Under necessity, whatever can be found. To use two cloths without an excuse is Makruh.

The khirqah should reach from the breasts to the thighs.
The khimar should be 3 arm spans long.
The shrouds are perfumed in odd numbers. The lifafah is laid out, then the izar over it. The corpse is placed on the izar. The dir' is put on. Her hair is made into two plaits and are placed over the dir' on her breasts. The khimar is then put over that.83 The khirqah is then tied84 above the Qamis. The Izar is then folded then the lifafah. The sides of the shroud can be tied if it is feared that it will open.
82 Spread half the Qamis on the izar and fold the other half, leaving the head side free. When the corpse is put on the izar enter his head into the cut out part of the Qamis. Then spread out the top half over the corpse.

83 The khimar is put over her head and plaits from two sides is placed over her chest above the Dir'.

84 According to some Fuqaha the khirqah is tied after the other shrouds. We prefer what is in al-Ikthiyar because it is supported by Ahadith.

f: Is there corpse's hair combed?
b: Neither the hair nor beard is combed; nor the nails clipped; nor the hair cut.

f: Describe the Salah for the dead.
b:
The imam will stand in line with the corpse's chest. The people will stand behind him and try to form three rows.85 The Imam and the followers will proclaim Takbir and recite Thana and Allaah's praises. If they wish they may recite "SubhanakAllaahumma ..." until the end. After a second Takbir, Salat 'alan Nabi ﷺ is recited. After a third Takbir du'a is made for the deceased and the Muslim, living and dead. After a fourth Takbir, Salam is made.86

85 Malik bin Hubayrah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates: I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, "There is no Muslim who dies and three rows of Muslims pray upon him except that [Jannah] becomes compulsory." Because of this Hadtih Malik would form the people into three rows when they were few at a funeral. [Abu Dawud]
86 Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates from Hafs bin Ghiyath who narrates from Ash'ath who narrates from ash-Shu'va that after the first Takbir Hamd and Thana is recited, Salat 'alan Nabi ﷺ after the second, du'a after the third and Salam after the fourth.
In India and Pakistan the du'a narrated by at-Tirmizi is most frequently recited, "Allamaghir lihayyina wa mayyitina .."

f: What du'a is read for a child's funeral?
b: Allaahummaj 'alhu lana farataw wa ajra

f: Will they raise their hands for the Takbir of Janazah Salah?
b: No, only for the first Takbir.

f: Is Jam'ah a conidtion for praying this Salah? [i.e. Salatul Janazah]
b: No. Even if a single woman or man prays it, the Fard Kifayah is fulfilled.

f: What are the conditions and Fard of the Salah [Janazah]?
b:
Conditions include being free of al-Hadath al-Akbar and al-Asghar. The clothing and place must be clean. The deceased must have been purified and placed before the Musallis. There are two Fard:
Qiyam
and four Takbir
Everything besides that is Sunnah.

f: Can the Funeral Prayer be held in a Masjid built for five time's Salah?
b:
It is Makruh. The Nabi ﷺ would pray it outside of the Masjid where the deceased would be placed.87

87 Al-Bukhari narrates from Abu Hurayrah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ that Rasulullaah ﷺ announced the death of the Negus on the day that he died. He went with the Muslims to the Musalla, formed them into rows and recited four Takbir upon him.
'Abdullaah bin 'Umar  رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates that the Jews brought to Rasulullaah ﷺ a man and woman from them who had committed Zina. He ordered their execution. They were stoned near the place Funeral Prayers were held at the Masjid.
The first Hadith clarifies that he went out to the Musalla to pray, even though the corpse was not present. The second Hadith states that Funerals were at the Masjid.
Muhammad bin 'Abdullah bin Jahsh رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates, "We were sitting in the courtyard of the Masjid where Funerals were held. Rasulullaah ﷺ was sitting amongst us ..." This Hadith of Ahmad clarifies that the place of Funerals was the courtyard of the Masjid.
Ibnul Humam states in Fathul Qadir, "And then there is the narration in Muslim that when Sa'd bin Abi Waqqas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ died, 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا said, 'Bring him into the Masjid so that I may pray upon him.' They refused her and she said, 'By Allaah, the Nabi ﷺ prayed over the two sons of Bayda in the Masjid - Sahl and his brother.

f: Who is most entitled to lead the Salah?
b: The most entitled is the Muslim ruler if he is present, if not then the Imam of the district, if not then the guardian.

f: If someone besides the ruler or the Imam prayed it [i.e. Salatul Janazah], is the guardian allowed to repeat the Salah?
b: Yes.

f: If the guardian has prayed the Salah [Janazah], may anyone else repeat it?
b: No.

f: What is the ruling if the deceased was buried without Salatul Janazah?
b: It may be prayed at his grave for up to three days, and not thereafter.

f: How should the men carry the corpse and how should they walk?
b: They should take the four legs of the bier. They should walk with speed without shaking. One who wishes to carry the bier in such a way that the corpse's right shoulder will be on his right shoulder, then move back so that the right back portion is on his right shoulder, then the front left shoulder on his left shoulder then move back so that the back left portion is on his left shoulder.

f: Can the people sit in the graveyard?
b: Yes, although it is Makruh to sit before lifting the bier from the men's necks.

f: How should the grave be?
b: The grave should be dug to half a man's height or till the chest. If dug deeper then it is good. It is preferred then that the Lahd type then be dug. If the earth is soft they choose the Shiqq method then it too is allowed.

f: How is the corpse entered into grave?
b:
From the Qiblah side. The one who places it in the grave will recite, "Bismillah wa billah wa 'ala millati Rasulillah ﷺ.88 He will make it face the Qiblah, lying on its right side. The knots tied to prevent the shroud from opening will be untied. The Lahd will be closed with level unbaked bricks and then covered with soil.

88 At-Tirmizi narrates from Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to recite that when he entered the corpse into the grave. The narrator also said, "Bismillah wa billah wa 'ala sunnati Rasulillah."

f: If baked bricks, wood or reed is used to level and close the Lahd?
b: Baked bricks and wood is Makruh, reed is no problem.

f: How should the grave be completed after the sand was placed on it?
b: The grave should be like a camel's hump, not level. It should not be higher than a hand span.

f: What is the ruling on making the grave firm with lime or cement?
b: These are sins which Rasulullaah ﷺ forbade.

f: Is Salah read on a baby who was born, cried and died?
b: A baby which cried after birth or showed any sign of life is named, washed and his funeral held.

f: If he neither cried nor showed any sign of life?
b: He will be wrapped in a khirqah and buried without Salah.

f: Is there a difference in the laws of a martyr?
b: Yes, some laws differ.

f: Describe those laws [i.e. those which differ for a martyr]
b: A Muslim has been slain by Kuffar; or is found in the battlefield with wounds from which he died; or has been oppressively killed by other Muslims in a situation where Diya [bloodmoney] is not Wajib; then he will be shrouded and prayed upon without Ghusl.

f: If the martyr died while Junub will he be given Ghusl or not?
b: Al-Imam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى said that he will be washed and his two companions said that he will not be washed. They disagree in the same way about a child martyr. Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى said that he will be washed and they said that he will not be washed.

f: We know that a martyr is not washed like other dead, but is his blood washed and his clothing removed?
b: The blood is not washed and his clothing is not removed except for his fur, outer garments, leather socks and weapons are removed.

f: Someone has been wounded in the battlefield. He then eats, drinks or is treated. He then dies. Is he regarded as a martyr?
b: If Allaah wills he will receive a martyr's reward and is a martyr in the Sight of Allaah. As for the laws amongst humans, he is not regarded as a martyr who is not washed. The eating, drinking and medication is termed as irtithath.

f: What is the ruling of one who is wounded on the battlefield and remains alive and the Waqt of Salah passes while he retains his senses; or he is carried alive from the battlefield?
b: This is also irtithath. He will be washed like a normal deceased.

f: What is the ruling of one killed in hadd [prescribed Islamic punishment] or Qisas [retaliation]?
b: He will receive Ghusl and Salah.

f: Is Salah performed upon rebels and highway robbers?
b: No.

f: What is the meaning of Zakah linguistically and Islaamically?
b: Linguistically Zakah is purification and increase. In Shari'ah it is the decree of Allaah the Lawgiver, that the owner of a set amount makes a poor Muslim owner of a set portion of his wealth for the sake of Allaah, in a way that the first owner terminates his benefits of ownership in all aspects.

f: What is the status of Zakah in Islaam?
b:
It is a Fard amongst that which Allaah has made Fard. It is a Pillar of Islaam.91 Allaah has commanded it in His book, "And establish Salah and give Zakah." He who denies it being Fard is a Kafir and has left the pale of Islaam.

91 Must Fuqaha list Zakah before Fasting in following the sequence in the Quran and because it is the most virtuous act of worship after Salah. Allaah has linked Zakah with Salah 32 times in His Honourable Book. [Raddul Muhtar]

f: Upon whom is Zakah Fard?
b: It is Fard upon a free, mature, intelligent Muslim who owns the complete requisite amount in complete ownership upon which a year has passed.

f: What is the complete requisite amount [Nisab]?
b: It is to own 200 Dirham of silver; or 20 Mithqal of gold; or the equivalent of either amount in the prevalent currency; or a trader owning trade goods to the value of either amount.

f: A man has the requisite amount but in indebted. Is Zakah Fard upon him?
b: Substract the debt from his wealth. If the remainder equals or exceeds the Nisab then Zakah is payable on the remainded.

f: Is there Zakah on trade goods?
b: Yes, if it is worth either 200 Dirham or 20 Mithqal of gold.

f: What do you mean, "if a year passes"?
b:
If a free mature Muslim owns the Nisab or more, then he has to pay Zakah on it if he has owned it for a complete lunar year. The Solar year is not reckonded.92

92 Every year on the date the Zakah first became Wajib.

f: What do you say about residential buildings, the clothes worn on the body and furniture in the house?
b: There is no Zakah on these as well as one's transport, slaves used for service and weapons which are used.

f: If these items are for trading then is there Zakah? [i.e. for residential buildings, clothes worn on the body and furniture of the house, as well as one's transport, slaves and weapons]
b: Yes, if they reach the Nisab.

f: Is it permissible to give the price in Zakah if the Zakah was payable on gold, silver or goods?
b: Yes, giving the value of Zakah is allowed.

f: What is the ruling of someone who gave all his wealth in charity but did not intend Zakah?
b: The duty of Zakah has been lifted from him.

f: What should someone do if his wealth has been destroyed after Zakah has become Wajib?
b: If all his wealth has been destroyed then the duty of paying Zakah has also been lifted from him. If part of his wealth has been destroyed, then that proportion falls alway. That is if it was destroyed by others. If he himself destroyed it then Zakah does not fall away.

f: Upon what amount of silver is Zakah Fard?
b: When one owns 200 Dirham of silver and a year has passed in possession of it, then Zakah must be paid. He will pay a fortieth of his wealth, which amounts to 5 Dirham out of every 200.

f: If he owns more than 200 Dirham, how does he pay the extra amount?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى there is no extra Zakah until the extra amount reaches 40 Dirham. He will then pay another Dirham on the 40 in addition to the 5 and then again another Dirham for each additional 40 Dirham he might own. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he will pay in proportion to whatever exceeds 200, however little or much it may be.

f: Upon what amount of gold is Zakah Fard?
b:
When one owns 200 Mithqal93 of gold and a year has passed in possession of it, then Zakah must be paid. He will pay a fortieth of his wealth, which amounts to a half Mithqal. Thereafter for every 4 Mithqal he will pay 2 Qirat. There is no Zakah upon the extra amount less than 4 Mithqal according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. His two companions say that a half Mithqal is due on 20 Mithqal and anything above 20 is calculated proportionally.

93 Ad-Durr al-Muktar: "Nisab of gold is 20 Mithqal and silver 200 Dirham. 10 Dirham weights 7 Mithqal or Dinar. A dinar equals 20 Qirat. A dirham equals 14 Qirat. A Qirat is 5 barley. The Shar'i Dirham is thus 70 barley, and a Mithqal is 100 barley or 1 and three-sevenths of a Dirham."
As for the new weights, the people of accounting differ. Some say that 20 Mithqal equals 85 grams, others 87g, others 90g. Caution is desirous in the Shari'ah, hence one who owns 85g of gold or its value for a year should pay Zakah. There is a difference on silver as well. Some say 595.1g; or 609.2g; or 612.3g. Caution calls for that here too the least amount be declared the Nisab. So one who owns 595g of silver or lots value in the prevalent currency should pay Zakah on it.

f: Is there Zakah upon gold and silver ornaments or vessels?
b: All gold and silver are Zakatable, whether in nugger form, ornament or vessel and whether it is used or not.

f: What is the ruling on gold or silver which is debased with other metal?
b: If the overwhelming composition is silver then it is regarded as silver. If the overwhelming proportion is alloy then it is treated as an alloy. The same applies to gold.

f: A man neither has gold nor silver, but government recognised bank notes. Is there Zakah payable?
b: Yes, if the notes reach the value of either Nisab of gold or silver. It is like goods of value. Everything is bought with it and it is used in trade. The government is obliged to imburse one who brings these notes to the bank.

f: What is the ruling of Zakah on trade goods?
b: Zakah is Wajib on trade goods if the value reaches the Nisab of gold or silver. They will be valued to reach the value of either amount so as to benefit the poor. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى they will be valued with whatever is used to buy them. If they are bought with gold, they will be valued with gold. If they are bought with silver, they will be valued with silver. If they are bought with neither gold nor silver they will be valued according to the prevalent city. According to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى they will be valued according to the prevalent currency in all conditions.

f: How is Zakah of wealth paid?
b: The proportion Allaah has decreed, i.e. one-fortieth must be given to those whom it is permissible to be given to with a simultaneous intention to fulfill the Zakah when paying it or a simultaneous intention when setting aside the obligated amount.

f: What is meant by, "simultaneous when setting aside the obligated amount?"
b: When he calculates his wealth at the end of the year, he takes out the amount to be paid in Zakah and makes an intention that every time he finds someone entitled he will spend from it on him. Ever time a poor person comes and he gives him from that separated wealth the Zakah is being fulfilled even if he does not bear in mind the intention of Zakah at the time of payment.

f: A man with Nisab gets additional wealth during the year. Is Zakah payable on it?
b: He will add the additional wealth to the same type he owns and calculate the Zakah.

f: Is it permissible to pay Zakah before the end of his Zakah year?
b: Yes, the Zakah has been rendered.

f: A man possessing Nisab paid his Zakah at the end of the year. During the following year his wealth falls below Nisab. Does he pay Zakah?
b: If he again has Nisab by the end of the second year, Zakah is Wajib upon him. Nisab only need be considered at the ends of the years. The drop during the year is of no relevant.

f: A man has trade goods worth less than Nisab. He however also has gold and silver. Does he pay Zakah?
b: If the total value of the gold, silver and goods reaches Nisab then Zakah is payable.

f: A man has less than 20 Mithqal of gold and less than 200 Dirham of silver. Does he pay Zakah?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he will add the value of the two, and if the Nisab is reached Zakah is payable. According to his two companions they will not be added according to value, but according to proportion.

f: Please give an example of the above difference of opinion. [i.e. when a man has less than 20 Mithqal of gold and less than 200 Dirham of silver]
b:
A man has 100 Dirham of silver and 5 Mithqal of gold worth 100 Dirham. Zakah is Wajib according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى but not the other two. The Nisab has been attained according to him by way of value. It has not been attained according to them by way of proportion. On the other hand if the man had 100 Dirham and Mithqal worth 100 Dirham, Zakah is payable according to all of them. The Nisab has been reached according to both methods.95

95 The 100 Dirham is half Nisab and the 10 Mithqal is half Nisab. If the proportions are added then full Nisab is attained.

f: Is Zakah payable on anything else besides gold, silver and trade goods?
b: Yes, on Sawaim.

f: What are Sawaim?
b: Animals which graze in the fields like camels, goats and cattle. Zakah is only Wajib on them if they suffice on grazing for most of the year. If they have to be fed fodder for at least half the year, then Zakah is not payable.

f: What is Wajib in these categories? [i.e. related on Sawaim]
b: Each category has a different amount payable and different Nisab.

f: Is their Zakah on animals used for labour, carrying or are fed fodder at home?
b: No.

f: Explain the amount of Zakah paid on camels.
b:
There is no Zakah on less than 5 camels. If there are 5 to 9 which have grazed freely and a year has passed on them then a sheep is payable. Two sheep are payable on 10 - 1 4 camels. 3 sheep are payable on 15 - 19 camels. 4 sheep are payable on 20 - 24 camels. A camel in its second year is payable on 25 - 35 camels. A camel in its third year is payable on 36 - 45 camels. A camel in its fourth year is payable on 46 - 60 camels. A camel in its fifth year is payable on 61 - 75 camels. 2 camels in their third year is payable on 76 - 90 camels. 2 camels in their fourth year is payable on 91 - 120 camels.

The sequence then begins anew. At the next 5 camels a sheep and 2 camels in their fourth year is payable. At 10, 2 sheep with the camels. At 15, 3 sheep with the camels. At 20, 4 sheep with the camels. At 25, a camel in its second year with the camels. This sequence continues until a total of 150 camels are owned. Upon that, 3 camels in their fourth year are paid.

The sequence then begins anew. At the next 5 camels a sheep and 3 camels in their fourth year is payable. At 10, 2 sheep with the camels. At 15, 3 sheep with the camels.
