At 20, 4 sheep with the camels. At 25, a camel in its second year with the camels. At 36, a camel in its third year with the camels. This sequence continues until a total of 196 camels are owned. Upon that and until 200, 4 camels in their fourth year are paid.

The sequence begins anew as per the calculations of 50 until after 150.

f: Is any distinction in the amounts made between Arabian camels and cross-breeds?
b: No.

f: Explain the amount of Zakah payable on cattle.
b:
There is no Zakah on less than 30 heads of cattle. If the number reaches 30 cattle which spent most of a year freely grazing and they have been possessed for a full lunar year then Zakah of a calf - male or female - in its second year is payable. For 40 cattle a calf of either sex in its third year is payable. According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى an additional calculation is made for an amount above 40 until 60. A fortieth of a third year female calf is due on one above 40; two-fortieths on 2; 3 fortieths on 3. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى there is no extra Zakah on the extra amount above 40 until 60. When the cattle reach 60 heads96 then 2 calves in their second year of either sex are due. On 70 a calf in the third year and a calf in the second year are due. On 80, 2 calves in their third year are due. On 90, 3 second year calves are due. On 100, 2 second years and 1 third year. In this way, in every 10 the Zakah will change between second and third years.

96 There is no difference amongst them on less than 40 and 60 and above.

f: How is Zakah on buffaloes calculated?
b: There is no difference between calculation on cattle and buffaloes.

f: Explain the Zakah payable on goats.
b: There is no Zakah on less than 40 sheep. If one owns 40 sheep which have freely grazed for most of a year and have owned them for a year, then on 40 - 120 sheep, 1 is due in Zakah. 2 Sheep are due on 121 - 200 sheep. 3 sheep are due on 201 and then 4 sheep are due on 400. Then 1 sheep for every 100.

f: Is there a difference between the Zakah of sheep and goats?
b:
No.98

98 Ash-Shami stated, "if he has sheep below the Nisab and also has goats that if they are added together then the Nisab is reached, the Zakah becomes Wajib. The Nisab will be taken from the respective animal and if it was reached by combing the two then Zakah is taken from whichever is most. If they are equal then from whichever he wants to.

f: Is Zakah payable on horses?
b:
If one owns Sawaim horses (whether male or female) for a year then one has a choice - either pay a Dinar for each horse or value them and pay 5 Dirham in every 200 of the value. According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى if only stallions are owned then Zakah is not due.99

99 Al-Hidayah: because they do not reproduce. Similarly if there are only mares owned.

f: Is there a difference regarding Zakah on horses?
b: Yes, Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى disagree with Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and say that there is no Zakah on horses.

f: Is Zakah payable on mules and donkeys?
b: Only if they are for trade in which case the Zakah payable on trade goods must take them into account.

f: What does Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى say about the offspring of camels and cattle?
b: There is no Zakah on the babies of camels, sheep and goats according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى unless they are with adults. It is Wajib according to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. [There are further details to his view which can be read in al-Hidayah].

f: What does the Zakaat-collector do if he does not find in the herd what must be taken?
b: He will take a lesser animal and more to equal the amount due, or he will take a higher animal and pay the difference back.

f: Should the collector take the best wealth or the worst?
b: He should take something in between.

f: If the Nisab remains but the non-Zakatable excess has been destroyed, is Zakah calculated on the entire remainder or is it decreased in proportion to the destroyed wealth?
b: The principle according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى is that Zakah is Wajib on the Nisab not the excess. Hence the Wajib is intact according to them. According to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Zufar رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the Wajib decreases in proportion to the loss.

f: I do not understand. Please explain by way of an example. [i.e. with regards to question 419: if the nisab remains but the non-zakatable excess has been destroyed]
b:
Ponder over this example carefully. A man has 9 camels over which a complete year has passed. 4 then were destroyed. He must pay a complete sheep, just as if there had been no excess over 5. The destroyed 4 are overlooked as normal excess in which Zakah is not paid until the camels reach 10. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى.

According to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Zufar رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he has to pay 5-ninths of a sheep. They have spread the Wajib across the 9 camels and proportionately decreased the loss over the nine.

A second example: A man has 80 goats of which 40 were destroyed after the year. According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى a sheep is due on the remainder. According to the others, a half sheep.

If 60 were destroyed then a half is due according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and a quarter according to the others. [See Fathul-Qadir, al-'Inayah and al-Jawharah an-Nayyirah]

f: Is Zakah payable on fruits and crops?
b: Yes, one-tenth or one-twentieth is paid according to the water used.

f: Is there a Nisab in that? [i.e. regarding fruits and crops]
b: Not according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. Zakah is on whatever comes from the earth, whether little or many, except wood, reeds and grass which does not have Zakah according to him. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى there is no Zakah unless something has remaining fruits and it reaches 5 Wasq. There is no Zakah on vegetables according to them.

f: What is a Wasq?
b: A measurement of the people of al-Madinah equal to 60 Sa'.

f: What are the details of the payment of a tenth and half of that?
b: A tenth is due on plants naturally water e.g. rain. A twentieth is due from plants watered by artificial irrigation such as water-wheels and water-scoops, according to one of the two views.

f: What do Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى say about crops which are not measured with Wasq such as saffron and cotton?
b: According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى if the crop is valued at 5 Wasq of the lowest value crop measured in Wasq then a tenth is due. According to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى a tenth is due when the crop reaches 5 of its biggest measurements e.g. 5 bales of cotton and 5 Amna [a measurement] of saffron.

f: Is Zakah paid on honey?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى, yyes, whether a little or a lot. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى there is no Zakah until it reaches 10 bags, according to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى 5 Farq.

f: How much is a Farq?
b: 36 'Iraqi Ritl.

f: Is 'Ushr paid on land on which Khiraj is paid?
b: The Khiraj suffices.

f: Are expenses like workers' wages, expenses on cattle etc. deductible from the tenth or twentieth.
b: No the Zakah is paid from the entire amount, be it a tenth or twentieth.

f: Upon whom can Zakah be spent?
b:
Allaah has explained it in His Honoured Book, "Verily Sadaqah is for the Fuqara, Masakin, the workers on it, whose hearts are to be united, slaves, debtors, in the way of Allaah and travellers." There are thus 8 categories:
Fuqara
masakin
workers on it
whose hearts are to be united
slaves
debtors
in Allaah's way
travellers

f: Who is a Faqir?
b: He who has minimal possessions which does not reach Nisab.

f: Who is a Miskin?
b: He who does not have anything.

f: What is meant by, "workers on it"?
b: Those whom the ruler sends to collect the Zakah from the Muslims. They go to them and collect, spending their time in that. The ruler will pay them from the Zakah according to their labour.

f: What is the meaning os alves?
b:
To help a Mukatab100 free himself.

100 A slave who has a contract with his owner that if he pays the owner a certain amount he will be set free.

f: Who is a debtor?
b: One who is indebted that he is unable to repay it from his wealth.

f: What is meant by, "in the way of Allaah"?
b: Those who have gone to Jihad and have been separated from their groups and are in need of money for expenses.

f: Who is a traveller?
b: A traveller who does not have money on his journey even if he has money at home.

f: Define whose hearts are to be united.
b:
They are those whom Rasulullaah ﷺ gave from the wealth of Zakah to, to soften their hearts to enter Islaam. They were leaders of tribes. It was hoped that through them becoming Muslim, their people would accept Islaam. When Islaam gained victory and became independent of them the ruling of giving to them was dropped. They are not given wealth after the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ.101

101 Ibnul Humam said, "They were of three types - Kuffar whom Rasulullaah ﷺ gave to soften their hearts to enter Islaam; some whom he gave to in order to avert their evil; and some who had embraced Islaam but were weak and needed strengthening."

f: That leaves 7 categories [i.e. besides "whose hearts are to be united"]. Must one paying Zakah give each category or will some suffice?
b: He can pay a single person of a single category, or may spread it amongst more.

f: Can Zakah be paid to a Kafir who is Faqir or Miskin?
b: No, even if he is under Muslim rule.

f: Can Zakah funds be used for shrouding or building a Masjid, Madrasah, bridge or public road?
b: No, and if done the Zakah must be paid again. The principle in Zakah is that one entitled must take ownership of it. There is no taking possession in the examples given.

f: What is the ruling if the Zakah was given to one in charge of the Madrasah?
b: It is allowed if he made the supervisor his representative to spend it on the Faqir and Miskin students, on condition that the supervisor makes them the owners. The Zakah is not fulfilled by simply making the food permissible for them; nor by constructing buildings of the Madrasah; nor by using it for the salaries of the teachers or other employees of the Madrasah.

f: Is Zakah fulfilled if used to buy a slave and then freeing him?
b: No.

f: Is it allowed to pay one's Zakah to one's poor relatives?
b:
There are two kinds of relatives. One kind is by birth e.g. parents, grandparents, children and grandchildren. The other is nor by birth e.g. brothers, sisters, paternal uncles and aunts, maternal uncles and aunts, and their descendants. Zakah cannot be paid to the first category. The Zakah is not fulfilled if given to any parent or grandparent or descendant of either sex.
Zakah can be given to the second category for which there is two rewards - the reward of Zakah and the reward of maintaining family ties.

f: How should it be given? Must you say, "This is Zakah?"
b: There is no need to expose that. One may give it in the guise of a gift as long as one intended it as Zakah, the Zakah is fulfilled. The recipient must also be of the categories we explained who are entitled to take Zakah and may not be of Banu Hashim.

f: Is Zakah fulfilled when given to one's husband/wife?
b: It is not fulfilled according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى, according to his two companions it is fulfilled if a woman gives it to her husband.

f: What is the ruling of giving Zakah to a rich man or his son?
b:
It is not permissible to give Zakah of any kind of wealth to a rich man i.e. the one who has Nisab102 free of his principle needs. It cannot be given to his son who is small and has not reached puberty. It can be given to a rich man's adult son if he is poor, not possessing Nisab.

102 Fathul Qadir (202/2): "In summary Nisab is of three kinds. One is which makes Zakah Wajib upon its owner. It increases naturally or by adding, and he is free of debt. Another Nisab is that which does not necessitate Zakah and that is when it is encompassed by the needs of the owner who can then accept Zakah. If not in his need, then Zakah is Haram for him e.g. his clothing equals Nisab and he does not need them all nor he does not need to use all his furniture in his house; or a slave whose service he does not need; or a horse he does not ride; or a house he does not need to live in. If he is really in need of any of these then he is a Faqir and one can give him Zakah. However, begging is not allowed for him. The third Nisab is that which prohibits beginning. It is when he owns enough food for the day or does not own it but is capable of earning it or owns 50 Dirham (with different views on this amount)."

f: Is there such a Faqir or Miskin to whom Zakah cannot be given?
b: Yes, Zakah cannot be given to Banu Hashim, even if they are poor. They are the descendants of 'Ali رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, Al-'Abbas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, Ja'far رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, 'Aqil رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ and Harith bin 'Abdil Muttalib رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ.

f: If these people [i.e. Banu Hashim] are in need, how can they be helped?
b: Donate to them without intention of Zakah or any other compulsory charity.

f: A man paid his Zakah to someone whom he thought is entitled. It then became known that he was rich or a Hashimi or a Kafir; or he gave it to a poor man in the dark who turned out to be his father. Has his Zakah been fulfilled?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it has been fulfilled. Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى says that he should pay it again in all these scenarios.

f: What do out three Imams say about someone who paid Zakah to someone he thought was entitled and then leart that he is his Mukatab or slave?
b: They all say that his Zakah has not been fulfilled.

f: Can Zakah be paid to a healthy man who earns but does not own Nisab?
b: Yes.

f: Is it permissible for somone to send his Zakah to a land where he does not live?
b: In principle, each people should spend their Zakah amongst themselves and not send it to another land. It is Makruh to do that unless it is sent to relatives or to a people in greater need than his own people.

f: What is the ruling of Sadaqatul Fitr?
b:
It is Wajib upon a free Muslim if he owns Nisab of any form of wealth, in excess of his residence, clothing, furniture, transport and weapons.103

103 It applies to a well-off person who is forbidden to take Zakah.

f: On whose behalf does one have to pay?
b: Himself, his small children and his slave who serves him, even if the slave is a Kafir.

f: Does he pay for his small children from his own wealth or theirs?
b: If they have wealth then from theirs, otherwise from his own.

f: Is a man obligated to pay on behalf of his wife and adult children?
b: No, even if they are of his household, just as he is not obligated to pay for his slaves whom he buys and sells.

f: Who should pay for a slave owned by partners?
b: It is not Wajib on any of them.

f: When does Sadaqatul Fitr become Wajib?
b: It is Wajib at true dawn of 'Idul Fitr. Someone who dies before that need not have it paid on his behalf. Similarly one who is born or accepts Islaam after that is not obligated nor is it Wajib on his behalf.

f: Is there a recommended time? [i.e. for Sadaqatul Fitr]
b: On 'Idul Fitr before going to the Musalla.

f: What is the ruling of paying it [i.e. Sadaqatul Fitr] before 'Idul Fitr?
b: It is allowed.

f: If he delays it [i.e. Sadaqatul Fitr] after 'Idul Fitr?
b: It is not forfeited. He must still pay it.

f: Who are entitled to receive Sadaqatul Fitr?
b:
The Faqir and Miskin who do not own any form of wealth.104

104 An indication that the well-off person who cannot receive Zakah, also cannot take Sadaqatul Fitr. Those others mentioned who cannot be given Zakah also cannot be given Sadaqatul Fitr.

f: What is the benefit of paying Sadaqatul Fitr?
b: Abu Dawud narrates that 'Abdullaah bin 'Abbas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ made Sadaqatul Fitr compulsory as a purification of the fast from any wasted time or obscenities and as a means of feeding the poor."

f: How much is Sadaqatul Fitr?
b: A half Sa' of wheat, or a full Sa' of dates, raisins or barley.

f: What is the ruling if he paid [i.e. Sadaqatul Fitr] with something else, such as Dirhams, money, rice or corn?
b: It is fulfilled if he paid with something of equal value to one of the above nad intended it as Sadaqatul Fitr.

f: How much is a Sa'?
b:
It is 8 'Iraqi Ritl according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is 5 and a third Ritl.105 

105 Sharhul Wiqayah: "A Sa' equals 8 Ritl of Majj or lentils because these two seeds are the most uniform unlike other seeds which differ greatly in size and other qualities... Know that this Sa' is the 'Iraqi one not the Hijazi which is 5 and a third Ritl..."

f: What is the ruling on fasting in Islaam?
b:
The fast of the month of Ramadan is Fard upon every mature Muslim, male and female. Allaah says, "O you who believe! Fasting has been prescribed upon you just as it was prescribed upon those before you that you may acquire Taqwa." [al-Baqarah:183]
The fasts besides the fast of Ramadan are voluntary and one gets rewarded for them just as in other voluntary worship. Howver, if one has made nazr [vow] of a fast then it becomes Wajib to fulfil it.

f: What is the meaning of Sawm linguistically and in Shari'ah? What are the beginning and ending times?
b: Sawm means abstention linguistically. In Shari'ah it means to abstain from food, drink and sex from true dawn until sunset with the intention of fasting.

f: Is there any leeway for anyone not to fast during Ramadan?
b: Yes, someone who is a traveller of Qasr distance; or is sick and fears that the fast will worsen the sickness, then they are allowed not to fast during Ramadan. They must filfil the missed days thereafter. It is however better for the traveller to fast if he will not experience difficulty by it.

f: A traveller did not fast during his travel, or a sick person did not fast during his sickness. Then they die in that state of travel or sickness. Is anything Wajib upon them?
b: No.

f: If the sick person is cured or the traveller becomes resident, is Qada necessary?
b: Yes, upon the sick person in the days he is well and upon the traveller in the days he stays resident, whether homeland or temporary.

f: Is there anyone else besides a traveller and a sick person who are allowed not to fast in Ramadan?
b: A pregnant woman or a woman feeding milk to a baby who fears destruction of herself or her baby is allowed not to fast in Ramadan. The missed days must be kept afterwards.

f: Is there anyone who compulsorily does not fast in Ramadan?
b: Yes, it is Wajib on a woman in her menses or childbirth period not to fast. They are not allowed to fast, their state negates fasting.

f: Will they [i.e. a woman in her menses or childbirth period] fulfil their missed fasts after Ramadan?
b: Yes.

f: Are there people upon whom missed Salah is not Qada, but Fidyah [compensation] is Wajib upon them?
b: Shaykh Fani.

f: What is meant by Shaykh Fani?
b: Someone so old that he will neither be able to fast during Ramadan nor after it right until the end of his life.

f: What is Fidyah?
b: To feed everyday a Miskin just as one feeds them in Kaffarat.

f: What is done when someone did not fast due to travel or illness and then had days to make Qada but did not do so and then his death approaches?
b: He should seek forgiveness and turn unto Allaah. He must also leave a bequest to his executor, instructing him to feed on his behalf a Miskim from his wealth a half Sa' of wheat or a Sa' of dates or barley.

f: If a child attains puberty or a Kafir embraces Islaam in the day of Ramadan, what should they do?
b: They should abstain for the rest of the day from that which terminates fast and should fast the remainder of Ramadan.

f: Do they [i.e. a child who attains puberty or a Kafir who embraces Islaam in the day of Ramadan] keep Qada for the partial day they reached?
b: No.

f: What is the ruling of someone who was unconscious during Ramadan?
b: If someone fell unconscious during a day of Ramadan after having made intention of fast, need not keep Qada of that day. He will keep Qada of any subsequent days.

f: What is the ruling of an insane person who regains his sanity during the day of Ramadan?
b: He will make Qada of the passed days and fast the remaining days.

f: If a traveller who was not fasting reached home during the day of Ramadan or a woman in her menses attained purity during the day, what should they do?
b: They should abstain from the three nullifiers for the rest of the day out of honour for the month.

f: When does the fast of Ramadan become Wajib and when does the month become established?
b:
Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Fast when you see it and stop fasting when you see it. If it is cloudy then complete 30 days of Sha'ban." [al-Bukhari and Muslim]

It is thus Wajib on the people to search for the new moon on the 29th of Sha'ban. If they see it they must fast the next day. If the moon is covered by clouds [they cannot see it] they must complete 30 days of Sha'ban and then fast.

f: If a single man testified that he saw the new moon of the 29th of Sha'ban and the sky was not clear, will his testimony be accepted?
b: Yes, the testimony of a single Muslim will be accepted in that case, be it male or female, free or slave.

f: And if the sky was clear and one or two men testified?
b: The testimony will not be accepted unless a large group testifies so that there is no doubt of their news.

f: That concerns establishing the new moon of Ramadan. What of the new moon for 'Id?
b: If the sky is not clear then the testimony of two men or a man and two women will only be accepted. If it is clear then a whole group must testify so that there is no doubt.

f: What should a man do who has seen the moon of Ramadan or 'Id and the Imam did not accept his testimony?
b: If it occurred for Ramadan then he should fast alone. If it occurred for 'Id then he should fast with the people and ignore his sighting.

f: You mentioned the condition of intention when you defined fasting. What are the details thereof?
b:
The intention is the affirmation in the heart that one is fasting a particular fast.
There are several categories of fasts:
Fard i.e. Ramadan
Specified Nazr [vow] such as vowing to fast next Thursday or the day a particular date will occur.
General vow such as vowing to fast for the sake of Allaah.
Qada of Ramadan.
A Wajib Qada of nullified Nafl Fast.
Kaffarat e.g. broken oath; broken fast; Zhihar and killing.
Nafl.
The fast of Ramadan and specified vow and Nafl can be intended from the night but it is not a condition that it is made at night. If no intention was made until the morning then it is valid until before half the day.107 

Fasts of Qada of Ramadan; general vow; Kaffarat and Qada of nullified Nafl are not valid except with an intention from the night.

107 It is necessary that there be an intention for most of the day. The half is from dawn until bright morning, not Zawal which is later. The intention must therefore be made before that so that most of the day is covered.

f: If someone is performing a Tamattu' or Qiran108 Hajj because he cannot afford Hady, must he intend the fast from the night?
b:
Yes, just as the fasts of the other Kaffarat.

108 These will be defined in Kitabul Hajj

f: It is apparent from your words that Qada is made for nullified Nafl. Please explain.
b: The one performing Nafl is in control of himself before commencing. Once he begins it is Wajib to complete. If he nullifies it then it is Wajib to make Qada of what he started, be it fast, Salah, Hajj or 'Umrah.

f: What nullifies Fast?
b:
Ejaculating due to kissing or touching.
Swallowing a pebble or iron or seed.
Intercourse whether vaginal or anal.
To take an enema or snuff.
To put drops of medicine in the ear.
Taking medication which reaches the stomach or brain.
Having Suhur [predawn meal] and thinking that dawn did not arise when it did.
Having Iftar [breaking fast meal] thinking that the sun set when it did not.
In all these scenarios the fast is void. Qada must be kept but not Kaffarah.

f: If he places drops on the outer opening of the urethra?
b: The fast is not void according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. It is void according to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى.

f: Does unintended vomiting or induced vomiting nullify the fast?
b: If he is overpowered by vomiting then the fast is not void. If he deliberately vomits a mouth full then he must render Qada.

f: What makes Qada and Kaffarah Wajib together?
b: One who intentionally has intercourse - vaginal or anal - or one who eats or drinks food or medicine. His fast is void and he must make Qada and Kaffarah.

f: What is the Kaffarah?
b: To free a slave. If unable to then fast two months consecutively in which there is no Ramadan or days wherein fasting is forbidden - we shall explain that InshaAllaah. If he is unable to do that then he must feed 60 Miskin.

f: Is there kaffarah for voiding fasts besides Ramadan?
b: No, even if it is voiding Qada of Ramadan.

f: Mention those things which the fasting person undergoes which do not break the fast.
What is Makruh for the fasting person to do?
b: To kiss, if he cannot control himself. If he can control himself then there is no harm. It is also Makruh to taste or chew or clean the mouth with anything besides Miswak, such as medicinal powder. It is Makruh for a woman to chew food for her child is she can avoid it. If it is unavoidable then there is no harm.

f: Must Qada of the fasts of Ramadan be kept consecutively?
b: No, one may keep them separately or consecutively.

f: What should he do if he delayed it [i.e. Qada of the fasts of Ramadan] so long that the next Ramadan arrived?
b: He should first fast the current Ramadan and then keep the Qada. There is no Fidyah to be paid for this.

f: A man died with unfulfilled Qada. He left a bequest that his executor pays his Fidyah from his estate. What is the duty of the executor?
b: The bequest may be fulfilled from a third of the estate only. The executor will then feed on his behalf a Miskin for every day missed, a half Sa' of wheat or a Sa' of dates or barley.

f: Are there fasts outside of Ramadan?
b: The Fast of Ramadan is Fard. If he keeps Nafl fasts outside of Ramadan he will be rewarded if Allaah wills

f: Are there days when voluntary Fasts are forbidden?
b:
Yes, there are five days when fasting is forbidden:
'Idul Fitr
'Idul Adha
The three days thereafter called the Days of Tashriq.

f: Is there greater virtue for some fasts over others?
b:
Yes, the Ahadith mention the virtues of certain special fasts:
'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to fast Mondays and Thursdays." [at-Tirmizi]
Abu Hurayrah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "deeds are presented Mondays and Thursdays. I like that my deeds be presented and I am fasting." [Ibid]
Abu Hurayrah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ would never leave the fasts of Ayyamul Biaz whether at home or travelling."109 
Abu Qatadah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "For the fast of 'Arafah110 I hope that Allaah will forgive the sins of the passed year and the next year. For the fast of Ashura111 I hope that Allaah will forgive the sins of the passed year." [Muslim]
Abu Ayyub al-Ansari رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "He who fasts Ramadan and then follows it with six days of Shawwal is like one who fasted the whole period (year)." [Muslim]
109 Narrated by an-Nasai. In the narration of at-Timirzi they are explained as the 13th, 14th and 15th of each month.

110 9th Zul Hijjah.

11 10th Muharram.

f: What is the definition and status of I'tikaf?
b: It is to stay in the Masjid with an intention. It is Sunnah Muakkadah upon Kifayah during the last days of Ramadan. If a single man of the area sits for I'tikaf then the obligation is lifted from the community, if not, then they are all guilty of abandoning that Sunnah.

f: Is there any other kind of I'tikaf in Shari'ah?
b: Yes, there are Mustahab and Wajib I'tikaf. The least Mustahab I'tikaf is for a single moment in which one enters the Masjid and intends I'tikaf. He will remain in I'tikaf until he leaves the Masjid.

f: When does I'tikaf become Wajib?
b: When one makes a nazr [vow] of I'tikaf it becomes Wajib.

f: If one vowed I'tikaf of the day, does the night become Wajib as well?
b: Yes, the nights are subsidiary to the days, even if he did not stipulate it.

f: Is fasting a condition for a vowed I'tikaf?
b: Yes, even if he says, "For Allaah I will make i'tikaf for a month without fasting."

f: What is the Mu'takif [one making I'tikaf] forbidden from?
b: He is prohibited from sex and its incitements such as touching and kissing. If he has sex in the day or night, forgetfully or deliberately; or ejaculates due to kissing or touching his I'tikaf is void and one must make Qada.

f: Can the Mu'takif leave the Masjid?
b: He may not leave except for natural needs such as urinating and defecating. According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى if he leaves for even a moment without an excuse then the I'tikaf is void. According to his two companions it is only void if he left for more than half a day.

f: If he is in I'tikaf in Masjid where there is no Jumu'ah, how does he pray Jumu'ah?
b: When the time is for Jumu'ah he will got to a Masjid where Jumu'ah is prayed and return to I'tikaf after the Salah.

f: What is the Mu'takif allowed to do?
b: He may eat, drink and sleep in the Masjid. He may buy and sell in the Masjid without bringing the commodity itself.

f: We see that people in I'tikaf not talking, thinking that that nullifies the I'tikaf. What do the Fuqaha say about that?
b: Talking does not nullify the I'tikaf. However, he should only speak good things and bad speech is prohibited in all circumstances. Silence with the belief that it is part of I'tikaf is Makruh.

f: What is Hajj linguistically and Islaamically?
b:
Linguistically it is an intention to do something which is honoured. In Shari'ah it is the visiting of specified places at specified times with specified actions. We shall explain all these in detail InshaAllaah.112

112 The special place is the Ka'bah and the Plains of 'Arafat. The special time is the times specified for Tawaf, staying at 'Arafat. The special acts are Ihram with the intention of Hajj which should be made before the Tawaf and 'Arafat.

f: What is the status of Hajj in Islaam?
b: It is a pillar of Islaam. Whoever disputes its being Fard is out of the pale of Islaam. Allaah says, "For Allaah upon the people is that they make Hajj of the House upon whoever has the means to do it."

f: Upon whom is Hajj Fard?
b: Hajj is Fard upon free, mature, intelligent, healthy Muslims on condition that the way is safe and they have means of travel, provision and transport, whether through possession or rental. Another condition is that his wealth be in excess of his residence, other necessities and expenses on his family until his return.

f: Are there any additional conditions for a woman?
b: Yes, she must travel with a Mahram or husband. She may not travel without one of them if her home is at least the distance of Qasr away from the Ka'abah.

f: What is Fard in Hajj?
b:
There are 3 Fard:
Ihram
Wuquf [staying] at 'Arafat
Tawafuz Ziyarah

f: What is Wajib in Hajj?
b:
They are as follows:
Wuquf of Muzdalifah after dawn on the Day of Nahr.
Sa'y between as-Safa and al-Marwa.
Pelting the Jimar.
Tawafus Sadr [when first coming] for one from Afaq [outside the Haram and Hill].
Shaving or shortening the hair.
Extending the Wuquf of 'Arafat until sunset.
For one performing Qiran [Qarin] or Tamattu' [Mutamatti'] to slaughter a Hady.
A Mufrid [one performing Ifrad] should observe the sequence of pelting and then shaving. The Qarin and Mutamatti' should observe the sequence between pelting then slaughter then shaving.
To perform Tawafuz Ziyarah during the Days of Nahr.
Shaving or shortening the hair within the Haram;
and that they be in the Days of Nahr.

f: What are the Sunan? [i.e. of Hajj]
b:
They are:
Tawaful Qudum for a Mufrid from Afaq as well as a Qarin.
Ramal and Idtiba' in Tawaf and to intend Sa'y thereafter between as-Safa and al-Marwa.
To go to Mina on the Day of Tarwiyah and to spend the following night there.
To leave Mina for 'Arafat after the sun has risen on the Day of Arafat.
To spend the night of the Day of Nahr at al-Muzdalifah.
To make Ghusl at 'Arafat.
To spend the nights at 'Mina of the days of Nahr (i.e. 10th/11th/12th)

f: What are the Miqat which are not permissible to pass except in a state of Ihram?
b:
The Nabi ﷺ established 5 Miqat:
Zul Hulayfah for the people of al-Madinah. [about 14km from al-Madinah in the direction of Makkah]
Zatul 'Irq for the people of 'Iraq. [It is no longer known where it is, they therefore go through al-Madinah and enter into Ihram at Zul Hulayfah]
al-Juhfah for the people of Syria. [This was a big town in the era of Rasulullaah ﷺ. It was 4 miles from Rabigh on the left side when going to Makkah. It has become effaced and the roads of the Hujjaj do not pass through it. The people of Syria enter Ihram when they pass Zul Hulayfah]
Qarn for the people of Najd.
Yalamlam for the people of Yemen. [It is also called Sa'diyah today. It is a mountain the people of Yemen pass when going to Makkah]
These are for the people of the lands mentioned and whoever passes them.

f: Those Miqat are for people living outside those borders. What about those people who live at the Miqat, between the Miqat and the Haram, or in the Haram?
b: He who lives at the Miqat will enter into Ihram there. The Miqat of one living between the Miqat and the Haram is the Hill. The Hill is the area between the Miqat and Haram. The Hajj Miqat of one living in the Haram is the Haram and his 'Umrah Miqat is the Hill.

f: Is it permissible to enter Ihram before these Miqat?
b: Yes, in fact it is better to enter early into Ihram in the months of Hajj when it is better if he can control himself from the Ihram restrictions.

f: And if he enter Ihram after the Miqat?
b: That is not permissible. If he did it after passing the Miqat then Damm is Wajib on him.

f: A man travelling to Makkah does not pass any of the mentioned Miqat. Where should he enter Ihram?
b: When he crosses a line going through two Miqat on either side of him.

f: What is Ihram?
b:
Intention of Hajj or 'Umrah with Talbiyah.113

113 The intention need not be joined specifically with Talbiyah which is Sunnah. It is allowed to join it with any other Zikr. Talbiya must be with the tongue, if only in the heart then it is not valid. [Raddul Muhtar 158/2]

f: Is there a Sunnah method of Ihram?
b:
Yes. When one intends Ihram one should make Wudu, although Ghusl would be better. He will then don two new or at least washed cloths which are not stitched like clothing. One will be the Izar [cover the lower body] and one will be the Rida [cover the upper body]. He will apply fragrance if he has. He will pray two Rak'at covering his head. Thereafter he will uncover his head and say as an intention of Hajj, "O Allaah, I intend Hajj, so ease it for me and accept it from me."

He will then recite the Talbiyah,
"Labbayk, Allaahumma labbayk. Labbayka la sharika laka labbayk. Innalhamada wanni'mata laka wal mulk. La sharika laka"
"At Your service, O Allaah at Your service. At Your service, there is no partner unto You, at Your service. Verily praise and bounties belong to You and the kingship. There is no partner with You."

He will not add in between these words. It is allowed to add words afterwards. Once he recited the talbiyah then he is in Ihram. He should now be careful of the Ihram restrictions.

f: If a woman is in her menses or childbirth period, may she enter Ihram of Hajj or must she wait until the bleeding stops?
b: She will not wait. She will make Ghusl if she finds a place to do it. She will then comb her hair and enter Ihram without the two Rak'at. She will intend Hajj or 'Umrah and recite Talbiyah. She is now in Ihram. When she enters Makkah she will await the end of the bleeding. She will then make Ghusl and Tawaf.

f: What are the restrictions when in Ihram?
b:
They are as follows:
Obscenity.
Lewdness.
Dispute.
Hunting land animals.
Showing where prey are to be found;
Indicating where it is [i.e. prey].
Wearing a shirt, trousers, cap, robe or anything which is stitched or embroided or made in the shape of the body.
Wearing gloves or leather socks, unless one does not find sandals. In that case it will be cut to expose the Ka'ab [humped bone on top of the feet].
Covering head or face. No cap or turban may be worn.
Applying fragrance.
Shaving or shortening the hair on the head or the beard or removing a hair from the body wherever it may be.
Cutting the nails.

Wearing cloth dyed with substances like safflower and saffron unless it has been washed and does not exude fragrance.

f: Are these [i.e. the 13 restrictions mentioned in question 532] the restrictions of Ihram of Hajj or 'Umrah?
b: Both.

f: Is there a difference between the restrictions of a man and a woman?
b: They apply to both, except that she will wear the clothing she normally wears. She will cover her head but not her face.

f: Can one in Ihram [Muhrim] bath?
b: Yes, but without any kind of fragrance including soap. He may not wash away dirt [in such a way that hair falls].

f: May the Muhrim rest in the shade of a house, car, tent etc?
b: All these are allowed.

f: What is the ruling to read a great quantity of Talbiyah?
b: It is Mustahab, especially after Salah and dawn, when changing in any state, when morning or evening begins, when ascending a height, when going down a valley or meeting a group

f: What does a Mufrid do when entering Makkah?
b:
He should first go to al-Masjid al-Haram in a state of Wudu. When he sees the Ka'bah he should recite, "Allaahu Akbar!" and, "La ilaha illAllaah!" He will then make Tawaf which will be the first Tawaf of the Hajj -e- Mufrid. It is a Sunnah for the Afaqi who came from beyond the Miqat. It is called Tawaful Qudum. It is not a duty for the people of Makkah and the Hill.114

114 Ghunyatun Nasik: It is Sunnah for the Mufrid Hajj and the Qarin. If he entered before the months of Hajj then it is not Sunnah for one making 'Umrah, the Mutamatti', the Makki, the people of the Miqat and those living between there and Makkah."
Al-Fath: "It is Sunnah for the Afaqi not for others."

f: Explain how Tawaf should be performed?
b: He will begin by al-Hajar al-Aswad. He will face it and raise his hands when saying "Allaahu Akbar." he will then say, "La ilaha illAllaah", and place his hands on it [Istilam] and kiss it if he can do it without harming any Muslim. If he cannot kiss it without harming a Muslim he will place his hands on it and kiss his hands. If he cannot, then at least one hand and kiss it. The right hand is preferred. If he cannot do that hen he should touch the stone with something he is holding such as a staff, then kiss that object. If he cannot do that he should stand in line with the stone and face it. He will raise his hands in line with his ears as at the time of Takbir, with his palms facing the Stone. He will be indicating as if he is placing his palms on the Stone. He will then kiss his palms. He will then move to the right of the Stone to the section where the Door of the Ka'bah is. He will keep the Ka'bah to his left and will pass on the outside of the Hatim. He will make Istilam of the Yemeni Corner when he reaches it. He will then again make Istilam of the Stone and kiss it. This is a complete single circuit. Seven circuits must be completed. Istilam of the Stone must be done as mentioned. The Tawaf begins and ends with Istilam of the Stone.

f: What is the ruling of Ramal and Idtiba'?
b: They are Sunnah for one intending to perform Sa'y between as-Safa and al-Marwa after the Tawaf. Ramal is only Sunnah in the first three circuits. Idtiba' is Sunnah in all seven. Thus one who intends Sa'y between as-Safa and al-Marwa will perform Ramal and Idtiba', otherwise not. The one performing 'Umrah will perform both acts in his Tawaf because he will make Sa'y between as-Safa and al-Marwa after his Tawaf of 'Umrah.

f: Explain the Sunnah of Ramal.
b: It is to shake the shoulders during his walk like one going for a duel between two armies. He should hasten in his walk.

f: What is Idtiba?
b: To take the end of the Rida from his right shoulder and throw both ends of his left shoulder. The right shoulder will be left exposed.

f: Is anything Wajib after Tawaf?
b: Yes, two Rak'at.

f: Were are they [i.e. the 2 Rak'at after Tawaf] prayed?
b: It is best at Maqam Ibrahim عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ, in such a way that it is between him and the Ka'bah. If prayed anywhere else in the Masjid where it is easy for him, it is permissible.

f: Are the Masnun Surahs to be recited in them? [i.e. in the two Rak'at after Tawaf]
b: Jabir رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrated that Rasulullaah ﷺ recited al-Kafirun in the first Rak'ah and al-Ikhlas in the second Rak'ah. [Muslim]

f: How is Sa'y between as-Safa and al-Marwa performed?
b:
When the one performing Hajj or 'Umrah intends to make Sa'y he must make Istilam of the Black Stone after the two Rak'at of Tawaf. He will then go to as-Safa and ascend it at least a bit. He will recite, "Innas-Safa wal-Marwa min Sha'airillah." He will face the Ka'bah and recite Takbir and, "La ilaha illAlaah", and salutations upon Rasulullaah ﷺ. He should ask Allaah for his needs. As per the narration of Muslim it is Sunnah to recite the following thrice, "La ilaha illahu wahdahu la sharika lahu. Lahul mulku wa lahul hamdu wa huwa 'ala kulli shayin qadir. SadaqAllaahu wa'dahu wa nasara 'abdahu wa hazamal Ahzab wahdah. - There is no illah but Allaah alone who has no partner. To Him belongs all kingship and praise and He has power over everything. Allaah was true to His promise and helped his slave and alone defeated the confederates."

He will then head for al-Marwah at a normal pace. When he reaches the green markings he will hasten until the next green marking whilst reciting, "O my Rabb, Forgive me and have mercy. You are Most Honourable and Noble. Overlook that which You know of."115 

After the passing the second green marking he will resume a normal pace. When he reaches al-Marwah, he will climb it and do the same as per as-Safa. This is one circuit. He will complete seven circuits. He began at as-Safa and will end at al-Marwa. He will remember Allaah throughout the Sa'y. Everytime he passes between the green markings he will run, going time and coming time. A woman will not run, she will walk at her normal pace throughout the Sa'y.

115 At-Tabarani, narrated from Ibn Mas'ud رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ.

f: The Hajji has completed the Tawaful Qudum and the Sa'y. What should he do whether there are many or few days left for Hajj?
b: He will stay in Makkah in Ihram. He will make Tawaf at every opportunity. He will pray the 5 Salah in al-Masjid al-Haram. He will not miss them with congegration, because the Salah there is worth 100,000 Salah elsewhere. On the Day of Tarwiyah he will go to Mina.

f: What will he do when he reaches Mina?
b: He will stay there until after sunrise on the Day of 'Arafat. He will pray 5 Salah with congegration at Mina.

f: What will he do when the sun has risen on the Day of 'Arafah?
b: When the sun rises over Thabir, the mountain at Mina, he will head for 'Arafat and stay there until the sun sets. After Zawal the Imam will lead the people in Zhuhr and 'Asr. He will deliver two Khutbahs before Salah in which he will teach the people about the Salah, the Wuquf of 'Arafat, the Wuquf at al-Muzdalifah, the pelting of the Jimar, the slaughter, the sahving and Tawafiz Ziyarah. He will lead them in Zhuhr and 'Asr in the Waqt of Zhuhr, with one Azan and two Iqamah. This is joining of the two Salah in the earlier Waqt. The conditions for this are that the Imam of the Muslims or his representative lead the Salah, that they be in Ihram of Hajj and the Waqt be Zhuhr. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. The one praying on his own or behind any other Imam besides the Imam of Hajj will pray each Salah in its own Waqt. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the Salah will be joined even for one praying on his own.

f: What will he do after Salah? [i.e. on the Day of 'Arafah]
b: He will then stay at a place of Wuquf. All of 'Arafat is a place for Wuquf except the low point. It is recommended that he engage in as much du'a as possible until sunset. He will pray 'Asr in its Waqt if he did not do so with the Imam of Hajj. It is Mustahab to make Wuquf near Jabal ar-Rahman, standing as much as possible and making du'a. It is also allowed to engage in du'a at one's tent. It is Mustahab for the Imam of Hajj to make Wuquf at 'Arafat upon his mount, making du'a and teaching people the laws of Hajj.

f: After the Wuquf at 'Arafat, what should be done after the sun sets?
b: When the sun sets he should leave 'Arafat and head for al-Muzdalifah. He will not pray Maghrib at 'Arafat, nor on the way to al-Muzdalifah. At al-Muzdalifah he will pray Maghrib and Isha combined, whether the Imam of Hajj or not. This is the joining in the latter Waqt.

f: Will he join the Salahs if praying alone [i.e. combining Maghrib and Isha at al-Muzdalifah]?
b: Yes. Congegration is not a condition.

f: What is the ruling of praying Maghrib at 'Arafat or on the road?
b: It is void and must be repeated.

f: What will he do after these two Salah? [i.e. the combined Maghrib and Isha at al-Muzdalifah]
b: He will spend the night at al-Muzdalifah until true dawn. He will then pray Fajr with congegration while it is still dark. He will remain and remember Allaah and offer du'a until just before sunrise. All of al-Muzdalifah is a place for the Wuquf except for the Valley of Muhassar.

f: What does the Hajj do after the Wuquf at al-Muzdalifah?
b:
A short while before sunrise he will head for Mina. When he reaches there he will pelt Jamratul 'Aqabah with 7 pebbles, such as the pebbles used in Hazaf [a game where a pebble is flung from the nail of the numb]. He will recite each time he pelts, "In the Name of Allaah, Allaah is the greatest. For the pleasure of ar-Rahman, and to displease the Satan."

He will not hang about there after the pelting. He will end the Talbiyah with the throwing of the first pebble.

f: Does he have to slaughter? [i.e. the Mufrid]
b: For the Mufrid slaughter is Mustahab only.

f: What does he [i.e. the Hajji after pelting] do next?
b: After pelting Jamratul 'Aqabah on the Day of Nahr, the Mufrid will clip his hair. To shave it is better. He is now released from Ihram and all restrictions except (taking benefit from) woman are lifted from him. He may wear stitched trousers and shirts etc. He may apply fragrance to his body and clothing, cut his hair and clip his nails. The Mutammati' and Qari must slaughter the Hady after the pelting of Jamratul 'Aqabah. He will then only cut or shave his head.

f: If a Mufrid wants to slaughter, should he cut or shave his head before or after the slaughter?
b: Both are allowed, but to do so after the slaughter is better.

f: Where will he cut or shave?
b: Within the boundaries of the Haram. If he does so outside the boundaries then he has to pay the Damm.

f: Are there any other duties remaining on the Day of Nahr after shaving?
b: Yes, Tawafuz Ziyarah which is a Fard Tawaf. Its time is the three days from sunrise on the Day of Nahr until sunset on the 12th. It is best to do it on the Day of Nahr. After shaving or cutting his head he will go to Makkah and circle the Ka'bah seven times as we discussed under Tawaful Qudum. After Tawaful Ziyarah women become permissible for him as well.

f: Will he make Ramal and Idtiba' as well? [i.e. during Tawafuz Ziyarah]
b: If he did not do Sa'y between as-Safa and al-Marwa after Tawaful Qudum he must do so now after Tawafuz Ziyarah. He will not make Ramal in the first three circuits of Tawafuz Ziyarah. There is no opportunity for Idtiba' as he wears normal clothing after shaving.

f: What is the ruling if he delays the Tawafuz Ziyarah after the thre days you have mentioned?
b: Damm is Wajib upon him according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى but not according to his two companions.

f: What does he do after Tawafuz Ziyarah?
b: He will return and stay at Mina. He will pelt the 3 Jimar on the 11th and 12th. Each day the pelting will be after Zawal. He will first pelt the Smallest Jamrah, which is closest to Masjidul Khayf; then the Middle Jamrah; then the Biggest Jamrah which is Jamratul 'Aqabah. He will pelt each Jamrah with 7 pebbles, reciting Takbir and "La ilaha illAllaah" with every pebble. After pelting the first two he will turn to the right of the place of pelting and make du'a. He will not pause for the du'a after pelting the Biggest Jamrah, but will offer his du'a whilst walking away from it.

f: If he pelts during these two days before Zawal, is it valid?
b: The Waqt of pelting in these two days is from Zawal until true dawn. He who hastens and pelts before Zawal must repeat his pelting.

f: What does he do after pelting the 3 Jimar on these two days?
b:
He may either leave for Makkah or stay at Mina and pelt on the 13th as well. Allaah says, "He who hastens for the two days only there is no sin on him. He who tarries beyond that, there is no sin on him - for those who have Taqwa."

However, if the sun sets on the 12th and he is still at Mina, it is Makruh for him to leave Mina before pelting on the 13th. If he is at Mina when true dawn arises on the 13th, then the pelting of that day becomes Wajib.

f: When must one who tarries to pelt on the 13th do it?
b: It is Sunnah to pelt after Zawal. The time on this day is until sunset, so it is incorrect after sunset. According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is allowed to pelt before Zawal, although it is Makruh for being contrary to the Sunnah. His two companions say that pelting is not correct before Zawal on that day as well.

f: A man stays at Mina to pelt during these days. Is it permissible for him to take his luggage to Makkah?
b: It is Makruh for him to take his luggage to Makkah while he stays at Mina.

f: What should he then do when he reaches Makkah after the first or second Nahr?
b: After the pelting the only act of Hajj which remains is Tawaful Wida'. It is also called Tawafus Sadar. It is Wajib upon the Afaqi. When he returns to Makkah he may now perform Tawaful Wida' and return to his homeland. If he is prevented from leaving for any reason, he can stay how long he wishes.

f: Should he then perform Tawaful Wida' when he leaves Mina or delay it until he ultimately leaves Makkah?
b: As soon as he makes a Tawaf after Tawafuz Ziyarah is counts as Tawaful Wida', even if his intention was Nafl Tawaf. It is however Mustahab for him to delay his intended Tawaful Wida' until he is going to leave for his homeland.

f: Is there Ramal and Idtiba' in Tawaful Wida'?
b: No, because there is no Sa'y thereafter.

f: A man enters Ihram at the Miqat and does not enter Makkah. He goes and does Wuquf at 'Arafat without having made Tawaful Qudum. What should he do?
b: Tawaful Qudum falls away from him.

f: A man reaches 'Arafat after sunset on the Day of 'Arafah. Is his Hajj valid?
b: Whoever makes Wuquf of 'Arafah anytime from the Day of 'Arafat from Zawal until dawn of the Day of Nahr has attained Hajj; however short the time.

f: Is it a condition to make du'a at 'Arafat to attain Hajj?
b: The du'a is Sunnah. One who passes through 'Arafah even for a short time, whether he was awake or asleep or unconscious; as long as he was in Ihram his Wuquf is valid, even to the extent that he did not know that that was 'Arafat.

f: Are all these the regulations for a man alone or for a woman as well?
b:
A woman does the same except that she does not expose her head.
She will not drape her Rida or veil over her face.
She will not raise her voice in Talbiyah.
She will not make Ramal in Tawaf.
She will not run between the green markings during Sa'y.
She will clip her hair and not shave it.
If she is in her menstrual or childbirth period when entering Ihram or after entering, and does not become pure until the Day of Tarwiyah, she will not perform Tawaful Qudum. She will in that case go to Mina and perform all the rest of the Hajj rituals, except that she will not make Tawafuz Ziyarah until she is pure. If she has menses or childbirth after Tawafuz Ziyarah and the time has come for her departure, then she may omit Tawaful Wida' without any penalty.

f: What is 'Umrah linguistcally and in Shari'ah? What are its Fard and Wajib actions? How is it performed?
b:
Linguistically 'Umrah means to visit. In Shari'ah it encompasses the following four:
Ihram
Tawaf of the Ka'bah
Sa'y between as-Safa and al-Marwah
Shaving or cutting the head
The first two are Fard and the second two are Wajib. When one wants to perform 'Umrah then one will enter Ihram at the Miqat. First perform Wudu or Ghusl and then two Rak'at. Then say the intention of 'Umrah, "O Allaah I intend 'Umrah. Ease it for me and accept it from me." Then recite Talbiyah as we mentioned in the Ihram of Hajj. Once the Talbiyah is recited then Ihram has been entered. Upon entering Makkah he will circle the Ka'bah seven times and then make Sa'y between as-Safa and al-Marwah. He will then shave or clip hair off the head. Upon doing that the 'Umrah is complete and he has emerged from the Ihram as well.

f: Are there restrictions in the Ihram of 'Umrah?
b: Yes. They are the same as the restrictions of the Hajj Ihram mentioned.

f: What is the Miqat for 'Umrah Ihram?
b: For the Afaqi it is the same as the Miqat of Hajj. The Hilli will enter Ihram from the Hill. The one in the Haram will leave for the Hill where he will enter Ihram.

f: What is the status of 'Umrah in Islaam?
b:
It is Sunnah Muakkadah once in a lifetime for one who is able to reach Makkah. It has great virtues.116 

116 Abu Hurayrah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "One Umrah to the next expiates what is between them. There is no reward for an accepted Hajj except Jannah." [al-Bukhari and Muslim]

f: What is the ruling of talbiyah in the Ihram of 'Umrah?
b: Talbiyah is a condition for entering Ihram. It is Mustahab to recite it frequently thereafter just as in the Ihram of Hajj. One will stop reciting it when beginning the first circuit of Tawaf.

f: Is there Tawaful Qudum and Tawaful Wida' in 'Umrah?
b: No. Every Tawaf made after Ihram will be part of the 'Umrah.

f: Is there a specified time for 'Umrah as in Hajj?
b:
No. One may perform 'Umrah whenever one wishes, except that it is Makruh Tahrimi from the 9th Zul Hijjah until the last day of Tashriq. There is greater reward for 'Umrah during Ramadan. 'Umrah then earns the reward like that of Hajj.117

117 Ibn 'Abbas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "An Umrah in Ramadan equals a Hajj." [Muslim]

f: Can 'Umrah be made with Hajj?
b: Yes, it will be explained in the discussion on Tamattu' and Qiran.

f: May the Ihram of Hajj and 'Umrah be joined?
b: Yes. It is better than Ifrad and Tamattu'. Tamattu' is better than Ifrad. Whoever joins the two Ihram is called Qarin and his Hajj is Qiran.

f: Describe the Qiran.
b:
One will enter Umrah and Hajj together at the Miqat. After the two Rak'at one will recite, "O Allaah! I intend Hajj and 'Umrah. Ease them for me and accept them from me."
Then recite Talbiyah which will enter you in Ihram of Hajj and 'Umrah. When entering Makkah circle the Ka'bah seven times with Idtiba' for 'Umrah. Make Ramal in the first three and then at a normal pace in the remaining four. Then make Sa'y between as-Safa and al-Marwah for 'Umrah. Those are the acts of 'Umrah. Then make Tawaful Qudum followed by Sa'y between as-Safa and al-Marwah for Hajj as we explained in the Hajj of the Mufrid. Remain in Ihram until the Day of Tarwiyah when one will go to Mina and perform the Hajj just like the Ifrad described.

f: Is there anything extra that the Qarin must do compared to the Mufrid?
b: Yes, it is Wajib upon him to slaughter a Hady after pelting the Biggest Jamrah on the Day of Nahr. He will slaughter a sheep or a sevent of a Budnah in grattitude to Allaah for allowing him to join the two acts of Hajj and 'Umrah. He will then only shave or clip his hair. He is then released from both Ihram at the same time just as he had entered both at the same time. He is not allowed to shave or clip except after the slaughter. All restrictions are now lifted from him except the restriction of women which is only lifted after Tawafuz Ziyarah.

f: What does he do [i.e. the Qarin] if he does not have money to buy a Hady?
b: He will fast three days during Hajj, the last day being the Day of 'Arafat. He will then fast 7 days when he returns home. That completes 10.

f: What is the ruling if he missed a day of fasting and it is already the Day of 'Nahr?
b: He has no option now except slaughter of a Hady.

f: is it allowed to fast the remaining 7 whilst still in Makkah, i.e. before returning home?
b: Yes.

f: What is the ruling of one who entered Ihram of Hajj and 'Umrah but did not enter Makkah but he went straight to 'Arafat?
b: When he makes Wuquf at 'Arafat he has dropped the 'Umrah and does not have to slaughter the Hady of Qiran. He must pay Damm for omitting the 'Umrah and must make Qada of it as well.

f: What is Tamattu'?
b: It is to enter Ihram at the Miqat and then go to Makkah and perform 'Umrah during the months of Hajj. He will stop Talbiyah when commencing Tawaf. After Tawaf he will make Sa'y. After shaving or clipping his hair he is out of the Ihram of 'Umrah. He will remain at Makkah without Ihram and will make as many Tawaf as he can. He will pray the 5 Salah in congegration in al-Masjid al-Haram. He will then enter Ihram of Hajj in the Haram on the Day of Tarwiyah. He will perform his Hajj just as the Mufrid. After pelting the Biggest Jamrah on the Day of Nahr he will slaughter a Hady out of gratitude to Allaah for allowing him to join the Hajj and 'Umrah. If he cannot afford it then he must fast three days in Hajj, the final day being the Day of 'Arafah. He will also fast 7 days when he returns home. He will not shave his head until he has slaughtered. We have mentioned certain rules of the fast under Qiran.

f: What do you say about someone who entered Ihram of 'Umrah and brought his Hady with him?
b: There are two kinds of Mutamatti'. One who does not bring a Hady, and we have described his Tamattu'. The other is the one who makes Ihram of 'Umrah only at the Miqat and goes to Makkah with his Hady. If it is bovine he will tie a bag or sandal around its neck. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى, Ish'ar is done on camels. The famous narration from Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى is that it is Makruh because people started to exceed the bounds. It is the slitting the hump from the right. When he enters Makkah he will make Tawaf and Sa'y of 'Umrah. He will not leave his Ihram but will continue in that state. On the Day of Tarwiyah he will renew his Ihram and do his Hajj as a Mufrid does. He will slaughter the Hady after pelting the Biggest Jamrah. He will then shave or clip his hair. Upon that he will be free of both Ihrams.

f: If the Mutamatti' advances his Ihram and enters Ihram before the Day of Tarwiyah, is it allowed?
b: Yes, that is also Tamattu'.

f: What are the months of Hajj?
b: Shawwal, Zul Qa'dah and the first ten days of Zul Hijjah.

f: The rites of Hajj are during five days. Why have Shawwal and Zul Qa'dah been made months of Hajj?
b: Because certain laws apply then. One of these are that if one entered Ihram of 'Umrah and completed most of the circuits of the Tawaf before the new moon of Shawwal set in, then one will not be a Mutamatti'. Another is that it is Makruh to enter into Ihram of Hajj before the new moon of Shawwal.

f: Someone entered into Ihram of 'Umrah during Shawwal or Zul Qa'dah. He completed the rites of 'Umrah. He went home and returned for Hajj. What is the status of his Tamattu'?
b: His Tamattu' is void in this scenario if he is not bringing a Hady. He will not give Damm of Tamattu'. This is because Tamattu' is the joining of Hajj and Umrah in a single journey. By going home inbetween it is no longer in a single journey.

f: Can the people of Makkah perform Qiran and Tamattu'?
b: No. The people living within the Miqat - the people of Makkah, the Haram and the Hill may not perform Qiran and Tamattu', only Ifrad.

f: What is a Jinayah [violation] in Hajj and 'Umrah?
b:
There are two kinds:
Violating the restrictions of Ihram.
Violating the actions of Hajj and 'Umrah, such as leaving a Wajib, mixing the order, delaying a Fard or Wajib from its time.

f: Explain the violations of Ihram.
b:
They are 8:
For men to wear stitched clothing.
For men to cover their heads.
For men and women to cover their faces.
To apply fragrance on the body, clothing or bedding.
Shaving or clipping hair from any part of the body.
Cutting the nails.
Hunting a land animal, indicating or showing where it is.
Sex and it preludes such as kissing and touching with lust.

f: Explain the details of the violation of wearing stitched clothing and its penalties?
b: If a Muhrim wears stitched clothing; that is clothing which is normally worn as in conformity with the body or a part of the body, whether deliberately or forgetfully or by mistake; whether willingly or by force; whether with or without an excuse then there is a penalty.

f: What is the penalty? [i.e. if a Muhrim wears stitched clothing]
b:
He must pay Damm if he wore it for a day or a night or the duration of one of the two; i.e. he must slaughter a sheep118 in the Haram.

118 Damm is a Thani sheep free of defect. Thani will be discussed under Hady. Sadaqah for violations of Ihram is a half Sa' of wheat or a Sa' of dates/barley/raising or their price.

f: What is his penalty if he wore it for less than that? [i.e. if the Muhrim wore stitched clothing for a day or a night]
b: Sadaqah like Sadaqah of Fitr if he worte it for at least an hour, if less, then a handful of wheat.

f: If he wore it [i.e. a Muhrim with stitched clothing] for several days and nights will he pay a separate penalty for each day?
b: A single Damm will suffice. However, if he wore it again after the slaughter or cotninued to wear it then another penalty is due.

f: If he wore different kinds of prohibited clothing at the same time for the duration of the day, e.g. trousers and shirt, does he pay multiple pentalties?
b: No, a single Damm suffices.

f: If he wore a shirt as a cloak or a lower-body garment; or wore a trouser on the upper part of his body, what is the penalty?
b: No penalty. The violation is to wear normal clothing in the normal manner.

f: Is there a penalty for wearing an Izar or Rida with stitched intervals or edges?
b: No, that does not make them garments in the shape of the human body or organs. However, it is better that there be no stitching.

f: What is the penalty for wearing stitched fragranced clothing for the duration of a day?
b: One Damm for the clothing and another for the fragrance.

f: Is there a penalty for wearing shoes or socks?
b: Damm is Wajib if he wore them for a day or night or the duration of one. If he wore less than that Sadaqah is Wajib. The penalties are only if they covered the Ka'b, the protruding bone on the upper part of the foot.

f: Explain the penalties for covering the face and head.
b: If the Muhrim covers his whole head or face or even a quarter of either one; or a Muhrimah covers her face or a quarter for a day or a night or the duration of either, then Damm becomes Wajib. This is irrespective whether they did it ignorantly or knowingly, willingly or by force, by mistake, forgetfully or deliberately, wakefully or in sleep, with an excuse or without. If done less than the mentioned time or less than a quarter of the said organs then Sadaqah is Wajib.

f: What is Wajib if the Muhrim covers his ears, or nape, or the part of his beard below the chin?
b: Nothing.

f: What if he [i.e. a Muhrim] covers his head with a metal sheet or stone or wood?
b: There is no penalty. The restriction is on wearing that which is normally considered a covering such as a cap, turban, hanky, etc.

f: Is there a penalty if he puts his head under the covering of the Ka'bah?
b: No. However, if the covering covers his head or faces it is Makruh.

f: What is the penalty if the Muhrim/ah applies fragrance on the body?
b: Damm is Wajib if fragrance is applied to a complete organ or more. If on less than a complete organ then Sadaqah is Wajib. By organ is meant for example the head, thigh, calf, lower arm and upper arm. This is if the fragrance is a little. If it is much then the Damm is Wajib even if it is on less than an organ. The custom of the people will determine what is meant by a little and a lot. These apply to large organs as mentioned. As for smaller organs like fingers, ears and eyes, then the ruling is on the least of what is Wajib in the big organ regarding Damm or Sadaqah.

f: If fragrance was applied to the entire body, are there multiple penalties?
b: If done at a single time then there is one Damm. If done in multiple sittings then the Damm must be added up according to the number of sittings.

f: What is the ruling if a woman applied Hinna to her hand?
b:
Damm is Wajib for that as well.

NOTE: There is no condition in fragrance that an amount of time has to pass. Thus if the fragrance was applied and immediately washed off, the Damm or Sadaqah as applicable, is due. As opposed to clothing, where Damm is payable when worn for the mentioned duration.

f: What is the penalty for the Muhrim who applies fragrance to his clothing?
b: Damn is Wajib if he applies it to the clothing he is wearing or clothing he then puts on; and the applied area is more than a hand-span by a hand-span; and the time he wears it is complete day or night. If it is a hand-span by a hand-span then he wears it for a day or night then he must pay Sadaqah. If less than that then a handful of wheat. This is if the fragrance is little. If it is a lot then Damm is Wajib even if the less than a hand-span of the cloth was afflicted. [Raddul Muthar (201/2)]

f: What is the penalty for applying scented oil?
b: It is the same as fragrance. Thus if he applies it on his head, Damm is Wajib.

f: What is the ruling of a Muhrim cutting his nails?
b: If he cuts the nails of his hands and feet, or the nails of one hand or one foot in one sitting then one damm is Wajib. If he cuts all the nails of the hands and feet in separate sittings, then there is a separate penalty for his sitting.

f: What is the ruling for cutting less than 5 nails?
b: Sadaqah for each nail.

f: What is the ruling of cutting 5 nails from separate places, e.g. 2 nails from each hand and one from a foot?
b: There is also Sadaqah according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى.

f: What is the penalty upon the Muhrim for shaving his hair?
b: Damm is Wajib if he shaves his head or beard or a quarter of either. For less than a quarter the penalty is Sadaqah. If he shaves his armpits or pubic hairs then Damm is Wajib. Shortening the hair and shaving it is the same in regards Damm and Sadaqah. If it removed in some other way, or plucked out or combed out then it is the same as ruling as shaving.

f: What is the ruling if the area of cupping was shaved on his neck?
b: Damm according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Sadaqah according to his two companions.

f: What is the ruling upon a woman in that? [i.e. shaving in Ihram]
b:
The ruling as above in shaving the armpits, pubic area and head is the same for a woman as for a man.

NOTE: The penalties are equally applicable whether he did it himself or someone else; with or without his order; willingly or forced; ignorantly or mistakenly; forgetfully or deliberately.

f: What is the ruling of one who wore stitched clothing; applied fragrance; covered his head or face; shaved his head; or clipped his nails for a valid reason?
b:
If the Muhrim violates any of these restrictions for a reason, e.g. he was afflicted with feverm there was severe heat or cold, headache or exessive lice then he has a choice in every situation wherein Damm is Wajib to either slaughter a sheep in the Haram or give Sadaqah of 3 Sa' of wheat, or 6 Sa' of raisins/dates/barley to 6 Miskin; giving each of them a half Sa' of wheat or a Sa' of raisins/dates/barely; or he can fast 3 days.
The rule applies equally to rich and to poor.

If the violation required Sadaqah instead, and he had a reason, then he has a choice Sadaqah or half Sa' of wheat or fasting a day.

f: Explain the violations of Ihram concerning sex.
b:
They are as follows:
If a Muhrim of Hajj or 'Umrah kisses or touches a woman or beardless boy with lust, then he must pay Damm, whether he ejaculated or not.
If a Muhrim of Hajj has vaginal or anal sex before the Wuquf of 'Arafat his Hajj is void and he must slaughter a sheep. He will continue the actions of Hajj as if he is still in Hajj and will perform Qada after that year.
If the Hajj had sex after Wuqf of 'Arafat, before Tawafuz Ziyarah and before he shaves his head, then he has to slaughter a Badnah and his Hajj is not void.
If he had sex after shaving his head, before Tawafuz Ziyarah; or after Tawafuz Ziyarah but before shaving, then he must slaughter a sheep.
If a Muhrim of 'Umrah has sex before completing 4 circuits, then his 'Umrah is void. He must make Qada and slaughter a sheep.
If a Muhrim of 'Umrah has sex after completing 4 circuits, then his 'Umrah is not void. He need make Qada but must slaughter a sheep.

f: Is there a difference between having sex deliberately and forgetfully?
b: No. The ruling is the same.

f: If the Hajj is going to make Qada of the Hajj he nullified, is he obligated to separate from his wife in that journey?
b: No.

f: Explain the violations of the acts of Hajj?
b: There are several kinds of volitions. These include Tawaf without Taharah; omitting a Wajib; mixing the order; and delaying a Rukn or Wajib from its time. The details are as below.

f: What is the penalty for making Tawaf without Taharah?
b:
The details are:
If the Hajji makes Tawaful Qudum or Tawafus Sadar and he is Muhdith then he must pay Sadaqah of half a Sa' of wheat for every circuit. The same rule applies to any Nafl Tawaf.
If the Hajji makes Tawaful Qudum or Tawafus Sadar and he is Junub, or a woman who is in menses or childbirth periods then they must slaughter a sheep.
If the Hajji makes Tawafuz Ziyarah and he is Muhdith then he must slaughter a sheep,
If the Hajji makes Tawafuz Ziyarah and he is Junub, or a woman who is in menses or childbirth periods then they must slaughter a Badanah [camel]
NOTE: If he made Tawaf while Muhdith or Junub and then repeated the Tawaf with Taharah, then the penalty is dropped.

f: What is the penalty for omitting a Wajib act of Hajj?
b:
It is as follows:
One who omits Wuquf at al-Muzdalifah after dawn must pay Damm.
One who omits Sa'y between as-Safa and al-Marwah must pay Damm.
He who omits the pelting of the Jimar on all the days or the pelting of the Biggest Jimar on the Day of Nahr; or omitted most of the pebbles on a given day of pelting; must pay Damm in each of these scenarios. If in a day he left out one of the three Jimar then he must pay Sadaqah.
He who leaves 'Arafat before sunset must pay Damm unless he returns before sunset.
He who leaves out Tawaful Wida' or 4 circuits of it must pay Damm. If he omitted 3 then he must pay Sadaqah. The penalty is dropped if he returns to Makkah and makes Tawaful Wida'.

f: What does the Muhrim do if he mixed the Wajib order?
b:
It is as follows:
If Mutamatti' or Qarin slaughters before pelting the Biggest Jamrah or shaved before slaughter then he must pay Damm.
If a Mufrid shaved before pelting the Biggest Jamrah then he must pay Damm.

f: What delay makes a penalty Wajib?
b:
It is as follows:
Damm is Wajib when a Mutamatti' or Qarin delays his slaughter after the Days of Nahr.
Damm is Wajib if any Hajji delays his shaving or clipping after the mentioned days.
NOTE: Women will never be allowed for a Hajji until he performs the complete or most of the Tawafuz Ziyarah.

f: What are the violations of 'Umrah?
b:
It is as follows:
Damm is Wajib if he delayed entering Ihram to after the Miqat.
Damm is Wajib if one made Tawaf of 'Umrah as a Muhdith or Junub; or a woman was in her menses or childbirth period. There is no difference here between the Muhdith or the Junub, between a little and a lot. The Damm is Wajib if even a single circuit was made without Taharah.
Damm is Wajib if he shaved before Sa'y.
Damm is Wajib if he shaved his head outside the Haram.
NOTE: The penalty of Damm or Sadaqah for violating Ihram is the same whether it was Ihram of Hajj or 'Umrah.

f: Is there a penalty for a Muhrim of Hajj or 'Umrah if he kills a prey?
b: There is a Wajib penalty upon a Muhrim who kills a prey; shows someone where the prey is; or even indicates to a hunter. The forgetful one, deliberate one, beginner and repeat offender are all equally liable.

f: What is the penalty?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the prey will be evaluated in the place it is killed or the nearest place if it was on land. Two just Muslims will do the evaluation. The killer then has a choice between buying at that price a Hady to slaughter in the Haram or to buy food to give as Sadaqah to the Miskin. He will give each Miskin a half Sa' of wheat or a Sa' of dates/barley. If he wishes he can instead fast one day for each half Sa' of wheat or one Sa' of barley. If there was extra food less than a half Sa', he may give it as Sadaqah or he may fast a full day in lieu. The ruling is the same for a small prey which does not reach the value of a full Hady.

f: Does Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى bin al-Hasan have a different view? [i.e. regarding the penalty for a Muhrim of Hajj or 'Umrah killing prey, see question 634]
b: Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى rule according to monetary evaluation and then a choice as discussed above. Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى declared that the prey's equivalent animal be used where such exists. Thus the penalty of a deer or hyena will be a sheep; a kid for a rabbit; a Budanah for an ostrich and a lamb for a jerboa. As for hat which does not have a physical equivalent then his ruling is the same as the two Imams.

f: What is the ruling if the Muhrim wounds the prey, plucks its hair or cuts limb?
b: He is penalised the value of the damage caused.

f: What is the ruling if he plucked the feathers of a bird or cut the legs of an animal?
b: If the animal then escapes from his sole control then he is penalised with the full price.

f: If he breaks the egg of a prey?
b: If a dead chick emergens then the penalty is equivalent had it been alive. If there was no chick in it then he is penalised the value of the egg.

f: What is the penalty for killing lice or locusts?
b: He can give what Sadaqah he wishes. A date is more than a locust.

f: What is the ruling of killing a beast whose flesh is not eaten?
b: The penalty is imposed on him, except that it will not exceed the value of a sheep.

f: Is there a penalty if the beast attacked the Muhrim who then killed it?
b: No.

f: Are there any animals or birds the Muhrim is allowed to kill?
b: He may kill crows, vultures, wolves, snakes, scorpions, rats and vicious dogs.

f: What is the penalty for killing mosquitoes, fleas and apes?
b: Nothing.

f: If the Muhrim is forced to eat the flesh of prey and kills it for that purpose, is there still a penalty upon him?
b: Yes.

f: What do you say about a dove with striped hindquarters or a tame deer?
b: There is still a penalty for killing them.

f: If a Muhrim slaughtered a prey, may a non-Muhrim eat from it?
b: The slaughter of a Muhrim is carrion. It is not permissible for him or anyone else.

f: Can a Muhrim slaughter that which people usually slaughter to eat?
b: Yes, a Muhrim may slaughter a sheep, cow, chicken and duck. He and others may eat from these animals if he slaughtered them.

f: A non-Muhrim hunted and killed a prey. Can the Muhrim eat from it?
b: He can eat from it if he did not show the hunter where it is nor ordered him to hunt it.

f: What is the penalty if two Muhrims joined to kill a prey?
b: Each will pay the full penalty.

f: If a Muhrim killed a prey and then sold it while in Ihram; or bought it from a Muhrim or a non-Mughrim; what is the ruling?
b: His selling is valid, his buying is void.

f: What is the ruling of a Qarin who violates the Ihram?
b:
He has to pay 2 Damm, one for violating the Hajj Ihram and one for the 'Umrah Ihram.
The exception is if he crossed the Miqat without Ihram and then later entered into Ihram of Hajj and 'Umrah, then he is only liable for one Damm in that case.

f: What is the ruling of one who does not enter Ihram at the Miqat and intends entering Makkah?
b:
If an Afaqi Muslim who is Mukallaf [responsible for obeying Shari'ah] intends going to Makkah or enter the Haram, even if it is only for business or tourism, and he crosses the Miqat by land, sea or air without Ihram, then whether he later enters Ihram or not he has sinned and must pay Damm.119

119 Ibn Hajar said in Fathul Bari: Malik has quoted the narration of 'Ibn Umar in his Muwatta from Nafi', "'Abdullaah bin 'Umar left Makkah. When he reached Qadid news of trouble reached him and he returned to Makkah without Ihram." In short he regarded Ihram only for one intending Hajj or 'Umrah based on the narration of Ibn 'Abbas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, "He who intends Hajj and 'Umrah...." This means that one going to Makkah without intending Hajj or 'Umrah does not need Ihram. The 'Uluma have differed about this. The famous view of ash-Shafi'i is that it is not Wajib... The famous view of the other three Imams is that it is Wajib in all circumstances. There are narrations from all of them that it is not Wajib. This is the view of Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا, az-Zuhri, al-Hasan and the Ahluzh Zhahir.... Ibn 'Abdil Barr claimed that most Sahabah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ and Tabi'in said that it is Wajib.

f: Is there a way out of the sin and Damm?
b: If one crossed the Miqat without Ihram, it is necessary to return to the Miqat, whether the one he crossed (which is best), or the closest one or even the furthest away. When he then enters Ihram for Hajj or 'Umrah at the Miqat, the sin and Damm will lapse.
