f: What is the penalty if he [i.e. the one who crossed the Miqat without Ihram] does not return to the Miqat and enters Ihram for Hajj or 'Umrah in the Hill or Haram?
b: The sin and Damm remains. He must seek forgiveness from Allaah and repent. He must slaughter a sheep in the Haram - his Damm.

f: A man crossed the Miqat without Ihram. He fears that if he returns to the Miqat he will miss the Hajj and therefore enters Ihram where he is. What is the ruling?
b: He should not return in that circumstance, but should slaughter a sheep for his violation of crossing the Miqat without Ihram. He must seek forgiveness from Allaah and repent.

f: A man crossed the Miqat without Ihram. He fears for the safety of his life or wealth if he returns to the Miqat and therefore enters Ihram of 'Umrah where he is. What is the ruling?
b: It is no longer Wajib to return to the Miqat. Slaughtering the sheep in the Haram will suffice.

f: A man enters Makkah or the Haram several times without Ihram. What is the ruling?
b: If he enters Makkah or the Haram without Ihram then for every entry he must make a Hajj or 'Umrah [which now becomes Qada]. If in the same year he enters Ihram for the Hajj or a vowed Hajj or Qada or vowed Qada or Sunnah 'Umrah or Mustahab 'Umrah; that will suffice him for his Qada of entry whether he made intention or the Qada or not. If he does that in the next year then he must make intention.

f: An Afaqi comes from a journey to the Miqat at Jaddah. He does not intend Hajj or 'Umrah, nor entry into Makkah or the Haram. What is his ruling?
b: There is no sin or penalty upon him.

f: If after coming to Jaddah he [i.e. an Afaqi coming from a journey to the Miqat at Jaddah] then wishes to enter the Haram or Makkah, what must he do?
b: In this scenario it is permissible for him to enter Makkah or the Haram without Ihram. If he intends Hajj or 'Umrah after reaching Jaddah, then he must enter Ihram from Jaddah or any place in the Hill.

f: Are the people of the Miqat or Hill allowed to enter the Haram or Makkah without Ihram?
b: They are allowed to when they do not intend Hajj or 'Umrah. If they enter Makkah or the Haram without Ihram, and intended Hajj or 'Umrah, then Damm becomes Wajib upon them. They will have to return to their Miqat, which is the Hill. If they entered Ihram of Hajj or 'Umrah at the Haram and did not return to the Hill; or they did return but did not make Talbiyah there before beginning Tawaf, they are sinners and the Damm is still payable.

f: Is one living in the Haram allowed to enter Ihram of 'Umrah in Makkah or the Haram?
b: No. For the people of the Haram, their Hajj Miqat is the Haram and their 'Umrah Miqat is the Hill. If they do not enter Ihram at their specified Miqat they have sinned and must pay Damm.

f: What are the violations of the Haram?
b:
They are two:
Killing prey in it.
Cutting its trees and grass.

f: What is the penalty for killing prey in the Haram?
b: He must give the value as Sadaqah to the poor. Fasting will not suffice.

f: What is the penalty oof two men out of Ihram who kill prey in the Haram?
b: Each is liable for a complete penalty.

f: If a Muhrim kills a prey in the Haram is there a multiple penalty upon him?
b:
No, the one penalty is incorporated into the other and the Sadaqah of the value of one prey will suffice.120

120 Whilst logic dictates that there be two penalties, the summary from al-Kifayah is that based on the juristic principle of Istihsan the prohibition of the Ihram is greater because it forbids hunting in the Hill and the Haram. Thus the greater prohibition already incorporated the lesser prohibition of hunting in the Haram.

f: What is the penalty of cutting or uprooting trees and grass of the Haram, whether by a Muhrim or non-Muhrim?
b: It is Wajib to give the value of the tree in Sadaqah if the tree does not have an owner and is not the kind people plant.

f: And if someone owns it? [i.e. a plant/tree in the Haram]
b: The destroyer will have to pay its value in Sadaqah as the right of Shari'ah; and also the same price to its owner as his right. That is if it is not dry. If dry, then he only need to pay the owner and there is no further Shar'i penalty.

f: Are there any exceptions? [i.e. regarding trees and grass of the Haram]
b: Yes, it is allowed to cut Izkhir, a famous grass. Dry trees and grass can also be cut.

f: Are these the rules [i.e. regarding cutting or uprooting trees and grass of the Haram] for Muhrims or non-Muhrims?
b: It applies to both. The cutting of trees and grass is prohibited due to the Haram, not the Ihram.

f: What is the ruling of two Muhrims cutting a tree on which there is a penalty?
b: The price of one is due on both.

f: Can one make Miswak from the trees of the Haram?
b: No, unless it is a dry tree.

f: What should a Muhrim do in the case of Ihsar?
b: If a Muhrim falls ill or an enemy prevents him from continuing, he is allowed to terminate his Ihram.

f: How does he do that? [i.e. a Muhrim terminating his Ihram due to sickness or danger]
b: If he is in the Haram then he should slaughter a sheep and shave or clip his hair. If he has not reached the Haram, then he should depute a man with a sheep or its price who will slaughter the sheep on his behalf in the Haram. They would stipulate an exact time when the sheep will be slaughtered. When it is slaughtered he will be out of Ihram.

f: What should he do if he is Qarin? [i.e. a Muhrim terminating Ihram]
b: He will pay two Damm if he is in the Haram. If not, he will send the two sheep to be slaughtered on his behalf after which he is released from both Ihram.

f: Why must the sheep be sent to the Haram? Can he not slaughter wherever he is?
b: The slaughter is the Damm of Ihsar. It is not permissible except in the Haram.

f: Can the Damm of Ihsar be made before the Day of Nahr?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى, yes. His two companions say that the slaughter for Ihsar of Hajj can only be done on the Day of Nahr.

f: What can one intending 'Umrah slaughter whne he has been prevented?
b: He may slaughter when he wants but it must be in the Haram. This is unanimous.

f: After the prevented one [Muhsar] from Hajj has been released from Ihram does any other obligation remain?
b: Yes, he must make Qada of a Hajj and an 'Umrah. As for the Muhsar of 'Umrah he must make Qada of 'Umrah only.

f: If a Qarin has been prevented, what must he do after release from Ihram?
b: A Hajj and 2 'Umrah.

f: A Muhrim was prevented from Hajj. He sent someone to slaughter on his behalf, and then the prevention terminated. What should he do?
b: If he can afford a Hady and Hajj, then he is not allowed to leave the Ihram. He must continue the rites of Hajj. If he cannot afford the Hajj but can only afford the Hady then he may leave the Ihram. If he can only afford the Hajj and not the Hady then he may leave the Ihram but it will be better if he fulfils the Hajj.

f: A man entered Ihram and reached Makkah. He was prevented from Wuquf at 'Arafat and Tawafuz Ziyarah. Is he classified as Muhsar?
b: Yes he is.

f: Is the Muhsar prevented from either Wuquf of 'Arafat or Tawafuz Ziyarah?
b: The laws of Ihsar do not apply to him. If he is prevented from Tawafuz Ziyarah he will do his Wuqf and then do the Tawafuz Ziyarah when the Ihsar has ended. If he cannot do the Wuquf then he is like one who has missed the Hajj and must do as anyone else who has missed it.

f: When the Hady is slaughtered, is it sufficient for his release from Ihram or must he first shave or clip his hair?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he is released from Ihram upon the slaughter. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he must shave or clip to be released.

f: What is the ruling of a Muhrim of Hajj who missed Wuquf of 'Arafat until dawn of the Day of Nahr?
b: His Hajj has been missed. He should remove his Ihram after doing the rites of 'Umrah i.e. he will make Tawaf, Sa'y and shave or clip his hair.

f: Is there anything after that? [i.e. for the Muhrim of Hajj who missed Wuquf of 'Arafat until dawn of the Day of Nahr and after removing his Ihram has to do the rites of 'Umrah]
b: Yes, he must make Qada of the missed Hajj the next year.

f: Is there Damm? [i.e. for the Muhrim of Hajj who missed Wuquf of 'Arafat until dawn of the Day of Nahr and after removing his Ihram has to do the rites of 'Umrah]
b: No.

f: Is there such a thing as a missed 'Umrah?
b: No, because 'Umrah is not specified to a particular time. As we mentioned before, it is permissible throughout the year and Makruh for 5 days.

f: What is Hady?
b: It is the animal slaughtered in Hajj and 'Umrah. Either the Muhsir slaughters it for release from Ihram, or the Mutamatti' or the Qarin slaughters it out of gratitude to Allaah for allowing the Hajj and 'Umrah to be joined. It is also slaughtered as compensation for violating the Ihram or omitting a Wajib of Hajj or 'Umrah. It may also be voluntarily slaughtered.

f: What animal is the Hady?
b: It can only be camel, cattle or goat/sheep, no other animal. Male and female is allowed.

f: Can any of the three categories [i.e. of Hady] be slaughtered as one wanted, or are there restrictions?
b: Yes, there are two conditions. The animal must be Thani or above; and must be free of defects.

f: What is a Thani?
b: A Thani is a goat which has completed a year and is in its second year; or a calf which has completed 2 years and is in its third year; or a camel which has completed 5 years and is in its sixth year.

f: Is less than a Thani sheep allowed?
b: Yes, a Jaza' or a sheep which has completed six months is allowed which is mixed with other Thani will seem to an onlooker like it is a Thani.

f: What is the meaning of free of defect?
b: That all the organs be intact. Thus a Hady with a cut hoof, leg, ear or tail is not vali;d nor one which has lost an eye; nor an insane animal; nor a cripple which cannot walk to the place of slaughter.

f: Can an animal which has only a part of an ear or tail cut off be used as a Hady?
b: If most of the ear or tail is cut off then it is not a valid Hady.

f: Can one slaughter the Hady wherever one wishes?
b: The slaughter is not valid anywhere besides the Haram.

f: In what circumstances are camels and cattle specified for slaughter?
b: A complete camel or cow must be slaughtered as compensation for making Tawafuz Ziyarah as a Junub and not repeating the Tawafuz Ziyarah. It is also the compensation for one who had sex after Wuquf at 'Arafat but before shaving and before Tawafuz Ziyarah. In these two scenarios only a cow or camel will suffice. In all other cases a sheep will suffice, be it for Damm of Ihsar, Damm of Tamattu', Damm of Qiran, Damm of violations; or simply voluntary Hady.

f: Can more than one person share in the slaughter of certain Hady?
b: Yes, up to 7 people can share in a camel or cow on condition that all 7 intend it as a worship.

f: What is the ruling of 7 people sharing in a Hady and one of them has only made intention of the meat?
b: The Hady is not valid for any of them.

f: Can the meat of Hady be eaten?
b: The owner of the Hady can eat form voluntary Hady, Tamattu' and Qiran. It is not allowed for him from Damm of Ihsar and Damm of violations.

f: Is there a specified time for slaughtering Hady?
b: It is not permissible to slaughter Hady of Tamattu' and Qiran before the Day of Nahr. It must be slaughtered on the Day of Nahr or the two days thereafter. He may not delay the slaughter of the Hady after the 12th of Zil Hijjah. He may not slaughter before pelting the Biggest Jamrah on the Day of Nahr. It is allowed to slaughter for Damm of Ihsar and violations at any time.

f: What is the ruling of delaying the Hady of Tamattu' or Qiran after the Days of Nahr?
b:
In addition to the delayed Hady, he must slaughter another Hady for the delay.121

121 If in additon he shaved before slaughter, then he will owe a third Hady as well for incorrect order.

f: Is it Wajib to give the meat of the Hady as Sadaqah to the poor of the Haram?
b: No, it is not specified for the poor of the Haram. It is permissible to give the Sadaqah to those poor or others.

f: Is it Wajib to take the Hady to 'Arafat?
b: No.

f: What is the difference between Zabh [slaughter across the throat] and Nahr [spearing the throat]?
b: The Sunnah for camels is Nahr and for cattle and sheep it is Zabh. If done in the opposite it is permissible but Makruh.

f: Is it Wajib to slaughter or make Nahr oneself?
b: No, someone else can do it. It is however better to do it oneself if one is capable.

f: A man was brining a camel and then was forced to ride it, may he do so?
b: He may ride it only if forced to.

f: May he use the milk of the sheep or camel he is bringing for slaughter?
b: He may not milk them. He should moisten the udders with cold water to stop the milk.

f: If the Hady perishes on the way, what should he do?
b: If it was voluntary then he need not replace it. If it was Wajib then he must slaughter a substitute.

f: What is the ruling if a defect afflicts the Hady which prevents its validity for slaughter?
b: If it is Wajib Hady then he must slaughter a substitute and may do with the defective one what he wants to. If it is a voluntary Hady then he should slaughter it despite the defect.

f: What should he do if he was bringing a Budanah and it was about to perish on the way?
b: If it was voluntary he should slaughter the camel and dip the sandals he hung around it in its blood. He should then place it on the hump as a sign that he left it for the poor. Neither he nor the wealthy may eat from it. If it was Wajib then he must substitute it and do with the original what he wishes.

f: What is the ruling of hanging around its neck?
b: It is Mustahab for the voluntary Hady and Tamattu' and Qiran. Damm of Ihsar and violations should not have anything hanged around.

f: What should he do with the blanket and rope of the Hady?
b: Give it away in Sadaqah.

f: Can the slaughterer be paid his fee from the meat?
b: No. It must be given from his own funds. [Muslim and al-Bukhari, narratinon of 'Ali رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ]

f: What is Bay' [trade]?
b: An exchange of a commidity for a commidity with the happy consent of the transacting parties.

f: How is a transaction contracted?
b: It is contracted by offer and acceptance when both speak in the past tense, e.g. one says, "I have sold," and the other sayd, "I have bought."

f: When one party has made an offer, does it become binding on the other party?
b: No. When one offers, the other has a choice. He may accept it in the same Majlis [sitting, gathering] or reject it. Once the second party accepts it, it becomes binding. Neither then has a choice.

f: Why have you mentioned accepting in the gathering?
b: When an offer has been made and either moves from the gathering before the acceptance then the offer is void.

f: Once the transaction has been completed, does the buyer have any further options?
b: Yes, if a defect becomes apparent in the goods he bought he has a choice. He may return then or he may take them. The buyer has the same option of returning or accepting as long as he did not see the goods.

f: Is a transaction valid with deferred payment?
b: Transactions are valid with immediate payment and deferred payment if the period has been defined.

f: A man sold goods. He pointed at it and did not declare the quantity, weight or measure. Or two men bartered goods and did not declare the quantity, weight or measure but each pointed at his goods. Are these two transactions valid?
b: Both are valid. Pointing out the goods or price does not require further defining for the validity of the transaction. Pointing out something is the most exact form of defining something.

f: What is the ruling if the price was undefined in terms of amount and type of currency?
b: If the buyer said for example, "I have bought from you for silver/gold/Dirham/Dinar/wheat," and did not specify the amount or type, then the transaction is not valid. For the validity of the transaction the amount must be mentioned, e.g. "I bought from you for X amount of Dirham." The description must also be mentioned, e.g. "Egyptian/Syrian; Pure/Alloyed."

f: If only the description of the price was given, e.g. he said, "I sell you this for 10 Dirham," and in the city there are several descriptions of money used, is the transaction valid if the buyer accepted?
b: Yes, the money will be defined as the one the people most commonly use in the city.

f: The Dirham was left undefined and there are different kinds in terms of monetary value. Will the transaction be valid?
b: The transaction is incorrect unless one was defined and the amount is known.

f: Is a sale of food and seeds in measure or amount valid?
b: It is permissible to sell it for Dirham/Dinar/currency/seeds. However, it is not allowed to sell a quantity of food for food of the same type because of the possibility of Riba [interest].

f: A man said, "I am selling you this wheat to the extent that it fills this container." The buyer accepts although he does not know the exact amount the container can hold. Is this valid?
b: The sale of the specified container is valid even if he does not know the exact amount it will contain.

f: If he buys equal to the weight of a specific stone, whose weight he does not know, what is the ruling?
b: That is also permissible.

f: A man bought a basket of food, each Qafiz [a dry measure] for a Dirham. Is the transaction valid?
b: The transaction is only valid for 1 Qafiz and invalid for the rest, unless the total Qafiz has been stipulated. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. His two companions say that it is valid in both cases, whether the total had been mentioned or not.

f: What is the ruling of Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى if someone sold a flock of sheep and said, "A Dirham per sheep."?
b: The entire transaction is incorrect according to him. His two companions say that it is correct in all.

f: What did Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى say about selling cloth for a Dirham per arm span and the total length had not been mentioned?
b: The transaction is incorrect in total as well as per arm-span.

f: What do you say about someone who sold a basket of 100 Qafiz of food for 100 Dirham, the buyer then discovers that it is less then 100 Qafiz?
b: The buyer can either cancel the sale or pay the proportionate amount only.

f: What is the ruling if he found it to be more than 100 Qafiz? [i.e. if someone sold a basket of 100 Qafiz of food]
b: The extra amount must be returned to the seller.

f: A man bought a 10 arm-span cloth for 10 Dirham; or he bought a 100 arm-span land for 100 Dirham. He then found the cloth or the land to be less than what the seller claimed. What is the ruling?
b: The buyer can either take it at full price or cancel the sale.

f: If he finds it to be more then what the seller claimed? [i.e. a man buying a 10 arm-span cloth for 10 Dirham; or buying a 100 arm-span land for 100 Dirham]
b: The cloth or the land is for the buyer at the stipulated price. The seller has no choice.

f: What do you say if the seller had to say, "I am selling you this which is 100 arm-spans for 100 Dirhams, each arm-span for a Dirham," and the item turns out to be more than that or less?
b: The buyer has a choice if it is less. He can take the item at the proportionate price or he can cancel the sale. If it is more then his choice is to take the total at a price of a Dirham per arm-span or he can cancel the sale.

f: A seller says, "I am selling you this bundle of 10 cloths for 100 Dirham. Each cloth is 10 Dirham." What is the ruling if they are more or less than 10?
b: If it is less then the sale is valid at the proportionate price. If it is more then the sale is Fasid [invalid].

f: A man sold a house and did not mention anything else. What else is included in the term "House"?
b: When a house is sold, it includes the courtyard, the building, the keys and locks, even if they were not specifically mentioned.

f: What do you say about the sale of a land which has trees on it?
b: The trees are included in the sale, whether they were mentioned or not.

f: What is the ruling if the land with crops was sold, but the crops were not mentioned?
b: The crops are not included in the sale of the land, unless otherwise stipulated.

f: Someone sold a date-tree or other fruit-tree. Who owns the fruit?
b: The seller keeps the fruit, unless the buyer had stipulated otherwise. The seller must cut off his fruit and hand the tree over to the buyer.

f: Is it permissible to buy unripe fruit which is still on the tree?
b: It is permissible to sell fruit which is on the tree - whether ripe or unripe - but the seller must immediately cut them off.

f: What is the ruling if a condition of leaving the fruit on the tree was made?
b: The sale is Fasid.

f: If the fruit was on the tree and was sold except for a specified Ritl [weight], what is the ruling?
b: The sale is Fasid.

f: Is the sale of wheath in its sheathe and beans in its pods permissible?
b: It is allowed if sold for something of a different type. If sold for the same thing then it is not permissible due to the possibility of Riba [usury].

f: Something was sold by weight or measured dimensions. It was so much that a measurer/scale had to be hired. Who bears the hiring fees?
b:
The seller.122

122 Just as if a professional counter had to be hired.

f: The buyer offered Dirham/Dinar. The seller needed other currency and had it changed. Who bears the exchange fee?
b:
The seller.123

123 The buyer according to the narration of Ibn Sima'ah from Muhammed.

f: The Dirham or Dinar were many and needed to be weighed. Who bears the fees of the weighing?
b: The buyer.

f: Is it Wajib to give the goods first, or is it Wajib upon the buyer to pay first?
b: If paid for with money then the buyer must pay first. If goods are exchanged for goods or one currency for another, then they should exchange it simultaneously.

f: What is the ruling of right of withdrawal [khiyarush Shart] for the buyer and the seller?
b: It is permissible for either party.

f: Is there a limitation to it? [i.e. to right of withdrawal (khiyarush Shart)]
b: Yes, three days or less. More than that is not allowed according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى more than that is allowed if the one with the right stipulates it and the other party agrees.

f: Two men conducted a sale. The seller maintained the right of withdrawal for himself. The buyer took the goods which were then destroyed in his possession within the period of the right. What is the ruling?
b: In the principle the right being maintained by the seller prevents ownership from leaving him. The buyer thus took the seller's goods. If it perished in his possession during the period of the right he must replace it with the same kind of good if it is a standard good, and with the price if it is not standard.

f: Does the ownership remain with the seller if the buyer maintains the right of withdrawal?
b: The buyer maintaining khiyarush Shart does not prevent the ownership from leaving the seller. According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى ownership is not transferred to the buyer either in that case. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is.

f: The buyer assumed khiyarush Shart and took possession of the goods. It perishes in his hands. Who is liable in this case?
b: The buyer is now liable to pay the seller the agreed upon price.

f: The buyer has khiyarush Shart and has the goods. A defect develops. What is the ruling?
b: If the defect is irreverisble e.g. a slave loses his hands; then it is as a perished good. The buyer must pay the price they had agreed upon. If it is reversible then he maintains khiyarush Shart for the period. Once the period passes the buyer can no longer return the goods. He is now liable for the agreed upon price even if the defect remained.

f: What is the benefit of khiyarush Shart to the owner thereof?
b: He may either rescind the sale or confirm it within the period.

f: Is it necessary to rescind or confirm the sale in the presence of the other party?
b: Confirmation can take place in his absence, but rescinding must be done in his presence.

f: What can the buyer do if the seller sold him a slave claiming him to be a baker or scribe and he was not?
b: The buyer can keep him at the agreed price or he can cancel the sale and return the slave.

f: The party with khiyarush Shart died before confirming the sale and before the period elapsed. Do his heirs inherit the right?
b: The right is terminated and cannot pass to the heirs. The sale is regarded as complete.

f: A man bought goods he did not see. Is the sale valid?
b: The sale is valid. However, the buyer maintains the right to cancel the sale or accept the goods when he eventually does see it. He may also cancel before seeing it.

f: Is there a time limitation for this right? [i.e. when a man bought good he did not see]
b: No, it remains until there is any indication that the buyer is pleased with the goods.

f: What do you say about a seller who did not see his goods?
b: He has no right of sight.

f: The buyer saw the outside of a basket, the outside of a folded cloth, the face of a slave-girl or the face of an animal and took it. Is his right void?
b: This is deemed a sighting and he does not have a further right of sight.

f: Is it deemed a sighting if he saw the courtyard of a house and did not see the rooms?
b: According to the writers of the original texts this is a valid sighting and he does not have further rights. This is however based on the fact the houses in al-Kufah were all standard. Hence the Fatwa is on the view of Imaam Zufar رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى that he must see the inside of the house, because rooms differ.

f: What is the ruling if a blind man buys or sells?
b: His transactions are valid and he maintains the right of sight when buying.

f: How can he see when he is blind? [i.e. with regards to a blind amn having the right of sight]
b: He will touch the goods when the goods are such that are recognised by touch. Similarly he will taste or smell the goods. These will substitute his seeing them.

f: A blind man wishes to buy land. How will he recognise it?
b: The land will be described to him as there is no other way for him to recognise it. Once it is described and he is happy with it, his right has terminated.

f: A man sold someone else's possession, without his authorisation. What is the ruling?
b: The owner can either confirm or rescind the scale. He may confirm the sale as long as the four parts of the sale exist - the buyer, the seller, the possession and the owner. If the owner dies before confirmation of the sale is rescinded and the heirs cannot confirm it. When the sale is rescinded the buyer must seek restitution from the seller not the owner.

f: A man bought two robes in one sale. Can he return both if he then sees one?
b: Yes.

f: A man saw an item and bought it after some time has elapsed. Does his right of sight remain?
b: If the item remained as it was when he saw it he has no right. If he sees that it has changed then he has the right of sight.

f: A seller who had right of sight dies. What happens to his right?
b: The sale is confirmed and the right becomes void. It is not transferable to the heirs.

f: A man bought an item and then discovered a defect which existed when in the hands of the seller. Can he return it?
b: If the buyer did not see the defect at the time of purchase, nor at the time he took possesion, nor did the seller tell him of it; then he has a choice. He may accept it at the full price agreed or he may return it.

f: Can the buyer not keep it and reduce the price as per the defect?
b: No.

f: What is deemed a defect in these Masail?
b: Whatever will necessitate a reduction in price in the practice of traders is deemed a defect.

f: Give some examples of defects which permit a return of the goods by the buyer.
b: A slave who runs away or urinates in the bed. A child who steals is defective, once he attains puberty it is no longer a valid defect. A slave girl who sweats and stinks. That is not a defect for a slave unless due to an illness. Fornication and being illegitimate are defects in slave-girls not slaves.

f: A defect occurred in the possession of the buyer then he learns of a defect which already existed in the hands of the seller. What can he do?
b: He may seek a reduction for the defect in the good, but he may not return it to the seller unless the seller is willing to accept the new defect.

f: A man bought a cloth and cut it, stitched it or dyed it. Or he bought cereal and mixed it in butter. He then discovered a defect which existed in the hands of the seller. What is the ruling?
b: He may seek a reduction for the defect in the good, but he may not return it to the seller unless the seller is willing to accept it as it is.

f: What do you say about a man who bought a slave and freed him or the slave died, he then learns of a defect that was in the hands of the seller?
b: He may receive a reduction for the defect, but may not return it because there is nothing to validly return.

f: If the buyer killed the slave or he bought food and ate it.
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he does not receive anything. According to his two companions he will receive a reduction for the defect.

f: A man sold a slave and then the buyer resold it. The second buyer returned him to the first buyer because of a defect. May he return the slave to the first seller?
b: If the second seller i.e. the first buyer is forced by a court ruling to take the slaveback then he may return him to the first seller. If he accepted the slave without a court ruling then he may not.

f: A man bought a slave. The seller said, "I am absolved of all defects." The buyer then finds a defect. Can he return the defective good?
b:
He may not, even though the seller did not list all the possible defects.

NOTE: Cheating and hiding defects are Haram. Muslim narrates from Abu Hurayrah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ that Rasulullaah ﷺ passed by a basket filled with food. He entered his hand in it and his fingers emerged wet. He said, "What is this, O owner of the food?" "It rained on it, O Rasulullaah ﷺ," he said. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Why did you not place it on top of the food so that people can see it? He who deceives is not of us."

Ibn Majah narrates from Wathilah bin Asqa': I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "He who sells a defective product and does not expose the defect is eternally under the anger of Allaah."

f: Explain the types of transactions in terms of correctness.
b:
There are four kinds of transactions:
Sahih or valid: That which the Shari'ah recognises in its origin and in its description as correct. The transaction is in effect in itself if there are not any other prohibiting factors.
Batil or void: The Shari'ah does not recognise it in its origin. Under no circumstances can the transaction be in effect.
Fasid or incorrect: The Shari'ah recognises it in its origin, but not its description. It can take effect if the buyer takes possession of the goods. The Fuqaha have granted leeway for this category and sometimes apply the term Fasid for Batil.
Mawquf or suspended: such as when someone sells someone else's property. The transaction is suspended until the real owner validates it or voids it.

f: Explain Batil transactions concisely.
b: If one or both of the goods/price is Haram or not owned then the transaction is Batil.

f: Give some examples [i.e. of Batil transactions].
b:
The sale of something non-existent or that which has no monetary value is Batil such as blood and carrion [except fish and locust]; camel sperm, camel foetus, fruits which haven't grown yet, an animal which was slaughtered and Bismillaah deliberately omitted, carrion hide before tanning, a slaughtered sheep joined with a sheep which died naturally, human hair [out of respect it is void], pig hair [due to its filth], human excreta for as long as it is not consumed by earth, selling that which the owner does not have in his ownership yet unless by means of Salam,126 fish which has not yet been caught, birds in the air, milk still in the udder, pearls still in the oyset, wool still on the sheep, wine, pigs, a slave joined with a free man just as selling the grass on a pasturage is void.127 

126 Will be defined in a later chapter inshaAllaah.
127 In view of the Hadith declaring it in the common property of the people. Similarly it cannot be rented in that that will destroy a public possession. Most Mashaikh have however given permission when a man plants and waters it himself.

f: If the master sells his Ummul Walad [slave girl who gave birth to the master's child], or Mudabbar or Mukatab is the transaction valid?
b:
All these transactions are void.128

128 Selling the Ummul Walad is like selling a free person because Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Her child has set her free."
An aspect of freedom is created in the Mudabbar in the future death of the master. The sale of the general Mudabbar is void, not the sale of the conditional Mudabbar. The general Mudabbar is the one to whom the master, "You are free after my death." The conditional Mudabbar is the one whom the master says to, "If I die on this journey/of this sickness then you are free."
A Mukatab is also entitled to freedom. If however he is pleased with being sold then it is allowed.

f: A man lays a net/trap and says to another that whatever is caught is for the buyer at a given price. What is the ruling?
b: It is void. The prey was not in his possession at the time of the transaction.

f: What do you say about a man who combined in a single sale a slave and a Mudabbar or his slave and someone else's slave?
b: The transaction is valid for his slave for a proportionate price. It is not valid for the Mudabbar and the other's slave.

f: What is the ruling of a Batil transaction?
b: The transaction is not contracted and the buyer does not assume ownership when he takes the goods.

f: Give some examples of Fasid [incorrect] transactions.
b: Muzabanah - selling dates on the tree in exchange for plucked dry dates; or grapes on the vine in exchange for raisins. Mulamasah - the sale is in effect by mere touching without right of sight e.g. it was dark or the cloth was folded. There is also no right to withdraw within the gathering. Munabazah is that each throws his goods at the other and the sale is made. These were transactions which were regarded as correct before Islaam. Throwing a stone on a group of items. Whichever one it falls on is sold. Similarly selling an animal or slave-girl and excluding its foetus is Fasid. Selling an arms-span of a robe where it will cause damage to the whole big price as well for as selling a beam of a roof is incorrect. Or buying a [unspecified] robe out of two robes.

f: Does setting preconditions make the transaction Fasid?
b:
Yes, it is Fasid unless the condition is such which is needed for the transaction to reasonably take effect; it is suitable and there is a benefit for one party or the goods, or it is a condition he is entitled to, or it is known in the custom of the people, and if the Shari'ah has not forbidden these conditions.129

129 Thus conditions like the seller will keep the goods until the buyer pays do not make the transaction Fasid or condition established by Shari'ah like Khiyarush Shart. Or conditions well known in that society e.g. the seller will keep the fruits of a sold tree.

f: Give some examples which make the transaction Fasid.
b: If someone sold a slave on condition that he will set the slave free or make him Mudabbar or Mukatab; or the seller will use his services for a month; or he sells a slave-girl on condition that the buyer will seek to impregnate her; or a house on condition that the seller will inhabit it for a set time; or that he will not give the goods until the end of the month; or that the buyer will loan him a Dirham; that he must give him a gift. These conditions make the transaction Fasid.

f: What do you say about a man buying a cloth on condition that the seller cuts it and makes it into a shirt; or a sandal on condition that the seller puts in laces/straps.
b: The transaction is Fasid.

f: What is the ruling if the seller sets a condition that he will defer payment to the Persian feast of Nawruz or Mahrajan, or the fast of the Christians or the end of the fast of the Jews; and the seller accepts the condition?
b: It is Fasid unless both parties know when these dates will be.

f: Is it permissible to set the time of payment until the harvest, or the milling of the wheat, or the plucking of the fruits, or the return of the Hajjaj?
b: The transaction is Fasid.

f: They agreed to the above times [i.e. until the time of harvest, or the milling of the wheat, or the plucking of the fruits, or the return of the Hajjaj] then agreed to drop that condition before that time arrived. Is the transaction correct?
b: Yes, it has now become correct.

f: Is the sale of dogs, cheetahs and beasts of prey permissible?
b: Yes.

f: What is the ruling of selling silkworms and bees?
b:
The silkworm can only be sold with the silk.131 The bee can only be sold with its hive.

131 According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the silkworm is a vermin and may not be sold at all. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it can be sold by the way when it shows that it is producing silk. According to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى upon whose view the Fatwa is, the silkworm can be sold under any circumstance since it has benefit.

f: What is the ruling of a Fasid transaction?
b: If they had entered into the Fasid transaction in which there is an exchange of goods having a monetary value, and the buyer takes the goods with the consent of the seller, the buyer becomes the owner and is liable to pay the seller. However, it is Wajib upon both of them to cancel the transaction in obedience to Shari'ah.

f: They did not cancel the Fasid transaction. In fact, the buyer sold the goods to a third party. Does the new sale take effect?
b: Yes.

f: The buyer made a profit in selling the goods as above [i.e. after a Fasid transaction the buyer sold the goods to a third party]. What is the status of the profit?
b:
The profit is not wholesome. He should give it away in charity.132

132 The first seller however need not give away his profits.

f: What is the ruling on auctions?
b: There is no harm in it. Rasulullaah ﷺ auctioned a bowl and a blanket. [Abu Dawud, narrated by Anas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ]

f: Is the seller obligated to sell his goods at the last offered price in an auction?
b: No, he can choose.

f: Do Kuffar living under Muslim rule have to observe Islaamic financial regulations in terms of validity and incorrectness of transactions?
b: They are bound just like Muslims, except in wine and pigs. Their transaction with wine is just like a Muslim's transaction with juice. Their transaction with a pig is like a Muslim's transaction with a sheep.

f: Allaah says, "O you who believe, when the call is made for the Salah of the Day of Jumu'ah hasten to Allaah's remembrance and leave trade."
b:
Thus trade from the Azan of Jumu'ah until the end of the Salah is prohibited. Rasulullaah ﷺ has also forbidden Najash [to increase a bid and raise the price for others without intending to buy it oneself]; offering a higher price after the seller had already accepted the buyer's offer; and a city person going out and buying the crops of the farmers as they come to the city; and city-folk taking the goods of farmers and selling it for themselves.

NOTE: If someone owns two child slaves who are blood relations of each other, then he may not separate them in a sale by selling each to different masters. If one is a child and the other an adult it would be Makruh to separate them but the sale would be valid. If they are both adults then there is no harm in separating them.133

133 Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "He who separates a mother from her child, Allaah will separate him from his loved ones on the Day of Qiyamah."
Rasulullaah ﷺ gave 'Ali رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ a gift of two small brothers. He ﷺ asked, "What has happened to the brothers?" He said, "One is sold." Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Join them. Join them."
This applies to relatives who cannot marry each other. Thus relatives who can marry or those who cannot marry but are not blood relatives are not included in this rule. Thus a cousin who is also a foster-brother would be included in the rule.

f: What is Iqalah? What is its status in Shari'ah?
b: It is the rescinding of a transaction after the buyer and seller had already completed it. It can only be rescinded with the consent of both parties and for return of the original price.

f: What is the ruling if one of the two stipulates more or less than the original price [i.e. in the case of Iqalah]?
b: The condition is void. The goods will be returned at the original price.

f: Is Iqalah a cancellation of sale or a new sale?
b:
It is a cancellation with regards the original parties and a new transaction with regards the rights of third parties. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى.134

134 e.g. A man had a right to buy a property first. He allowed it to be sold to someone else. The sale was then rescinded. The man again has a claim on the "new" sale.

f: What is the status of the Iqalah when the product or the price perishes?
b: The perishing of the price does not prevent Iqalah, the perishing of the product does.

f: Some of the goods sold perished. Can the sale be rescinded in the remaining goods?
b:
Yes.

NOTE: To accept the request of the other party regretting the sale is Mustahab and entails great reward.135

135 Shurayh رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "He who agrees to cancel the sale of his brother, Allaah will cancel his sins on the Day of Qiyamah." [at-Tabrani in al-Awsat].

f: What is Murabah and Tawliyah in the terminology of the Fuqaha?
b:
Murabah is to mention what was required at the higher price with a profit.

Tawliyah is to mention what was acquired at the acquired price without a profit.

f: Are there conditions for the validity of Murabahah and Tawliyah?
b: Yes, the items must be such which have similar replacements e.g. they are products sold by volume or weight.

f: A man bought a cloth for example. He washed it, dyed it and embroided it. The price hence increased. Or he bought food and paid a porter to carry it. Or put a silk border on the cloth he bought. What is the method of Murabahah here?
b: Murabahah is allowed, but he may not say, "I bought it for so much," he must say, "This has cost me so much."

f: A man bought an item on Murabahah, and then discovered that the seller lied to him. What is the ruling?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he may either accept it at the total price or return it.

f: What can he do if he was cheated in Tawliyah?
b: If he thought the seller was true then he may reduce the excess from the price.

f: Is there a difference amongst Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and his two companions in this? [i.e. if someone was cheating in Tawliyah]
b: Yes, Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى said that the excess will be reduced from the price in both Murabahah and Tawliyah. There is no option for rescinding. Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى said that in both cases he will choose between taking it at the price or rescinding the sale. There is no option of reducing the price.

f: A man bought an item. Can he sell it before taking possession of it?
b: A moveable item cannot be sold until it is in his possession. Unmoveable items such as land may be sold before taking possession according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. It is not permissible before taking possession according to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى.

f: Is it necessary for the buyer to measure or weigh the product after taking possession?
b:
If he bought a product according to volume which is sold per volume, or according to weight which is sold per weight then consuming it or selling it is Haram until he reweights it.136

136 By Haram is meant Makruh Tahrimi. Jabir رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ forbade selling food until two scales have weighted, the scale of the first seller and the scale of the buyer. [Ibn Majah]. It is also clear that if the items were bought by amount then there is no need for the double weighing.

f: A man sold a product and did not yet take possession of the price. May he deal in the money before taking possession?
b: Yes.

f: Can the price or the goods be increased after the transaction is concluded?
b: It is permissible if the buyer wishes to pay more or the seller wishes to give more.

f: What is the ruling if the seller discounts the price after conclusion of the transaction?
b: It is also allowed.

f: If in these scenarios of the buyer paying more, the seller giving more or charging less, is the difference now part of the parties' rights?
b:
Yes.137

137 E.g. The buyer now cannot demand the goods until he pays the extra he offered. If the goods have to be returned they will be returned will the extra amount.

f: A man sold goods for immediate payment and then gave a set date for payment. What is the ruling?
b: It becomes a credit sale. Any amount payable for which the creditor grants terms becomes credit; except for loans because time is not factored in them.

f: What is Riba linguistically and in Shari'ah?
b: Linguistically it is an increase, in Shari'ah there are two kinds - trade Riba and loan Riba. Both are Haram. Severe warnings have been given the giver and the taker.

f: What is loan Riba?
b: A man lends someone Dirham or Dinar for example and stipulates that the borrower will return a greater amount to him.

f: What is trade Riba?
b: Sale of a measured in volume or weighed product in exchange for a product of the same category [Jins] for an excess amount; or selling them on credit whether of the same category or not.

f: Is there a narration from Rasulullaah ﷺ on that? [i.e. on trade riba]
b:
Abu Sa'id رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ al Khudri رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Gold for gold139, silver for silver, wheat for wheat, barley for barley, dates for dates and salt for salt - the same for the same, hand to hand. He who increases it or seeks increase has done Riba. The taker and the giver are equal in it. [Muslim]

'Ubadaha bin as-Samit رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Gold for gold, silver for silver, wheat for wheat, barley for barley, dates for dates and salt for salt - the same for the same, amount for amount, hand to hand. If the categories differ, then sell as you wish when it is hand to hand."

Rasulullaah ﷺ mentioned these six things. He commanded that these things not be exchanged for something of the same category [Jins] unless it be of the same kind, equal amount and hand to hand. He declared that what is increased is Riba from whichever side it may be. He said, "The taker and the giver are equal in it. He allowed the exchange of these goods of another category [Jins] whether in equal or differing amounts on condition that it is done hand to hand.

From this Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى has established that Riba takes place from measured volume goods with its Jins and weighed goods with its Jins. These goods are either measured or weighed. Thus if a weighed item is exchanged for a good of the same category - even if they are not of the specific six mentioned - and the exchange is for equal amounts, then the sale is correct. If there is an increase on either side then it is not allowed. If they are of different categories then an increase is allowed but not credit. When both criteria - measure/weight and Jins - are missing then both increase and credit are allowed.
When both criteria exist then an increase and credit are both Haram. If only one is found then an increase is allowed but credit is Haram.

139 Meaning, "Sell gold for gold..."

f: Are differing amounts allowed between good wheat exchanged for lower quality wheat?
b:
No, they are of the same category. This ruling applies to all measured and weighed products.142

142 Abu Sa'id al-Khudri رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates: Bilal brought Barni dates to Rasulullaah ﷺ. He asked him, "Where is this from?" He replied, "I had some low quality dates. I gave 2 Sa' of that for 1 Sa' of this." He said, "That exactly is Riba. Do not do that. When you want to buy that, then sell your dates in a separate sale and then buy them with your money." [al-Bukhari and Muslim]

f: How are categories defined as measured or weighed?
b: Whateve Rasulullaah ﷺ declared to be measured by volume in which excess is forbidden will be regarded as a measured product forever even if the people no longer measure them e.g. wheat, barley, dates and salt. Whatever Rasulullaah ﷺ declared to be weighed in which excess is forbidden will be regarded as a weighed pproduct forever even if the people no longer weigh them e.g. gold and silver. Whatever Rasulullaah ﷺ did not explicitly define will be treated according to the custom of the people. If something is weighed in the custom of the people then it is a weighed product. If something is measured in the custom of the people then it is a measured product. If something is counted in the custom of the people then it is a counted product.

f: When must possession be taken?
b: In the monetary category - gold and silver - the exchange must be made in the gathering. This is called Bay'us Sarf (currency dealings). Besides the monetary category, any other good wherein there can be Riba must have the terms of taking possession stipulated. Imnmediate exchange is not a condition.

f: Is it permissible to exchange wheat for its flour or cereal; or the cereal for the floor?
b: These transactions are not allowed; neither in different nor in equal amounts.

f: What is the ruling of Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى concerning exchanging meat for an animal?
b: It is permissible.

f: What do the other two Imams say? [i.e. about exchanging meat for an animal]
b: Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى agrees with Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى says that the exchange is not allowed until the meat is more than that in the animal. The flesh will equal each other and the excess will be for the offal etc.

f: What does Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى say about exchanging an equal amount of dry dates for moist dates or grapes for raisins in the same way?
b: It is permissible according to him because they are of the same category. According to the other two it is not permissible.

f: Is it permissible to exchange olives and olive oil; or sesame seeds for sesame oil?
b: It is not allowed unless the oil is more. The oil will match the oil inside and the excess oil will be for the rest of the olive/sesame.

f: Can two different kinds of meat be exchanged, one more than the other?
b: Yes.

f: Can camel-, cow, and goat-milk be exchanged for each other in different amounts?
b:
Yes, these too are permissible.143

143 Because they are sub-categories in such a way that they are regarded as independent categories.

f: A man exchanged vinegar made from reject dates with grape-vinegari n differing amounts. What is the ruling?
b: Permissible as well.

f: What do you say about exchanging wheat-bread for wheat or wheat-flour in different amounts?
b: Permissible as well.

f: A man permitted his slave to trade. He then buys something from his slave in a Riba transaction. What is the ruling?
b: The transaction is valid. There is no Riba between an owner and his slave. The slave and whatever is in his possession belongs to the owner in any case.

f: What is the ruling of a Muslim having a Riba dealing with a Harbi [Kafir of Darul Harb] in Darul Harb [land of hostile Kuffar]?
b: There is no Riba ruling between a Muslim and Harbi in Darul Harb.

f: What is Sarf?
b: It is the terminology for the Fuqaha for the exchange of monetary item for monetary item such as gold for silver.

f: What is the ruling of exchanging gold for gold or silver for silver?
b: It is only allowed if done equal amount for equal amount, hand to hand, as discussed under Riba.

f: Are different amounts allowed if the two gold/silvers are of different qualities and make?
b: No, becuase quality and manufacture are not considered in Sarf.

f: What is the ruling of exchanging gold for silver?
b: The categories differ, hence the amounts may differ but it is Wajib to take possession in the gathering of the agreement.

f: If they separated and one or both did not take possession what is the ruling?
b: The agreement is void.

f: Is it permissible to transact with the goods received in Sarf before taking possession?
b: No.

f: A man sold gold for silver in number of units. What is the ruling?
b: It is allowed because the categories are different. There is no condition of the amounts having to be equal, but physical exchange must take place before separation.

f: A man sold a sword decorated with silver for 100 Dirham and the decoration cost 50 silver Dirham. The buyer paid 50 Dirham to the price and the remainder was left as a debt. What is the ruling of the transaction?
b: The transaction is correct. The amount taken goes for the silver even if not stipulated and the outstanding amount is a debt for a time which the two agree upon.

f: If the buyer said, "Take this 50 for both?" [i.e. regarding a sword sold for 100 Dirham which has silver decoration worth 50 Dirham]
b: That is also allowed.

f: If they separated before taking possesion? [i.e. when a sword with silver decoration worth 50 Dirham is sold for 100 Dirham, see question 846]
b: The transaction is void regarding both the sword and the decoration if the decoration cannot be separated without difficulty. If it can easily be separated then the transaction is correct in the sword but void for the decoration.

f: A man sold a silver vessel for gold or silver? They separated and he only took part of the price. What is the ruling?
b: The transaction is void in the amount he did not take and correct in regard to the amount he took. They are now partners in the vessel.

f: What can the buyer now do? [i.e. when a man sold a silver vessel for gold or silver and they separated and he only took part of the price]
b: He can purchase the rest of the vessel with the remainder of the price or he can rescind (cancel) the sale.

f: He sold a piece of ingot (pieces of raw silver) then became a partner in it (discovers that someone else has a right over part of it). Is there a choice in this scenario also?
b: No, he will take the part which remains according to the outstanding amount.

f: 2 Dirham and a Dinar were exchanged for 2 Dinar and Dirham. Is this allowed?
b: Yes, each category will be regarded as exchanged for the opposite category.

f: If 11 Dirham were exchanged for 10 Dirham and Dinar, is this allowed?
b: Yes, the 10 is for the 10 and the one Dirham for the one Dinar.

f: Is the exchange of 2 Dirham and a Dirham of wheat for one Dirham and two Dirham of wheat allowed?
b: Yes.

f: Can a gold Dinar or silver Dirham with alloy be exchanged for its same category in a different amount?
b: If the overwhelming metal of the Dinar is gold it will be treated as gold; and similarly with the Dirham. Thus the prohibition of differing amounts in proper gold/silver will apply. If most of the metal is alloy then they will not be regarded as gold/silver. They will be regarded as goods. If it is sold for its category in different amounts then it is correct. (Immediate possession is still necessary because there is gold/silver in the goods which cannot be removed with ease.)

f: A man bought goods with alloyed Dirham/Dinar. The people then stopped using those coins before the seller took possession of them. What is the ruling?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the transaction is void. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the buyer must pay the price which was prevalent on the day of the sale. According to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he must pay the price of the last day the old coins were still used by the people.

f: Can something be bought with accepted currency without specification?
b: Yes, and if it is no longer accepted then it is not allowed until it is specified.

f: If he buys with accepted currency and the currency is no longer accepted by the time the seller takes possession, what is the ruling?
b: The sale is void according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and the other two differ as above.

f: A man bought goods with a half Dirham worth of currency [e.g. coins]. Is this permissible?
b: Yes, he owes the half Dirham worth of currency.

f: A man gives a money-exchanger a Dirham and says, "Give me a loose currency for the half Dirham and for the other half give me a half dirham except a Habbah [small bit]. Is the sale valid?
b: It is void according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. According to the other two Imams it is valid in the loose change and void in the rest.

f: If he said, "Give me a half Dirham worth of loose currency and a half except for a Habbah?" [i.e. a man gives a money-exchanger a Dirham]
b:
It is permissible.144

144 Because in this case he made the whole Dirham in exchange for what he asked. Hence his half Dirham less the Habbah will be in exchange for its equal and the remainder of his Dirham will be for the loose currency.

f: If he instead said, "Give me a small Dirham weighing a half Dirham except a Habbah and give me the rest in loose change," is this permissible? [i.e. a man gives a money-exchanger a Dirham]
b: Yes, the small Dirham will be in exchange of the half Dirham less a Habbah and the loose currency in exchange for the remainder.

f: Are there transactions where immediate exchange of the goods is not needed?
b: Yes, it is called Salam. It is an exchange of Dayn [deferred payment] for 'Ayn [immediate payment]. It is allowed even though the buyer only takes the goods after a specified time.

f: What is the general rule for Salam's permissibilty and impermissibility?
b: Salam is permissible in whatever can be fully described and quantified. If these cannot be described then Salam is not allowed.

f: List the categories in which Salam is allowed.
b: It is allowed in what can be measured in volume, weighed, measured in length, and counted (where the items do not differ e.g. walnuts and eggs). It will not be permissible in a bundle of wood or bunch of straw.

f: Are there conditions for this kind of sale? [i.e. Salam]
b:
Yes, they are as follows:
The category [jins] must be known.
The type must be known.
The description must be known.
The quantity must be known.
The quantity of the payment must be mentioned if it is such which must be quantified e.g. measured by volume or weight or number.
The place where it will be delivered when there is carrying and effort involved.
The sale is only correct if on deferred delivery and the time has been set. [Sale is not correct except on credit, hence the date of execution of sale (i.e. handing over the goods) must be known.)

f: Is there a difference between Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and the other two Imams? [i.e. regarding Salam]
b: Yes, they say that the payment need not be mentioned if it is known. It is also not necessary to mention the place of delivery. In which case it will be delivered at the place where the agreement had been concluded.

f: Is Salam allowed in cloth?
b: It is allowed if the length, breadth, thickness, description, category and type have all been mentioned.

f: Is Salam allowed in jewels and brocade?
b: No.

f: Is Salam allowed in unbaked and baked bricks?
b: It is allowed if a known brick mould is mentioned.

f: The seller hands the goods when the period had expired. When must the payer pay? [i.e. in Salam]
b: The Salam will only be valid if the buyer paid in the Majlis (in the same gathering prior to separation) of the agreement before they separate.

f: A Salam sale was concluded. The seller then wished to transact with the payment received or the buyer wished to transact with the goods receivable. What is the ruling?
b: Neither may transact until the goods are possessed. This includes that no partnership or Tawliyah transaction may be done before the possession.

f: Are there any other conditions for the Salam to be valid.
b:
Yes, the Fuqaha have also stated that the goods must be in existence145 from the time of the agreement until the expiry of the time.

145 Meaning that it should not disappear from the markets.

f: A man concluded Salam on a specific article. Is this valid?
b: No.

f: If the Salam was concluded on food from a specific town or fruit from a specific tree. Is this valid?
b: This is also not correct.

f: What is Rahn linguistically and in Shari'ah?
b: Linguistically it is simply to retain something for any reason. In Shari'ah it is the retaining of something in order to secure the fulfilment of a right.

f: How is a Rahn agreement made and fulfilled?
b: It is made with offer and acceptance. It is fulfilled when the one who has the right [Murtahin] receives the collateral. Thus if he takes possession in a way, that the collateral is separate and completely in his control then the fulfillment is complete.

f: Offer and acceptance was made but the Murtahin did not take possession of the collateral. What is the ruling?
b: For as long as the Rahn has not been given over, the one who must give it [Rahin] may either hand it over or he may rescind the agreement. Once it is handed over it falls in the responsibility of the Murtahin.

f: Why has Rahn been allowed in Shari'ah?
b: So that there is an assurance of fulfilment of debt, and the right of the creditor not be lost. Thus Rahn is not correct without being attached to a debt.

f: The Murtahin took control of the collateral and it perished in his hands. Upon whom is the responsibility?
b: We have already mentioned that the Murtahin is responsible once he assumes control over the collateral. The Fuqaha have mentioned that he is responsible to the value of the debt or the collateral, whichever is the lesser.

f: What do you mean, "the debt or the collateral, whichever is the lesser?" [i.e. if the Murtahin took control of the collateral and it perished in his hands]
b: If the collateral is destroyed in the hands of the Murtahin and its value equalled the debt, then legally the Murtahin has had his debt fulfilled. If the value is less then the debt, that amount is deducted from the debt and the Murtahim claims the remainder from the Rahin. If the Rahn is more than the debt, then the excess is treated as a "trust" with all the applicable laws. Thus if the collateral perished in the hands of the Murtahin, he has no responsibility for the excess because there is no claims for responsibility for trusts. The debt is forfeited in lieu of the value of the Rahn which was destroyed in the creditor's hands.

f: You mentioned that the Rahn must be separate and completely in the Murtahin's hands. What is the difference that these conditions make?
b: These conditions exclude whatever do not fall within their ambit. Hence a jointly owned Rahn is not allowed, as are fruits on trees without the trees, crops in the earth without the land, and land without the crops.

f: Can Rahn be taken from trusts like Wad'iah and 'Ariyah (deposits and borrowed items)?
b: No, because there is no liability if these things perish.

f: Can Rahn be taken for Capital of a Mudarabah and partnerships?
b: No.

f: Can Rahn be taken for the money given in Salam [prepayment]; or Sarf; or the good for which the Salam payment was made?
b: Yes.

f: A Salam or Sarf agreement was concluded. The Murtahin took possession of Rahn which perished in the same gathering. What is the ruling?
b: The Salam or Sarf is concluded. The Murtahin's claim has legally been met with.

f: The two parties agreed to a Rahn, but stipulated that a just person keep it. Is there a problem with that?
b: No.

f: They both agreed to keep the Rahn with a just third-party. Can either party take it from him?
b: That is not permissible for either of them.

f: Who is liable if it perishes [i.e. the Rahn] in the hands of the third party?
b: The Murtahin is liable because it perished under his responsibility. His debt is fulfilled just as if it was in his own physical possession.

f: What do you say about Dinar and Dirham; or measured goods or weighed goods as Rahn?
b: It is permissible. If they were given as Rahn for a debt of the same Jins and perishes, then the like amount is reduced from the debt even if they differed in quality and manufacture.

f: The creditor took a like amount from his debtor. After spending it he learnt that it was counterfeit. What is the ruling?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى his debt has been fulfilled by what he took and spent. According to the other two Imams he will return an amount equal to the counterfeit and claim the correct amount.

f: He gave two slaves as collateral for a debt of 1000. He then paid the part of the debt equal to the proportion of one of them. May he take that slave back?
b: He may not take either one until he pays the full debt.

f: Can the debtor appoint the creditor or the just man keeping the collateral or someone else to sell the collateral on his behalf upon settlement of the debt?
b: Yes, the appointment of these agents is allowed.

f: If the above appointment [i.e.  the debtor appoints the creditor or the just man keeping the collateral or someone else to sell the collateral on his behalf upon settlement of the debt] was a condition of the Rahn, can the Rahin cancel the appointment?
b: No, and if he does so the agent remains the agent.

f: Does the agency terminate if the Rahin as above [i.e. the debtor appoints the creditor or the just man keeping the collateral or someone else to sell the collateral on his behalf upon settlement of the debt], dies?
b: No.

f: Can the creditor demand payment of his debt while he holds the collateral?
b: Yes.

f: The debtor wishes to sell the collateral in order to pay off the debt. Is it Wajib upon the Murtahin to faciliate the sale?
b: It is not. He may say to the debtor, "Pay the debt and then take your collateral." Upon payment the creditor must return the collateral.

f: What is the ruling when the debtor sells the collateral without the creditor's permission?
b: The sale is suspended until either the Murtahin confirms it or the debt is paid.

f: A man was already holding a slave as collateral when the owner set him free. Is this valid?
b: Yes, the slave is free.

f: What resort does the creditor now have after the slave was freed to recover his debt? [i.e. a man was already holding a slave as collateral when the owner set him free]
b: If the debtor is well off and the debt is immediately payable, then the creditor may demand payment of the debt. If it was for a specified time, then he may claim from him the value of the slave and retain it as collateral. If the debtor is not well off, then the creditor may demand that the slave earn towards paying the debt. The slave must reclaim his payments from the former owner.

f: How can the slave claim from the old owner? [i.e. when the creditor demands that the slave - who was freed whilst being collateral - earns towards paying the debt. After which, the slave must reclaim his paiments from the former owner]
b: Because he had set him free at no charge. The earnings given towards the debt were acquired after being free.

f: The Rahin destroyed the collateral. The creditor has no collateral at hand. What should he do?
b: The Rahin is liable for the price of the collateral which will be given as new collateral.

f: The collateral is in the hands of the creditor. A third party destroys it. Who is liable for the destroyed item? What does the Murtahin keep as collateral?
b: The Murtahin must claim compensation from the third party. He will take the price and keep it as collateral.

f: What is the ruling of the Rahin damaging the collateral?
b: He is liable [because he is violating the right of the Murtahin]

f: What is the ruling of the Murtahin damaging the collateral?
b: The value of the damage is reduced from the debt. He is liable for any amount in excess of the debt.

f: If the collateral causes damage to the persons or wealth of the Rahin or the Murtahin, who is responsible?
b: The damage of the Rahn is upon them and damage to their wealth is forfeit.

f: The Murtahin needs to hire premises for the collateral. Who pays that cost?
b: The Murtahin.

f: If the collateral is a goat or camel for example, and needs a herder. Who pays his fees?
b: The Rahin.

f: Who pays the living expenses of the collateral?
b: The Rahin.

f: Who owns any produce of the collateral e.g. milk, baby, wool, fruit etc?
b:
It belongs to the Rahin, but he may not take possession. It will be included as part of the collateral.146

146 Although the Murtahin may hand it over to the Rahin if he wishes (al-Jawharah)

f: The produce remained in the hands of the Murtahin and perished in his hands. What is the ruling?
b: There is no liability.

f: If the original colleteral perished and the produced remained?
b:
The Rahin will reduce his debt by the proportion of the original. He will spread the debt over the value of the collateral the day the Murtahin took it; and the value of the produce the day of the reduction. The debt will be reduced according to the proportion due to the original. The proportion of failing on the produce is the Rahin's.147

147 E.g. a man gave a sheep worth 10 Dirham as collateral for a 10 Dirham loan. She gave birth and then died. If the value of the lamb is 10 Dirham, the sheep died as half the value of the debt i.e. 5 Dirham. If the lamb grew to value so that the day of claim it was worth 20 Dirham then the sheep's proportion is 2 and two-thirds of a Dirham. If the lamb is 30 Dirham the sheep's proportion is a quarter. If the lamb fell in value to 5 Dirham, the sheep's proportion is two-thirds or 6 and two-third Dirham. (al-Jawharah)

f: The Murtahin already took the collateral. He now wants more collateral or the debtor wants an increase in the debt. What is the ruling?
b: The collateral can be increased but not the debt according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى, except that it will no longer be classified as Rahn. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى an increase is allowed in both.

f: A man took a joint loan from two men. He gives a single item as Rahn. What is the ruling?
b: It is permissible. The item is collateral for each of the two.

f: What is the liability in that single item? [i.e. a man took a joint loan from two men and gave a single item as Rahn]
b: It is the responsibility of in proportion to each one's share of the debt.

f: If one debt is paid, can the Rahin take back that proportion from the collateral? [i.e. a man took a joint loan from two men]
b: No. It is now entirely collateral in the hands of the other until his debt is settled.

f: A man sold a slave on condition that the buyer gives a specific item as collateral for the price. The buyer refused to hand over the collateral. What is the status of the sale and the Rahn?
b: The sale is valid. The buyer cannot be forced to give the collateral. The seller can then either forfeit the Rahn or cancel the sale; unless the buyer immediately pays the price or gives the value of the collateral to keep as collateral. He will then keep it until settlement of the debt.

f: Can the Murtahin leave the collateral with his wife or child for safekeeping?
b: Yes. He may guard it himself or give it to his wife, child or servant who is of his household.

f: If he [i.e. the Murtahin] left it [i.e. the collateral] in the care or trust of someone outside his household, what is the ruling?
b: He bears liability becuse he exceeded the bounds.

f: If the Murtahim exceeded the bounds on the collateral, how is his liability treated?
b: It will be deemed as Ghasab [usurpation] for the entire value.

f: What is the ruling if the Murtahin returns the collateral to the Rahin?
b: He is no longer responsible for it. If it now perishes in the hands of the Rahin he has no liability.

f: Can the Murtahin ask for the Rahn back after he returned it?
b: Yes. When he takes it back his responsibility also returns.

f: If the Rahin dies before settlement of the debt, how can the Murtahin claim his debt?
b: The Rahin's executor will sell the Rahn and pay the debt. Any excess will be paid into the estate for distrubution amongst the heirs.

f: Who sells the Rahn if there is no executor?
b: The judge will appoint an executor to sell it and pay the debt.

f: Are there people who are interdicted from transacting?
b:
Yes, there are three causes for incapacitation in Shari'ah:
Childhood
Slavery
Insanity

f: Explain further [i.e. the causes for incapacitation].
b: A child may not transact except with the permission of his guardian. A slave may not transact except with the permission of his owner. A madman may not transact at all.

f: A man bought or sold with a child or slave who understands148 and aims to transact. What is the ruling?
b:
The guardian/owner may confirm the transaction or rescind it.

148 Understanding trade is a condition for the validity of the transaction.

f: Do these three causes prevent transacting in words only or actions as well?
b: The child and madman are incapacitated in regards words. The details of the slave will be discussed later inshaAllaah.

f: A child or madman destroyed someone's wealth. Is the liability from their wealth?
b: Yes, this is what is meant that they are not incapacitated in regards to their actions. It does not mean that they are not forbidden from destroying the wealth of people.

f: What is the effect of Hajr in words?
b: The contracts, confessions, divorce and setting slaves free are void.

f: What are the details of Hajr on a slave?
b: His words are implemented with regards to his rights, not the rights of his owner.

f: A slave confessed to owing money in regards himself. What is the ruling?
b: He, not the owner, is obligated to pay the amount. The obligation is only enacted after he gains freedom, not immediately.

f: If a slave confesses to a crime regarding penal punishment or execution, when will the punishment be inflicted?
b: He will be immediately punished. It will not be stalled until his freedom.

f: Does the divorce of a slave fall when he pronounces divorce upon his wife or does his owner declare the divorce?
b: The divorce is in effect when the slave divorces his wife, not when his owner declares so.

f: What is the ruling of the transactions of a man with his own wealth if he is free and adult but silly and incompetent [Safih]?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى if a man has intelligence, has attained puberty, and is free, he may not be incapacitated. He is allowed to transact with his wealth, even if he wastes and destroys his wealth in something without purpose e.g. he throws his wealth into the sea or burns it.

f: Is there a limit according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى for when the wealth of a Safih will be handed over to him?
b: Yes, according to him even a man attains puberty without competence then his wealth will be withheld until he is 25 even if he has still not attained competence. Transaction before that will be in effect though.

f: What do Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى say about the Safih?
b: The say that he will be declared incapacitated and will not be allowed to transact with his wealth. If he sells anything his sale will be void unless the judge sees some benefit in it. He who attains puberty without competence will not be given his wealth until he attains competence, however long that may be. He may not transact in it, however, his Zakah and expenses for his wife, children and whatever other blood-relatives he must support will be taken from his wealth.

f: What is the ruling of a Safih freeing his slaves?
b: He is free according to all the Imams, however Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى say that the slave has to earn and compensate his price to the Safih.

f: What is the ruling of a Safih marrying?
b: The marriage is valid. The mahr [dowry] he offered must be examined. The amount up to Mahr al-Mithl is correct and the excess void.

f: Is the Safih permitted to perform the Fard Hajj?
b: Yes, he should not be stopped. However, the judge will not give him his money. He will give it to a reliable person amongst the Hujjaj who will fulfil his Hajj expenses.

f: A Safih is sick and leaves a bequest for relatives and other good avenues of spending. Is the bequest valid?
b: It is valid up to a third of his wealth.

f: What is the ruling of preventing a bankrupt person who has outstanding debts from transacting?
b: Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى said, "I do not declare bankrup persons incapacitated because of debts. For when he is liable to pay the debts he will simply plead incapacitation. He should therefore not be declared incapacitated."

f: A bankrupt man has wealth but refuses to pay his debts. Will the judge intervene in his wealth according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى?
b: He will not transact with it, but will withold it until the owner sells it and pays his debts.

f: It is apparent that the debtor owns Dirham and Dinar. How will the judge see to the payment of the debt? [i.e. when a bankrupt man has wealth but refuses to pay his debts]
b: If the debt is in DInar and he has Dinar, or the debt is Diram and he has Dirham, then the judge will have his debts paid from that even if the debtor is displeased. If the debt is Dirham and he owns Dinar or vice-versa, the judge will sell the coins and pay the creditors.

f: What do Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى say about declaring a bankrupt man incapacitated?
b: They judge will only declare an interdict of incapacitation against him when the creditors seek such. He will then be prevented from buying, transacting and confession in order that he does not harm the creditors. The judge will sell his goods when he is prevented from selling. He will share the proceeds amongst the creditors in proportion to their claims. The judge will spend from the debtor's wealth upon his wife, small children and blood relations.

f: What is the ruling of the incapacitated bankrupt person confessing to a debt during his incapacitation?
b: He is liable to pay it after the settlement of the prior debts.

f: The debtor is not known to have any wealth. When the creditors seek an interdict against him he says, "I have no wealth. What can the judge do?" What is the ruling?
b: The judge will detain him for every debt which generated wealth in his hands such as proceeds of a sale and loans; also for every debt incurred by contract such as dowry and Kafalah. He will not be detained for anything else such as compensation for usurpation and fines and blood-money, unless there is proof that he has wealth.
