f: Will the judge detain him forever or for a set time? [i.e. a man who when the creditors seek an interdict against him he says, "I have no wealth"]
b: The aim is not detention, but to expose any money he may be hiding. The judge will detain for two-three months. He will investigate from the people about his condition and wealth. If any wealth is not discovered he will release him or if it is proved that he has no wealth.

f: Can the creditors be kept away from him after he was released when no wealth was discovered? [i.e. whilst the debtor claimed he had no wealth]
b: They will not be kept away from him. They may not prevent him from trading and travelling. They may demand payment and may take from his earnings anything in excess of his expenditure upon himself and his family. They will divide the excess in proportion to their claims.

f: Do the other two Imams differ in this? [i.e. about creditors being kept away from a debtor who was released when no wealth was discovered whilst he claimed he had none]
b: Yes, they differ with Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and say that the creditors will be kept away from the debtor whom the judge has declared bankrupt unless they can prove that he has acquired wealth.

f: Will an open sinner be declared incapacitated?
b: Not if he manages his wealth.

f: A man was pious and became a sinner. Will he be incapacitated?
b: No, an original sinner and a new sinner are the same in this.

f: A man bought something and took possession of it. He is indebted for the price. He then becomes bankrupt and has creditors from before this sale. The goods he bought are still with him. Can the creditor claim it exclusively?
b: He is the same as the other creditors in it.

f: At what age will a boy or girl be declared to have attained adulthood?
b: A boy is an adult if he has a nocturnal emission, ejaculation or impregnates a woman if they had sex. If none of that occur then when he reaches 18 years. A girl attains adulthood upon menses, nocturnal emission or pregnancy. If none of that occur then when she is 17 years.

f: Do all three Imams say that? [i.e. about when a boy and girl attain adulthood]
b: The others differ with Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and say that if none of the above factors occur then when they turn 15. The Fatwa is on this.

f: A boy or girl is close to the age of puberty and it is not clear if they have attained puberty. They declare that they have attained puberty. Will their word be accepted?
b: Yes, and the laws of adults will apply to them.

f: What is the ruling of Confession in Shari'ah?
b: When a free, adult, intelligent person confesses, his confession becomes obligatory upon him, whether for the unknown or known, his confession holds him liable.

f: How can he be held for something unknown? [i.e. with regards to his confession]
b: He will be aksed to explain the unknown thing he confessed to. If he refuses then the judge will force him to explain.

f: A man said, "I owe something." the people questioned him and the judge forced him to explain, so he said, "Yes, I owe, I owe a drop of water or a grain of wheat." What is the ruling?
b: His explanation will not be accepted. He must mentioned something which has a price.

f: Someone confessed to something, known or unknown, but the one for whom he confessed claimed more than that. What will the decision be?
b: If he confessed to an unknown amount or said, "I owe him money," then the decision will be upon what he explains that to be. His word will be accepted upon him taking an oath. His word will be accepted in the greatness or the smallness of the amount.

f: If he confesses, "I owe him a great amount," then says that it is 10 Dirham, will he be believed?
b: His confession will not be accepted for less than 200 Dirham.

f: If he confesses, "I owe him many Dirham," and then says it is 3, will that be accepted?
b: No, when he said many, he will not be believed in less than 10.

f: If he says, "I owe him Dirahim."?  [plural of Dirham]
b: He is responsible for at least 3 Dirham because 3 is the least plural [in 'Arabic], unless he confesses to the exact amount.

f: If he said, "I owe him so much, so much Dirham," or "I owe him so much and so much Dirham," what is the ruling?
b: He will not be believed in less than 11 Dirham [Ahada 'Ashar] in the first sentence and in less than 21 [Ahad wa 'Ishrin] in the second.

f: If he says, "For him upon me is ..." or "For him from my side ...?"
b: It is deemed a confession of debt.

f: If he says, "I have with me his ..." how is this confession interpreted?
b: It is a confession of a trust he is holding.

f: A man claims against another, "You owe me 1000 Dirham" The one addressed replies, "I have paid it/ You received payment already/ The account is balanced/ Give me respite," what is the ruling?
b: These are interpreted as confessions.

f: A man confesses that he owes an amount and was given respite to pau. The other acknowledges the amount but denies that respite was given. Will a ruling of respite be given or may he pay immediately?
b: He will pay immediately and the creditor will take an oath that no respite was given.

f: Someone confesses to an amount but immediately declares an exception to that amount. What is the ruling?
b: The exception is valid and he is liable for the rest, whether the exception was for most of the amount or a minority amount.

f: And if he excepts the entire amount? [i.e. someone confeses but immediately declares an exception to that amount]
b: The exception is void and he owes the amount he confessed to.

f: What is the ruling if he says, "I owe him 100 Dirham except a Dinar/a Qafiz of wheat."
b: He will owe 100 Dirham lessthe value of a Dinar or less the value of a Qafiz of food.

f: He said, "I owe him 100," without saying what and adds, "and a Dirham." What does he owe?
b: He owes 101 Dirham. It will be ruled that he left out the word Dirham after 100.

f: If he says he owes a 100 and a cloth?
b: He owes a cloth and he will be questioned what the 100 is.

f: A man confesses to the right of another and immediately utters, "InshaAllaah." What is the ruling?
b: He owes nothing. The addition is such that it removes the statement from being a confession and makes it as if it was never uttered.

f: A man confesses to the right of another and adds, for example "I have an option for three days." What is the ruling?
b: The confession is valid and the option is void, because the option is for rescinding which the confession precludes.

f: A man confesses to owing a house except the actual building.
b: He will owe the house and the building. His exception will be disregarded.

f: If he says, "The building of the house is mine and the courtyard belongs to so and so,"?
b: His statement will be accepted.

f: He confesses to owing dates which are on the branch.
b: He will owe the dates and the branch.

f: He confessed to owing an animal which is in the stable.
b: He will owe the animal only.

f: He confesses, "I usurped a cloth wrapped in a handkerchief/a cloth in a cloth."
b: He owes the cloth and handkerchief/ both cloths.

f: He confesses, "I owe a cloth in 10 cloths."
b: According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he owes one clloth and according to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he owes 11.

f: He confessed to usurpong the cloth of someone. He brings a defective cloth and says that that is the cloth. Will that be accepted?
b: He will take an oath and his statement accapted.

f: He confessed to Dirhams but said that they were counterfeit.
b: He will take an oath and his statement accepted.

f: He says, "I owe 5 by 5," intending mathematical multiplication
b: He owes 5 once.

f: He says, "I owe 5 with 5."
b: He owes 10.

f: He says, "I owe from a Dirham up to 10."
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the last exteme is omitted he owes 9. According to the other two it is included and he owes 10.

f: If he says, "I owe him 1000 Dirham for a slave I bought which I did not take possession of," must he pay anything?
b:
If he mentions a specific slave then it will be said to the seller, "If you wish, give him the slave and take the 1000, or else there is nothing for you." If he does not mention a specific slave, then according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he owes the 1000.149

149 And his addition, "which I did not take possession of," will not be accepted, whether he says it immediately or after a pause. It will be treated as a recanting after having confessed to owing the money. Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى said that if he said it immediately it will be accepted and he does not owe anything. If he pauses it will not be accepted if the seller denies it is from that sale.

f: What does he owe if he says, "I owe him 1000 Dirham for pigs/wine."?
b: He owes 1000. His statement that it is the price of pig/wine will not be accepted.

f: A man confesses to owing 1000 for a sale and says that it is counterfeit that he owes. The seller claims it to be correct currency he owes. How will a decision be made between them?
b: He owes correct currency according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he will be believed if he said it immediately and will not be believed if he paused in between and will then owe correct currency.

f: A man confesses to owing a ring or a sword, what does he owe?
b: He owes the ring with the stone/the sword with the sheathe and strap.

f: He confessed to owing a covered canopy and does not mention the curtain and poles.
b: He owes the canopoy with the curtain and poles.

f: He says, "I owe her foetus 1000."
b:
If he explains that it is a bequest from someone or that the foetus's father died and the foetus is his heir, then the confession is valid. If his confession is ambiguous [he did not add any explanation] then it is not correct. This is according to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. According to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the confession is valid and he owes that amount whether he explained it or not.150

150 And his words will be interpreted as in the given explanation of bequest or in inheritance.

f: He confesses that the foetus in a slave-girl or a sheep belongs to a certain man. Is this confession valid?
b: Yes. He owes what he confessed to.

f: A man confesses to debts on his deathbed. He had other debts incurred during his health. There were also debts incurred during his final illness with know causes. Which of the two will take preference?
b: The debts during his health and the debts with known causes take preference.

f: If he does not have debts incurred while healthy, what is the status of the debts to which he confessed to in his final illness?
b: His confession is valid. The rights of the creditor take preference over that of the heirs.

f: What is the status of the confession if he confesses to owing one of the heirs?
b: The confession is void unless the other heirs accept it.

f: He confessed on his deathbed to owing a stranger. He then added, "He is my son." What is the effect of the two confessions?
b: The confession of lineage will be accepted and the son's lineage establishes as his. The confession of debt is void.

f: A man confessed on his deathbed to owing a woman. He then marries her.
b: The confession is valid. The marriage does not nullify it.

f: A man divorced his wife thrice on his deathbed. He then confesses to owing her an amount and dies. What does she take from the estate?
b: She takes the lesser of either the debt or the inheritance share.

f: A man confesses that a slave is his son. What is the ruling?
b: If the slave does not have a known lineage then his lineage will be established as per the confession.

f: A man confessed that a slave is his son. The lineage is thus established and the man dies. Will the slave receive a share with the other heirs?
b: Yes.

f: Can a man confess that a person is his father/mother/wife/son/Mawla? [freed-slave or the freed slave's master]
b: Yes.

f: Can a woman confess that a person is her father/mother/husband/Mawla? [freed-slave or the freed slave's master]
b: Yes.

f: What is the ruling of her confessing to a child?
b: If the husband does not confirm it then her confession will not be accepted. If he does confirm, or a capable woman testifies that she witness the birth, then the lineage will be established to her husband.

f: If someone confesses to a lineage other than parents and children, e.g. he says, "This is my brother/paternal uncle." will it be accepted?
b:
It will not be accepted in terms of lineage.151 As for inheritance, if the confessor has an heir, whether close or far, then that heir is more entitled than the one confessed about.152 If he does not have an heir, then the other party will inherit it.153 

151 Because it claims lineage to a third party.
152 Since the lineage is not established, his claim cannot violate the rights of the heir.
153 Since he may do with his wealth as he wishes when there is no heir.

f: A man whose father died confessed to having a brother. Will the lineage be established?
b: No, but the one confessed about will share wtih the confessor in the inheritance.

f: What is Ijarah?
b: It is an agreement to receive some benefit in exchange for compensation.

f: Are there conditions for its [i.e. Ijarah] validity?
b: Yes, the benefit and the fee must be known.

f: What compensation can one use to hire?
b: That which can be measured. Whatever can be used as payment in a sale can be used as a fee in hiring.

f: The payment can be measured in numbers or weight. How is the benefit measured?
b:
Benefit is sometimes measured in time e.g. renting a house to stay in for a month or a year; or hiring land to farm for a year or two. The contract will thus be valid for a certain agreed period.

It is sometimes measured in specifiek work e.g. hiring a man to dye a cloth or stitch it; or hiring an animal to carry a specified weight to a specified destination; or to ride it for a specified distance.
It is sometimes defined through specification and indication e.g. hiring a man to move food to a specified place.

f: What is the ruling of hiring animals and houses?
b: Houses may be rented for living and animals may be hired for trade and manufacture.

f: Can the Mustajir [Hirer] do with it as he pleases?
b: He may do what he pleases except activities like iron-smithy, beaching and milling which would require the Muajjir's [lessor] permission.

f: Can land be rented for farming?
b: Yes, on condition that the contract states what will be planted or that the lessee may plant what he wishes. He contract will include the right of watering and right of using the paths even if the contract does not state this explicitly.

f: Can an open land be rented to build something on it, or plant a tree in it?
b: Yes.

f: The land was rented for building or planting and the contract period has expired. How will the land be returned to the owner?
b: The tree/building must be removed and the empty land returned to the owner. The land owner also has the option to offer him the price of free of the land and buy it from him or he may leave it as it is, each owning his possession.

f: A man rented a property and the landlord stipulated that a specific person whom he names may only stay in it. Can the man let someone else live there?
b: Yes, because the land will not change with the change in inhabitant.

f: What is the ruling on renting a shop, whereby the landlord says, "If you use it for selling perfume then it is a Dirham a month and if as a ironsmith then for 2 Dirham a month."?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the terms are valid and he will pay according to the usage. According to the other two Imams the contract is Fasid.

f: A man rents a house at a Dirham per every month.
b: The contract is valid for the first month, and Fasid in the rest unless the total months have been stipulated. If he is still living there the next month for even a moment, then the landlord may not evict him until the end of the month; and like that every month in which he stays there at the beginning for even a day or a moment.

f: A man rents a house for 10 Dirham for the year and does not mention the division of the rent on a monthly basis. Is this valid?
b: Yes, there is no problem with that.

f: A man rented a house. He received control of it but never stayed there, what is the ruling?
b: He owes the rent, because he was in a position to receive benefit of the house.

f: A man rents a house and someone usurps it from him. What is the status of the rent?
b: If the usurpation was before he inhabited it, the rent is forfeited. If it was usurped after he inhabited it, he is liable to pay the rent for the time he stayed there and the balance is forfeit.

f: A man rents a house and then discovers a defect which makes living in it difficult. What can he do?
b: He may rescind.

f: If the house is ruined; or the water of the area is cut off; or does not reach the water wheels, what is the ruling?
b: The contract is automatically rescinded without any party rescinding it.

f: What is the ruling of joint hiring?
b: It is not allowed according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and is allowed according to the other two Imams.

f: A man rented clothing and left the terms general. Can he let someone else wear it?
b: In that scenario, yes. If however he said that a specific person would wear it and he dressed someone else in it then he is liable for any damages.

f: Can one hire wet-nurses to breastfeed the children?
b: Yes, she may be hired for a specified fee; such as her food and clothing according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. It will also be her duty to prepare food for the child, since according to custom that is part of the services of the nurse.

f: A man hired a wet-nurse and insisted that her husband not have sex with her. What is the status of this prohibition?
b: The prohibition is not permissible. However, if she falls pregnant then the child's family is entitled to cancel her contract if they fear her milk will harm the baby.

f: A nurse was hired to breastfeed a baby for a set period. She instead fed him sheep's milk. Is she entitled to her fee?
b: No, she did not fulfil her duty.

f: Is hiring animals for riding or carrying loads permissible?
b: Yes.

f: A man hired a camel to carry his provisions during a journey. As he travels he eats from that and the provisions decrease. Can he replenish the supplies for the camel to carry?
b: Yes, he may add back the amount by which the provisions decreased.

f: A man hired an animal to ride and someone else mounted it. Is that allowed?
b: If the terms of riding were general he can let anyone ride it. If the rider was specified and the hirer let someone else ride then he is liable for any injury the animal may suffer. The same rule applies for any change in the usage.

f: A man hired an animal to carry a named type and weight of an item, e.g. 5 Qafiz of wheat. Can he load 5 Qafiz of something else besides wheat on it?
b: He can load whatever is of the same or lesser burden than wheat e.g. barley and sesame. He may not lead that which is a great burden than wheat, e.g. salt, iron and lead. Similarly if he hired it to carry a certain weight of cotton he may not load it with iron, even if it be the same weight mentioned.

f: He hired the animal to carry a certain weight of wheat and loaded it with more than that. The animal was injured. What is his liability?
b: If the animal was capable of carrying that weight, then he is liable for the excess of the weight. If the animal was not able to carry it, then he is responsible for the entire damage.

f: He hired an animal to ride and put someone at the back with him. The animal was injured, what is the liability?
b: He is responsible for half the price of the animal [in addition to the fee] if the animal could bear the load. If not then he owes the full price.

f: If he reins in the animal or hit it and thereby injured it, what is his liability?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he owes the full price of the injury. According to the other two Imams there is no liability if he acted in a recognised way.

f: A man hired a camel to carry a load and two people to Makkah.
b: This is permissible. He may load what is commonly considered to be a load, but if a camel-rider testifies to what is an appropriate load it would be better.

f: What is the ruling of hiring a stallion to breed with a mare?
b: Not permissible.

f: Can fees be charged for the public baths and for cupping?
b: Yes.

f: Can fees be paid for music and professional mourning?
b: They cannot be hired, nor can any fee be paid for any sin.

f: What is the ruling of hiring someone for Azan and Iqamah or teach Quran or Hajj?
b:
None of these are allowed according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى.154

154 In previous era provision was made from the public treasury for the teachers of the Quran etc. As this is no longer the case, payment can be made lest the memorising of the Quran disappears. This same applies to teachers, Muazzins and Imams of Salah.
The latter 'Ulama have given Fatwa according to al-Imam ash-Shafi'i's permission due to the force of circumstances and the need of the Ummah. The recipients should not make this an enriching scheme, but should be content with a little.
Ibn 'Abidin said, "Hiring someone to read Quran and to convey the reward to the dead is incorrect. None of the Imams have given permission for it. The 'Uluma have said that the one who reads for the sake of money, receives no reward. What then is he gifting to the dead? It is pious deeds which benefit the dead. [Rasail ibn 'Abidini p175]

f: Have the Fuqaha made any distinction in the work and entitlement of fee regarding the labourer?
b: Yes, there are two categories - Ajir Mushtarik [joint] and Akir Khass [special].

f: What is a Ajir Mushtarik or public worker?
b: He works for whoever hires him for a task, such as a dyers and bleachers. The goods he receives is a trust. He is not liable if it is destroyed without negligence. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. According to the other two Imams he is liable.

f: What happens if the goods were destroyed due to him [i.e. Ajir Mushtarik or public worker], such as a porter dropping the load; the rope tying the goods snaps; or the ship sinks?
b: He is liable for these damages but not for any humans who mught have drowned from the ship or fell from the mount. Similarly a phlebotomist (one who removes blood) is not liable if he did not exceed the usual place. If there is excess then he is liable.

f: What is a Ajir Khass [special worker]?
b: A man who is hired to work for someone for a specified time, such as a man hired to work for a man for a month as his servant or shepherd.

f: What is his [i.e. a Ajir Khass, special worker] liability for something which perishes in his hands?
b: There is no liability for something which perishes in his hands or through his work unless there was negligence.

f: A man hired a slave to serve him. Can he travel with him?
b: He may not, unless that was stipulated in the contract. The reason is because service during a journey is more difficulty.

f: What are the details of time of entitlement?
b: The general worker is not entitled to his fee until he completes the work. The special worker is entitled to his fee by handing himself over in the period of hire, even if the employer does not use his labour.

f: Can you explain further? [i.e. the details of entitlement] There are many kinds of work with many differences between them.
b:
The fee does not become payable with the mere making of the agreement. The labourer is entitled in one of three ways - either the condition of early payment is made, or the hirer pays early, or the conditions of the agreement were fulfilled. Here are some examples:
A landlord can daily demant rent for a house, unless the contract stipulates a time of entitlement.
A camel-driver can ask for his fee at every stopping station from his passengers.
A man hires a baker to bake bread at his house at a Dirham per Qafiz. THe baker is not entitled to the fee until the bread is taken out from the oven.
A man hires someone to make bricks. According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he is not entitled to his fee until the brick is formed. According to the other two, he is not entitled until the bricks are piled up and dry.

f: A man was hired to cook for a wedding-feast. He cooked the food. When is he entitled to his fee?
b:
He is entitled when he dishes out to the guests because that is normally included in the cook's work according to custom.

NOTE: Every craftsman, whose work has an effect on a good, may retain that good until his fee is settled. The labourer whose work does not have an effect on the product may not retain the goods e.g. porters and sailors.

f: If the hirer stipulated that the manufacturer produce the goods himself, may he use others in the manufacture?
b: No.

f: If no condition was set that he do it himself [i.e. that the manufacturer produce the goods himself], and the matter was left open?
b: He may then use others for the work.

f: A man says to a tailor, "If you stitch this cloth into a Persian robe then it's a Dirham and if in a Roman robe then it's two Dirham." What is the ruling?
b: This is permissible. He will be entitled to whatever of the two he does.

f: If he says, "If you complete the robe today, then one Dirham, if you complete it tomorrow, then a half a Dirham."
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he will pay one Dirham whether today or tomorrow. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the contract is valid and he will be paid according to what was stipulated and agreed upon by both parties.

f: A man gave a cloth to a tailor. After completion the owner says, "It told you to make a robe and you made a shirt." The tailor says, "I did as you told me to." Or he gave it to a dyer. After completion the owner says, "I told you to dye it red and you dyed it yellow." The dyer says, "I did as you told me to." Whose word will be accepted?
b: The owner's word will be accepted under oath. The tailor/dyer will be responsible for opposing their instructions. The owner can either claim the price of the cloth before any work was done on it and not pay the fee; or he can take it and pay the fee according to the work done, but not exceeding the initial agreed upon fee.

f: If the owner claims that the craftsman worked for free and the craftsman claims he worked for a fee, how will it be resolved?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the owner's word will be accepted under oath. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى if the owner had a relationship of paying a fee to the craftsman he will pay a fee, otherwise not. Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى added that if the craftsman commonly practised the craft for a fee, then his word will be accepted under oath.

f: Does the contract remain in effect if one of the two parties die?
b: If he contacted it for himself, the hire is immediately terminated with his death. If he acted on behalf of someone else, such as an agent for his principle, a guardian for a child, a parent for his son, then it is not terminated.

f: Is the contract terminated by a valid excuse?
b: Yes, for example a man rents a shop in the market to trade in and he loses his wealth; or a man rents out a house or a shop and becomes so bankrupt that he cannot pay his debts except by selling the house or the shop, in which case the judge will cancel the contract and sell the house/shop to pay the debt.

f: A man hires a mount for a journey and then cannot go on the journey. Is that a valid excuse for termination of the contract?
b: Yes.

f: A man hires mounts to travellers. He agreed to take a man on a journey and then was unable to. Is this an excuse?
b: No, he should send the animal with a hireling if he cannot go himself.

f: Does the hiring become Fasid through any conditions?
b: Yes, conditions which are not necessary for the fulfilment of the agreement make the contract Fasid just as in the case of sales with such conditions.

f: If the contract is Fasid and the hireling stil does his labour, what must the hirer pay him?
b: He must pay him the market value of such labour, not what they had stipulated.

f: Are conditions of Khiyar allowed in hiring?
b: Yes, just as they are in sale of goods.

f: What is Shuf'ah linguistcally and in Shari'ah?
b: The word is derived from Shaf' meaning "to join" [because the property is joined to the Shafi' [pre-emptor]. In the terminology of the Fuqaha it is the right to take possession of a house and land to prevent the harm of a neighbour e.g. if a man sells his house or land and tells his neighbour or partner about this sale the partner/neighbour has a right to object to the sale. He can take that was sold at the price at which it was sold. The one who has this right, is called a Shafi' [pre-emptor].

f: When does pre-emption become Wajib?
b: It is activated for a partner in the thing sold; then for a partner who has a right in the thing sold such as right to water or right of passage; then for the neighbour. The partner with a right to water/passage and the neighbour do not have rights with a partner in the thing sold [Mabi']. Only when the partner forfeits his right of pre-emption does the partner with a right in the Mabi' receive his right of pre-emption. If he also renounces his right then only does the neighbour receive his right.

f: When is Shuf'ah activated? When is it established? When does possession pass?
b: The sale activates the right. It is established by testimony/ Possession passes by taking it when the buyer gives it up or when the judge rules accordingly.

f: Explain the testimony. [i.e. when Shufa'h is activated]
b: When the Shafi' learns of the sale, he must immediately testify to two men in the same gathering in which he is, that he is claiming his right. This testimony is called Talabul Muwathabah or immediate demand. He will then go and inform the seller (if the mabi' is still in his possession) or the buyer (if he has taken possession) or at the property in question. Once he has done that his right is established. This is called Talabat Taqrir [demand of establishment].

f: If the Shafi' has done all this [i.e. see answer to question 1066] but delays lodging his claim by the judge, does he forfeit the claim?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى his claim does not drop if he has made Talabul Muwathabah and Talabut Taqrir. According to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is forfeited if he leaves it for a month.

f: Is the pre-emption in public baths and in mills?
b: The right is in all property even if it cannot be divided. Thus in this general rule baths, mills, wells and small houses are all included.

f: What is the ruling on just a building or a tree? [i.e. regarding pre-emption]
b: There is no pre-emption if it is sold without the land.

f: Is there pre-emption in goods and ships?
b: No.

f: Is there a difference between Muslims and Zimmi? [i.e. regarding pre-emption]
b: No, both have equal entitlement in this.

f: Is there pre-emption if someone came to own the property by way of gift, for example?
b: The principle is that the right arises when someone takes the property for monetary compensation, be it an open sale or a "gift" on condition of compensation. If he does receive the property in a genuine gift with no compensation for it, then there is no pre-emption. Similarly there is no pre-emption in the following scenarios: a man gave the house as dowry; a woman paid her husband the house as Khul'ah; a man gives the house as rent for another house; he gave the house to make Sulh (reconcilation) in a murder dispute; or he gave it to free a slave; or made Sulh on it by denial or silence. As for Sulh by admission, there is Shuf'ah for such a Sulh is deemed a sale.

f: How does the Shafi' claim his right after the two Talabs?
b: He will present the defendant i.e. the buyer to the judge. If the defendant admits to the plaintif's claim, it will be ruled against him i.e. the judge will order the defendant to surrender the housse or property to the plaintiff and take the price from him. If the buyer denies the plaintiff's right, the judge will impose upon the plaintiff that he present his evidence. If he cannot produce evidence, the buyer will be made to take an oath. He will swear by Allaah that he does not know that the plaintiff is the owner of the property/house by way of pre-emption. If he refuses to take an oath or if the plaintiff obtains proof, then the judge will ask, "Did you buy it or not?" If he denies having bought it, the judge will ask the plaintiff to produce evidence that he did. If he cannot, then the buyer will be made to swear, "By Allaah, I did not buy it/ By Allaah this plaintiff is not entitled to pre-emption on this house as per the reason he claims."

f: Must the plaintiff bring the price to the courtroom when he presents his claim?
b: He need not bring it before the judge's decision. If the judge rules in his favour then he must bring the price.

f: A Shafi' bought a house by way of pre-emption. He then sees a defect or had not seen the house. Can he return it because of the defect or right of sight?
b: Yes.

f: Can the Shafi' take the seller to court? [i.e. if a Shafi' bought a house by way of pre-emption and then sees a defect or had not seen the house]
b: If the house is still in the hands of the seller, he may take him to the judge. The judge will not hear the evidence until the buyer is presented. The judge will then cancel the sale with the buyer's testimony. The Shuf'ah is returned to the seller and the responsibility rests on him.

f: The Shafi' did not make witnesses when he learnt of the sale. What is the ruling?
b: If he did not make anyone witness to his claim when he learnt of the sale and he was able to do so, then his right is void. Similarly if he did make witnesses at the gathering, but failed to testify by one of the two parties or the land, then his right is void.

f: He agreed to give up his return in return for a payment. What is the ruling?
b: His right is void and it is Wajib for him to return the money.

f: The Shafi' or the buyer dies. Is the right forfeited?
b: The right is void with the death of the Shafi', but not with the death of the buyer.

f: The Shafi' sold the property through which he has a right on the claimed property. What is the ruling?
b: If he sold it before the ruling was given, then his right is forfeited.

f: A man sells a house and appoints the Shafi' as his agent to sell the house. The agent conducts the sale. Does he still have right of pre-emption?
b: No.

f: And if the Shafi' was the agent for the buyer?
b: He retains his right. It is not forfeited by buying it for another party.

f: A man wants to buy a house but fears making a loss in the deal. A man guarantees him that it is a good deal from the seller. That man was also the Shafi' does his right still exist?
b: He does not have the right any more, because the deal was concluded because of him.

f: A man sold the house with right of withdrawal. Can the Shafi' claim his right?
b: No, because the ownership is still with the seller in this case.

f: A man sold his house with the right of withdrawal. He then forfeits the right. Can the Shafi' now claim his right?
b: Yes.

f: A man bought the house with the right of withdrawal. Can the Shafi' claim his right?
b: Yes, because in this scenario the ownership has passed from the seller.

f: If the house is bought in a Fasid transaction, how is the right of pre-emption affected?
b: There is no right of pre-emption in a Fasid transaction. The two parties however should rescind their sale. Upon the cancellation the right can be claimed.

f: A Zimmi bought a house with pigs/wine. The Shafi' is a Muslim or Zimmi. How will the Shafi' pay?
b: The Zimmi will pay with an equivalent wine/the price of the pig. The Muslim will pay the price of the wine/pig.

f: Whose word will be accepted when the Shafi' and buyer dispute the price?
b: The buyer's word will be accepted under oath.

f: What will the judge rule if both present evidence? [i.e. when the Shafi' and buyer dispute the price]
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he will rule according to the evidence of the Shafi'. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he will rule according to the buyer's evidence.

f: The buyer and the seller disagree on the price. The buyer claimed a higher price than the seller. Which price will the Shafi' pay?
b: If the seller has taken the price then the buyer's word will be taken. If he has not, the seller's word will be taken.

f: After the sale, the seller reduced the price or the buyer offered more. Both parties were pleased with this. Which price must the Shafi' pay?
b: If the seller reduced part of the price, then the Shafi' pays the reduced price. If he reduced the entire price, then it is not reduced for the Shafi' and is deemed a separate transaction. If the buyer offered more, then the Shafi' is not liable for the extra amount.

f: A man bought a house on credit. The Shafi' claimed the house and the court ruled in his favour. Can he be forced to pay immediately?
b: He can take the house and pay immediately; or he can wait until the expiry of the period and then pay and take the house. He cannot be forced to pay immediately.

f: A man buys a house with a measured or weighed good(s). What must the Shafi' pay?
b: He must pay the same measured or weighed good(s).

f: A man buys a house with trade goods. What must the Shafi' pay?
b: The price of the goods.

f: A man buys a house with another property. What must the Shafi' pay?
b: Each house will be valued at the price of the other house.

f: A house was sold and the Shafi' told that it was sold for 1000 so he renounces his right. He then learns that it was sold for less than that or for wheat/barley worth 1000 or more. Does he still have the right of pre-emption?
b: His renouncing is ignored and he retains the right, because the information was deceptive.

f: The Shafi' heard that the house was sold for 1000 Dirham and renounces his right. He then learnt that it was sold in Dinars worth 1000 Dirham. Is this deception?
b: This is not deception. His right is renounced.

f: The Shafi' heard that a certain person was buying the house and hence renounced his right of pre-emption. He then learnt that someone else actually bought it. Does he have a right again?
b: He still has his right of pre-emption.

f: A man appoints an agent to buy a house for him. He bought a house. The Shafi' then demands the house. With who will his dispute be?
b: The defendant will be the agent. If the agent haded the house to the principle, the principle will be the defendant.

f: A man bought a land and built a building/planted a tree on it. The judge then ruled the land for the Shafi'. What happens to the tree/building?
b: He can pay for the building/tree a price free of the land or he can demand that the buyer remove them.

f: The Shafi' acquired a land through his right and then planted a tree/built a building there. It then transpires that someone else has a right to the land. What can he do?
b: He can claim the price he paid, but not the price of the building/tree.

f: Through no human intervention, the house got destroyed or burnt or the trees of the garden dried up. The court then rules in the Shafi's favour. How much must he pay?
b: He must pay the full amount or he may rescind his offer.

f: What must the Shafi' pay if the buyer destroyed the house and left the land vacant?
b: He may pay the proportionate price or he may renounce his right of pre-emption. He may not claim the ruins.

f: A man bought a land with fruit-laden trees. The Shafi' received his right. Does he take the land with or without the trees?
b:
He takes it with the fruit.155 

155 If the fruit was stipulated in the sale, because the fruit is not included without stipulation.

f: A man buys a land with trees and fruit and cuts off the fruit. What will the Shafi' pay?
b: The Shafi' will take what is left at the proportionate price.

f: A man bought a house and the Shafi' renounced his right. The buyer then returns the house on right of withdrawal/right of sight/defect. Is the Shafi's right reinstated?
b: If it was returned by a court order then there is no reinstating. If it was without the court or a mutually agreed rescinding, then his right is reinstated.

f: The partners in a property divided the property amongst themselves. Can the nieghbour claim Shuf'ah?
b: There is no pre-emption for the neighbour in this scenario. Division is not a sale. It is a distinction of rights.

f: A house is sold and there are several people with a right of pre-emption to it. How will the house be divided amongst them?
b: It will be divided according to their number, not according to what they own.

f: Explain my means of an example. [i.e. A house is sold and there are several people with a right of pre-emption and it will be divided according to their number]
b: Three men share a house whereby one has half, the second a third and the third a sixth. The owner of the half sells his half. The other two have claims to equal amount in it, the one with a sixth will not get less then the other.

f: The sale agreement was made upon a price, but then the buyer gave a cloth instead. What will the Shafi' pay?
b: He will pay the first price. The agreement was not upon the cloth. The cloth was acquired in a second transaction.

f: Are there situations where the right is forfeited?
b: If the entire property except for the strip adjoining the neighbour's property is sold then the neighbour has no right even if the strip is only an arm-span wide, because his land does not join the sold land. This is a device people use to avoid pre-emption.

f: Are there other devices like this? [i.e. where the right is forfeited]
b: Yes, someone buys a share of the house and then buys the rest. The neighbour does not have a right in the second share [because the one with an existing share has a prior right.]

f: Are these devices not Makruh? [see questions 1112 and 1113]
b: According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is not Makruh. According to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is Makruh.

f: What is Sharikah?
b: It is the mixing of different wealth in such a way that a distinction is no longer drawn between them. This can either be by way of a mixing from two parties, or by way of receiving a joint property without them having mixed it e.g. inheritance or a joint gift for two parties, or when one of the parties merges his wealth in the wealth of the other without any action in a way that there is no longer a distinction between their wealth.

f: What kind of partnerships are there?
b: There are two kinds: Shirkatul Amlak [wealth] and Shirkatul 'Uqud [contracts].

f: What is Shirkatul Amlak?
b: This occurs for example, when two people receive a single commodity jointly as inheritance or they buy the same thing jointly.

f: What is the ruling of this partnership?
b: The partners may not transact in their share without the permission of the other. Each one with regard to the other's share is like a stranger.

f: What is a partnership of contracts?
b:
There are four types, each which has its own regulations:
Shirkah Mufawadah [Negotiated]
Shirkah 'Inan [Restricted]
Shirkatus Sanai' [Craftsmen]
Shirkatul Wujuh [Reputation]

f: What is the definition and regulations of Shirkatul Mufawadah?
b: It is the partnership of two men whereby they will be equal in their wealth, transacting, debts and it encompasses Wakalah and Kafalah (agency and debts). Whatever any of them buy will belong to the partnership, except their food and clothing for the family. Whatever debt one of them incurs by way of something which can be jointly owned, and then the other partner is responsible for its payment as well. This kind of partnership is permissible between adult, intelligent Muslims. It is not allowed between a freeman and a slave; or between a child and an adult; or between a Muslim and a Kafir.

f: Two men conclude a Shirkatul Mufawadah agreement. One of them inherits such wealth which can be jointly owned or he receives such a gift. The wealth has reached him. Does the partnership stay as it was?
b: The partnership is nullified and becomes a Shirkatul 'Inan.

f: Are there any other conditions for Shirkatul Mufawadah?
b: Yes, it cannot be concluded except with Dirhams, Dinars and currency. It is not permissible in anything else, unless it is something which people treat as an exchange medium such as gold nuggets.

f: They have neither Dirham nor Dinar. They only have goods. How can they become partners?
b: The one sellf half of his goods for half the goods of the other. The partnership will be concluded.

f: What is Shirkatul 'Inan?
b: It is the partnership of two people in a specific or general kind of trade.

f: What are the regulations of this partnership? [i.e. Shirkatul 'Inan]
b: It is permissible and entails Wakalah [agency], but not Kafalah [responsibility for another's debts.] It means that if one of them bought something for the partnership, the price can only be demanded from him, not from the other. That partner will then go to the other partner to claim his share of the payment. The debts of one is not the responsibility of the other.

f: Can there be a difference in their contributions or must it be the same? [i.e. in Shirkatul 'Inan]
b: The capital can be the same or different, just as the profit shares can differ even if the capital shares are the same.

f: Can this partnership [i.e. Shirkatul 'Inan] be established where each one gives only part of his wealth, not all?
b: Yes.

f: With what is this partnership [i.e. Shirkatul 'Inan] established?
b: As explained in Mufawadah, it is established with Dirhams, Dinars or whatever people may be using as mediums of exchange, such as gold nuggets.

f: Can it [i.e. Shirkatul 'Inan] be established with one contributing Dirhams and the other Dinars?
b: Yes.

f: If both of their capital or the capital of one of them perishes before they jointly buy anything, then what happens to the partnership? [i.e. in Shirkatul 'Inan]
b: It is void.

f: If one of them bought something and the capital of the other perishes before the purchase, what is the ruling between them? [i.e. in Shirkatul 'Inan]
b: The purchase is between them as per their agreement, and the one who bought the goods will seek claim from the partner his share of the price.

f: Two men wish to engage in an 'Inan partnership without mixing their wealth. Is the partnership valid?
b: Yes, it is not a condition of 'Inan that their wealth mix.

f: An 'Inan partnership was concluded. One of the partners stipulated for himself a specified amount of Dirhams. What is the ruling?
b: The partnership is not valid in this case. It is possible that the total profit will not be more than the amount he demands.

f: What options do the partners in a Mufawadah and 'Inan agreement have?
b: Each may invest the capital, may give it to a Mudarabah, may appoint an agent to transact in it, may give and accept collateral, may hire a third party over it, and may sell for cash or credit. Each one acts on the basis of a trust.

f: What is a form of a Sana'i [craftsmen] partnership?
b: Two tailors or dyers for example form a partnership to accept work and share the earnings.

f: What obligates each of them? [i.e. in a Sana'i partnership]
b: Whatever work one of them accepts and becomes compulsory upon him, obligates the other partner as well.

f: If only one did a job, is he entitled to the entire fee? [i.e. in Shirkatul Sana'i]
b: No, it must be shared between them.

f: What is Shirkatul Wujuh?
b: Two men form a partnership that they will buy goods based on their reputations and sell them, whereas they have no capital. This kind of partnership is permissible. Each will be a Wakil [agent] for the other in what he buys.

f: Can they share the profits in different proportions to the goods? [i.e. in Shirkatul Wujuh]
b: No, if they stipulated that the goods will be equal amongst them then the profit must be the same, if they stipulated that the goods will be in thirds, then the profits will be the same.

f: What is the ruling on partnerships in wood-gathering, grass-gathering and hunting?
b: This is not permissible. Whatever wood, grass or prey he gets is his alone. They cannot be partners in capital or profits.

f: A man owns a mule and another owns a water-bag. They made a partnership to fetch water and sell it to the people on condition that both will share in the profits. Is this partnership valid?
b: No.

f: If one of them uses both to fetch the water, how will the earnings be shared?
b: The entire earnings is for the one who fetched the water. If the worker was the owner of the mule he owes the other the fee for the bag. If he was the owner of the bag he owes the fee of the mule.

f: Two men concluded a Fasid partnership. How are the earnings shared?
b: According to their capital contribution ratio. Any stipulation to the contrary is void.

f: Can one partner pay the Zakah of the other?
b: He may not, except with the other's permission.

f: If he gave permission [to pay the Zakah of the other] and then both paid the Zakah of one of them, is the partner liable?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he must reimburse him, whether he knew that he paid the Zakah or not. The other two Imams say that he is not liable if he did not know that the Zakah was already paid.

f: Is the partnership ever nullified without the partners cancelling it?
b: It is nullified when one of the partners dies or abandons Islaam and flees to the lands of the Kuffar.

f: What is Mudarabah linguistically and in Shari'ah?
b: The word is derived from Darb in the meaning of travelling (i.e. to travel the earth). In Shari'ah it is a contract whereby profits are given to one partner in lieu of capital and to the other in lieu of labour. The capital must be wealth which we discussed before.

f: What are the conditions for the validity of the Mudarabah?
b:
There are two conditions:
That the wealth be so handed over to the Mudarib so that the capital contributors have no control over it.
That the profits be divided on a ratio basis and no party will claim a specific amount of Dirhams.

f: If the contract is correct, what may the worker do?
b: If the Mudarabah is general, and not confined to any specific time, place or goods, then the Mudarib may buy, sell, travel, invest and appoint agents as he wishes. If the capital contributor has specified certain places/goods then the worker may not exceed that.

f: What is the ruling of the capital contributor stipulating a time period for the contract?
b: It is permissible. The Mudarib may not exceed the time period, as when the specified date is reached the Mudarabah is terminated.

f: Can the Mudarib hand the capital over to another person [second Mudarib]?
b: Only if the capital contributor permits him or said, "Work as you see fit."

f: If the first Mudarib handed over the capital to a second party without permission, is he liable for the amount?
b:
He is not liable by the mere contract with the second Mudarib or by the second's transacting with the money. He is liable once the second Mudarib earns a profit to pay the money to the capital contributor.156 

156 Once the capital-contributor makes the first Mudarib responsible, the contract with the second is validated and the profits will be divided as what the two agreed upon.

f: The capital-contributor gave the money to the Mudarin on condition that they would share the profits 50-50. He also permitted him to give the money to another party as Mudarabah. What is the ruling?
b: It is permissible.

f: How will the profit be divided amongst these three parties?
b:
If the capital-contributor had stipulated half the profit for himself and said, "What Allaah gives will be half-half between us," and the Mudarib gave the money to a second Mudarib on the terms of the second receiving two-thirds of profits, then the capital contributor will receive his half, the first Mudarib one-sixth and the second Mudarib one-third.

If the capital-contributor said, "Whatever Allaah gives you is between us half-half," and the Mudarib said to the second Mudarib, "Two-thirds of the profit you earn is mine and a third is for you," then the third is for the second Mudarib and the two-thirds will be divided between the first Mudarib and the capital contributor.

f: If the capital-contributor stipulates half of the profits for himself, "Half of what Allaah gives is for me," and the Mudarib offers the second Mudarib half of the total profits, how will the profits be shared?
b: The Capital-contributor will receive half, the second Mudarib will get his half and there is nothing for the first Mudarib.

f: How will the profits be shared in the above scenario if the second Mudarib was promised two-thirds of the total?
b: They will share it in half as above. In addition, the first Mudarib is liable to pay the second Mudarib from his own money to the value of one-sixth of the profits so that his receipts reach the two-thirds agreed upon.

f: The Mudarib sees the father/son of the capital-contributor being sold as slaves in the market. Can he buy them?
b: He may not buy them or anyone else who is automatically freed in the owner's possession.

f: If he did buy them, what is the ruling?
b: It will be ruled that he bought them for himself and that will not be from the money of the partnership.

f: Can the Mudarib buy a slave who will be freed in his possession?
b: If there is profit in the money, then he may not buy them. If he does buy them, then he must pay the partnership back. If there was no profit in the money then he may buy them.

f: The value of the slaves increased after he bought them and a profit emerged. Can he free them from his share and owe the capital-contributor the balance?
b: He will free his share in the slaves. He does not owe the partner anything. The freed slave will earn and repay the partner.

f: Can the Mudarib sell on credit?
b: He may sell on cash or credit, because these are necessities of trade.

f: If the Mudarib bought a male/female slave from the capital of the partnership can he let them get married?
b: No.

f: What is the status of the transactions of the Mudarib if the capital-contributor has removed him?
b: If he did not know and he bought/sold, the transaction is valid. If he knew and he has goods of the partnership in his possession then he may still sell them despire being removed. He may not however buy anything with the obtained price. If at the time of his removal the partnership's wealth is Dirham and Dinar then he may not transact with them.

f: The Mudarib and the capital-contributor have separated and there remain outstanding debts of the partnership. From whom will the debts be claimed?
b: If there is a profit amount in the wealth of the partnership then the judge will force the Mudarib to pay. If there is no debt then the judge will order him, "Make the capital-contributor the agent for paying the debt."

f: What happens if the capital or the profit is destroyed?
b: Any losses will be deducted from the profits not the capital, even if the loss is greater than the profits. The Mudarib will not be liable for the loss.

f: After the profits were shared, the entire assets or part of it was destroyed. What do they do?
b: They will return the profits until the capital-contributor restores the capital. If there is an excess then they may share it. If there is a shortfall in the capital the Mudarib is not liable.

f: They divide the profits and terminate the partnership. They establish a second partnership and all or some of the assets are lost. Do they return the profits of the first business?
b: No, there is no relation between the profit of the first business and the second business.

f: How does the partnership become void?
b: When either party dies; or if the capital contributor abandons Islaam and goes to the land of the Kuffar - may Allaah save us. It is also terminated if the capital-contributor stipulated a time limit which expires.

f: What is Wakalah?
b: In Shari'ah it is to appoint someone else in one's place to perform a known transaction. Whatever transaction one is allowed to do oneself, one may appoint a Wakil [agent] to perform.

f: Why does the Shari'ah recognise Wakalah?
b: Because people may need someone else to perform a transaction due to some weakness or absence.

f: What kinds of transactions do agents perform?
b:
There are two broad categories:
That which is attributed to himself e.g. buying, selling and hiring. The rights and duties of these contracts are attributed to the agent, not the Muwakkil [principle]. The agent hands over sold goods, takes the price, takes goods bought, takes the price and handles the dispute in defective goods bought.
That which is attributed to the principle e.g. Marriage, Khul', and Sulh or settlement of blood money. The rights and duties of these contracts are attributed to the principle, not the agent. The bride will thus not claim her dowry from the agent, nor is the agent responsible for bringing her to her groom.

f: Can one appoint an agent [lawyer] to handle and settle disputes in rights; thus an agent of the plaintiff presents a correct claim and/or the agent of the defendant presents a correct response and whatever relates to the dispute.
b: Yes.

f: Can an agent be appointed in a dispute without the consent of the party?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى an agent can only be appointed with the consent of the disputant unless he is away by the distance of three days' journey or more; or is ill. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is permissible without the consent of the disputant.

f: What is the ruling on appointing an agent to fulfil one's right?
b: It is permissible, except in the case of Hudud [penal punishment] and Qisas [death penalty]. The principle must attend the hearing himself in these two cases.

f: Can an agent be appointed in currency and Salam transactions?
b: Yes. Thus if the agent separates from the other party before taking possession, then the contract is void. The principle leaving will not be considered.

f: Are there any conditions for the validity of the agency?
b: Yes, the principle must be a person permitted to transact and who is obligated under laws. The agent must be a person who understands buying and selling and can fulfil its aim.

f: An adult free man appoints an agent like him; or a slave permitted to trade appoints one like him. What is the status of these agencies?
b: Both are permissible.

f: A man appoints as agent a child of the age of incapacitation who nevertheless understands buying and selling; or he appoints an incapacitated slave.
b: The agencies are valid, but rights and duties are attributed to the principle, not the agents.

f: The appointed agent sold something on behalf of the principle. The principle demands the price from the buyer. What must the buyer do?
b: The buyer may refuse to pay the principle. If he does pay, the agent may not demand the payment from him a second time.

f: Are there any necessary conditions when appointing an agent for buying?
b: Yes, the type, description and maximum price must be stipulated unless general permission is specifically given e.g. "Buy for me what you deem right."

f: An agent bought and took possession of some goods. He finds a defect in them. Can he return them to the seller?
b: He may return them as long as they are in his possession. Once he gives it to the principle, he may not return it unless the principle permits him.

f: An agent bought goods for the principle with his own money. How is he reimbursed?
b: He can claim the amount from the principle and may retain the goods until he is paid.

f: The agent is holding some goods which perish before he can hand them over to the principle. What is the ruling?
b: The goods are deemed to have perished from the principle. The principle is not absolved of paying the price.

f: If the goods perished while the agent was retaining them in order to receive his payment of the goods, what is the ruling?
b:
According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it has perished with the liability of collateral. According to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى157 it has perished with the liability of trade goods. 

157 And according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى

f: A man appoints two agents. Do they have to work jointly in the work of the agency?
b: Yes, each of them may not transact in what they were appointed without the other. Exception are if they were appointed to as representatives in a [court] dispute or to divorce his wife without compensation; or similarly to set free his slave; or return a wadi'ah (commodity under one's safe keeping) he was holding; or to settle his debt.

f: Can an agent appoint an agent to do what he was appointed to do?
b: He may not, unless the principle permits him or said, "Work as you see fit."

f: What is the ruling if the agent appointed a second agent without permission and the second agent concluded a transaction?
b: If he concluded the transaction in the presence of the original agent, it is correct in regards the rights of the original agent. It is also correct if he was not present but validated it. If not, then it is not valid.

f: Are there restrictions upon the transactions of the agent?
b: Yes, according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the agent of buying and selling may not transact with his father, grandfather, son, grandson, wife, slave and Mukatab [contracted slave]. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he may transact with them at market rates but not with his slave or Mukatab.

f: Can an agent of selling, sell cheap and expansive prices?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he may. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he may not sell at such a loss people would not accept in a like item (not sell lower than current related price).

f: What are the restrictions on the price the buying agent pays?
b: He may pay at market price up to maximum which people would tolerate in buying such an item. He may not pay such an excessive price which people would not tolerate.

f: What is an excessive price which people would not tolerate?
b: A price no trader would ever value the goods at.

f: An agent was appointed to sell his principle's slave and he sold half the slave. Is that permissible?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is permissible. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is not permissible unless he sells the other half as well.

f: What is the ruling of an agent appointed to buy a slave and he bought half?
b: This is a suspended sale. If he buys the second half the principle is liable.

f: The agent was appointed to buy 10 Ritl of meat for 1 Dirham. He bought 20 for 1 Dirham of such meat which is normally sold at 10 Ritl for a Dirham. What is the principle liable for?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he is liable for 10 Ritl at a half Dirham. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he is liable for 20 at 1 Dirham.

f: An agent was appointed to buy a specific item. Can he buy it for himself?
b: No, if he does buy it for himself the purchase is for the principle.

f: An agent was appointed to buy any slave. He bought a slave. To whom does the slave belong?
b: He belongs to the agent unless he said, "I intended it for the principle/I bought it with the principle's money."

f: Can an agent appointed for dispute retain whatever he obtained from the dispute?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى, Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the agent for dispute is an agent for taking possession as well. According to Imaam Zufar رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he may not take possession.

f: Can an agent be authorised to collect a debt dispute [in court]?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى an agent for debt is an agent for dispute as well. According to the other two Imams he is not.

f: Can an agent for dispute confess against his own principle?
b: He may confess to the judge against his own principle. According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he may not confess to anyone besides the judge, unless he withdraws from the dispute. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he may confess to someone besides the judge as well.

f: A man claims that he is an agent for collection of debt on behalf of an absent principle. Will the debtor be ordered to pay him?
b: If the debtor believes him, he will be ordered to do so.

f: The judge ordered the debtor to pay the debt to the one who claimed to be the agent because the debtor believed him. The absent creditor then comes. What will the judge order the agent and the debtor?
b: If the creditor verifies the agent then there is no need for further enquiries. If he does not, then the debtor must pay the creditor again and claim the amount he paid the "agent" from the "agent", if he still has the amount with him.

f: A man said to someone who was keeping a wadi'ah (commodity under one's safe keeping), "I am appointed to collect the wadi'ah. If the person believed him will he be ordered to hand it to the "agent"?
b: No.

f: An agent sold goods. He gave a pledge of responsibility for the buyer's debt. Is this valid?
b: No, his pledge is void [lest the claimant and the defendant become the same person].

f: If the principle terminates the agency and the agent still transacts after that, what is the ruling?
b: If he knew that he has been removed then his transacting is not permissible. If he did not receive the notice of termination then he is still the agent and his transactions are valid and binding upon the principle, until he learns of the termination.

f: Under what circumstances does the agency dissolve?
b:
They are as folllows:
Death of the principle.
His complete insanity (lasting for 1 year or more. Zalai).
His leaving for the lands of the Kuffar as an apostate.158 
Separation of partners where one of the partners was agent for the other.
When the Mukatab is unable to fulfil his contract of buying his freedom then the agent he appointed is no longer his agent.
Renewal of incapacitation upon a slave who was permitted to trade and appointed agent. In these scenarios the agency is terminated whether the agent knows or not.
Death of the agent.
His (the agents) complete insanity.
His leaving for the lands of the Kuffar as an apostate, unless he returns as a Muslim before the decision is passed, then it is as if he never did that and the agent reamins upon his agency.
The principle personally transacts what he appointed the agent to do.
158 If he returns as a Muslim before the decision is passed, then it is as if he never did that and the agent reamins upon his agency.

f: What is Kafalah?
b: To undertake a liability for another's liability when it is claimed.

f: Are there different categories of Kafalah?
b: Yes, Kafalah of a person [bail] and Kafalah of wealth.

f: How is guarantee of a person effected?
b: By someone saying, "I am guarantee for his person/neck/soul/body/half/third." Or if he says, "I am responsible for him/he is upon me/he is to me/I am his surety/I stand in his stead."

f: What is the obligation of the Kafil [guarantor] in a guarantee of person?
b: He must present the Makful bihi [the one for whom presentation of a person has been guaranteed]. If a condition of the guarantee was presentation at a specific time, then he is obliged to do so when the Makful lahu [one given the guarantee to] demands him at that time. If he does not present him, then the judge will detain him until he does present him.

f: How does the guarantor become absolved of the guarantee of person?
b: He is absolved when he presents the Makful bihi in a place where the Makful lahu can conduct his case against him. He is also absolved upon the death of the Makful bihi.

f: Is he absolved if he guaranteed to present him to the judge but presents him at the market or a desert?
b: He is absolved if he presents him in the market, but not in the desert.

f: The guarantor guaranteed that he would be liable for the liability of the Makful bihi if he does not fulfil it. He does not present him at the time which was stipulated. What is the ruling?
b: He is obliged to pay the liability and is not absolved of presenting the Makful bihi.

f: What is the ruling of Kafalah of a person in Hudud and Qisas?
b:
It is not allowed according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى.159

159 According to al-Jawharah it means that according to him he will not be forced to undertake the guarantee. According to the other two he will be forced in the case of slander... All of them agree that there is no guarantee in the actual punishment as that cannot be fulfilled by a third party.

f: What is Guarantee of Wealth?
b:
It is a guarantee of the guarantor that he will settle amount owing to the one entitled. This is allowed in Shari'ah, whether the Makful bihi [the amount] is known or not, as long as the debt is valid.160

160 E.g. price of a sale, fines for violations, compensation for destroying property, loans etc.

f: What are the words of enacting the guarantee?
b: "I guarantee 1000 Dirham on his behalf/I stand guarantee for what he owes you or what is due to you from this sale."

f: When the guarantee is given, can the Makful lahu claim from the Makful 'anhu (the one for whose debt the guarantee is given)?
b: The Makful lahu can claim from the Makful 'anhu or the guarantor.

f: Can conditions be set for the guarantee?
b: Yes, for example he says, "I am responsible for what you sold him/I am responsible for what he usurped from you."

f: The guarantor said, "I guarantee whatever he owes you." The guarantor and Makful 'anhu then disagree on the amount. What will be decided between them?
b: He will pay whatever according to the evidence produced, e.g. it is proven that the Makful 'anhu owes 1000 Dirham, then he is liable for 1000 Dirham.

f: If there is no evidence? [i.e. when the guarantor and Makful 'anhu disagreeo n the amount guaranteed]
b: The guarantor's word will be taken under oath for whatever amount he admits to.

f: If the Makful 'anhu admits to an amount greater than that which the guarantor said, will he be believed?
b: He will be believed in terms of himself, but not in terms of the guarantor.

f: Can a guarantee be given without the assent of the Makful 'anhu?
b: Yes. If the guarantee is given with his assent, the guarantor will claim the amount from him. If he did not give his assent, the guarantor cannot claim from him.

f: When can the guarantor claim the money from the Makful 'anhu?
b: He cannot claim until he has paid the debt of the Makful 'anhu.

f: A man gave guarantee for 'Amr. The creditor then pursues the guarantor. What can he do?
b: He should pursue the Makful 'anhu until he is left alone.

f: The creditor absolves the debtor; or the debtor settles the debt. Are there any responsibilities of the guarantee left on the guarantor?
b: No, he is entirely absolved.

f: What is the ruling if the creditor absolves the guarantor?
b: The guarantor is absolved, but not the Makful 'anhu.

f: Can the guarantee be given without a condition?
b: No.

f: Can the guarantor guarantee for the buyer and the seller?
b: If he guarantees to pay the amount of the buyer it is valid. If he guarantees to produce the items sold on behalf of the seller then it is not valid.

f: A man hires a mount to load goods. Another man guarantees himm transport of the load. Is the guarantee valid?
b: If he guarantees the specific mount, then it is not valid. If it is not specific then it is valid.

f: Must the Makful lahu accept the guarantee for it to be valid?
b: The guarantee is not valid unless the Makful lahu accepts it in the Majlis of the transaction. An exception is if a sick person instructs his heir to stand as his guarantee. In that case the guarantee is valid even though the creditor was not present.

f: Two men sought credit and stood guarantee for each other. They paid his debt. Can he seek imbursement from the second debtor?
b: No, unless he paid an amount above what he personally owed.

f: Two men stood guarantee for a third man having a debt of 1000. Both would also be guarantors for each other. One of them paid part of the amount or the entire amount. Can he ask for reimbursement from his partner?
b: Yes, he can ask for half the amount he paid, be it a little or much.

f: Can a guarantee be given for Kitabah [contract whereby a slave pays a specified amount for his freedom]?
b: No, neither a free man nor a slave may stand guarantee in this case because it is not a true debt.

f: A man dies without any assets and has unpaid debts. Can someone guarantee to the creditors for his debts?
b: Not according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى but the other two Imams permit it.

f: What is Hawalah?
b: It is the transfer of debt from one person's responsibility to another's responsibility. It is permissible with debts, not goods and rights.

f: Is the consent of both parties a condition? [i.e. for Hawalah]
b: The consent of the Muhil (who is the debtor); Muhtal (creditor); and Muhtal 'alayhi (the one who undertakes to pay the debt) are all required.

f: Can the creditor then claim from the original debtor? [i.e. after Hawalah]
b: Once the debt is transferred the debtor is absolved. The creditor may not claim from him unless his rights become Tawa.

f: What is the meaning of Tawa? How does it arise?
b: Tawa is destruction. It arises according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى in one of two ways - if the Muhtal 'alayhi denies the transfer under oath and the creditor does not have proof; or if the Muhtal 'alayhi dies bankrupt. The other two Imams add a third form of Tawa which is if the court rulers that the Muhtal 'alayhi is bankrupt while still alive.

f: If the Muhtail 'alayhi demands from the Muhil an amount equal to the amount transferred and the Muhil says, "I do not owe you anything. I transferred a debt you owed me", will his word be accepted?
b: No, he will owe the amount equal to the debt.

f: If the debtor claims the transferred amount from the Muhtal, "I transferred to you an amount for you to take on my behalf." The Muhtal denies this, "You transferred a debt you owed me." How will a decision be made?
b: The Muhil's word will be accepted under oath.

f: What is the ruling of safatij (Bills of Exchange) according to Fuqaha?
b: Makruh.

f: What does the word and term mean? [i.e. safatij]
b:
It is the plural of Suftajah meaning a paper. It is a loan given so that the lender is safe in his travel.161 

161 E.g. a man gives a trader x amount of Dirham on condition that the trader's agent at another city will pay him that amount. If done without conditions then there is no harm. If safety of the road is stipulated thne it is Makruh because that is deriving benefit from a loan [al-Jawharah].

f: What is Sulh?
b: A dispute erupts between two parties concerning rights. They agree to accept part of what is disputed and renounce the remaining claim. This is called Sulh. "Sulh is best."

f: How many types of Sulh are there?
b:
There are three categories:
Sulh with confession.
Sulh with silence.
Sulh with denial.
All three are permissible in Shari'ah.

f: What is the meaning of Sulh with confession?
b: The defendant confesses to a right against him. The plaintiff then compromises upon something.

f: What is the meaning of Sulh with silence?
b: The defendant neither admits to nor denies the claim, but is pleased to compromise to free himself of the dispute.

f: What is Sulh with denial?
b: The defendant denies that there is a claim against him but is willing to compromise to end the dispute.

f: What is the ruling of Sulh with confession?
b: If it is compromise of money on money then it is treated as a sale. If it is on a benefit it is treated as a hire.

f: What is the ruling of Sulh with denial or silence?
b: These are implemented with oaths. With regards to the defendant it is deemed the termination of the dispute. With regards to the plaintiff it is deemed an exchange.

f: What is the ruling of pre-emption if they compromised with a house or about a house?
b: Pre-emption arises if they compromised with giving a house. It does not arise if they compromised about a disputed house.

f: If the compromise is with confession, can the defendant demand his share which he is entitled to under the compromise?
b: Yes, he can claim what was offered in exchange.

f: The defendant gave up in a compromise of silence or denial. It is discovered that a third party is entitled to the disputed item. What does the plaintiff do?
b: He will return what the defendant gave him and continue the case with the new claimant. If his claim is established in part of the disputed item, then he will have returned that proportion from whatever the defendant had given in exchange. He will continue the remainder of the dispute with the new claimaint.

f: A man claimed a right in a house but did not specify the right. The defendant gave him a substitute as a compromise on the claim. Someone then claims part of the house. Will the original plaintiff return what the defendant gave him?
b:
No, he need not return anything.162

162 Because it is possible that his claim is in the part of the house which the new claimaint does not dispute. The matter is different if he is entitled to the entire house. [al-Jawharah]

f: Can compromise be made on a claim to wealth, a benefit, deliberate violations, mistakes [jinayatul 'amad wal khata] and penal punishments?
b: It is allowed in all that except penal punishment.

f: A man claims that a woman is his wife. She denies it and pays him as a compromise to leave her. Is this valid?
b: The compromise is valid and is deemed a Khul' [payment from the woman for divorce].

f: A woman claims a man is her husband. He denies it and pays her as a compromise to leave him alone. Is this valid?
b: The compromise is not valid.

f: A man claims another as his slave. The defendant pays him as a compromise. What is the ruling?
b: It is permissible. It will be deemed from the claimaint's side as freeing a slave in exchange for money.

f: The man appointed an agent to compromise on his behalf. Is it the agent's duty to present the amount compromised on?
b: No, unless it was stipulated. The money is the liability of the principle.

f: If a man compromised on behalf of another without his authorisation, who is liable for payment?
b:
There are four scenarios:
He compromised with money and took liability for the money.
