b: The marriage is valid and she is entitled to a year's service from him.

f: The guardian takes liability for the woman's dowry. Is this valid?
b: Yes, she may demand her dowry from the guardian or her husband.

f: The marriage was Fasid and the court separated the couple. What is the status of giving the dowry?
b: She is not entitled to any Mahr if they were separated before sex; even if there was complete seclusion. If they did have sex then he will pay her Mahr Mithl but not more than the Mahr they had agreed upon.

f: What is the status of her 'iddah after such a separation [i.e. the marriage was Fasid and the court separated the couple], and attribution of lineage if she gives birth to his child?
b: She will fulfil the iddah of divorce and the child will be attributed to him.

f: The Majbub [amputated penis] was alone with the woman and then divorced her. What Mahr does he owe her?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he must pay the full Mahr because she had surrendered herself to him. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى she is entitled to half Mahr.

f: What is Khalwah Sahihah?
b: That there be no obstacle to sex, e.g. none of them is sick, fasting Ramadan, being in Ihram for Hajj or 'Umrah, nor is the woman in menses.

f: Why have you stipulated that the fast be that of Ramadan?
b: If a man is alone with his wife whilst either one is keeping a voluntary fast then it is deemed Khalwah Sahihah.

f: You have mentioned Mahrul Mithl over and over again in your answers. What is it?
b: Dowry similar to the dowries of her sisters, paternal aunts and daughters of paternal uncles if these women are similar to her in age, beauty, wealth, intelligence, piety, city and time. Her mother and maternal aunts are not considered if they are not of the same tribe as her.

f: What is Mut'ah?
b:
It is three pieces of clothing of her worth13, Dir' [loose outer garment with sleeves], Khimar [head covering] and Milhafah [wrap].

13 This would seem to mean that the clothing be according to her status, whereas it is according to his, because Allaah says, "Upon the wealthy his ability and upon the straitened his ability."

f: For which divorcees is Mut'ah Wajib and for which is it only recommended?
b: It is Wajib for a woman who's husband divorced her without having sex with her and they did not stipulate what her Mahr is. It is Mustahab for every other divorcee except for woman whose husband divorced her without having sex with her but did mention a specific Mahr.

f: A man married a woman who has a defect. Can he cancel the marriage?
b: He may not. He may however divorce her at any time.

f: If a woman marries a man and she then discovers him to be mad or a leper, can she claim Faskh (termination)?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى she may not. According to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى she may.

f: A woman discovered her husband to be impotent. She requested the judge to terminate the marriage. What should he rule?
b: The judge will summon the husband and give him a year's respite to undergo treatment. If he has intercourse with her in that period she has no further option. Otherwise the judge will separate them if she so requests [after the year of unsuccesful treatment].

f: What is the status of the separation if the judge separates them? [i.e. a woman discovered her husband to be impotent and requested the judge to terminate the marriage]
b: It is deemed Talaq Bain.

f: What is the status of the Mahr in this case? [i.e. a woman discovered her husband to be imported and requested the judge to terminate the marriage]
b: Full Mahr if he was secluded with her.

f: What will the judge rule if she finds her husband Majbub [amputated penish] and demands that he separate them?
b: He will immediately separate them because there is no hope that the husband will be able to have sex for the rest of his life.

f: And if she finds him castrated and demands a separation?
b: He will be given a year's respite just as for an impotent man.

f: A woman embraces Islaam. Her husband is a Kafir. Will she be separated from him because of her Islaam?
b: She will not be separated solely because of her Islaam. The judge will offer Islaam to him. If he accepts then she remains his wife. If he refuses, then the judge will separate them. According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the separation will be a Talaq Bain. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is a separation without divorce.

f: A man married to a fire-worshipper embraces Islaam. Will she be separated from him?
b: She will not be separated solely because of her Islaam. The judge will offer Islaam to her. If she accepts then she remains his wife. If she refuses, then the judge will separate them. This separation will not be a divorce because it arose from her refusal.

f: What is the status of the Mahr in that case? [i.e. a man married to a fire-worshipper embraces Islaam, she refuses to accept Islaam and the judge separates them]
b: If they had had intercourse then she is entitled to full Mahr, otherwise none.

f: The husband of a Christian/Jew embraces Islaam. Will they be separated?
b: There is no need for separation. If a Muslim man can initiate a marriage with a Christian/Jewish woman then he can also maintain his marriage with her.

f: A woman in the land of the Kuffar is married to a Kafir. She embraces Islaam. Are they separated?
b: She will not be separated from him until she completes three menstrual periods. When she finishes the third, then they are separated.

f: A husband/wife left the hands of the Kuffar for the lands of the Muslims, as a Muslim. When are they separated?
b: His/her leaving for the lands of Islaam separates them in itself. There is no additional factor required.

f: A woman embraces Islaam in the lands of the Kuffar and makes Hijrah to the lands of Islaam. Her husband is there. Must she spent an 'iddah?
b: No, she may marry immediately according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى if she is not pregnant. If she is pregnant then she may not marry until she gives birth.

f: One of the spouses apostatises from Islaam - Allaah protect us. When does the separation occur?
b: They are separated immediately without divorce.

f: What is the status of the Mahr in that case? [i.e. when one of the spouses apostatises from Islaam]
b: If it is the husband who is the apostate and they had sex, then he owes her the full Mahr. If they did not, then he owes her half Mahr. If the wife is the apostate then she is still entitled to full Mahr if she apostatised after sex; if before then she is not entitled to Mahr.

f: A couple abandonded Islaam together - Allaah save us - and returned to Islaam together. What is the ruling on separating them?
b: They will not be separated and they remain married to each other.

f: If a man or a woman leaves Islaam whom can they marry?
b: A male apostate may not marry a female Muslim, or an aspostate, or a woman who was always a Kafir. Similarly a female apostate may not marry a Muslim, or an apostate, or a man who was always Kafir.

f: A Kafir husband or wife living in the lands of the Kuffar was captured and brought to the lands of Islaam. When will they be separated?
b: They are separated immediately upon entry into the lands of Islaam. If they are captured together then their marriage is not terminated.

f: Of his two parents, only a child's father is Muslim. Whose religion does the child follow?
b: He will follow his father. If any parent accepts Islaam and the child is small, then the child will be Muslim due to whichever parent's Islaam.

f: A child's one parent is a Christian/Jew and the other a Fire-worshipper. Which religion will he follow?
b:
He will follow the Christian/Jew on the principle of following the parent with the better religion.

NOTE: 
If a Kafir marries without witnesses or marries during the 'iddah period and then the couple embraces Islaam then their marriage is valid if those practices are valid in their religion. They are not required to perform a second marriage.
If a Fire-worshipper marries his mother or daughter and then they embrace Islaam, they will be separated.

f: What is the maximum allowed period for breastfeeding after which it is not allowed?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is 30 months. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is 2 years.

f: Which laws apply due to breastfeeding?
b:
If breastfeeding has taken place within the period as per the difference in opinion, be it a little or much, then marriage is Haram between two Radi', and between a Radi' and its Murdi'ah [wet-nurse], her ancestors, descendants and her relatives of the same line. Allaah has mentioned the prohibition of marrying one's wet-nurse and sisters through breastfeeding. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Allaah has forbidden through breastfeeding what He has forbidden through lineage."15

15 Narrated by Muslim.

f: What is the ruling if a woman breastfeeds a boy or a girl after the prescribed period?
b: Breastfeeding after the prescribed period is not permissible. If done it does not bring about the prohibition of marriage.

f: Explain the regulations of prohibition through breastfeeding in detail.
b:
Understand and remember the following Masail:
If a boy and a girl drank from the same woma, they may not marry each other.16 
A woman may not marry any descendant of the woman who breastfed her.
When a woman breastfeeds a girl, that girl is prohibited unto her husband, her ancestors and her descendants. The husband through whom the nurse got her milk will be the girl's father through breastfeeding. The jurists term this mas-alah Labanul Fahl [stallion's milk].
A boy may not marry the sister of the husband of the woman who breastfed him, because she is his paternal aunt through breastfeeding.
A man may not marry the wife of a boy who is his son through breastfeeding just as he cannot marry the wife of his biological son.
A man may marry the sister of his Radi' brother just as in certain scenarios one may marry one's brother's sister e.g. someone has a half-brother with a common father. He can marry the half-brother's half-sister who shares the same mother with the half-brother.
16 Nor may they marry her, her children, or grandchildren etc.

f: You mentioned that whoever is Haram to marry through lineage is Haram to marry through breastfeeding, with certain exceptions. What are these exceptions?
b:
The following are exceptions:
One may marry the mother of one's sister through breastfeeding, but not the mother of one's biological sister.
One may marry the sister of one's son through breastfeeding, but not through lineage.
One may marry the mother of the paternal uncle and paternal aunt through breastfeeding, but not through lineage.

f: The milk of two women was mixed and fed to a boy or girl. To which of the two will the prohibition of marriage be attributed?
b: According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it will apply to whichever one's milk was the most. According to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it applies to both.

f: If a virgin gets milk in her breast and she feeds a baby, what is the ruling?
b: The prohibition of marriage applies.

f: If a man should produce milk and he breastfeeds a boy or a girl, do the laws of marital prohibition apply?
b: No.

f: A boy and a girl drank from the same sheep. Do the laws of marital prohibition apply?
b: No.

f: A man married an adult woman and a girl of breastfeeding age. The adult breast-fed the girl. What is the ruling of this breastfeeding?
b: Both wives become Haram for him.

f: What is the status of the Mahr in the above case? [i.e. a man married an adult woman and a girl of breastfeeding age, and the adult breast-fed the girl]
b: If he did not have sex with the adult then she is not entitled to Mahr and the girl receives half Mahr. He will claim the half Mahr from the adult if she had intended mischief. If she did not then she is not liable.

f: How is Rada' proven?
b: Through the Arsh (testification) of two men, or a man and two women. The Arsh of only women is not accepted.

f: A woman's milk was mixed with water. A boy or a girl drank the mixture. Do the laws of marital prohibition apply?
b: If it is motly milk they apply. If mostly water then they do not.

f: And if the woman's milk was mixed with food? [i.e. do the laws of marital prohibiton apply then?]
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى they do not apply even if the milk is dominant. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى they apply if the milk is dominant.

f: And if the woman's milk was mixed with medicine? [i.e. then do the laws of marital prohibition apply?]
b: The laws apply if the milk is dominant.

f: A woman died. Her milk was extracted and put in a vessel and fed to a baby. What is the ruling?
b: The laws of prohibition apply.

f: A woman's milk was mixed with a sheep's milk. What is the ruling if a baby drinks it?
b: If the woman's milk is dominant then the laws of prohibition apply. They do not if the sheep's milk dominates.

f: If a man marries a woman and they are not compatible, what should they do?
b: Allaah commands, "Treat them [wives] with goodness." If it becomes impossible and he wishes to separate then Allaah has made a way out, which is for the man to divorce his wife. He will take her out of his marriage. The man is called Mutallig and the woman is called Taliq.

f: Are there different kinds of divorce?
b:
There are three kinds:
Ahsanut Talaq [the best divorce]
Talaqus Sunnah
Talaqul Bid'ah

The first means to divorce her once whilst she is in a state of purity in which the husband didn ot have sex with her. He then does not have sex with her until her 'iddah finishes.
The second is to divorce thrice the wife whom he had sex with. The three pronouncements will be in three purity periods without sex. The jurists also call this at-Talaq al-Hasan. The Sunnah in this divorce is from two aspects - time and number. The Sunnah of amount applies equally to a woman who had sex with her husband [Madkhul biha] and a woman who did not [Ghayr Madkhul biha]. The Sunnah of time is specific to the woman whom the husband had sex with. He should divorce her in a purity period in which they did not have intercourse.
The third kind is to pronounce three divorces in a single sentence; or to divorce her thrice during a single purity period. If a man pronounces a single divorce on his Madhkhul biha the divorce falls against her. However, she will not separate from him until the completion of her 'iddah. If he wishes to take her back he may do so during her 'iddah. If she is Ghayr Madkhul biha she will separate from him upon one divorce. In this case the husband may not take her back whether during or after the 'iddah. InshaAllaah we shall elaborate on this.

f: What is the status of Talaqul Bid'ah?
b: The divorce occurs even though the husband is a sinner for transgressing the Sunnah.

f: Does divorce occur when given during menses?
b: It occurs but is forbidden. He is obligated to take her back.17 If he then wishes he may divorce her in a purity period in which they did not have sex. This is if she is Madkhul biha. If she is Ghayr Madkhul biha he may divorce her during menses.

f: What is the status of divorcing her when she is pregnant?
b: It is permissible even if it is following intercourse.

f: A man intends divorcing a Madhkul biha thrice according to the Sunnah. How is it done?
b: He will pronounce the first divorce in a purity period in which they did not have sex. He will then pronounce the second divorce in the next purity period and the third in the third period.

f: He intends divorcing her according to the Sunnah, but she does not undergo menses. What should he do?
b: He should divorce her once in the month. When the month passes he should divorce her in the second month, and like that the third divorce in the third month.

f: Can one divorce one's wife who does not undergo menses whereby there is no gap of time between the divorce and having had sex with her?
b: It is permissible.

f: A man wishes to divorce his pregnant wife according to the Sunnah method. How will he separate the three divorces?
b: He will separate them in months according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. According to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he cannot divorce her according to Sunnah and must divorce her once only.

f: Does the divorce of every husband take effect?
b: The divorce of a husband falls if he is a sane adult. The divorce of a child, madman and sleeping man does not take effect.

f: What is the status of the divorce of a drunken man and one forced to give divorce?
b:
The divorce occurs.18

18 Referring to a drunk who still has his senses. However, if he has completely lost his senses then the divorce does not occur e.g. he cannot tell the difference between a man and a woman; the earth and the sky. Drink refers to consuming any intoxicant including honey wine, and drugs like opium etc.

f: What is the status of the divorce of a mute?
b: His divorce by indication occurs.

f: A slave marries a woman with the permission of his owner. Who can divorce her?
b: The slave has the right to divorce her. If the owner divorces her it does not fall.

f: How do Talaq Raj'i and Bain occur?
b:
There are two kinds of divorce with regards wording. Sarih [explicit] and Kinayah [indirect]. 

Explicit is when the husband says, "You are divorced/you are now a divorcee/I divorce you." This divorce is Raj'i and only one occurs even if he intended more than one. No attention is paid to whether he actually intended the divorce or not. Amongst those words deemed explicit are, "You are Talaq/You are a divorcee in divorce/You are a divorcee given a divorce". If he had no intention with these words then it is one Raj'i divorce. If he intented two, then it is still one. However, if he intended three then it is three. If he says, "You are divorced. You are divorced," then it is two Raj'i. Allaah says, "If divorce has been given twice retain her in kindness or leave her in an amicable manner."

The second kind, Kinayah, is when the words are not explicit. The divorce will not occur except with an intention or an indication of the condition.

f: Please explain further? [i.e. see answer to question 1572: how do Talaq Raj'i and Bain occur with regards to Kinayah, indirect divorce]
b:
There are two kinds of indirect words of which three words result in one Raj'i divorce when if he intended two or three. They are, "Go into 'Iddah/Clear your womb/You are now single." The rest of the indirect words result in one Bainah if he intends one or two, but if he intends three it will be three. These words include, "You are Bain, Battah and Batlah [separated, broken and cut off - because she is cut off from returning]/You have free rein/Go join your family/You are free/You are alone/I have gifted you back to your family/You choose/I have separated from you and you are free/Veil yourself from me/Cover yourself from me/Be a stranger to me/Seek another husband."

If he did not intend divorce then the divorce does not occur with these words. If however it was within the discussion of divorce then legally20 it is a divorce, but not between him and Allaah until he intends it as such.

If it was not in a dicussion of divorce but both were angry or arguing, then the divorce occurs with any indirect word which was not an insult or abuse. If the insult or abise was intended as divorce then the divorce occurs.

In Summary:
Raj'i divorce occurs with explicit words.

Related to this is when he says, "Go into 'Iddah/Clean your womb/You are single." Bain divorce is with indirect words when he intends thereby divorce or the condition indicates thus. The Talaq Raj'i becomes Bain if the 'iddah passes and he did not take her back in it. 

Mughallazh Divorce occurs with three pronouncements, whether it be in three purity periods, three months, in a single sentence, in three sentences in the same purity period, or he intended three divorces with indirect words - except that which are exception from it.

20 Meaning amongst humans. If he protests at a court that he did not mean it then his protest will not be accepted. This applies to words which can be given to the woman as reply to her request for divorce and not a refusal e.g. "Go into 'Iddah/The matter is in your hands, you choose."

f: What kind of divorce falls if the husband pronounced it with an additional description?
b:
It will be Bain. The woman will be separated from him and he may not take her back, e.g. "You are divorced Bain/You are divorced in the worst way/in the most shameful divorce/the divorce of the devil/Talaqul Bid'ah/You are divorced like a mountain/ a houseful of divorce."21

21 If he says to her you are divorced in the most intense way/a thousand times/a houseful of divorce", then that is one Bainah unless he intends three."

f: Does the divorce occur if he attributes the divorce to her body parts?
b:
The divorce occurs if he attributes it to her in her entirety or that which indicates her entirety, e.g. "You are divorced/your neck is divorced/your soul is divorced/your body is divorced/your physique is divorced/your vagina is divorced/your face is divorced."

Divorce does not occur with, "Your hand is divorced/your leg is divorced", because hands and legs do not symbolise the entirety.

f: If he instead mentions a fraction of her, e.g. half/a third of you is divorced?
b: The divorce occurs.

f: If he fractions the divorce instead e.g. "You are given a third/half/two-thirds divorce."
b: One complete divorce occurs because divorce cannot be fractioned.

f: A man says, "If I marry you then you are divorced." What is the status of this addition?
b: The divorce occurs immediately after the marriage.

f: If he adds a condition like, "If you enter the house you are divorced", what is the ruling?
b: The divorce will occur upon fulfilment of the condition whatever the condition is - except if he says, "You are divorced", and immediately adds, "if Allaah wills". Divorce does not occur with that condition.

f: If he says to a stranger, "If you enter the house you are divorced." He then marries her and she enters the house. Does the divorce fall?
b: No divorce takes place. It can only occur after the fulfilment of the condition if he "owned" the woman in terms of marriage rights at the time of making the oath or it is attributed to ownership.

f: What words are used in these conditions, what is the status of using them? [i.e. words used for words for a condition]
b: The words include in, iza, iza ma, mata and mata man [if/when]. If the divorce is attributed to one of these words, then the divorce takes place after the condition occurs. He is then released from the oath.

f: What do you mean by release from the oath?
b: The effect of the condition takes place only once. When it occurs the divorce occurs. Thereafter if the condition arises again there will not be another divorce from that oath and condition.

f: Are there such words whereby the divorce will recur if the condition recurs?
b:
Yes it recurs with kullama [every time/whenever].

A man says, "Every time you enter the house you are divorced." She enters the house and is divorced. She enters again and is divorced again. She enters again and is divorced again. Thereafter there is no divorce from this because there is no more than three divorce in Shari'ah.

f: She was divorced thrice because of the recurring condition as above. [i.e. a man says "Every time you enter the house you are divorced" and she entered the house thrice]. She marries another man and then remarries the first husband. If she again enters the house is she divorced?
b: No.

f: If he says, "Every woman I marry I divorce" will each woman be divorced whom he marries for the rest of his life?
b: Yes, his words encompass every woman.

f: He says to her, "If you enter the house you are divorced." He then divorces her with a normal pronouncement. After her 'Iddah he remarries her. She then enters the house. Does the divorce fall?
b: Yes, the loss of marriage does not fulfil the oath. It is fulfilled when the condition is found and she is divorced.

f: He attached a condition to divorce but divorced her normally before the condition could occur. She was separated from him and then the condition occurred. He then remarries her. Is she divorced?
b: No, the condition occurred outside of his ownership. He is released from the oath.

f: He made a divorce attached to a condition. The couple then dispute whether the condition is found. Whose word will be accepted?
b: His word will be accepted, unless she produces proof that the condition os found.

f: Certain matters are only known to the wife. If he made a condition of such matters then whose word is accepted, e.g. he says, "If you bleed your menstruation then you are divorced." How will the matter be resolved if they dispute the occurrence of the condition?
b: In such matters affecting the woman personally her word will be accepted.

f: What do you mean, "...affecting the woman personally"? [i.e. see the answer to question 1598 with regards to a man who said "If you bleed your menstruation then you are divorced" and then they dispute about the occurrence of the condition; in such matters affecting the woman personally her word will be accepted.]
b:
It will be clear to you from the following examples. He says to her, "If you menstruate then you and your co-wife are divorced." If she says, "I am menstruating", then she will be divorced and not the co-wife, unless the husband accepts her word.
If he says, "If you love me/are angry with me then you are divorced." She says, "I love you/I am angry with you." Her words will be proof against her even if they contradict what is in her heart. Her words will not be used against a third party however.22 

22 Such as if he said, "If you love me then you and your co-wife are divorced." If she says, "I love you" then she is divorced but not the co-wife.

f: If he says, "If you menstruate you are divorced/If you menstruate a menses period then you are divorced", what is the status of the conditions?
b:
They have two separate rulings:
When he says, "If you menstruate you are divorced", and she sees her menstrual blood, the divorce does not occur until she bleeds for three days and nights. Upon the completion of the three days and nights it will be ruled in retrospect that the divorce fell upon the bleeding. That is because bleeding for less than that is not menstruation, but is Istihadah. That is why she must wait for the minimum period of menses.

When he adds, "... a menses period ..." then she is not divorced until she enters her purity after her menses. The difference between the two lies in the additional words which stipulate a complete menstruation.

f: If he says, "You are divorced in Makkah", and she is not in Makkah, what is the ruling?
b: She is divorced immediately wherever she may be. Similarly she is divorced if he says, "You are divorced in the house", and she is not in the house. He did not make entry of Makkah or the house a condition for divorce.

f: If he says, "You are divorced if you enter Makkah", is that different from the above question?
b: Yes, here he makes entry into Makkah a condition, hence the divorce does not occur until she enters Makkah.

f: If he says, "You are divorced tomorrow", when does the divorce occur?
b: When true dawn rises.

f: If he says, "You are divorced thrice except one/thrice except two", what is the status of the exception?
b: The exception will be taken into consideration; hence two divorces occur in the first scenario and one divorce in the second scenario.

f: What is the ruling of divorce between consummation?
b: If a man pronounces divorce before consummation then the divorce occurs. If he pronounces three divorces in one sentence then all occur. If he pronounces them separately, she becomes Bain with the first pronouncement and the second and third do not fall on her. Divorce in the case of non-consummation will never be Raj'i. It will either be Bain or Mughallazh.

f: He says to her, "You are divorced one and one/ one before one/ one after it another one." How many divorces fall on her?
b: Only one falls in all these cases.

f: If he says, "You are divorced one after one/one with one/one with it one", how many fall in these cases?
b: Two divorces occur in all these cases.

f: He says, "if you enter the house you are divorced one and one." She enters the house. What is the ruling?
b:
According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى one divorce occurs. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى two occur.

NOTE: That distinction is for a woman whose husband did not consummate the marriage. If it was consummated then two apply in all cases.

f: A man says to his wife, "Choose yourself", meaning divorce or he says, "Divorce yourself." Can she divorce herself?
b: She may divorce herself from him in these two cases as long as she remains in that gathering. If she leaves the gathering or begins doing some other deed then she loses the option, unless he said, "Divorce yourself whenever you want to." She may then divorce herself in the gathering or thereafter.

f: If he told her, "Choose yourself", and she does in the gathering, what is the ruling?
b: A single Bain divorce occurs. Her divorce will not be three, even if the husband intended that. For the divorce to occur, it is necessary that either he or she mention nafs [self].

f: If he told her, "Divorce yourself", and she did so, which divorce falls?
b: One Raj'i. If the husband intented three then three occurs. If he intended two then that is not correct unless his wife is a slave.

f: If he appoints an agent and says to him, "Go divorce my wife." Is the agency confined to the gathering?
b: No, he may divorce her in the gathering and after, if he left it general and did not mention any wish. If he says, "Divorce her if you wish", then it is confined to the gathering.

f: Are there situations when the woman still inherits from the man after he divorces her?
b: If a man divorces his wife Talaq Bain during his final illness and dies before her 'Iddah is complete, she inherits from him. If he dies after the 'Iddah then she does not inherit. The ruling of Talaq Mughallazh is the same as Bain in this. The jurists call this Mas-alatul Fazz [jumping] because the husband hastens the divorce to disinherit her. She remains entitled to inheritance during the 'Iddah. The 'Iddah will be deemed the longer of the two periods, as will be discussed in the chapter on 'Iddah InshaAllaah.

f: How many divorces can a freeman and a slave give?
b: According to the Ahnaf this is determined according to the wife, not the husband. If the woman is a slave, then she can get two divorces and her 'Iddah is two menstruations, whether her husband is a slave or a freeman. A freewoman can be divorced thrice, whether her husband is free or a slave. In summary, a slave-girl's husband does not own more than two divorces. If he divorces her twice then he has used up what he got. Two regarding her is like three regarding a freewoman and the divorce is Mughallazh.

f: Can a man and woman be separated by something besides divorce?
b: If a man comes to own his wife or a share of her; or if she comes to own her husband or a share of him then they're separated.

f: Is there another way for a woman to leave the marriage besides divorce?
b:
If the couple are at ends and fear that they will not be able to adhere to Allaah's limits then there is no harm for the wife to ransom herself with money to free herself from her husband. If she says, "I cast you off [Khul] for such-and-such amount", and he accepts, a Bain divorce takes place and she is liable to pay the amount. This is called Khul'.

If the breakdown in the marriage was from his side then it is Makruh for him to take the money. If it is from her side then it is Makruh for him to take more than what he gave her. In both cases he may legally take the money and the divorce is Bain.

f: He divorced her in exchange for money and she agreed. Neither used the word Khul'. Is the divorce valid?
b: Yes, the divorce falls and she is liable to pay the money. The divorce is Bain.

f: A Muslim woman offered wine/pig for Khul'. The husband accepts. What is the ruling?
b: She will not pay anything. The separation will be Bain.

f: He divorced her for wine/pig without mention of Khul'. Does the divorce occur?
b:
Yes, the divorce occurs as Raj'i23 and the compensation is void.

23 Because in the previous mas-alah the factor was the Khul' and here it is an explicit divorce.

f: What kind of wealth kind the wife pay as Khul'?
b: Whatever is a valid Mahr can be offered as a valid Khul'.

f: She says, "Grant me Khul' in exchange for whatever is in my hand." He accepts and learns there is nothing in her hand. What does she owe?
b: She owes nothing. The divorce is Bain.

f: She says, "Grant me Khul' in exchange for whatever wealth is in my hand." He accepts and learns there is nothing in her hand. What does she owe?
b: She must return her Mahr if she took possession of it. The divorce is Bain.

f: She says, "Grant me Khul' in exchange for whatever Darahim is in my hand." He accepts and learns there is nothing in her hand. What does she owe?
b:
She owes three Darahim.24 

24 Because she used the plural term and the smallest plural [in 'Arabic] is 3.

f: She says, "Divorce me thrice in exchange for 1000." He divorces her once. What does she owe?
b: She owes a third of 1000. [Divorce is Bain].

f: She says, "Divorce me thrice upon 1000." He divorces her once. What does she owe?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى she does not owe anything and he retains the right to take her back. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى she owes a third of 1000 as above.

f: He says to her, "Divorce yourself thrice in exchange for/upon 1000." She divorced herself once. What is the ruling?
b: No divorce occurs and she owes nothing.

f: The couple entered into a Khul'. Each had rights remaining against the other, or at least one had a claim against the other. What is the status of these rights?
b:
According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the Khul' cancels all rights related to the marriage. As for rights not related to the marriage e.g. one took a loan from the other and then they had Khul', then fulfilment remains Wajib. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the Khul' does not cancel any rights except what they stipulate.

There is another scenario for forfeiting of rights called Mubara-ah or mutual absolving. According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the right of each with regards marriage is forgiven. According to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى Mubara-ah and Khul' are the same, the rights do not fall away except that which they stipulate.

f: You have mentioned that if a man gives a woman one or two Raj'i divorce he may take her back during the 'Iddah. Is the consent of the woman required for this?
b: No, he may take her back whether she is pleased or not.

f: How does he take her back? [i.e. after a man gives a woman one or two Raj'i divorce]
b: He may take her verbally back by saying, "I am taking you back/I am taking my wife back". If he has intercourse with her, kisses her, touches her with lust, or looks at her inner vagina with lust then these are counted as taking her back by action.

f: Is it Wajib for him to establish witnesses to him taking her back?
b: It is not Wajib but Mustahhab for him to establish two witnesses in order for him to take her back. If he does not then his Raj'ah is still valid.

f: He gave her a Raj'i divorce. After the 'Iddah he claims, "I took you back during the 'Iddah." What is the ruling?
b: If she confirms him then it is Raj'ah. If she denies him then her word will be accepted under oath according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى.

f: He says, "I take you back." She replies, "The 'Iddah is finished." Is the Raj'ah valid?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is not. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is valid.

f: A man marries a slave-girl and divorces her Raj'i. After the 'Iddah he says to her, "I took you back during the 'Iddah." Her owner verifies him but she denies it. Whose word will be taken?
b:
According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى her word will be taken.25

25 According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the word of the husband and owner will be taken. [al-Hidayah]

f: The bleeding of the third menstruation of the divorcee has stopped. Does this mean that she cannot be taken back?
b: If it stopped upon ten days she cannot be taken back and the 'Iddah is finished even if she did not make Ghusl yet. If it stopped before ten days then she can be taken back until she makes Ghusl, or a Waqt of Salah passes over her, or she makes Tayammum and prays Salah. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. According to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى if she makes Tayammum he cannot take her back even if she has not prayed.

f: She made Ghusl but forgot an organ or the water did not reach there. Can he take her back?
b:
If it is a complete organ or more then he can take her back. If less than a complete organ then he may not.

NOTE: It is Mustahab for the husband of the divorcee not to enter her presence until he asks her permission or lets her hear his approaching footsteps. It is Mustahab for her to adorn herself to attract him. If he then has sex with her he has not sinned because Raj'i divorce does not prohibit sex. He thus take her back through that action, as we have already mentioned.

f: If a man gives his wife a Bain divorce less than three, may he remarry her?
b: He may remarry her during and after her 'Iddah. Another man can only marry her after the 'Iddah.

f: A man divorces his freewoman wife thrice, whether according to Sunnah or Bid'ah. Can he remarry her?
b: Three divorces for a freewoman or two for a slave-girl is called Mughallazh Divorce. The husband who divorced her may not remarry her until she marries another man in a proper marriage after her 'Iddah. The second husband must have sex with her; and then divorce her or die. After this 'Iddah she may remarry the first husband.

f: What do you mean by "proper marriage"? [i.e. the husband who divorced her may not remarry her until she marries another man in a proper marriage after her 'Iddah.... see question 1637] What effect does this benefit have?
b: It means it must be a legally effective marriage, not Fasid. If he has sex with her after a Fasid marriage then the first husband still does not become permissible for her, because this marriage has no effect in Shari'ah.

f: A slave-girl was given two divorces. Her divorce is thus Mughallazh. Her owner then has sex with her by right of ownership. Does that sex make it permissible for her husband to remarry her?
b: No, the ayah of the Quraan stipulates that she marry another husband. The owner is not her husband.

f: The ayah does not mention sex with the second husband. Why have you made it a condition? [i.e. the Ayah of the Quraan stipulates that the slave-girl marry another husband. Her having sex with her owner does not count as the owner being her husband]
b:
It is established from Rasulullaah26 ﷺ.

26 Hadhrat 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا narrates: The wife of Rufa'ah al-Qurazhi came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "I was with Ruf'ah. He divorced me irrevocably and I married 'Abdurrahman bin az-Zabir. He does not have any power except like that of the fringe of a cloth." He said, "Do you want to go back to Rufa'ah?" "Yes", she said. "Not until you taste his honey and he tastes your honey." he replied. [Muslim and al-Bukhari].

f: A woman was given Mughallazh divorce. After her 'Iddah a man married his near pubescent [Murahiq] son to her. The boy has sex with her. Does this sex make her permissible for the first husband?
b: Yes, a Murahiq is like an adult in the case of making her permissible for the first husband.

f: A man marries a woman who was divorced Mughallazh in order to make her Halal for the first husband. Is the marriage valid? Can she marry the first husband after sex with the second husband?
b: Marriage specifically on condition of making her Halal for the first husband is Makruh Tahrimi. Nevertheless if all the requirements for marriage are met the marriage is valid. If he then divorces her after sex or dies after sex, then she is permissible for the first husband.

f: A man divorces a freewoman once or twice. After her 'Iddah she marries a second man. She later remarries the first husband. How many divorces can the first husband give her?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he can divorce her thrice, the second husband having restored them to him. According to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he does not restore it.

f: A man divorces his wife thrice. She marries another man and returns to the first in accordance to all requirements of Shari'ah. How many times can the first husband divorce her?
b: He can divorce her thrice according to all three Imams.

f: A man divorces his wife thrice. She says, "I completed my 'Iddah and married another man who had sex with me. He divorced me and I completed that 'Iddah." Can the first husband marry her?
b: He may if he thinks that she is most probably speaking the truth and that the time frame allows for her words to be true.

f: What is 'Iddah? Why is it called that?
b: If a man divorces his wife a Raj'i/Bain/Mughallazh divorce; or they are separated without divorce; or he dies; then she is not allowed to marry another man until she has spent a specified time. The time differs according to the woman on months or menstrual periods. This waiting period is called 'Iddah [counting] because the woman counts her months or menstruations.

f: Explain the details of the above. [i.e. the previous question's answer mentioned that a woman's period is called 'Iddah [counting] because the woman counts her months or menstruations]
b:
It is as follows:
If the divorcee is a freewoman who menstruates then the 'Iddah is three complete menstruations.
If she does not menstruate, whether due to small age or old age, then her 'Iddah is three months.
If a freewoman's husband dies and she is not pregnant, then the 'Iddah is four months and ten days.
If she is pregnant when divorced or her husband dies, then her 'Iddah is until she gives birth.

f: You mentioned a freewoman. Is there a difference in the ruling of a slave? [i.e. with regards to the 'Iddah]
b: Yes, the 'Iddah of a slave-girl who menstruates is two menstruations. If she does not menstruate, whether due to small age or old age, then her 'Iddah is one-and-a-half months. When her husband dies her 'Iddah is two months and five days. If she is pregnant then her 'Iddah is until she gives birth, whether she is divorced or whether her husband has died.

f: If a man divorces his wife while she is menstruating, does that menstrual period count as one of the three periods?
b: No, after that period three complete menstrual periods will be counted.

f: A man divorces his wife on his death-bed. He then dies during her 'Iddah. Which 'Iddah will she have to spend?
b:
According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى she will spend whichever of the two is longer.27

27 According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى if it is Bain or three then she will spend three menstruations. If it is Raj'i then it is unanimous that she will spend the Iddah of death. [al-Hidayah]

f: What is meant by whichever is longer? [i.e. with regards to a woman's 'iddah when a man divorces his wife on his death-bed and he then dies during her 'Iddah]
b: If the 'Iddah of death is longer she must spend it; if the 'Iddah of divorce is longer she must spend it.

f: How does that benefit her? [i.e. a woman must observe whatever is longer: the 'Iddah of death or the 'Iddah of divorce when her husband divorces her on his death-bed]
b: She is still entitled to inherit from him as long as she is in his 'Iddah. Thus prolonging the 'Iddah benefits her.

f: A man divorced his wife a Raj'i divorce. The owner frees her before the end of her Iddah. Which Iddah will she spend?
b:
The Iddah of a freewoman.28

28 She will not begin anew, but will continue her Iddah as a freewoman. [ash-Shami:605/2]

f: A slave-girl is freed whilst spending the Iddah of Bain or Mughallazh or death. How will she fulfil it now?
b:
She will continue the Iddah of a slave and will not extend it to the Iddah of a freewoman.29

29 The difference is that in Raj'i the marriage is not yet terminated. [see question 1653]

f: A woman no longer has menstruation. Her husband divorces her and she spends her Iddah according to months. She then sees menstrual blood. What should she do?
b: She must begin anew according to menses. What has passed of her Iddah is void.

f: A man married a woman in a Fasid marriage30 and had sex with her. The judge then separates them or the husband dies. What Iddah does she spend?
b:
She will spend three menses if she is a woman who menstruates, otherwise three months. If she is pregnant then until she gives birth.

30 There were no witnesses/the woman is married and the second husband does not know. If he did know and had sex then there is no Iddah because it was adultery. Also if a man went to the wrong woman on their wedding night and thought that the woman he is having sex with is his wife, if he claims that he thought so.

f: A man mistook a woman and had sex with her. He dies or the judge separates them. Is there an Iddah?
b: Yes, three menstruations.

f: An Ummul Walad slave-girl's owner died or freed her. Is there an Iddah?
b: Yes, three menstruations.

f: A boy's guardian married him to a woman. He dies and she is pregnant. What Iddah does she spend?
b: If she is pregnant at the time of his death then the Iddah is until she gives birth. If after his death then the Iddah is four months and ten days.

f: When does the Iddah begin?
b: The Iddah of divorce begins upon the divorce. The Iddah of death begins upon his death. The Iddah when they are forcefully separated begins upon the separation or the commitment of the man who had sex with her not to have sex with her.

f: A woman's husband gave her divorce or died. She did not know of the divorce or death until the time of the Iddah had already passed. What is the ruling?
b: Her Iddah is complete with the passage of the required time. She need not start a second Iddah upon receiving the news.

f: A woman was spending her Iddah of divorce when a man mistook her and had sex with her. Does her Iddah begin anew?
b: She will not begin anew, but she is obliged to spend a second Iddah. The two Iddah will overlap each other.

f: How do they overlap? [i.e. when a woman was spending her Iddah of divorce when a man mistook her and had sex with her and she is now obliged to spend a second Iddah; the two Iddah now overlap each other]
b:
Whatever blood she sees will be of both Iddah together. When the first Iddah finishes and the second is not complete then she will complete what remains of the second.31 

31 If he had sex with her after the menses of the first period then she must still complete two menses of the first Iddah. These two will be counted towards the second Iddah as well. When she completes the next menses then the second Iddah is complete as wel..

f: A man gave his wife a Bain divorce. He then marries her during her Iddah. He again divorces her without having sex. Does she begin the Iddah anew?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى yes. According to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى completing the first Iddah is sufficient.

f: Does he owe her Mahr? [i.e. when a man gave his wife a Bain divorce, remarried her during her Iddah, and then divorced her without having sex]
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he owes her a full Mahr. According to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he owes her a half Mahr.

f: Is there any obligation upon a woman who is divorced or whose husband died, besides Iddah?
b: An adult Muslim woman irrevocably divorced or whose husband has died must observe Ihdad during her Iddah.

f: What is Ihdad?
b: It means that she has to leave fragrance and adornment. She may not apply Hinna. She may not wear clothing dyed with fragrance such as saffron. She may not apply oil or antimony except for a valid need.

f: You stipulated an adult Muslim. [i.e. who is irrecovably divorced or whose husband has died and now must observe Ihdad during her Iddah] Is the ruling different for a girl or Kafirah?
b: Yes, there is no Ihdad on a minor girl or Kafirah.

f: What is the status of Ihdad in regard a slave-girl?
b: If the slave-girl is an adult Muslim then she must observe Ihdad as well if she was irrevocably divorced or her husband died. If her owner dies and she was his Ummul Walad, then there is no Ihdad upon her.

f: Are there any other regulations for a divorcee and a woman whose husband has died besides Ihdad?
b:
A divorcee, whether revocable or irrevocable, may not leave the house, day or night. A widow may leave in the day and part of the night but may not spend the night in another house.32

32 Because she receives no allowance from her husband unlike the divorcees. [al-Hidayah]

f: Where does the divorcee and widow spend their Iddah?
b: They will spend it in the house given to them for living at the time of the divorce or husband's death.

f: A widow's inherited share of the house of the deceased suffices her. Can she leave the house to stay with her parents or somewhere else?
b: She may not without a valid reason.

f: If her part of the house is insufficient [i.e. a widow who inherited a share of the house ] and the other heirs leave her out of their share, may she move?
b: Yes.

f: Can a man propose to a widow while she is in Iddah?
b:
He may not do it explicitly but may hint to her.33

33 In the explanation of Ibn 'Abbas رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he may for example say, "A wish to marry a woman who is like this and that."

f: A Zimmi divorced his Zimmi wife or he died. What is the ruling of her Iddah?
b: If she is not pregnant then there is no Iddah. If she is pregnant then there is Iddah.

f: A Muslim divorced his Jewish/Christian wife or he died. Does she spend Iddah?
b: Yes, she spends Iddah, whether pregnant or not. Nobody may marry her during her Iddah.

f: A woman became pregnant through Zina. She now wants to marry. Can she?
b: If she marries the marriage will be valid, but her husband may not have intercourse with her until she gives birth. However, if she marries the man who committed the Zina with her and from whose sperm the foetus is created then they may have sex after marriage.

f: How is lineage of children established to their fathers?
b: A man marries a woman. After six lunar months or more she gives birth. The child's lineage is attributed to him if he consents or if he remains silent. If the baby is born sooner than six months from the day of the marriage, then the baby is not attributed to him.

f: It is possible that the woman committed Zina and the foetus is from that act. How will its lineage be established to the husband?
b: The child will be attributed to the husband and no attention should be paid to such possibilities. Even if she really did commit Zina the lineage will still be established to the husband. Rasulullah ﷺ said, "The child is for the [husband of the] bed and stones are for the adulterer." [al-Bukhari]. If however the husband denies the child, then Li'an will take place. Its meaning and method will be explained in the next chapter InshaAllaah.

f: A woman has given birth and her husband denies the birth. How will the birth be established?
b: The Arsh (testification) of one woman will establish that the birth took place.

f: You have mentioned the law in regard establishing lineage to a husband she is married to. What about a husband who divorced her?
b:
There are details in this matter as follows:
A Raj'i divorcee will have her child attributed to the husband if she gave birth after two years or more, as long as she says her Iddah has not terminated. In the second scenario it will be said that he had sex with her during the Iddahi and hence took her back.
If the Raj'' i divorcee gives birth in less than two years the lineage is established from the husband and she becomes Bain.
An irrevocable divorcee's child is attributed to the husband if she gave birth within two years. If she gave birth two years from the day of separation or more the lineage will not be attributed to him unless he claims it.
The child of a widow is attributed to the husband if born within two years of the day of death.
A woman admits that her Iddah is complete. If she then gives birth within six months the child is the husband's. If after six months then the lineage is not established.

f: Are there other conditions for establishing the lineage of the child of a woman in Iddah besides what you have mentioned?
b:
According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is a condition that two men or a man and two women testify that she gave birth. If however her pregnancy was apparent, or the husband admits to it, then the lineage is established without Arsh.

According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the Arsh (testification) of one woman establishes the lineage in all scenarios.

NOTE: The maximum pregnancy period is two years and the minimum is six months.

f: You mentioned in the previous chapter that if the husband denies the child to whom his wife gave birth to, then Li'an becomes compulsory upon him. We wish to know what is Li'an and how is it conducted?
b:
If a man accuses [Qazaf] his wife of Zina, and both of them are legally qualified to testify, and the woman is such whose slanderer will be inflicted with the penal punishment [Hadd]; or he denies the lineage of her child; and the woman demands her rights when slandered; then he will have to undergo Li'an. If he refuses to then the judge will detain him until he either commences the Li'an or he belies his statement in which case the punishment of slander will be inflicted upon him.

The procedure of Li'an is that the husband presents himself before the judge and will take an oath four times. In each he will say, "I testify by Allaah that I am certainly of the true ones when I accuse this woman of adultery." At the fifth time he will state that may Allaah's curse definitely be upon him if he is of the liars in accusing her of adulterly. He should indicate to her in all this. The woman will then testify four times, saying in each Arsh (testification), "I testify by Allaah that he is certainly of the liars in accusing me of adultery." The fifth time she will say that may Allaah's anger be upon her if he is of the true ones in accusing her of adultery.

f: A woman institutes a claim of slander and the judge orders Li'an. The husband is prepared to undergo it, but she now refuses. What will the judge do?
b:
Li'an is Wajib upon her if the husband is prepared to do it. If she refuses, the judge will detain her until she performs the Li'an or verifies her husband's accusation.34

34 In which case he will not be punished for slander, nor will she be punished for adultery simply for verifying the husbad. [ad-Durr al-Mukthar].

f: Why have you stipulated that the couple be people who can testify and that the woman be such whose slanderer is punished? [i.e. both of them have to be legally qualified to testify for Li'an]
b:
If the husband is a slave, or Kafir35, or has been punished for slander before; and he accuses his wife of adultery, then he will be punished for slander without resorting to Li'an.

If the husband is a man who can testify but she is a slave, Kafir, punished for slander, or a woman whose slanderer is not punsihed36, then there is neither Hadd upon him nor Li'an.37

35 She became Muslim and he accused her of adultery before he was presented with Islam.
36 i.e. she must be a chaste woman.
37 No Hadd but because he has blemished her so he will be punished otherwise by Ta'zir.

f: The judge ordered them to commence Li'an which they did. Does their marital relation still exist? Is the child's lineage established to the husband who performed Li'an?
b: When they perform Li'an the judge separates them. According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the separation is Bain. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the separation permanently makes them Haram for each other. If the Li'an was due to a denying a child, then the judge cancels its lineage to the man who performed the Li'an and joins it to its mother.

f: After the Li'an the man recants his accusation and accepts that he was false. What is the ruling?
b: The judge will inflict the Hadd upon him.

f: Can he now marry her a second time? [i.e. after the Li'an the man recants his accusation and accepts that he was false]
b: He can remarry her after admitting that he was false.

f: A man slanders a woman who is not his wife and is inflicted with the Hadd. Can they marry each other?
b: Yes.

f: A woman fornicated and was inflicted with the Hadd. A man then makes Qazaf against her. Can he then marry her?
b: Yes.

f: A man slanders his minor/insane wife. What is the status of Li'an between them?
b: There will be no Li'an nor will he be inflicted with the Hadd.

f: And if the husband slanders her and he is minor/insane?
b:
There will be no Li'an.38

38 Because he is not a person who can testify.

f: A mute accuses his wife. Will the judge decree Li'an between them?
b: There will be no Li'an.

f: If the husband says, "This foetus is not mine", will Li'an commence?
b:
There is no Li'an in this case.39

39 Because there is no certainty that it will remain a slander due to the possibility that it is only a swelling of the stomach. If his allegation firmly remains such as when she gives birth in less than six months then it is as if he said, "If you are pregnant then it is not mine", and slander is not established on conditions. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى if she gives birth in less than six months then Li'an will be conducted.

f: If he says, "You have committed Zina and this foetus is not mine", what effects do these words have?
b:
They will perform Li'an but the judge will not negate the foetus from him.40

40 Because there is no ruling against him until the birth. [ad-Durr al-Mukthar]

f: When is the man's negation of the wife's child in effect?
b: When he negates immediately after the birth, or in the condition when congratulations are accepted on the birth, or when the goods for the birth are being bought; then his negation has an effect and they will perform Li'an. If he delays negating beyond that time then his negation of the child's lineage will not be accepted. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he can negate the lineage throughout the Nifas period.

f: A woman gives birth two twins. The husband negates one and accepts the other. What is the ruling of Li'an and establishment of lineage?
b: The lineage of both will be established, whichever of the two he negated. If he negated the first one only then the Hadd of slander will be inflicted upon him. If he negated the second one only then Li'an will commence.

f: What is Ila linguistically and in the terminology of Fiqh?
b: It is ala on the scale of if'al, meaning to take an oath. Technically it means when a man vows not to approach his wife.

f: What is the status of ila in the Shari'ah?
b:
There are various scenarios which are as follows:

If the man says to his wife, "By Allaah, I shall not approach you for four months", then he is muli [comits Ila]. If he has sex with her within four months then he has broken his vow. He is liable to pay Kaffarah for breaking his vow and the Ila is terminated. The meaning of the termination is that if he approaches her after that, he is not liable a second time. This approaching her is called Fay which means terminating the oath. If he does not approach her until four months pass she becomes Bain with one divorce and the oath is terminated.41 

If he says, "By Allaah I shall not approach you/By Allaah I shall never approach you", and then approaches her within four months he has violated his vow and must pay Kaffarah. If he does not approach her until the four months are complete she is divorced one Bain. However, in this case the oath remains. Hence if he remarries her the Ila is reinstated. If he then has sex with her in the four months he must pay Kaffarah or else another divorce falls. If he then marries her a third time the Ila is again reinstated. If they have sex within four months he must pay the Kaffarah or else a third divorce falls at the end of the four months. If he then marries her again after she marries another man the Ila is not reinstated but the oath remains. Thus he will pay Kaffarah if they have sex.42

41 Based on al-Baqarah:227, "For those who make Ila with their wives is a waiting of four months. If they then make Fay then Allah is Most Forgiving Most Merciful. And if they resolve upon divorce then Allah is All-Hearing All-Knowing."
42 The Ila ends with the third divorce but the oath remains.

f: A man pronounced Ila against a divorcee. Is the Ila valid?
b: If she is a revocable divorcee then it is Ila, but not if she is Bain [irrevocable]

f: What is the ruling if he vowed for less than four months? [i.e. to abstain from his wife for less than four months of sex]
b: There is no Ila if he vowed for less than four months. This means that if they have sex within the vowed period then he must pay Kaffarah. If he does not, even for four months or more, then she is not divorced.

f: What is the period of Ila if the slave-girl's husband pronounces it on her?
b: Ila for her is two months. If her husband does not have sex with her in that period then she is divorced one Bain.

f: If he husband regrets making the Ila and wishes to make Fay i.e. have sex with her within the four months as cancellation of the Ila. However, he is ill and unable to have sex; or the wife is sick or so young that she cannot have sex; or they are so far away from each other that they cannot meet in the Ila period. How then can he make Fay?
b: In such circumstances he will make Fay by verbally saying, "I have made Fay to her." In that way the Ila is terminated.

f: He made a verbal Fay but the excuse was resolved within the Ila period. What is the status of his Fay?
b: The verbal Fay is void. He must make Fay by sex.

f: What is Zhihar linguistically and in Shari'ah?
b: Linguistically is derived from Zhahr [back]. If a man says to his wife, "You are to me as my mother's back", then he has committed Zhihar in Shari'ah, to which there are certain laws attached.

f: Explain these laws. [i.e. of Zhihar]
b: When a man pronounces Zhihar against his wife she becomes Haram for him. He may not have sex with her, nor touch her, nor kiss her, until he pays the Kaffarah of Zhihar. If he does have sex before paying, then he should seek Allaah's forgiveness and not do it a second time until he pays the Kaffarah. He is still liable for a single Kaffarah, nothing in addition.

f: Do the very words of Zhihar make Kaffarah Wajib or is there something else?
b: Yes, he must pay when he is resolved to have sex with her again. Allaah says, "Those who pronounce Zhihar against their wives then wish to retract their words, must set free a slave before they touch each other..."

f: What is the ruling if he compares her [i.e. his wife] to a body part besides the back?
b: It will also be Zhihar if he says, "You are as to me as my mother's stomach/thigh/vagina."

f: And if he says, "Your head/vagina/neck/half/third are to me as my mother's back"?
b: That will also be Zhihar.

f: Is Zhihar specific to a comparison with a mother or is it general to any woman one cannot marry?
b: It is general and covers all such women whom one cannot ever marry e.g. sister, paternal aunt, foster-mother etc. If he says, "You are to me as my sister's back/thigh/vagina", then it is Zhihar.

f: What is the ruling if he says to his wife, "You are to me like my mother/similar to my mother"?
b: He will be asked what he intended. If he says, "I meant to honour her", then it is as he says. If he says, "I intended Zhihar", then it is Zhihar. If he says, "I intended divorce", then it is an irrevocable divorce. If he had no intention then it is nothing.

f: A man with several wives says to them, "You are as to me as my mother's back." What is the ruling?
b: He has made Zhihar with each of them. A separate Kaffarah would have to be paid for each.

f: What is the Kaffarah of Zhihar?
b: Allaah Ta'ala has explained it in the beginning of Suratul Mujadalah. It is to free a slave. If he cannot then he should fast two months consecutively. If he cannot, then he must feed 60 Miskin. All that must be done before touching her.

f: A man wishes to free a slave as Kaffarah of Zhihar. What kind of slave will suffice?
b: He may free a slave, be it Muslim or Kafir; male or female; minor or adult. The slave may not be blind or short of his hands; or legs; or one hand and one leg from the same side; or with both thumbs lost. A hand and leg cut from opposite sides is not an obstacle.

f: Can he free a deaf slave? [i.e. as Kaffarah for Zhihar]
b: Yes.

f: Will his Kaffarah be made if he sets free an insane slave with no sense? [i.e. for Zhihar]
b: No.

f: And if he frees a Mudabbar, or Ummul Walad, or a Mukatab who had already made a partial payment? [i.e. as Kaffarah for Zhihar]
b: The Kaffarah is not made.

f: And if he freed a Mukatab who did not pay anything? [i.e. as Kaffarah for Zhihar]
b: It is allowed.

f: He bought his father or his son and intended thereby that they would be free and his Kaffarah paid. Does that suffice his Kaffarah? [i.e. for Zhihar]
b: Yes.

f: A man and his partner own a slave. He frees his half as Kaffarah and accepts liability for the partner's half. The partner then sets his half free. Has the Kaffarah been fulfilled? [i.e. for Zhihar]
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is not fulfilled. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى if the one setting him free is well-off then it is fulfilled, if he is poor then it is not.

f: If a man sets half his slave free as Kaffarah of Zhihar and later sets the other half free, is the Kaffarah fulfilled?
b:
According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is fulfilled on condition that he does not have sex with the wife against whom he pronounced the Zhihar in between the period of the two manumissions.43

43 Because he accepts partial manumission.

f: You have mentioned that if the man cannot free a slave as Kaffarah of Zhihar he may fast two months consecutively. Is his Kaffarah valid if he fasts Sha'ban and Ramadan?
b: It is not valid. The fast of Ramadan is Fard upon him due to him being a Muslim, not because of the Zhihar. Thus the fast of Ramadan cannot be included in the Kaffarah.

f: If he fasts Shawwal and Zul Qa'dah, or Zul Qa'dah and Zul Hijjah, is his Kaffarah acceptable? [i.e. for Zhihar]
b: No, because fasting on the Day of Fitr and Nahr and the Days of Tashriq are forbidden. Fasting those days will not fulfil the Wajib requirement.

f: What is the ruling if he has sex during the two months of Kaffarah with the wife upon whom he pronounced Zhihar?
b:
If he consciously has sex in the night or forgetfully in the day44 then he begins anew according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he need not begin anew.

44 If he had sex deliberately in the day then it is unanimously agreed that he will begin anew.

f: What is the ruling if he failed to fast a day during the two months, whether with or without an excuse? [i.e. as Kaffarah for his Zhihar]
b: He has to begin anew because he missed the condition of consecutiveness.

f: You mentioned that if he cannot fast two months consecutively then he must feed sixty poor. [i.e. as Kaffarah for his Zhihar] How is this feeding done?
b:
He must feed each poor person a half Sa' of wheat, or a Sa' of dates or barley or the price of these. If he feeds them lunch and supper until they are full,45  then it suffices for them whether they ate a little or a lot.

45 It is not valid if there is amongst them those who were full nbeofre the meal, or a small child not close to puberty.

f: What is the ruling if he fed one poor person for sixty days? [i.e. as Kaffarah for his Zhihar]
b: It suffices as his Kaffarah.

f: He gave a single poor person 30 Sa' of wheat or 120 Sa' of barley in a single day. Is his Kaffarah fulfilled? `[i.e. his Kaffarah of Zhihar]
b: Only his first day's Kaffarah is fulfilled. He must feed another 59 poor people.

f: He was giving a poor man a half Sa' of wheat each day. He approached the wife upon whom he had pronounced the Zhihar before the completion of feeding 60 poor. Must he begin anew?
b:
No, the text of the Quraan does not stipulate such a condition in reference to the feeding.46

46 The ayah states, "...he who is not able should feed 60 poor", and does not add onto the condition of feeding by saying "...before they touch each other..." as in the cases of freeing a slave and fasting.

f: Sundry Masail [extra's]
b:
If a slave pronounces Zhihar on his wife, his only recourse to Kaffarah is fasting, because he does not own anything. Even if his owner frees a slave on his behalf, or feeds 60 poor on his behalf then it will not validate as his Kaffarah.
A man is liable for two Kaffarahs of Zhihar. He set two slaves free but did not make a specific intention which is for which. Both his Kaffarahs are fulfilled.
Similarly if he is liable for two Kaffarahs and he fasted 4 months or fed 120 poor, and did not specify, then both Kaffarahs are fulfilled..
If he only freed one slave for two Kaffarahs, or only fasted 2 months, he may apply that as Kaffarah for whichever one he wishes.

f: Whom is it Wajib to spend maintenance on?
b: It is Wajib to spend on one's wives, children, divorcee, parents and blood relatives.

f: Explain the Masail of maintenace of wives.
b:
They are as follows:
It is Wajib for a man to maintain his wife, be she Muslim, Christian or Jew; when she has surrendered herself in his home. He is also obligated to feed and clothe her. Both of their conditions are taken into account for this, whether the husband is rich or poor.
If she is disobedient and does not surrender herself to his home, then he is not obligated to maintain her until she returns home.
If she refuses to give herself over to him until he pays her Mahr, then she is still entitled to maintenace.
If the wife is so small that she cannot be sexually enjoyed, then she is not entitled to maintenace even if she hands herself to him.
If she is an adult and hands herself to him. But he is a minor, incapable of sex. She will receive maintenance from his wealth.
If a woman is detained because of debts or is forcibly kidnapped, then she is not entitled to maintenance.
If she journeys for Hajj with someone besides her husband then she is not entitled to maintenance.
If she is ill in the husband's home, then he must maintain her.
A man marries a slave-girl. Her owner lets her stay with him. He must maintain her.

A slave marries a freewoman with his owner's permission. Her maintenace will be a debt against which the slave can be sold; unless the owner pays from his wealth.

f: A woman had a servant in her father's house before marrying. Is it the duty of the husband to pay for a servant for her?
b: Yes, if he is rich. Also, he is not obligated to hire more than one servant.

f: A man is unable to pay for his wife's maintenance. Will they be separated?
b: No, she will take credit against him. When he can afford he must pay those debts.

f: The judge ruled that he must spend on her according to a poor man. He later becomes rich and she claims the maintenance of the rich. Must he fulfil the maintenace of the rich to her?
b: Yes.

f: For some time he does not spend on her. She then demands the amount she spent on herself. Must he pay it?
b: No, unless the judge had ruled an amount for her, or he cmpromises on an amount.

f: The court has ordered a maintenace amount for her. Months pass and he does not pay and he dies. What is the status of that outstanding amount?
b: The maintenance is forfeit.

f: He gave her enough to last her a year. One of them dies before the amount is finished. Will it be claimed from her?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى no. According to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى her past expenses will be calculated and the remainder is the husband's.

f: You have mentioned that the husband must pay for her residence. In what house will he keep her?
b: He must keep her in a separate chamber where none of his family stays, unless she chooses otherwise.

f: He provided her with accommodation. [i.e. his wife] Her parents, family and children from another husband come to visit. Can he stop them?
b: He can stop them from entering, but he may not stop them from looking at her and speaking to her at any time.

f: Who must maintain a woman during her 'Iddah
b:
If a man divorces his wife, whether revocable or irrevocable48, he is responsible for her maintenance and accomodation. As for a widow, there is no maintenance from the husband's estate. She may spend her share of the inheritance.

48 As well as Mughallazh divorce.

f: Does any circumstance arise whereby a divorcee's maintenance is cancelled?
b: If the separation is due to a sin from her side, such as abandoning Islaam or giving herself to her husband's son before the divorce, then she is not entitled to maintenance.

f: And if he she gave herself to her husband's son after divorce? [i.e. then what is the status of her maintenance?]
b: She is still entitled to maintenance.

f: If a couple has a child, whether boy or girl, whose duty is it to maintain the child?
b: The father is responsible for maintaining minor children. Nobody shares that responsibility, just as nobody shares the husband's reponsibility in maintaining his wife.

f: Why have you stipulated "minor"? [i.e. the father is responsible for maintaining minor children]
b: The father is not responsible for maintaining adult male children because they are able to earn for themselves, unless the adult son is chronically adult, in which case the father is responsible for two-thirds of his maintenance and the mother is responsible for a third. The parents are also responsible for the unmarried daughter in the same proportion. They are only responsible for the adult chronically ill son and adult unmarried daughter if they are Muslims.

f: Is maintenance of minor children a duty in all circumstances?
b: The parents are responsible to spend on their maintenance if the children do not own their own wealth. If however, they do own wealth in their own right then they should spend on them from the children's wealth.

f: How can the minor have wealth when he cannot earn?
b: He can have wealth when someone gives him a gift; leaves him a beques after his death; or the child inherits wealth.

f: Whose duty is it to maintain the parents?
b: If someone owns wealth he will first spend on himself, whether he is young or old, man or woman. This rule is general and covers parents and others but not wives. The husband is responsible to maintain the wife even if she is rich. If one or both the parents are poor then the children are obligated to maintain them. Nobody shares the responsibility of the child to support his parents. Just as it is Wajib to maintain the parents, it is also Wajib to maintain grandfathers and grandmothers if they are poor.

f: The parents of an absent man, spend his wealth which they have in their possession, on themselves. Are they liable to repay it?
b: No.

f: An absent man had some goods or land which is parents sold to maintain themselves. Can they do that?
b: If they sold the goods because of a need to maintain themselves, then it is permissible according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. They cannot however sell the land.

f: A man is absent and his parents need him to spend on them. Can the judge rule that they will be spent upon from his wealth?
b: Yes, the judge will rule accordingly.

f: A stranger is holding the wealth of an absent son. The stranger spent on the son's parents from that wealth. Is he liable to compensate that amount?
b: If he spent with the court's permission then he is not liable. If he spent without permission then he is liable.

f: Is maintenance still a duty when the parties have different religions?
b: It will still be a duty to maintain one's wife, parents, grandfathers, grandmothers, children and grandchildren. Besides these, it is not a duty to spend on relatives of another religion, just as a poor man is not obligated to spend on them.

f: How can a minor child be of a different religion to his father's?
b:
For example, a Christian/Jew marries a woman of his religion. She bears his child and then embraces Islaam while he does not. The child will be a Muslim like its mother. The court will rule that the Kafir father must maintain his Muslim child.

NOTE: If a man admits that he is holding the wealth of an absent man and acknowledges that a certain woman is his wife, the judge will rule that he must spend from it on his wife, minor children and parents. The wife will stand as Kafil for the amount. The court will not rule for maintenance for any besides these people.

f: Is maintenance for relatives besides parents and children wajib?
b:
Maintenance is Wajib for blood relatives one cannot marry according to their inhertiance shares;50 when it is a poor minor, or poor adult female, or chronically ill male, or poor blind person.

NOTE: If the court rules that he must maintain children, parents and relatives and some time passes without him paying then the amount is forfeit unless the court permits them to incur debt against him.51

50 e.g. he has a grandfather and son of son. The grandfather is responsible for a sixth of his maintenance and the son's son for the rest; because if he dies then they inherit from him in that proportion.
51 i.e. the passage of time does not absolve him of liability of debts incurred with the court's permission.

f: Is a man obligated to pay for the maintenance of his slave or slave-girl?
