b: He must spend on them. If he refuses they may acquire earnings and maintain themselves from it. If they cannot earn then the court will force him to sell them.

f: A baby of breastfeeding age has both parents. Whose duty is it to see the child's breastfeeding?
b: If the mother is willing to breastfeed him then that would be best for the baby. However, she is not obligated to do so. I she refuses then the father must hire someone to breastfeed him on behalf of the mother.

f: Can the mother not feed him [i.e. a baby of breastfeeding age] in exchange for payment, just as another woman would be hired to do it?
b: If the nurse is the baby's father's wife or divorcee in 'Iddah who is receiving maintenance then she may not take a fee for feeding her baby; because her maintenance is Wajib upon the father from another aspect. If the divorcee has completed her 'Iddah, she may take a fee for feeding him.

f: The father hires a nurse, and the mother whose 'Iddah is complete is willing to accept the same fee as the nurse. Who is more entitled to feed the baby?
b: The mother is more entitled to feed her baby.

f: If the mother demands a fee greather than that of the other nurse [i.e. with regards to breastfeeding her baby], can the father be forced to accede?
b: No.

f: The couple has separated. Who is more entitled to the children?
b: The mother is most entitled. If there is no mother, then the mother's mother is more entitled than the father's mother. If there is no maternal grandmother then the paternal grandmother is more entitled than the sisters. If there is no paternal grandmother then the sisters are more entitled than the paternal - and maternal aunts. The sister with both parents in common is most entitled, then a sister with only a mother in common, then a sister with only a father in common. Thereafter the maternal aunts are more entitled than the paternal aunts. Then come the paternal aunts. The maternal and paternal aunts are ranked the same way as sisters in the three relevant categories.

f: Is the right to custody ever lost?
b: Whoever of the above [i.e. the mother, then the mother's mother, then the paternal grandmother, then the sisters; specically the sister with both parents in common, then a sister with only a mother in common, then a sister with only a father in common, then the maternal aunts and then the paternal aunts] marries looses her right of custody; except for a grandmother whose husband is the grandfather. Similarly the mother's right is not lost when she marries a Mahram of the child e.g. the child's paternal uncle.

f: The mother does not want custody and there are no other women who can assume custody. What is the ruling?
b: The mother will be forced to take the child.

f: If there are no women of the child's family to take custody of the child and the men fight over it, who will receive custody?
b:
The closest in terms of Asabiyah is most entitled.52

52 First will be the father, then the father's father and ascending thus. Then a full brother, then a brother with a common father. Then the son of the full brother. Then the son of the brother with a common father. And thus all their descendants. Then a full brother of the father. Then a brother of the father who has a father in common. Then cousins, first is the son of a full brother of the father; then the son of a brother of the father who has a father in common. The cousins will not get a girl's custody because they are not Mahram. Also she will not be given to an untrustworthy mother or sinful relatives; nor to the owner who set the slave free; in order to avoid trouble.

f: For how long are the women entitled to custody?
b: The mother and grandmother are entitled to a boy until he can do the following on his own: eat, drink, dress and Istinja. They are entitled to a girl until she menstruates. Women besides the mother and grandmother are entitled to the girl until she reaches an age when she is sexually desirable.

f: What are the custody rights of a Christian/Jewish woman who bore a child for her Muslim husband?
b: She is entitled to him as long as he does not yet understand the difference in religions and there is no fear yet of him being influenced by disbelief.

f: What are the custody rights of a slave-girl over her child?
b: A slave-girl and an Ummul Walad do not have custody rights before bein set free. Once free, they have the same rights as a freewoman.

f: A woman is divorced and being most entitled, gets custody over her child. She then intends taking the child away from the city where the child's father is. Can she do that?
b: She may not, unless she takes him to her homeland where his father married her.

f: A man has disappeared from his town and his location is not known; nor if he is living or dead. Who will guard his wealth and other issues?
b: The court will appoint someone to guard his wealth, fulfil his obligations and spend on his wife and minor children from his wealth.

f: Can the judge separate the missing man and his wife, and thereby permit her to remarry?
b:
He may not separate them until 120 years53 have passed since the day he was born. Upon completion of this period the judge will rule that he is legally dead and the wife will spend the 'Iddah of a widow. She may then remarry who she wishes.

53 This is according to Imam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and is the safest. However, the latter Hanafiyah observed the increased temptations and decrease in piety and patience of women, and hence ruled according to the Mazhab of al-Imam Malik رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. Accordingly the woman will present herself to the judge and provide Shar'i evidencethat her husband is missing. The judge will conduct further investigations. If nothing is learnt he will rule that the woman must wait a further 4 years. If in that period no further information is obtained and it is not known whether he is dead or alive then the court will declare him dead. She will spend the 'Iddah of a widow and may thereafter remarry.

f: How will the inheritance be divided if any of the missing man's heirs died beofre he was declared dead?
b: Only those heirs living at the time of the declaration will inherit.

f: Does the missing inherit from his relatives who die before he is declared dead?
b: He does not inherit from anyone who dies while he is missing.

f: How does a freeman/woman become a slave?
b: Jihad will continue until the Day of Resurrection. Thus when the Believers wage Jihad against the Kuffar and capture them, the Amirul Muminin may decide to enslave them. Once he decrees that, they are slaves and will be divided amongst those entitled to booty.

f: The enemies of Islaam object that enslavement is a violation of humanity.
b:
Their objections are mistaken and their words unsophisticated if Kuffar captives are returned to their lands they will be even harsher against Islaam and the Muslims. They will be even further from the guidance with which the Quraan was revealed. If the ruler should keep them imprisoned then their maintenance will be a urden upon the Public Treasury. That is an expense without any benefit. It is therefore appropriate that he divides them amongst the warriors to serve them. Each slave will earn for his master and eat from his home. The slave will thus not be a complete burden upon the master, but will be like a member of the household. In this way both the master and slave benefit in wordly terms. As far as Din is concerned, the slave will live in a Muslim home and observe their Salah, Fasting, Worship, Remembrance of Allaah and their good character. He will be affected by that and enter Allaah's Din. He will be saved from the punishment of Hell - what a great favour that is upon him. The pages of history are replete with slaves of either sex who embraced Islaam and acquired lofty stages in regards knowledge and pious deeds.

Enslavement is not necessary and the ruler has other options which will be described in Kitabus Siyar InshaAllaah. The Shari'ah greatly encourages manumission of slaves and commands that they be set free as Kaffarah. It also instituted the processed of declaring slaves Mudabbar and Mukatab as ways of freeing him.

f: How does a man free his slave?
b: If a sane adult says to his slave/slave-girl, "You are a free person/you are set free/you are freed/you are made free/I have freed you/you are manumitted", then the slave is free; whether the owner meant manumission or not, because these words are explicit manumission and do not depend on intention.

f: If the owner specifies the freedom to certain organs of the slave, is the slave free?
b:
If he says, "Your neck/face/head/body is free", then the slave is free. Similarly if he says to a slave-girl, "Your vagina is free."54

54 Because these words symbolise the entire body. [al-Hidayah]

f: What if he says, "I have no ownership over you?"
b: If he intended manumission then the slave is free, if not then the slave is not free. The same rule applies to any other non-explicit words of manumission, such as, "You have left my ownership/ I have no authority over you."

f: What if he says, "I have no Sultan [power] over you?"
b: The slave will not be freed even if the owner intended it as manumission.

f: If the owner says, "This is my son"55, and remains firm on his statement or says, "This is my freed-slave", or calls him, "O my freed-slave", is the slave free?
b: Yes, these expressions are treated as explicit declarations of freedom.

f: And if he says, "O my son/O my brother/You are like a freeman."
b: The slave is not freed.

f: If the owner says about a slave who cannot be his son, "This is my son", what is the ruling?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he is freed. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he is not freed.

f: If the owner says to his slave-girl, "You are divorced", and intends thereby freeing her, is she freed?
b: No.

f: If he says to his slave, "You are nothing but free", what is the ruling?
b: The slave is free.

f: What is the ruling if a man is forced to free his slave, or was drunk when he freed the slave?
b: The slave is free.

f: A man frees a pregnant slave-girl. What is the status of the foetus?
b: Mother and foetus are both free.

f: What is the ruling if only the foetus is freed?
b: The foetus and not the mother are free.

f: Can freedom be attached to possession or other conditions?
b: Yes, thus if he says to someone else's slave, "If I own you, you will be free", then the salve will be free if he comes to own him. If he says to his own slave, "If you enter the house you are free", and the slave enters the house then he is free.

f: Is there a way of manumission without the owner setting the slave free?
b: Yes, if someone acquires a Mahram blood relative, whether by purchase, inheritance or gift, then that relative is free even if the owner had no intention of manumission.

f: If the owner sets part of the slave free, is the part of the entire slave free?
b:
According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the part only is free and the slave will work to earn his complete freedom. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammad رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he is entirely free and need to work to complete his freedom.56

56 The principle according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى is that the slave can be divided into parts whilst according to them (i.e. Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى) as well as Imaam ash-Shafi'i رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it cannot.

f: Two partners share a slave. One frees his slave. What is the status of the remaining share?
b: If the freedom-grantor is rich then the partner has a choice, he may either free his share as well, or hold the other liable, or he can demand that the slave earn and pay him for his share. If the freedom-grantor is poor, the partner has the same option except that he cannot hold his partner liable. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he can only hold the rich partner liable and if the partner is poor he must demand that the slave pay him.

f: You have mentioned that if a blood-relative Mahram comes into possession he is automatically free. If two partners buy or inherit a slave who is the son of one of the partners, is the slave free? If so what is the other partner's right?
b: The father's share is freed and he is not liable for his partner's share. The partner can either free his share or make the slave work to compensate him.

f: Two partners own a slave and each claims that the other freed his share. Both deny that they set their share free. What is the ruling?
b: The slave will be entirely free. According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he will work to repay both partners, whether they are rich or poor. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he will only work and compensate a poor partner(s) and will not compensate a rich partner(s).

f: People free their slaves for Allaah's sake. If someone says, "I free you for Satan's sake/an idol's sake", is the slave free?
b: Yes.

f: Sundry Masail
b:
If a slave belonging to a Kafir flees from the lands of the Kuffar to us [i.e. Muslim lands] then he is free.
If a slave-girl bears the child of her owner, then the offspring is free.
Her child from her slave husband belongs to her owner.
The offspring of a freewoman from a slave is free.

f: What is Tadbir?
b: It is when the owner says, "When I die then you are free/You are free after [dubur] me/You are a Mudabbar/I have made Tadbir of you."

f: What is the ruling when he says that? [i.e. when a slave owner says "When I die then you are free/You are free after [dubur] me/You are a Mudabbar/I have made Tadbir of you."]
b: The slave is classified as a Mudabbar i.e. he will be freed upon the owner's death. He may not be sold; nor gifted to anyone; nor hired out; nor given to serve anyone else.

f: If he [i.e. the slave owner] makes Tadbir of a slave-girl, can he still have sex with her? Can he marry her to another man?
b: Both acts are permissible.

f: The owner then marries her [i.e. a slave-girl who is Mudabbar] to another man who fathers her child. What is the child's status?
b: The child is a Mudabbar like its mother.

f: When the owner dies, is the Mudabbar free without any price or must he compensate the heirs?
b: If the third of the estate in which the deceased could make bequest covers the slave's value then he is free without further liability. If the entire estate consisted of nothing but the slave, then the slave must compensate them for two-thirds of his value. If debts consume the entire value of the estate, then the slave will compensate the creditors for his entire value.

f: Is the Tadbir valid if the owner attaches a specific description to his freedom, e.g. "If I die in this illness of mine/in this journey/of such-and-such a disease"?
b: The slave is not a Mudabbar and may be sold and gifted away. However, if the specified condition is found, he will be freed from the third of the estate.

f: What is Istilad?
b: When an owner impregnates his slave-girl and she gives birth to his child, then he has made Istilad with her. The slave-girl is called Ummul Walad [child's mother]. This is on condition that he acknowledges the child, in which case its lineage will be attributed to him.

f: What are the regulations concerning an Ummul Walad?
b: She may not be sold or otherwise transferred into another's possession. The owner may have sex with her, take service from her, hire her out, and get her married. When the owner dies she is freed from the entire estate [i.e. she is not limited to the third only] and is not obligated to compensate the heirs or the creditors. If he had gotten her married and she then bears another child, the child is in the same status as her i.e. it will be free when she gains her freedom.

f: You have stipulated that the owner must acknowledge the child for Istilad. What happens if he does not?
b: The lineage will not be attributed to him.

f: He [i.e. the slave owner] acknowledges a child and then she [i.e. the Ummul Walad] bears a second child. Is it necessary for him to acknowledge the second as well, or is the first acknowledgement sufficient?
b: The second child's lineage will be attributed to him with need for acknowledgement. If however he specifically denies the child, then the lineage will not be attributed to him.

f: A man marries a slave-girl. She bears his child and he then comes to own her. Does she become his Ummul Walad?
b: Yes, the laws of Ummul Walad apply to her.

f: A man owns a slave-girl. His father has intercourse with her and she bears his child. The father claims the child. Will the child's lineage be attributed to him?
b: It will be attributed to the father who claimed him and she will be his Ummul Walad.

f: When she becomes the Ummul Walad of the father [i.e. the father of the slave-owner] who made the claim [i.e. claimed the child she bore], does the father have to pay his son who owned her?
b: Yes, the father is liable to pay her price to him.

f: Does he owe anything else, such as 'Uqr57 or the price of the child? [i.e. when the father of the slave-owner has intercourse with his slave-girl and she bears his child, and he has to pay her price]
b:
No.

57 Dowry for having sex by mistake [al-Mughrib]

f: A man owns a slave-girl. His grandfather has intercourse with her and she bears his child. The grandfather claims the child. Will the child's lineage be attributed to him?
b: If the owner's father is dead the lineage will be attributed to the grandfather, but not if he is alive.

f: A slave-girl owned by two partners bears a child. One of the partners claims the child. Will its lineage be attributed to him?
b: Yes, and the slave becomes his Ummul Walad. He must pay his partner half her 'Uqr and half her price. He is not liable for the price of the child.

f: What is the ruling if both parties claim the child? [i.e. a slave-girl owned by two partners bears a child]
b: The child will be attributed to both and she will be the Ummul Walad of both. Each will pay half 'Uqr. They will mutually settle their accounts.

f: How will the inheritance be distributed if one of these partners or the child dies? [i.e. when a slave-girl is owned by two partners bears a child and both parties claim the child]
b: The child will inherit from both of them as a full child. Each of them will inherit from the child as one father.

f: A man made his slave Mukatab. The Mukatab bought a slave-girl and the Mukatab's owner cohabited with her. She then bore his child. What is the child's status? What does the owner owe the Mukatab?
b: If the Mukatab accepts his word then the lineage is attributed to the owner who is liable for her 'Uqr and child's price. She does not however become his Ummul Walad. If the Mukatab does not accept his word then the lineage is not established to him.

f: What is the meaning of the owner making a Mukatabah agreement with his slave?
b: It is when the owner says to his slave or slave-girl, "i impose upon you 1000 Dirham (for example) payable to me within a specified period beginning from this date to that date. If you do that then you are free. If you do not then you remain a slave." If the slave accepts that then he becomes a Mukatab. This transaction is called Mukatabah. The amount which the slave renders to the owner is called Badalul Kitabah [exchange for written agreement]. Allaah says, "Those who seek a Kitab agreement from amongst your slaves then agree to it if you see good in them." [an-Nur:33]

f: Can the money be demanded immediately or must it be after a period? [i.e. from the Mukatab]
b: It can be immediate, deferred or specified for a date.

f: Can the owner make Mukatabah with a minor slave?
b: Yes, if the minor understands buying and selling.

f: When the owner makes a Mukatabah what laws are applicable?
b:
If the agreement is valid, then the slave is free of the master's control but does not leave his ownership. The slave is free to buy, sell and travel.58

58 Thus certain jurists define Kitabah as freedom of control for the slave without freedom in wealth.

f: Can the Mukatab marry?
b: Only with his owner's permission.

f: The Mukatab earned money for the Mukatabah. Can he give a gift or charity from it?
b: He may only give a small amount.

f: A Mukatab bought a slave-girl and had sex with her. She had his child. What is the status of the child?
b: The child enters the Mukatabah and is the same ruling as his father. His earnings are his.

f: The owner got his slave married to his slave-girl. He then made a Mukatabah agreement with both of them. The slave-girl has his child. What is the child's status?
b: He is included in his mother's Kitabah and his earnings are his.

f: A man makes Mukatabah with his slave-girl and then has sex with her. Does he owe her anything?
b: Yes, 'Uqr.

f: The owner violates the Mukatab slave-girl or her child. What is the violation?
b: He will be held accountable just af if anyone else had committed the violation.

f: The owner destroyed the wealth of the Mukatab slave-girl. What is the ruling?
b: He is liable for whatever he destroyed.

f: A Mukatab buys his father or son, will the father/son be automatically freed?
b: He will not be immediately freed. He will join him in the Mukatabah and will be free with the Mukatab.

f: The Mukatab bought the mother of his child [Ummul Walad] with his child. What is the child's satus?
b: The child enters into the Kitabah and he cannot sell the mother.

f: If he [i.e. a Mukatab] buys a Mahram blood relative other than his father or son, does that relative enter the Kitabah?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he does not enter the Kitabah unless he and the purchases have a relationship of birth.

f: The Mukatab pays his due on the set dates, and then a date arrives where he is unable to pay. Will the court declare him unable to pay?
b:
According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى59 if the slave has debts which he must pay or wealth advanced to him then there should not be haste in declaring him unable to transact. He should be given two or three days' respite. If thereafter he cannot present any valid excuse the owner may demand that he be incapacitated and the Kitabah annulled by the court. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he will not be incapacitated until he misses two dates.

59 And Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى [al-Hidayah]

f: When the Mukatab is again incapacitated does he become a normal slave again?
b: Yes, and whatever he earned belongs to the owner.

f: The Mukatab possesses the amount of the contract. Does his death annul the contract?
b: No, the amount of the Kitabah will be taken from his wealth and he will be deemed to have been free in the final part of his life.

f: After the court ruled that he was freed in the final part of his life and the amount of the Mukatabah taken from his wealth, some wealth was left. [i.e. the Mukatab possessed the amount of the contract but died]
b: His heirs will take it.

f: What is the status of his children? [i.e. of the Mukatab who possessed the amount of the contract but died]
b: They will also be deemed to have been freed.

f: The Mukatab did not leave enough to fulfil the contract and left behind a child born during the Kitabah period. What is the status of the child? Does it remain upon the Kitabah?
b:
The child will be a Mukatab and will pay according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى according to the dates of his father. Once he fulfils the amount the father will be deemed to have been freed before his death and the child will be freed as well.

If the Mukatab bought a boy during the Kitabah, the boy will either have to pay up the amount immediately or revert to full slavery.

f: A Muslim man demanded pig or wine from his slave as Kitabah. What is the status of the agreement?
b: The Kitabah is fasid.

f: If the Mukatab then pays the pig or wine will he be deemed free? [i.e. a Muslim man demanded pig or wine from his slave as Kitabah]
b: Yes, but he will have to earn the price of it and pay an amount not less than the stated amount but it can increase.

f: The Kitabah was for the value of the Mukatab himself. What is the status of this agreement?
b:
It is Fasid because the price is unknown in terms of number, type and description. Nevertheless, if he does pay it he is freed.60

60 Because he is the substitute.

f: The owner agreed to a Kitabah for an unspecified animal or cloth of unspecified type. What is the status of the Kitabah?
b:
It is valid in the first case, not the second.61

61 Meaning that if he specified the species but not the quality; it will be interpreted as medium quality. The owner will be forced to accept the price. If he did not specify the specie, e.g. he only says "A beast", then it is not valid. There are many species thus the requirement is completely unknown. [al-Hidayah]

f: The owner makes a Kitabah with his two slaves for 1000 Dirham. Is this correct?
b: Yes, thus if they render the amount they will both be freed, if they are unable, both revert to normal slavery.

f: He made a Kitabah of two slaves whereby each is liable for the other. Is this valid?
b: Yes, whichever pays the entire amount frees both of them and will claim half the amount from the other.

f: He [i.e. the slave owner] made a Kitabah and then freed the Mukatab. What is the ruling?
b: He is freed with the manumission and the amount of the Kitabah is forfeit.

f: The owner made a Kitabah agreement and then died. Is the agreement nullified?
b: No, the Mukatab will continue to pay the heirs upon the agreed dates.

f: If one of the heirs frees him, [i.e. the owner made a Kitabah agreement and then died] is his manumission valid?
b: If one frees him, he is not free. If they all free him then he will be free and the amount is forfeit.

f: Can the owner make Kitabah with his Ummul Walad?
b: Yes, but if he dies before the amount is paid she is still freed due to being his Ummul Walad.

f: He made Kitabah with his slave-girl and then impregnated her and she bore his child. What does she do?
b: She can either continue paying to free herself; or she can declare herself incapacitated and await his death for her freedom as her Ummul Walad.

f: What is the ruling if he makes Kitabah with his Mudabbar?
b: The Kitabah is valid. If the owner dies and leaves no wealth besides the slave, then he can either compensate the estate two-thirds of his value or the full Kitabah amount.

f: A man made Kitabah with his slave-girl then Tadbir. What is her status?
b: The Tadbir is valid. She maychoose to fulfil the Kitabah or she may incapacitate herself in which case the laws of Tadbir will apply upon her.

f: If she chose the Kitabah [i.e. a man made Kitabah with his slave-girl then Tadbir] and the owner dies, will she be freed on the basis of Tadbir?
b:
According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى if she chose the Kitabah and the owner dies and she is his only wealth, then she may either pay two-thirds of the Kitabah amount to the estate or two-thirds of her value.62

62 According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى she will pay whichever is the lesser of the two.

f: A Mukatab bought a slave from the Kitabah money. He then frees the bought slave in exchange for money. Is that permissible?
b: No.

f: If he [i.e. a Mukatab bought a slave from the Kitabah money] instead gives this bought slave as a gift in exchange for compensation?
b: The gift is not valid.

f: What is the ruling if the Mukatab makes Kitabah with the bought slave? [i.e. a Mukatab bought a slave from the Kitabah money]
b: The Kitabah is valid. If the second one pays his amount before the first then he is free and his wala is owned by the original owner. If the pays after the first Mukatab then the first Mukatab has his Wala.

f: Can the Mukatab get a slave-girl he bought married?
b:
Yes he can.63

63 Because he wil acquire the Mahr, hence it is an earning.

f: What is Wala linguistically and in Shar'iah?
b: It is derived from Wali, meaning "near". In Shari'ah it is the right of the ex-owner arising from freeing his slave; or Muwalah agreement. Thus there are two kinds of Wala - Walaul 'Itaqah [manumission] & Walaul Mawalah [voluntary clientship].

f: Explain the laws related to Walaul 'Itaqah.
b: When a man frees his slave, male or female, then he holds Walaul 'Itaqah. This is whether he frees him in exchange for wealth or for free. If the Mukatab is freed after the death of the owner then the heirs hold the Walaul 'Itaqah.

f: A man made Tadbir with his male or female slave, or he made his slave-girl Ummul Walad. Who holds the Wala?
b: The Mawla [owner] holds the Wala because they were freed through him.

f: You have mentioned that if one holds one's Mahram relative then the relative is freed. Does the owner then hold Wala?
b:
Yes, the owner holds Wala.64

64 An example is if one of two sisters buys their father and he then dies. The two sisters together inherit two-thirds as per the Quranic stipulation and the one who bought him gets another thirds as Wala holder. If there are no 'asabah relatives because Wala is further than 'asabah.

f: One man's slave married another's slave-girl. The slave-girl's owner then frees her after the slave husband had impregnated her? Who holds the child's Wala?
b:
The child is freed with its mother and its Wala is held by the one who freed the mother. It will not aver from him ever. The same applies if she gave birth to the child in less than six months.65

65 Because it is certain that she was pregnant with it at the time of manumission.

f: If she gave birth [i.e. one man's slave married another's slave girl, and the slave-girl's owner then frees her after the slave husband had impregnated her] after more than six months since manumission, who has the Wala of the child?
b: The mother's owner has the child's Wala as well, unless the child's father was also freed, in which case the Wala goes to the father's ex-owner.

f: A non-'Arab married a slave-girl whom an 'Arab had freed. She then has children. What is the status of the children in terms of Wala?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the mother's ex-owners hold the Wala. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the father holds the Wala because lineage is attributed to fathers.

f: A man frees his slave and stipulates that he does not hold his Wala, but the Muslims in general hold it. Is this valid?
b:
No, Wala is established to the one who freed the slave. His denial of it has no effect.66 

66 Because the stipulation contradicts the clear words of the Hadith, "Wala is for the one who frees." [al-Jawharah]

f: What is the effect of this Wala? [i.e. a man frees his slave and stipulates that he does not hold his Walah, but the Muslims in general hold it]
b: It has the effect of including one amongst the 'Asabah, who are those who inherit after the Ashab al-Furud [those stipulated in the Quraan. If the freed slave has 'Asabah in terms of lineage then they are more entitled than the ex-owner. If he does not have such 'Asabah, then the ex-owner inherits. The ex-owner is less entitled than the 'Asabah of lineage and more entitled than Zawil Arham [relatives not 'Asabah].

f: The ex-owner dies then the freed slave dies. The ex-owner has children. Who inherits the slave's estate?
b:
The sons of the ex-owner inherit, not the daughters.67 

67 Because the Wala is based on 'Asabah, which does not include females.

f: Do women acquire Walaul 'Itaqah?
b:
Yes, if women free a slave, or the slave they freed frees a slave; or they make Kitabah or the slave they made Kitabah with made Kitabah; or they made Tadbir or the slave they made Tadbir with made Tadbir; or drawing Wala of those they freed68; or the freed one of one they freed.

68 The scenario if the drawing: A woman owns a slave. With her permission he marries a slave-girl who was freed. She then bears his child. The child's Wala is held by the ex-owners of the mother. If the woman then frees her slave, the child's Wala becomes drawn to himself. The ex-owner then draws that to herself.
The scenario of drawing the Wala of a freed slave's freed slave is that a woman freed a slave then that slave bought a slave. The second slave then married a freed slave-girl who then bore his child. The ex-owners of the mother hold the child's Wala. If the first slave frees the second slave, the second slave draws the child's Wala, then the first slave draws it to himself, then the woman's ex-owner draws it to herself.

f: The ex-owner dies. He leaves behind a son and sons of another son. The freed-slave then dies. Who takes the inheritance of the freed-slave?
b: The son inherits, not the grandsons. Wala goes to the most senior i.e. the closest, and the son is closer to the deceased than the grandsons.

f: Explain Walaul Mawalah and its regulations.
b: When a man embraces Islaam on the hands of another and establishes Wala with him whereby the second man will inherit from him and pay any blood money that may arise; or if he establishes the Wala with one besides the man on whose hands he had embraced Islaam then the Wala is valid and the Mawla is liable for the blood money. If the man dies without heirs the Mawla inherits from him. If there is an heir, the heir is more entitled than the Mawla.

f: Two men established Wala. Can one of them change Wala to another man?
b:
It is allowed as long as the Mawla did not yet pay any blood money on his behalf.

NOTE: The Mawla of Walaul 'Itaqah cannot make Walaul Mawalah.69

69 The two differ in three aspects: In Walaul Mawalah both inherit from each other if they both agree, unlike Walaul 'Itaqah. Secondly, Walaul Mawalah can be cancelled unlike Walaul 'Itaqah. Thirdly, Walaul Mawalah has less entitlement than Zawail Arham, Walaul 'Itaqah is the opposite. [al-Jawharah].

f: What is Ibaq?
b: It is the deliberate, disobedient running away of a slave from his owner. The runaway is called Abiq.

f: A man returns a runaway slave to his owner. Does the man deserve a reward?
b: Yes, if he returned him from a distance of three days' journey or more then the owner must give him 40 Dirham. If less than that, then in proportion.

f: And if the slave is worth less than 40 Dirham? [i.e. he ran away but someone brought him back]
b: He will be paid the slave's price, less 1 Dirham.

f: A man seizes a runaway slave to return him to his owner. The slave escapes from the man. What is the status of his reward?
b: He is not entitled to a reward just as he is not liable for the slave escaping from him. It is apporpriate for him to make witnesses that he is taking the runaway to his owner when he seizes him.

f: The runaway was Rahn. A man seized him and returned him. Is his reward due from the Rahim or Murtahin?
b: Murtahin.

f: What are the linguistic and Shar'i definitions of Jinayah?
b: Linguistically it is to commit an act which causes harm to someone. In the terminology of the Fuqaha it is the transgression of one party against another in his life or appendages. Transgression in life means murder, whether it is deliberate or accidental. Transgression against appendages means cutting a hand, leg, ear or putting out an eye etc.

f: Are there different kinds of Qatl [murder]?
b:
There are five kinds:
Amad [premeditated]
Shibhu 'Amad [resembling premeditated]
Khata [mistake]

That which is legally deemed a mistake.
al-Qatl bi sabab [killing via a means]

f: Explain the regulations of these five categories [i.e. of the different kinds of Qatl (murder)]:
b:
Premeditated murder is the deliberate striking with a weapon or what can be used as a weapon such as a sharp piece of wood or stone. It is a sin and causes the perpretrator to be disinherited. Qisas [retaliation] will be implemented unless the Awliya [family] forgives him. No Kaffarah is accepted.
Shibhu 'Amad is the deliberate striking with that which is neither a weapon nor is used as a weapon. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى if one strikes with a large rock or large wood then it is also regarded as 'Amad. They define Shibhu 'Amad as deliberately striking with that which generally does not kill. In either case, both parties agree that it is a sin and Kaffarah must be paid. There is no Qisas, but there is Diyah Mughallazhah upon the 'Aqilah. We shall explain the meanings of these terms later InshaAllaah.
Khata consists of two kinds: Mistake in intention, e.g. a man shot another, thinking him to be prey. Mistake in action, e.g. he aimed at  a target but it hit a man instead. In these cases he is not guilty of murder but must pay Kaffarah which is Diyah to the 'Aqilah.
That which is legally deemed a mistake, e.g. someone is sleeping and turns over onto another person, killing him. The ruling is the same as Khata.
al-Qatl bi sabab e.g. a man digs a well or places a rock in a property which is not his. Someone slips and dies. He must pay Kaffarah, and diyah to the 'Aqilah.70

70 But he is not disinherited.

f: What is Qisas?
b: It is the killing of the murderer in retaliation for the life of the victim. It is Wajib for the killing of every person whose blood is held permanently sacred when killing deliberately.

f: What is the ruling of a freeman killing a freeman or a slave; or a slave killing a freeman or a slave?
b: In each case the murderer will be executed irrespective whether the murderer is slave/freeman or the viction is slave/freeman.

f: What is the ruling of retaliation for killing a Zimmi and Mustamin [foreign Kafir who obtained permission to enter tje lands of Islaam]?
b: A Muslim will be executed for killing a Zimmi. Neither a Muslim nor a Zimmi will be ececuted for killing the Mustamin.

f: What is the ruling if a man killed a woman; or a woman killed a man; or an adult killed a minor; or a healthy person killed a blind/chronically ill/insane/one who lost limbs?
b: Retaliation will occur in all these cases. Allaah says, "We had decreed upon them that a life for a life and an eye for an eye and a nose for a nose and ear for ear and a tooth for a tooth and retaliation for wounds." [al-Maidah:45]

f: Is there retaliation if a man killed his son/slave/Mudabbar/Mukatab/son's slave?
b: No.

f: A man has the right to claim retaliation against his father. Will the father be executed?
b: No, the execution wil be lifted due to respect of the fatherhood.

f: A child or madman deliberately killed. Will they be executed?
b: Their premeditated murder is deemed Khata. The 'Aqilah will pay Diyah.

f: What is the ruling if the killer pays a compromise to the Awliya of the victim?
b: The execution is omitted and the money is Wajib, however little or much it may be.

f: If one of the partners foregoes the retaliation; or compromises on his share for a cosideration, what do the rest do?
b: Retaliation is foregone in both cases. The remaining parties are still entitled to their shares of the Diyah. The murderer should not give them difficulty but should pay them in a good way, just as the family of the victim should not harm him. Allaah says, "He who is pardoned for killing his brother then he must be pursued in a good manner and payment made with kindness." [al-Baqarah:178]

f: A man killed several people. The victims' demanded retaliation. What is the ruling?
b: He will be executed as soon as retaliation is demanded for one of them. The claims of the rest are then forfeit.

f: A group of people killed one person. Will they be executed?
b: Yes, all will be executed.

f: A murderer died before he could be executed. What is the ruling?
b: The retaliation is forfeit. Nothing can be claimed from his estate.

f: A slave confesses to premeditated murder. Will he be executed?
b: Yes.

f: A man shot another deliberately. The arrow continued and killed another. What is the ruling?
b: He will be executed for the first murder and must pay Diyah to the 'Aqilah of the second victim.

f: A man made Kitabah with his slave. The Mukatab was then killed. Who is entitled to retaliation?
b: If the Mukatab has no other heir besides the owner, then the owner has right of retaliation if he did not leave enough to cover the Kitabah. If he did leave enough, and the heir is not the Mawla, then the Mawla does not have retaliation, even if the heirs are joined with the Mawla.

f: A man left his slave as colleteral. That slave was killed. Will the killer be executed?
b: Yes, retaliation is Wajib on condition that the Rahin and Murtahin both demand it.

f: A man wounded another. The victim remained wounded and bedridden until he died. Is there retaliation?
b: Yes.

f: How are executions performed?
b: Executions are only done by sword.

f: What are the laws of retaliation for body parts?
b:
If a man cuts the hand of another from the joint, the cutter's hand will be amputated. Similarly if he cuts a leg or soft part of the nose, those organs will be amputed from the cutter.
If a man strikes another on the eye and thereby puts it out then there is no retaliation. If the eye remains but is blinded, then there is retaliation. A mirror will be heated. Moist cotton will be placed on his eye. His other eye will face the mirror until it is blinded.71 
If a man extracts the tooth of another then there is retaliation. There is no retaliation in bones, other than teeth.
There is retaliation for fracturing a skull where fracturing can be mimicked.
There is no retaliation for cutting of the tongue or the penis, unless it is cut from the glans.72 
There is no retaliation between a man and a woman besides retaliation for a life; just as there is no retaliation between a freeman and a slave, and between two slaves for anything besides life.
There is retaliation for organs between a Muslim and a Zimmi.
A man cuts into half a man's arm and it heals. There is no retaliation.
If an internal wound is afflicted and it heals then there is no retaliation.
If a man with a cripple or defective hand cuts a non-defective hand then the victim has a choice - he can either have the perpetrator's defective hand cut with no further claim, or he can demand complete Arsh. (Diyaat - compensation)
A man fractures the skull of another, temple to temple. The victim has a choice. He can demand retaliation, beginning from whichever temple he wishes, or he can demand complete Arsh. (Diyaat - compensation)
If two men cut the hand of one man then there is no retaliation. Each of them must pay half the Diyah of a life.
A man cuts the right hands of two men. They both present their claims. They can cut off his hand and take half Diyah of life which will be shared in two halves amongst them. If one presents the case and has his hand cutoff, then the other can claim half Diyah.
Shibhu 'Amad is only found in life retaliation. Everything else is 'Amad or Khata.

71 This is according to the medical knowledge of the time. If modern medicinal methods are used, then there is no problem as long as the limits of retaliation have not been exceeded.

72 i.e. if the tongue is partially cut. If cut from the root, then there is retaliation according to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. As for the penis, it erects and subsides, hence equality in retaliation is impossible. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى there is retaliation if cut from the root.

f: What is Diyah linguistically and in Shari'ah?
b: It is a root-word on the scale of 'idah whereby the Faul Kalimah has been dropped. The grammatical sequence is read, "wada yadi wadyan wa diayatan fahuwa wadin." In Shari'iah it is money which becomes Wajib upon the killer when he committed Khata, or Shibu 'Amad, or cut an organ. The compensation for cutting organs is also called Arsh.

f: Explain the rules and amount of Diyah.
b:
When a man kills another Shubhu 'Amad then the killer's 'Aqilah must pay Diyah Mughallazha and the killer must give Kaffarah. According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى Diyah Mughallazhah is 100 camels as follows - 26 Bint Makhad [female in second year]; 25 Bint Labun [female in third year]; 25 Hiqqah [in fourth year]; and 25 Jaza'ah [in fifth year]. There is no Mughallazh in anything besides Shibhu 'Amad; and when Diyah is decided upon as anything besides camels then there is also no Mughallazh even in Shibhu 'Amad.
In Qatlul Khata, Diyah is Wajib upon the 'Aqilah and Kaffarah upon the killer. The Diyah here is in five groups - 20 Bint Makhad [female in second year]; 20 Ibn Makhad [male]; 20 Bint Labun [female in third year]; 20 Hiqqah [in fourth year]; and 20 Jaza'ah [in fifth year]. This Diyah is not Mughallazh.
Diyah in gold is 1000 Dinar and in silver is 10,000 Dirham.

According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى there is only these three kinds of Diyah. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى Diyah is of these three categories as well as cattle, goats and clothing. If the court rules according to cattle, it will be 200 head of cattle, if goats then 1000, if clothing then 200 sets - each set being two pieces of clothing.
A complete Diyah of a life is Wajib in Shibhu 'Amad and Khata and is Mughallazh in the first case.
A complete Diyah - 100 camels - is due for cutting of a nose, tongue or penis.
A complete Diyah is due if one struck a man on the head, making him lose his mind.
A complete Diyah is due if one plucked or shaved a man's beard and it did not regrow.
A complete Diyah is due if one plucked or shaved a man's head and the hair did not regrow.
A complete Diyah is due if one hit a man or otherwise did such an act which resulted in him losing his eyebrows or eyes.
A complete Diyah is due if one cut both hands/legs/ears.
A complete Diyah is due if a man's lips or two middle incisors were cut; or a woman's two nipples were cut.
If one of these things were cut then it is a half Diyah.
A complete Diyah is due if the eyelids were cut. If one eyelid was cut then a quarter Diyah.
Each finger or toe, irrespective which is a tenth of a Diyah.
For every joint of a finger or toe which has three joints the Diyah is a third of the Diyah of the digit. Similarly it is half for every digit which has two joints.
If all the fingers of a hand are cut, or the palm is cut with the fingers, then it is half Diyah in both cases.
If the arm is cut up to half the forearm, then for the fingers and arm there is half Diyah. Excess is judged by a just person.
For an extra finger will be the ruling of a just person.
If a toe is cut off and an adjacent toe becomes lame as a result, then there is Arsh for the two and not Diyah according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى.
For every tooth there are 5 camels. Molars and other teeth are treated equally.
If a tooth is taken out and another grows in its place then the Arsh is forfeit.
If an organ is struck and loses its use, then there is full Diyah just as if it was cut, e.g. if an arm becomes paralysed or an eye is blinded.
If it is undetermined whether an eye/tongue/penis ofa child does not function then the ruling of a just person is made.

f: Explain the kinds of skull wounds.
b:
There are ten kinds:
Hasirah [scratching the skin without bleeding]

Dami'ah [blood emerges but does not flow]

Damiyah [blood flows]

Badi'ah [the skin is cut]

Mutalahimah [the flesh is penetrated]

Simhaq [the periosteum or skin between the flesh and bone is penetrated]

Muwaddihah [the bone is exposed]

Hashimah [the bone is broken]

Munaqqilah [the bone moves after being broken]

Ammah [penetrates to the brain]

f: What are the rulings of these wounds? [i.e. skull wounds]
b:
Muwaddihah - if deliberate then there is Qisas.

There is no retaliation in other kinds of wounds.73
Anything less than Muwaddihah will be according to the judgement of a just person.

For Muwaddihah there will be a twentieth of Diyah if it was accidental.
For Hashimahi there will be a tenth of Diyah.
For Munaqqilah there will be a tenth of twentieth of Diyah.
For Ammah a third of Diyah.
For Jaifah74 there is a third of Diyah. If it penetrates both [hollows] then it is two Jaifah and for that there is two-thirds of Diyah.
73 Because exact equality cannot be assured.

74 Wound which penetrates to the hollow of the stomach or back.

f: A man wounded another Muwaddihah. As a result he lost his senses or hair. Does he pay two Diyah?
b:
No, the Arsh of Muwaddihah is included in the Diyah.75

75 Because the loss of senses is the loss of the benefit of all organs and the loss of hair is accounted in a Muwaddihah wound.

f: What is the ruling if he lost his hearing or sight or both?
b:
The Arsh of Muwaddihah and the complete Diyah are both payable.76

76 According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى Arsh of Muwaddihah is included in Diyah of hearing and speech but not sight.

f: A man wounded another's skull Mutalahimah. No trace remained and the hair grew again. What is the ruling?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the Arsh is forfeit. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he is liable for the Arsh of the pain. According to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he is liable for the doctor's expenses.

f: A man wounds another whereby retaliation becomes Wajib. When will it be taken?
b: When the victim recovers, not before.

f: A man cut another's hand by accident. Then before he could recover he killed him by accident. Do two Diyah become Wajib?
b:
He is liable for a complete Diyah and the Arsh of the hand is forfeit. If he recovered before being killed then there is Diyah of the hand and another for the life.

NOTE: The Diyah of a Muslim and a Zimmi are equal. The DIyah of a woman is half that of a man.

f: A man dug a well in the pathway of the Muslims or placed a rock there. As a result a human got killed. What is the ruling?
b: His 'Aqilah is responsible for a complete Diyah. We had mentioned before that there is no Kaffarah.

f: What is the ruling if an animal got killed? [i.e. a man dug a well in the pathway of the Muslims or placed a rock there.]
b: He is liable to pay for it.

f: A man constructs a skylight or gutter along the road. It falls and kills a man. What is the ruling?
b: Complete Diyah is liable, the 'Aqilah is responsible for it.

f: A man dug a well in his own property. Someone died because of it. Is the digger liable?
b: No.

f: A wall started leaning towards the road of the Muslims. The owner was requested to break and he did not. The wall then fell and killed someone or caused loss of wealth. Is the owner liable?
b: If witnesses were made to the request for demolishing the wall and he did not demolish it within a time that he could, then he is liable for whatever life or wealth is lost.

f: A Zimmi requested that he demolish it. [i.e. A wall started leaning toward the road of the Muslims. The owner was requested to break and he did not. The wall then fell and killed someone or causes loss of wealth] Is his rights the same as a Muslim's in this?
b: A Muslim and a Zimmi are the same in this.

f: A wall was leaning on a man's house. Someone besides the house's owner requested the wall to be demolished. The wall's owner did not, and it fell, destroying life or property. Is he liable?
b: The request is the exclusive prerogative of the house's owner. If there are other inhabitants then they may also request it.

f: If a mount knocks something, who is liable?
b: The rider is liable for what it tramples or destroys with its forelegs or bites. He is not liable for what is knocked by its hind legs or tail.

f: If the mount urinated or defecated in the road, by which a human got killed, is the rider liable?
b: No.

f: You only mentioned a rider. What about one who drags or pushes an animal? [i.e. if the animal knocks something]
b: The one who brings the animal up from its behind is responsible for the damage of its forelegs and hind legs. The one who brings the animal up from front is responsible ofr its forelegs, not hind legs.

f: A man leads a herd. One of the animals tramples a man or wealth. What is the ruling?
b: He is liable. If he had someone bringing the animals from behind as well then both are liable.

f: Two horsemen collided and died. Who is liable?
b: The 'Aqilah of each will pay the Diyah of the other.

f: Who is liable for the accidental violation of the slave?
b: The owner can either hand the slave over to the victim or he can ransom the slave by paying the Arsh of the violation.

f: If he commits a crime a second time? [i.e. who is liable for the accidental violation of the slave]
b: The ruling of the second is the same as that of the first.

f: What is the ruling if he commits two violations?
b: The owner may either hand him over to the two victims who will share him as per the value of their rights, or the owner may ransom him by paying the Arsh of both victims.

f: A slave committed a violation. His owner then set him free, knowing about the violation. What is the ruling?
b: The ex-owner is liable to pay the Arsh.

f: Who is liable if a Mudabbar or Ummul Walad commits a crime?
b: The owner is liable. He will pay whatever is the lesser of the slave's price and the Arsh.

f: If the slave commits another crime, and the owner had already paid the slave's price to a victim, what must the owner do now?
b: If he made the first payment through a court order, then he does not pay anything. The second claimant will claim from the first and they will share in what the first claimant took. If it was without a court order, then the second claimant may either claim from the slave's owner or from the first claimant.

f: A man killed a slave by mistake. What is he liable for?
b: He will be liable for the price of the slave. If however the price is 10,000 Dirham or more, then he will pay 10,000 less 10.

f: A man killed a slave-girl by mistake. What is he liable for?
b:
He is liable for her price. If her price is more than Diyah, then he must pay 5,000 less 5.77

77 Al-Hidayah mentioned "less 10", which is the Zhahirur Riwayah. Al-Quduri mentions the narration of al-Hasan from Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى.

f: What is a man liable for if he cuts off the hand of a slave?
b: He is liable for the price of the slave to an amount not exceeding 5,000 less 5. Whatever is valued in terms of Diyah for a free victim, is valued according to the price of the slave in regards his organs.

f: A man struck a freewoman's belly. As a result she had a miscarriage. What is he liable for?
b:
He is liable for Ghurrah which is a twentieth of a Diyah.78 

78 i.e. a twentieth of the Diyah of a man (500 Dirham), whether the foetus is male or female. This is when at least part of the foetus's form has become apparent. According to us the 'Aqilah must pay it within a year. [al-Jawharah]

f: If the baby came out prematurely because of the strike, [i.e. a man hit the belly of a pregnant woman], but was alive and only died later, what is the penalty?
b:
Complete Diyah.79

79 Upon the 'Aqilah [al-Jawharah]

f: What is the pentalty if she drops the dead foetus and then she herself died? [i.e. if someone hit a pregnant woman]
b: Complete Diyah for the mother and Ghurrah for the foetus.

f: And if she died and then the dead foetus emerged? [i.e. a man hit a pregnant woman]
b: Complete Diyah for the mother and nothing for the foetus.

f: If the mother died then the baby emerged alive and then died, what is the penalty? [i.e. if a man hit a pregnant woman]
b: Two Diyah.

f: What do you say if someone struck a slave-girl's stomach and she had a miscarriage?
b: If the dead foetus is male then the penalty is a twentieth of the boy's value had it lived; and if it is female then a tenth of the price.

f: Who is the recipient of the foetus' penalty? [i.e. if a man hit a pregnant woman]
b: If the mother was a freewoman then the penalty will be shared by the heirs of the foetus according to their inheritance shares. If the mother was a slave then her owner gets the penalty money.

f: You have mentioned that Kaffarah is due in the killing of Shibhu 'Amad and Khata. Explain whether this is Kaffarah.
b: Allaah has explained the Kaffarah of killing in SUratun Nisa, "... freeing a believing slave. He who does not find should fast two consecutive months as obtaining Allaah's forgiveness".

f: Is there Kaffarah for killing a slave, slave-girl or foetus?
b: No.

f: Can one not feed the poor as in Kaffarah of Zhihar?
b: No.

f: A man was found murdered in a certain district. The murderer is not known. How will the murder be investigated?
b: Rasulullaah ﷺ has taught a way for it. It is to take an oath from 50 men of that district. This process is called Qasamah.

f: Who chooses these 50? [i.e. for Qasamah when there's been a murder] How are the paths taken?
b: The Wali of the victim will choose them. There may not be any children, madmen, women, slaves, Mudabbars or Mukatabs amongst them. They will swear, "By Allaah, we neither killed him, nor do we know who killed him."

f: Are they completely absolved once they have taken the oath? [i.e. after 50 men have been summoned for Qasamah after there's been a murder]
b: No, the people of that district must pay Diyah.

f: If the Wali himself is of that district [i.e. where there was a murder], will the oath be taken from him as well?
b: He will not be forced to take the oath. He will not contribute to the Diyah even if he takes the oath.

f: The Wali chose the 50 men. [i.e. for Qasamah after a murder] Some of them refused to take the oath. What will be done?
b: They will be detained until they take the oath.

f: The Wali chose less than 50 men. [i.e. for Qasamah after a murder] What will be done?
b: Those chosen will repeat their oaths until 50 oaths have been taken.

f: A corpse was found with no sign of murder. Will Qasamah occur and Diyah paid?
b: There is neither Qasamah nor Diyah in this case.

f: Is there Qasamah if a corpse was found with blood flowing from its nose, anus or mouth?
b: This will not be regarded as murder. There will be neither Qasamah nor Diyah.

f: What is the ruling if blood is flowing from its eyes or ears? [i.e. when a corpse is found]
b: It will be deemed a murder and Qasamah will occur.

f: A man leads a beast on which a murdered corpse is found. What is the ruling?
b: The Diyah is Wajib up the 'Aqilah of that man, not of the district.

f: A man was found murdered in someone's house. Who will take the oath?
b: Only the person of the house will take the oath. The Diyah is upon his 'Aqilah.

f: Some of the residents of houses of a district are owners and others are tenants. Will the oath be taken from all of them? [i.e. Qasamah for murder]
b:
According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the tenant will not take the oath with the original owners who according to him are those for whom the ruler had allocated the land, not those who bought property there, even if there is only one of the original owners left.80

80 According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the buyers will also be included. [Sharhuzz Zayla'i]

f: Who will take the oath if a murder victim is found on a ship?
b: The passengers and sailors who are on the ship.

f: Who takes the oath if the corpse is found in the local Masjid?
b: Upon the people of the district.

f: If he is found [i.e. a corpse] in the Jam' Masjid or the Highway, from which district will the 50 men be chosen?
b: There is no Qasamah in these two scenarios. The Diyah will be paid from the Baytul Mal [Public Treasury]

f: If he is found between two towns [i.e. the corpse] upon who is the Qasamah?
b: Upon whichever town is closer.

f: If the corpse is found in the desert, who takes the oath?
b:
If there are no buildings nearby81 then no oath will be taken and there will be no consequence for his blood.

81 Nearby buildings are as defined previously as based upon if a shout can be heard.

f: If the corpse is found in a river, who will take the oath?
b: If the corpse was found in the middle of flowing water then there is no consequence to his blood. If it was found trapped on a bank, then the people of the nearest town will take the oath.

f: If the Wali makes an accusation against a specific person, does the Qasamah fall away from the rest?
b: No.

f: What is the ruling if he [i.e. the Wali] accuses a specific person who is not one of them? [i.e. the group of 50 people]
b: The Qasamah and Diyah fall away from them.

f: A man asked to take an oath testified to a specific person having committed the murder. Will his word be taken?
b: No, he will be made to swear, "By Allaah, I neither killed hi, nor do I know anybody to have killed him besides so-and-so."

f: Two men testified that a man outside the district had committed the murder. Will their Arsh be accepted?
b:
No.82

82 According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى, It will be accepted according to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى.

f: You have often mentioned that the 'Aqilah pays the Diyah on behalf of the killer. What is the meaning of 'Aqilah?
b:
'Aql/Ma'qulah is the paying of Diyah on behalf of the killer. Those who do this are called the 'Aqilah. Every Diyah Wajib due to actual killing [i.e. excluding compromise payments] is Wajib upon the 'Aqilah. According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى 'Aqilah is those on the Diwan83 if the killer is from amongst them. The Diyah will be taken from their stipends84 over a three year period. If the stipends are issued after longer than three years or less, the Diyah will still be taken from there. If the killer is not of the people of the Diwan then the 'Aqilah is his tribe. They will pay over three years. Each member will not pay more than 4 Dirham, 1 and third per year. If the tribe has many members then the individual contributions will be reduced. The killer will be included in their number and will pay the same as any other member.

83 The registered names of the army.
84 The annual or twice-a-year allotments made to the soldiers.

f: If the tribe is unable to pay, how will the Diyah be fulfilled?
b:
The closest tribe will be joined to them.85

85 In terms of lineage. First the closest then the next closest will be joined as per the 'Asabah sequence. [al-Hidayah]

f: Explain in detail what the 'Aqilah is liable for and what not.
b:
The 'Aqilah is responsible for the following:
Diyah of Shibhu 'Amad. We mentioned before that this Diyah is Mughallazah.

Diyah of Qatl al-Khata.

Diyah of Qatl bi Sabab.

Diyah if someone constricted a skylight or gutter along the public way and it fell and killed someone.

The deliberate murder by a child or madman is deemed Khata. The 'Aqilah must pay the Diyah.
When freman commits a violation by mistake on a slave then his 'Aqilah is responsible.
The 'Aqilah is not responsible for the following Diyah:
Every 'Amad in which retaliation is dropped due to doubt results in the Killer paying the Diyah, not the 'Aqilah.
If a father kills his son deliberately then the Diyah is from his wealth over three years, not the 'Aqilah.
The 'Aqilah does not pay for a slave's violation.
The 'Aqilah is not responsible if the perpretrator confessed to the violation. The Diyah is from his money. If they however proclaim his innocence then they must pay.
The 'Aqilah is not liable for amounts due to Sulh.

f: Sundry Masail
b:
The 'Aqilah of a freed slave is his Mawla's tribe.
The Mawla and his tribe are 'Aqilah for the one who entered into Mawalah with him.
The 'Aqilah is not responsible for less than a twentieth of a Diyah. They bear from a twentieth and greater. Less than that is the responsibility of the perpretrator.

f: What is Hadd linguistically and in Shari'ah?
b: Linguistically it is "prevention". In Shari'ah it is every prescribed punishment inflicted as fulfilling Allaah's right.

f: For which sins is the Hadd prescribed?
b: The ruler will inflict the Hadd for Zina, drinking wine, slandering a chaste man or woman with Zina, and cutting the hand for stealing. We shall discuss the first three first.

f: Explain the Hadd of Zina.
b: There are two categories: 100 lashes for non-Muhsan, whether male or female; and Rajm or stoning for the Muhsan, male or female.

f: How do the courts establish Zina to have been committed?
b:
It is established through evidence or confession.

Evidence: Four witnesses testify that a man or a woman committed Zina. After they testify the court will question them, "What is Zina? How was it done? Where? When? With who?" Once they have clarified that and said, "We saw him penetrating her vagina just as an antimony-stick enters the antimony bottle", the judge will investigate the piety and justice of the witnesses. If they fulfil the requirements of justice in secret and open, he will rule according to their Arsh and inflict the Hadd. If their number falls below four or one of them is established as Fasiq [open sinner] then all the witnesses will be inflicted with the Hadd of slander.

Confession: A sane adult confesses four times to having committed Zina. The confessions will be four separate gatherings. Each time he confesses the judge will refuse him. It is recommended for the judge to refuse him in these words, "Perhaps you just touched or kissed her." When the person completes his confession as mentioned, the judge will ask him "What is Zina? How was it done? Where? With who?" Once he does that the Hadd becomes mandatory.

f: You have mentioned that a non-Muhsan is lashed 100 times. Describe this lashing.
b: His clothing will be removed except that which is needed to cover his private region. He will then be lashed with moderate force using a lash which does not have any fruits on it. The lashes must be spread over different body parts. The head, face, penis and vagina may not be lashed.

f: Is the ruling of a man and woman different? [i.e. regarding lashes as a non-Muhsan]
b: They are the same except that a woman's clothing will not be removed except for her furs and padding.

f: Should they stand or sit while being lashed? [i.e. the non-Muhsan]
b: The man will stand and the woman will sit.

f: What is Ihsan [state of being Muhsan]?
b:
Ihsan of stoning86 is for the perpretator to be a free, sane, adult Muslim who has had sex with his wife from a correct marriage.87 It is a condition that both husband and wife must be Muhsan.88 

86 As distinguished from Ihsan of slander which does not have the conditions of marriage and sex,
87 As distinguished from a Fasid marriage e.g. marriage without witnesses.
88 Each has to be Muhsan for the other to be Muhsan. Thus if a freewoman or a slave-girl marries a slave then there is no Ihsan unless he has sex with her after manumission. The Ihsan only counts thereafter. So if a Zimmi has adultery with a Muslimah then accepts Islam he will be lashed not stoned.

f: How is one who commits Zina after Ihsan stoned?
b: He will be flung with stones until he dies. The judge will take him out of the land here sentence will be executed. The witnesses must begin stoning, then the judge, then the people. If the witnesses refuse to begin, then the stoning falls away. If the perpretator had confessed, then the judge will begin, followed by the people. If a hole is dug to place the woman to be stoned it will be better.

f: Will the executed adulterer be given Ghusl and Salatul Janazah?
b: Yes.

f: A man has a slave or slave-girl who must be lashed for Zina. Will he do it himself?
b: He may not without court permission.

f: A man retracts his confession. Will the Hadd still be inflicted?
b: He will be released even if he recants before or during the stoning and his retraction will be accepted.

f: What is the ruling if a witness recants after the decision for stoning has been passed but before the implementation?
b: All the witnesses will be lashed for slander. The stoning falls away from the accussed. If one of the witnesses recants after the stoning, he alone will be lashed and will be liable for a quarter Diyah.

f: When will the Hadd be applied and when not
b:
If a man has non-vaginal sex with an unrelated woman he will receieve Ta'zir not Hadd.
He who has sex with the slave-girl of his son or his son's son will not receive the Hadd even if he says, "I knew that she is forbidden unto me."

A man had sex with the slave-girl of his father, or mother, or wife. If he says, "I thought she is permissible for me", he will not receive the Hadd. If he says, "I knew that she is forbidden unto me", he will receive the Hadd. Similarly if a slave has sex with his owner's slave-girl and he says, "I thought she is permissible for me", he will not receive the Hadd. If he says, "I knew that she is forbidden unto me", he will receive the Hadd.
The Hadd will be inflicted if one has sex with one's brother's slave-girl or paternal uncle's slave-girl, even if one says, "I thought that she is permissible for me."
There is no Hadd if the woman presents someone other than his bride on the wedding night and says that she is his wife. If he has sex with her he must pay Mahr.
The Hadd is applied if a man finds a woman on his bed and has sex with her.
There is no Hadd if a man marries a woman he is forbidden to and has sex with her.
According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى Ta'zir and not Hadd will be inflicted on one who has anal sex with a woman or commits the act of the people of Lut عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is the same as Zina and the Hadd will be applied.89 
There is no Hadd upon one who commits bestiality.
There is no Hadd upon one who committed Zina in the lands of the Kuffar or the rebels and then returned to the land of Islaam.
89 Ash-Shami mentions that the Hadd will not be applied for once-off sodomy but the ruler will execute the sodomite for repeat offences.

Ibnul Humam narrates that Abu Bakr رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ consulted the Sahabah and they agreed with 'Ali رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ that the homosexual should be burned.
According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ there is no Hadd for sodomy not because it is lighter than Zina, but because of clear evidence. It is worse than Zina, because Zina is understandable intellectually and according to human nature, not so sodomy.

f: Sundry rulings
b:
If a male or female slave commits Zina he/she will be lashed 50 times because the Hadd of slaves is half that of free people. They are not stoned due to lack of Ihsan.
A Muhsan will not be lashed and stoned.
A non-Muhsan will not be lashed and exiled unless the ruler sees a benefit in it. In that case he will exile him for a period he deems appropriate.
If witnesses testified to a Hadd committed a while back and the distance from the court was not a factor in preventing them from testifying, then their Arsh will not be accepted, except for slander.
If a sick man commits Zina whereby the sentence is stoning, it will be implemented. If the sentence is lashing it will be postponed until he has recovered.
A pregnant woman will not be punished with the Hadd until she has given birth. If the punishment is lashing, she will only be lashed after her Nifas. If stoning, then she will be stoned during the Nifas.

f: What is Hadd of Shurb?
b:
It is the punishment for drinking wine. He who drinks wine and is seized and is still stinking of wine, or confesses and is still smelling of wine, will be inflected with the Hadd. If he confesses after the stench has departed then there is no Hadd.

There is no Hadd until he becomes sober.
The drinking is established through the Arsh of two witnesses or if he confesses once. The Arsh of women with men will not be accepted here.

f: Is the Hadd applied for drinking anything besides wine?
b:
Hadd will be applied if he becomes intoxicated90 with Nabiz [date infused water]. He will not be lashed until it is known that he became drunk with it and drank willingly.91

90 I.e. he will not be lashed if not intoxicated, as opposed to wine, the mere drinking of which is punishable. [al-Jawharah]
91 It is possible that he became intoxicated with another substance or was forced.

f: A man stinks of wine or vomits it. There are no witnesses to him drinking, nor does he confess. Will the Hadd be applied?
b:
No.92

92 Since he might have been forced, or had no water and had to drink the wine. The doubt lifts the punishment.

f: What is the punishment for a drinker of wine and a drunkard?
b: He will be lashed 80 times. The lashes will be spread over his body as we have mentioned in Hadd of Zina.

f: A man confessed to drinking wine or became drunk, he then retracted his confession. What is the ruling?
b: The Hadd is lifted.

f: What is the punishment for a slave that drunk?
b: Half that of a freeman, i.e. 40 lashes.

f: What is Hadd of Qazf?
b: The punishment for one who explicitly93 slanders a male or female Muhsan [chaste] with Zina. It is estbalished by the Arsh of two men or the confession once of the slanderer. The Hadd becomes Wajib if the slandered party requests redress.

f: What is the punishment of the slanderer?
b: He will be lashed 80 times. The lashes will be spread over his body. His clothing will not be removed except for fur and padding. Allaah says, "Lash them 80 times and do not ever accept their Arsh."

f: What is the ruling if the slanderer is a slave?
b: The Hadd is halved. He will be lashed 40 times.

f: What are the requisites for Ihsan in this case? [i.e. with regards to Qafz/slander]
b: The slandered must be free, adult, sane, Muslim and chaste from Zina. He or she who fulfils these requirements is Muhsan and his or her slanderer will be lashed.

f: What is the ruling if someone confesses to slander and then recants?
b: The retraction will not be accepted. The slanderer will be lashed if the slandered so desires.

f: A man says to another, "You do not belong to your father". Is that slander?
b: Yes, he will be lashed.

f: A man says to another, "O son of adultery (i.e. bastard)". The second man's mother is deceased and she was Muhsan. What is the ruling?
b: If the man demands it, the slanderer will be lashed. The Hadd may not be demanded in the case of a slandered dead person except by one whose lineage is defiled by the slander, i.e. the son and father.

f: A man slandered a Muhsan. Can the Muhsan's Kafir son or slave demand the Hadd?
b: Yes.

f: A slave has a free mother. His owner slanders his mother. Can the slave demand the penalty of slander against his owner?
b: No.

f: A man says to an 'Arab, "O Nabatean!" or what the Nabateans call themself, "O son of Heavenly Water!  Will the Hadd be applied against him?
b: No, that is not considered slander.

f: A man attributes the lineage of a man to the man's paternal uncle, or maternal uncle, or mother's husband. Is that slander?
b: No.

f: A man committed forbidden sex and the other party is not his possession. Another man slanders him about it. What is the ruling?
b: There is no Hadd for this slander.

f: A man slanders his wife. They do Li'an at the court. The man then again slanders her. What is the ruling?
b: If the Li'an was for the purpose of denying a child's lineage then the husband slanders her, there is no Hadd. If it was for the sole purpose of the husband having accused her of adultery without the involvement of any child, then he will be lashed if he slanders her after the Lian.

f: A man slanders a slave, slave-girl or Kafir. Is there Hadd?
b: There is Ta'zir, not Hadd.

f: If he says to a Muslim, "O Fasiq [open sinner]/Kafir/Khabith [spiritual filthy]", is there Hadd?
b: No, there is Ta'zir.

f: Is there Ta'zir or Hadd if he says, "O donkey/pig"?
b: Neither.

f: Is there Diyah if someone died while being Islaamically lashed for Hadd/Ta'zir?
b: No.

f: Is there any additional punishment for the slanderer besides being lashed?
b: A Muslim who has been lashed for slander may never again testify even if he repents. Allaah says, "Lash them 80 times and do not ever accept their Arsh."

f: A Kafir slandered someone and received the Hadd. He thereafter embraced Islaam. Can he testify?
b:
Yes, his Arsh is accepted.

NOTE:
The maximum Ta'zir is 39 lashes and the minimum is 3. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ the maximum is 75.
The judge may also detain him in addition to the lashes.
The hardest lashing is for Ta'zir, then Hadd of Zina, then Hadd of drinking, then Hadd of slander.

f: What is Sariqah linguistically and in Shari'ah?
b: Literally it is to take wealth secretly. In Shari'ah it is a Mukallaf [person obligated by Islaamic Law] taking something worth 10 Dirham or more which have been demarcated according to possession or otherwise protected.

f: What punishment does the Shari'ah stipulate for the thief?
b: When a sane adult, slave or free, male or female, steals at least 10 Dirham or its value, whether in the form of currency or not, from the Hirz (demarcated for possession) in which there is no doubt, then it is Wajib to cut the thief's hand. Allaah says, "The male and female thief - cut off their hands because of what they have earned as a punishment from Allaah." [al-Maidah:38]

f: From where is the thief's hand cut?
b: The right hand is cleanly cut off at the wrist.

f: And if he steals a second time? [i.e. after a thief's right hand is cut off after stealing]
b: The left foot is cut. If he steals a third time then he will be indefinitely imprisoned until he repents.

f: A man stole at least 10 Dirham from a demarcated area. His left hand is lame or amputated, or his left leg has been cut off from before. Will the judge rule that his hand still be cut?
b: No.

f: How is theft established?
b: Through his confession once or the Arsh of two witnesses.

f: Must the one who was robbed be present at the cutting? [i.e. cutting of hand/foot]
b: The thief's hand cannot be cut unless the victim is present. He will be summoned to establish the theft. Thus if he had gifted the item to the thief, or sold it, or it is worth less than the prescribed amount i.e. 10 Dirham, the thief's hand may not be cut.

f: Besides having his hand cut, is the thief liable for the stolen amount?
b: If the item remains intact in his possession then he is liable to return it. If it has been destroyed, then he is not liable.

f: A group committed the left. Will all their hands be cut?
b: If the value of the stolen goods divided amongst them is worth at least 10 Dirham their hands will be cut. If it is worth less, then none of their hands will be cut.

f: What is deemed Hirz in this law?
b: There are two categories: Place such as buildings, houses and shops and personal. Thus if the thief stole from a demarcated place or the goods were guarded by a person then the thief's hand will be cut.

f: A group entered a Hirz with the intention of stealing. Some of them were appointed to do the actual stealing whilst the rest did not. Will all of their hands be cut?
b: Each member of the group will have his hand cut if the loot is divded and equals at least 10 Dirham per head.

f: A thief enters his hand in the money-box or in someone's pocket. Will his hand be cut?
b: If the loot is worth at least 10 Dirham, yes.
