f: A man broke the wall of a house. He stole goods and passed it onto his accomplice outside. Will their hands be cut?
b: No.

f: If he threw the goods outside and then picked it up, will his hand be cut?
b: Yes.

f: A man broke the wall of a house. He loaded loot onto his donkey and led it out. Will his hand be cut?
b: Yes.

f: If he pierced the wall and entered his hand inside whilst remaining outside, and took something, will his hand be cut?
b: No.

f: What is the ruling if someone stole something from the Masjid?
b: His hand will be cut if the owner of the goods was by the goods.

f: In which circumstances will a thief's hand not be cut?
b:
It will not be cut in these scenarios:
For items which is regarded as free and permissible for all in the lands of Islaam e.g. wood, grass and reeds and fish which is still in the water nad prey which is still in the wild.
Items which swiftly detoriate, e.g. fresh fruit, milk, meat, watermelon, fruits on the tree, unharvested crops.
Mutribah [ilicit party] drinks.

Tunbur [eastern mandolin]

Tabl, Daff [eastern drums] and flutes.

Mushaf of the Quraan, even if be jewelled.

Crucifix, even if it be of gold and silver.
Chess.
Backgammon.
Kidnapping a free child, even if he has jewels on him.
Abducting an adult slave. However, the hand is cut for stealing a minor slave.
Registers, except for accounting registers.
Dogs and cheetahs.
The one who cheats does not have his or her hand cut.
Grave robber.
A looter.
Embezzler.
One who steals from the public treasury or booty.
Wealth in which one has a share.
Stealing from a parent, child or blood related Mahram.
One spouse stealing from the other.
If a slave steals from his owner, or owner's spouse.
If the owner steals from his Mukatab.
Stealing from public baths or a building in which the public is allowed access.
A guest who steals from his host.
If the thief claims that the stolen item is his property, even if he does not produce evidence.

f: You mentioned that there is no cutting off hands for stealing wood. Which wood did you refer to?
b: Worthless wood which is not demarcated for ownership, If wood which has worth, which is sold and demarcated, is stolen then the thief's hand will be cut, if the value reaches 10 Dirham e.g. Indian oak, bamboo, ebony and sandalwood. Hands are also cut for stolen woodwork such as utensils and doors.

f: A man stole an item and his hand was cut for it. He returned the item to the owner and then stole it again. What is the ruling?
b: If the item remains in its condition as when he returned it, his hand will not be cut. If the condition has changed then his hand will be cut, e.g. he stole thread and his hand was cut. He returned it and it was then embroided. He then came and stole it a second time. He will again be cut.

f: What is the punishment of highway robbers?
b:
Allaah has explained it thus, "Verily the punishment for those who wage war against Allaah and His Rasul and strive to spread corruption is to be killed or crucified or to have the hands and feet cut from opposite sides or to be exiled from the land. That is a humiliation for them in the world. In the Aakhirat (Hereafter) is a great punishment. Except those who repent before you gain control over them. Then know that Allaah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful". [al-Maidah:33-34]

Thus if a gang or an individual capable of obstructing goes out with the aim of highway robbery, and they are apprehended before having stolen anything or killed anyone, the ruler will detain them until they repent. If they had stolen wealth of a Muslim or Zimmi, to the extent that if divided amongst them it would be worth at least 10 Dirham per head, then the ruler will cut their hands and feet from opposite sides.

If they killed anyone without taking any wealth, they will be killed as per the Hadd. If the victim's family wish to pardon them, their pardon will not be considered. If they both killed and plundered, then the ruler may either kill them or crucify them.94

94 Whether with cutting their hands and feet first, or just killing/crucifying them. [al-'Inayah]

f: What is the method of cruficixion?
b: He will be crucified whilst living. His belly will be pierced with a spear until he dies. He will not be crucified for more than three days.

f: What is the ruling if amongst the gang was a child, madman, or blood relative of the victim?
b: The Hadd is lifted from the rest as well. The issue of the murder is taken to the victims' Awliya who may have them killed or pardoned.

f: One of the Highway Robbers murdered. Will the responsibility be applied to the entire gang?
b: Yes.

f: Which drinks are forbidden to consume?
b:
There are four forbidden drinks:
Khamr [wine]: It is grape juice when it ferments and becomes intoxicating and emits foam.

'Asir [juice]95 when it is boiled unless less than two-thirds evaporates.

Naqi96 of dates when it ferments and intoxicates.

Naqi' of raising when it ferments and intoxicates.

95 i.e. a grape juice.

96 When dates/raisins is soaked in water in order to absorb its sweetness, the resultant water is called Naqi'

f: What do you say about boiled Nabiz of dates or raisins?
b: It reamins Halal if slightly boiled even if intoxication sets in it, when drunk and one's overwhelming thought is that it will not intoxicate, when drunk nor merely for entertainment or frivolity.

f: What is the ruling of Khalitan?98
b:
Halal.

98 Mixing the date and raisin water and boiling it slightly and leaving it until it becomes fermented and potentially intoxicating.

f: What is the ruling of Nabiz of honey, figs, wheat, barley and sorghum?
b:
They are Halal whether boiled or not99 when drunk without frivolity and entertainment.

99 According to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى they are Haram in large or small quantities because according to him that which intoxicates in large quantities in Haram in small quantities and is Najas also. The Fatwa is on this.

f: What is the ruling of grape juice if boiled until two-thirds evaporate?
b: It is Halal even if it is potentially intoxicating.

f: What is the status of wine if it becomes or is made into vinegar?
b: It is Halal to eat both cases.

f: What is the ruling of making it [i.e. wine] into vinegar?
b: Permissible.

f: What is the ruling of making Nabiz in Duba [bottle gourd], Hantam [green earthenware jar], Muzaffat [vessel coated with tar] and Naqir [hollowed palm]?
b: It was forbidden and then allowed. [In narration by Muslim.

f: What is Sayd?
b: It is the act of hunting and is applied to the hunted animal as well, i.e. a beast which refrains from humans, whether edible or not. Hunting wild beasts which are not in anyone's possession is permissible for non-Muhrims outside the Haram. Allaah says, "When you become Halal [you may] hunt."

f: How does a Muslim hunt?
b: Hunting is permissible by means of trained dogs, cheetahs, falcons and any other fanged or taloned trained beast or bird of prey. Allaah says, "Say: The pure things have been made permissible to you and that which you have trained of hunting beasts, you train them from what Allaah has taught you."

f: If the hunter sends out the trained dog or cheetah and it kills a beast, is it Halal?
b: If the animal is such an animal which is permissible to eat; the hunter recited the Name of Allaah when sending the trained animal; and the animal seized the prey and wounded it from which it died, then it is Halal to eat. Similarly if he sent a trained falcon or eagle and recited Allaah's Name, and the bird seized the animal and wounded it from which it died, then it is Halal.

f: Why have you stipulated wounding and death? [i.e. when sending a trained animal or trained falcon/eagle]
b: The wound is necessary for the animal to be Halal. Through it Zakah Idtirari [forced slaughter] is established. It is to wound the animal in any part of its body. The stipulated of death means that if the dog or falcon seized and wounded the animal and then left it alive and the hunter reaches it then he must slaughter it. In such a situation Zakah Ikthiyari [voluntary slaughter] is stipulated. If he does not slaughter it and it dies, then it cannot be eaten.

f: You have stipulated that the animal be trained. What does its training entail?
b: The training of a dog and cheetah is that it is taught to seize an animal and not eat from it. When it is trained to do that and avoids eating thrice, it is deemed trained. The training of a falcon is that it returns when summoned. That is the difference in the ruling of a trained dog and trained falcon. If the dog eats from the prey, the meat may not be eaten. However, if the falcon eats from it, it may be eaten. The condition for the falcon's training is only that it obeys when summoned and not that it does not eat from the prey.

f: If the dog or cheetah strangles the animal and it dies before being slaughtered, can it be eaten?
b: No.

f: The hunter despatched his trained dog. Another dog joined it in killing. The second dog was either a non-trained dog, the Fire-worshipper's dog, or a dog upon which Allaah's Name had not been recited upon despatch. What is the status of the meat?
b: It is not Halal to eat.

f: You have mentioned hunting by birds and beasts of prey. Is there another method of hunting?
b: Yes, hunting by shooting arrows. If a Muslim shoots an arrow at an animal and mentions Allaah's Name at the time of shooting, the flesh of an animal the arrow strikes may be eaten if the arrow wounds it and kills it. If the hunter reaches the prey and it is still alive, he must slaughter it. If he does not, the animal is not Halal.

f: He shot an animal which then fell into water. The hunter then found it dead. Or it fell on a mountain or roof and then bounced down to the earth and died. What is the ruling?
b: It is Haram to eat.

f: Does the ruling change if it fell [i.e. the animal shot with an arrow] on the earth in the beginning and then died?
b: Yes, in that case it is Halal.

f: A man shot an animal. It bore the arrow and disappeared. The hunter then found it dead. Can he eat it?
b: If the hunter continuously pursued it until he found it dead, then it is Halal. If he paused in his chase and then found it dead then it cannot be eaten.

f: What is the ruling if when shooting an animal, an organ is cut off?
b: The animal can be eaten, not the cut off organ.

f: What is the ruling if the animal got cut into two portions?
b: If cut into third portion and two-third portion, whereby the larger portion is the hind portion, then all may be eaten. In the major portion is the fore-portion then the major portion may be eaten and the rest abandonded.

f: The arrow was shot and its side struck the animal. What is the ruling?
b: The animal may not be eaten unless the arrow had wounded it.

f: What is the ruling of hunting with Bunduqiyah [catapult]?
b: If the animal is killed with a catapult then it may not be eaten. If it is still alive after being struck and then is slaughtered, it may be eaten.

f: A man shot an animal. He neither wounded it nor demarcated it. A second man shot and killed it. Does it belong to the first man or the second? Can it be eaten?
b: It belongs to the second man and can be eaten.

f: What is the ruling if the first man wounded it [i.e. animal] and then the second shit and killed it? [i.e. does it belong to the first man or the second?]
b: The matter is reversed. It belongs to the first man and cannot be eaten. The second is liable to the first for the value of the prey less the value of the damage the first caused.

f: Is it permissible to hunt animals whose flesh cannot be eaten?
b: Yes, both animals which can be eaten and those which cannot be eaten, can be hunted.

f: Is there any category of person whose hunted animal cannot be eaten?
b:
The prey of the following cannot be eaten even if they mentioned Allaah's Name when shooting or sending the trained animal:
a Muhrim
a Fire-worshipper
an Apostate
an Idolater
The prey of a Muslim, Christian and Jew may be eaten if they recited Allaah's Name at the time of despatch.

f: What is slaughter? What are the conditions for the Zabihah [slaughtered animal] to be Halal for Muslims?
b: It is to cut the vessels which are between the throat and jaws of the animal. For the Zabihah to be Halal, the animal must also be such whose flesh can be eaten; the slaughterer must be a Muslim or Kitabi [Christian/Jew]; and the slaughterer must recite Allaah's Name at the time of slaughter. This is also called Zakah.

f: Which vessels must be slit at the time of slaughter?
b: There are four vessels to be slit - Hulqum [Windpipe], Mar-i [Foodpipe] and Wadajan [two Jugular veins]. When they are cut then it is Halal to eat or at least if most of them are cut according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى at least the food pipe, windpipe and one of the jugulars must be cut.

f: What is the status of the Zabihah if the slaughterer omitted Allaah's Name?
b: If he left it deliberately then the Zabihah is carrion and may not be eaten. If he left it forgetfully then it can be eaten.

f: Is it stipulated that slaughter can only be done with a knife?
b: No, if he slaughters with a bamboo, sharp stone, or anything which will make the blood flow the slaughter is valid. However, teeth and nails still attached to the body organ may not be used.

f: A sheep, cow or camel was slaughtered. A dead foetus was found in its belly. What is the status of the foetus?
b: It is carrion and may not be eaten, whether it has grown hair or not. If it emerges alive then it must be slaughtered and can be eaten. If it dies before slaughter it may not be eaten.

f: If a sheep is slaughtered from the nape, can it be eaten?
b: If the animal remains alive until the vessels are slaughtered then it can be eaten. The action however is Makruh. If it dies before the vessels are slaughtered then it is carrion and may not be eaten.

f: What is the ruling of slaughtering a wild animal which has been tamed and a domestic animal which has gone wild?
b: A tamed animal is slaughtered normally [Zakah]. A domestic animal gone wild is slaughtered by 'Aqr which is to wound it anywhere. This is called Zakah Idtirari [forced slaughter].

f: What is the status of the Zabihah of anyone besides Muslims and Kitabis?
b: The Zabihah of anyone besides these two categories cannot be eaten. The Zabihah of an Apostate, Fire-worshipper and Idolater may not be eaten, even if they recite Allaah's Name at the time of slaughter.

f: What is the status of the Muhrim's Zabihah?
b: If a Muhrim kills a prey, then it is carrion and may not be eaten. We had mentioned that in Kitabul Hajj. If he slaughters a cow, sheep, chicken or camel, they may be eaten.

f: Sundry Regulations
b:
It is Mustahabb for the slaughterer to sharpen his knife.
It is Makruh to let the knife reach the spine or to cut off the head. The Zabihah may nevertheless be eaten.
It is Mustahabb to make Nahr of the camel. If Nahr is made it is permissble but Makruh.
If an animal which cannot be eaten is slaughtered according to Shari'ah, its hide and flesh is clean, even if it cannot be eaten. The skin of humans and pigs will however not be regarded as pure because tanning and slaughter do not have effect upon them.

f: Are there animals which cannot be eaten?
b: Fanged beats, taloned birds, domestic donkeys, mules, hyenas, lizards and all forms of vermin may not be eaten.

f: What does Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى say about crow? [i.e. about eating it]
b: The omnivorous crow may be eaten, but not the spotted crow which eats carrion.

f: What does he say about horse meat?
b: It is Halal, but Makruh to eat lest the instruments of Jihad become scarce.

f: What is the status of rabbit meat?
b: There is no harm in eating it.

f: Can locust be eaten?
b: It is Halal. It need not be slaughtered.

f: What is the status of aquatic animals?
b: Aquatic animals are not Halal except for fish. That which died naturally and floats on the water is Makruh. There is no harm in eating the Jirrith fish and eel.

f: What is the status of Udhiyah in Islaam?
b:
It is Wajib upon every Muslim who is free, sane and well-off100 and resident. It is thus not Wajib upon the poor, slaves and travellers.

100 Well-off refers to those upon whom Sadaqatul Fitr is Wajib as has been discussed.

f: What must be slaughtered to fulfil this duty? [i.e. of Udhiyah]
b: A sheep for one person, or seven can share in a cow or camel on condition that none of the seven's share is less than a seventh. Also, all seven must intend for the sacrifice. If even one of them merely wishes for the meat, then none of the sevens Udhiyah is made.

f: When does the time of Udhiyah begin?
b: From true dawn on the Day of Nahr. Also, the people of cities may not slaughter before the 'Id Salah.

f: If one of them slaughtered before the Salah, what should he do? [i.e. before the 'Id Salah]
b: He must slaughter again.

f: Are the people of villagers where there is no 'Id Salah allowed to slaughter immediately after true dawn?
b: Yes.

f: Can Udhiyah only be done on the Day of Nahr?
b: Udhiyah can be done on that day, and on the two days thereafter. When the sun sets on that second day, its time has terminated. The best time is the first day, then the next, then the last day.

f: Can one slaughter during one of the two nights which fall between these days?
b: Yes, although it is Makruh due to the possibility that required vessels will not be slit.

f: Which animals cannot be slaughtered for Udhiyah?
b: Udhiyah is not permissible with animals which are blind, one-eyed, lame to the extent that it cannot walk to the sacrifice place, nor emaciated animals, which have no marrow in their bones, nor animals with cut ears or tails, nor that which most of the ear or tail is cut.

f: What is the ruling if most of the tail and ear is intact?101
b:
It may be slaughtered in Udhiyah.

101 The animal which has lost most of its sight is also not allowed. It is recognised by how it approaches offered fodder. The detail of this is in al-Hidayah. Refer to it.

f:
Can the following animals be slaughtered for Udhiyah?
Hornless
Castrated
Mad
Mangry
b: Yes.

f: Which animals can be slaughtered for Udhiyah?
b: Camels, goats and cattle and nothing else. In all these the animals must have completed at least a year except for a sheep in which case a Jaza' [six month old] is allowed. Goats of any of its three categories are allowed.

f: Can the meat of the Udhiyah be eaten and stored?
b: One may eat of it and feed rich and poor and store it. It is Mustahabb that at least a third be given in charity.

f: What must be done with the hide of the Udhiyah?
b: It can be given in charity or made into utensils such as sieves, water-bags etc.

f: Must one slaughter oneself or may one appoint an agent to slaughter?
b: It is best to slaughter by oneself if one is capable. It is also permissible for someone else to slaughter with one's permission.

f: What is the ruling if someone ordered a Kitabi to slaughter on his behalf?
b: It is Makruh, but the Wajib is fulfilled.

f: Two men each bought a sheep for Udhiyah. There was a mix up and each slaughtered the other's sheep. Have their Udhiyah been fulfilled?
b: Yes, there is no liability against them.

f: What is Ayman?
b: The plural of yamin [oath]. It literally means wound or strength. Technically it refers to strengthening one of two angels to some statement by means of an oath. This oath is called yamin because the one who takes the oath strengthens by oath to do something or leave something.

f: What are the types of oaths?
b:
There are three:
Ghamus [immersion]

Mu'aqidah [in effect]

Laghw [futile].

Al-Ghamus is to take an oath about a passed event and deliberately lying about it, e.g. "By Allah I did not do it," whereas he did do it. This is a major sin. It is called Ghamus because it immerses its perpretrator in sin and leads to Jahannum (Hell). Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "The major sins are to associate partners with Allaah, disobey partners, and al-yamin al-ghamus."102 

There is no Kaffarah upon the perpretrator. Instead, he should repent and seek forgiveness.

Al-Mun'aqidah is to take an oath about a future action, either to do it, or to refrain from it. If the oath is broken Kaffarah is compulsory.

Al-Laghw is to take an oath about a passed event, believing the oath to be true, but the reality was different. We hope that Allaah will not take the perpretrator to account for this kind of oath.

102 Narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitabul Ayman, Bab al-Yamin al-Ghamus.

f: You have mentioned that Kaffarah is payable in the event of al-Ghamus. Is this only when it was doen deliberately or in all scenarios?
b: It is payable in all scenarios, whether deliberately, absentmindedly or by force.

f: A man did not intend to take an oath, but was forced to. He then broke the oath. What is the ruling?
b: He must still pay Kaffarah.

f: What are the circumstances in which it will be deemed that a Muslim made an oath?
b: It is an oath if he swore by Allaah or any of His Names, such as "ar-Rahman" and "ar-Rahim", or by an attribute of His Being, such as, "The Honour/Majesty/Greatness of Allaah". However, "By the Knowledge of Allaah", is not deemed an oath.

f: What is the status of swearing, "By the anger/displeasure of Allaah"?
b:
That is not deemed an oath.103

103 That is customarily not deemed an oath.

f: Has he taken an oath if he says, "If I did so, then may the anger/displeasure of Allaah be upon me."?
b: No.

f: How does one make an oath by Allaah and His Attributes?
b: By applying huruful qasm [letters of oath] upon what one swears by.

f: What are these letters of oath?
b: They are three Waw [wAllaahi]; Ba [billahi] and Ta [tAllaahi]. The letters can also be hidden if applied in the meaning, e.g. "Allaahi I shall do so."

f: Is it an oath if he says, "Wa Haqqillahi - by Allaah's Right"?
b: According to Imaam Au Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى no.

f: Which words constitute oaths?
b: "Uqsimu/Aqsimu billaghi" I swear by Allaah, "Ash-hadu/Ushhidu billah" I testify by Allaah, "Wa 'Ahidillah/Mithaqihi" by the pact/covenant of Allaah.

f: What is the ruling if he swears by Allaah and adds InshaAllaah [if Allaah wills]?
b:
If he said it immediately after the oath then does contrary then he has not violated the "oath".104

104 Ibn Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrates thar Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "He who swears an oath then adds Inshaallah will not have contravention of oath against him." [at-Tirmizi and Abu Dawud]

f: Is it an oath if he says, "If I do so then I am a Jew/Christian/Fire-worshipper/Polytheist"?
b: Yes, it is an oath. Kaffarah is liable if he breaks it.

f: Is it an oath if he says, "If I do so then I am an adulterer/wine-drinker/usurer"?
b: No.

f: What is the ruling of swearing by anything besides Allaah, such as Rasulullaah ﷺ, the Quraan or the Ka'bah?
b: Swearing by any besides Allaah does not constitute a valid oath.

f: A man swore to sin, e.g. "By Allaah, I shall not pray Salah/I shall never speak to my father/I shall commit murder." What should he do?
b:
Resolve to sin is a sin in itself. He who swears to sin is amongst the worst sinners. Nevertheless he may not commit the sin he swore to. He should break the oath and pay Kaffarah.106

106 'Awf bin Malik narrates from his father: I said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ, what if I used to go to my cousin and ask him and he refused me and did not maintain ties with me. He then had a need and came to ask of me. I had vowed not to give or maintain ties with him." He ordered me to give what is good and pay Kaffarah for my oath. [an-Nasai and Ibn Majah]

f: A man declares forbidden upon himself something which he is capable of. Does it become Haram?
b: No, if he uses it he should pay Kaffarah.

f: What is covered by the saying, "Everything Halal is Haram upon me."?
b: In custom it covers food and drink, unless he intended something else.

f: A Kafir made an oath he then embraces Islaam. Does he have to pay Kaffarah if he broke the oath before or after embracing Islaam?
b:
The Shari'ah does not recognise his oath. There is no Kaffarah.107

107 An oath entails honouring Allah, which is lacking in a state of Kufr. [al-Hidayah]

f: A man vows to do an act which he is incapable of, e.g. "I shall climb up to the sky/I shall turn this rock into gold." Does this count as an oath? If so, when will the oath be regarded as violated?
b: The oath is established and immediately deemed violated.

f: A man vowed to go to al-Busrah and did not go until he died. At what point is the vow deemed violated?
b: At the last moment of his life.

f: A man vowed not to speak. He then recited the Quraan in Salah. Is the oath broken?
b: No.

f: A man vowed not to speak to someone for a Hin/Zaman [while]. How long is that?
b: Six months.

f: And if he vowed for a Dahr [era] [i.e. he vowed not to speak to someone for that duration]
b: According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is also six months. Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى did not decide, and said, "I do not know what Dahr is."

f: And if he vowed not to speak for "days"?
b: It is three days if said as a common known. If however he made it a proper noun, "the days", then it is 10 days according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and the days of a week according to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى.

f: What do the three Imams say about an oath not to speak for "months"?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is 10 months. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is 12 months.

f: A man vowed not to speak to another. He then spoke to him at a distance where he would be able to hear, but was sleeping. What is the ruling?
b: The oath has been violated.

f: A man vowed not to speak to someone without his permission. He granted permission. The one making the vow did not know about the permission but spoke to him anyway. Is the oath broken?
b: Yes.

f: A man vowed not to speak to "the owner of this shawl". The owner then sold it and the man spoke to him. Has his vow been broken?
b: Yes.

f: A man vowed not to speak to, "this youngster". He then spoke to him when he became an old man. Has his vow been broken?
b: [author of the book left his empty]

f: A man vowed not to speak to a certain person's wife. That person then divorced her and he spoke to her. Has his vow been broken?
b: No.

f: A man vowed not to speak to a certains person's slave or enter his house. The person then sold the slave and the man spoke to him, or he sold the house and the man entered it. Has his vow been broken?
b: No.

f: A man vowed not to eat ghada, 'asha or suhur. What is meant by these?
b: Ghada is a meal from dawn until noon, 'asha is a meal from noon until half the night, and suhur is a meal from half the night until dawn.

f: A man vowed not to eat bread. What does "bread" entail?
b:
The vow will cover whatever bread the people of his land are used to. Thus if a man of Iraq eats Qataif [small triangular] or rice-bread, then his vow is not broken.108

109 If he however eats it in Tabaristan where it is usual, then it is violated. [al-Hidayah]

f: A man vowed not to eat of "this wheat." He then ate the bread made from it. Is his vow broken?
b:
Not according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى, who says that it is only violated if he eats the actual wheat.109

109 According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is violated because eating the bread is the understood meaning of eating the wheat. According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى wheat is also directly consumed.

f: A man vowed not to eat of "this flour." He then ate the bread made from it. Is his vow broken?
b:
Yes.110

110 Because flour is not edible in itself. Hence the vew is interpreted to refer to the bread.

f: Is the oath violated if he swallows the flour? [i.e. after he vowed not to eat this flour]
b: No. [i.e. it was understood to mean he'll eat it as bread, because flour isn't eaten raw]

f: He vowed not to eat cooked food and ate cooked lentils or legumes. What is the ruling?
b:
The oat is only violated by eating cooked meat, nothing else.111 

111 Because that which is cooked refers to meat.

f: A man vowed not to eat heads. He then ate a sparrow's head. Is the vow broken.
b: No, because "heads" refer to that which is generally baked in ovens and sold in cities.

f: A man vowed not to eat roast. He then ate roast meat/eggplant/carrot. What is the ruling?
b: The oath is violated by eating the roast meat, not the roast eggplant and carrot.

f: A man vowed not to eat of "this wheat foetus." The foetus then was born and grew into a ram. He then ate the ram. Is his vow broken?
b: Yes.

f: A man vowed not to eat of "this date-tree." He then ate of its branches or roots. Is his vow broken?
b: The vow is interpreted according to custom to refer to the fruits. If he eats any other part of the tree then the vow is not broken, only if he eats the fruit.

f: A man vowed not to eat of "this unripe dates." He then ate the dates after they ripened. Or he vowed not to eat unripe dates and ate ripe dates. Is his vow broken?
b: No.

f: A man vowed not eat unripe dates. He then ate unripe dates starting to ripen. Is his vow broken?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى his vow is broken.

f: A man vowed not to eat "meat". He then ate fish. Is his vow broken?
b:
No.112

112 Although according to the juristic principle of Qiyas it is violated because the Quran calls fish "meat", fish flesh is not meat in the sense of that which which is made from blood because fish do not have blood.

f: A man vowed not to drink from the Tigris River. He then drank its water from a vessel. Is his vow broken?
b:
According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is not broken unless he places his mouth in the river.113

113 According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is violated with or without a vessel.

f: A man vowed not to drink from the water of the Tigris River. He then drank its waters from a vessel. Is his vow broken?
b: Yes.

f: A man vowed not to enter a dar [house]. He entered a ruin. Is his house broken?
b: No.

f: A man vowed not to enter "this dar [house]." It was destroyed and completely levelled. He then entered the land. Is the vow broken?114
b:
Yes.

114 Dar includes the land.

f: A man vowed not to enter "this bayt [house]." It was destroyed and completely levelled. He then entered the land. Is the vow broken?
b:
No.115 

115 Bayt necessitates a building where the night can be spent. Thus if the roof has collapsed and the walls remain, the vow will be violated as one can spend the night there.

f: A man vowed not to enter a house in which he is. He does not leave immediately, but reamins standing or sitting there for a while. Is the vow broken?
b: No, it is only broken if he enters after exiting.

f: A man vows not to enter a house. He enters the Ka'bah, a Masjid, church or synagogue. Is his vow broken?
b: [The author left this empty]

f: A man vowed not to enter "this house." He then stood on its roof or enters its Dhiliz [foyer]. Is his vow broken?
b: Yes, however if he stood in the doorway in a manner whereby the door is closed he is outside, then he has not broken the vow.

f: A man vowed not to live in "this house." He himself left it, but left his family and goods behind in it. Is his vow broken?
b:
Yes.117

117 By custom he is said to be inhabiting the house if his family and goods are there.

f: A man vowed not to buy, sell or hire. He appointed an agent to do these acts for him. Is his vow broken?
b: No.

f: A man vowed not to sit on the earth. He then sat on a mat or blanket. Is his vow broken?
b:
No.118

118 Since he is not regarded as sitting directly on the earth. However, if the only barrier is his clothing, then that is insufficient and his vow is broken. [al-Jawharah]

f: A man vowed not to sit on a seat. He then sat on a seat covered with a blanket. Is his vow broken?
b:
Yes.119

119 Because he is deemed sitting on the seat.

f: If he places another seat on top of the seat and sits on it?
b: His oath is not broken if he specified that he will not sit on that particular seat at the bottom.

f: A man vowed not to sleep on a bed. He then slept on the bed covered with a bed sheet. Is his vow broken?
b: Yes, if however he had placed another bed on top of the vowed bed and slept on the top bed then the vow is kept.

f: He vowed that his wife may not leave without his permission. He granted her permission once. She left and returned. She then left a second time without explicit permission. Is his vow broken?
b: Yes, his vow is broken if his words were as above. However if he had vowed whilst speaking to her, "By Allaah, you may not leave unless I permit you to", then if he permits her even once and she goes and returns and leaves again, his vow is intact.

f: A man vowed not to ride a certain person's mount. He then rode on that person's slave's mount that had been permitted to trade. Is his vow broken?
b: No.

f: A man vowed not to ride an animal he was riding at that moment, or not to wear attire he was dressed in at that moment. Is his vow broken?
b: If he immediately dismounts/disrobes that attire then the vow is kept. If however he stays on the beast or keeps that clothing on then the vow is broken. His continuation of riding/wearing is deemed a new ride/dressing.

f: A man vows to go to someone "if he is able to." What is meant by this?
b: It means his capability according to his health and removal of all obstacles. It does not entail whether Allaah decrees his coming or not.

f: A man vows: "I shall certainly pay him the debt owing today." He then finds the creditor and pays him. The creditor discovers that some of the coins are alloyed and some are rejected and some are genuine. Is the vow fulfilled?
b: Yes.

f: If they are lead or Suttuqah [copper covered silver]? [i.e. a man vows to pay the debt today and pays in coins made of this material]
b: His vow is broken.

f: What is meant if he vows to pay his debt "shortly" or "after a long time"?
b: Less than a month is "shortly". More than a month is "a long time."

f: A man vowed not to take his debt in instalments. He then took part payment. Is the vow broken?
b: Not bu just taking part payment. If however he takes the whole amount in instalments then it is broken.

f: He made the above oath [i.e. he vowed not to take his debt in instalments] and then took the amount whereby it was weighed in two weighings. What is the ruling?
b:
If he does not engage in any other act between the weighings besides weighing, then the oath is intact. If he does something else in between then it is broken.

NOTE: A ruler summons a man and makes him vow to inform the ruler of whatever corruption enters the land. This oath is specific to his rule. If the ruler loses his post the man's oath is not broken by not informing him.

WARNING: 
If a man vows, "By Allaah I shall do that act", his vow is fulfilled if he does so once in his life. If he sets a condition of time or place then it must be done according to that condition or else he has violated the oath. If he vows not to ride someone's animals and he rides it his oath is broken, but not if he rides someone else's animal.
If he vows not to do something, "I shall not do that act", then he must avoid it for the rest of his life. If he does it even once then his oath is broken.

f: A man says, "There is a nazr on me/for Allaah" He does not mention what he has pledged. What is the ruling?
b:
Although the words are nazr the meaning is yamin [oath]. Kaffarah of yamin is payable.120

120 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Kaffarah of nazr is the Kaffarah of yamin." [Abu Dawud]

f: What is the ruling if someone made nazr and mentioned what he pledged?
b: If he did not mention a condition fulfilling the nazr, then he must fulfil whatever he pledged to do, e.g. "For Allaah I shall fast a month/perform Hajj/pray two Rak'at."

f: If he attaches a condition to the nazr what is the ruling, e.g. "If Allaah cures me/if my son comes then I shall fast/pray/perform Hajj/free a slave", etc.
b:
It is Wajib to fulfil in this case also because the words of the ayah are general, "And they fulfil their nazr."
It is narrated that Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى said, "If someone makes nazr, 'if I do so then I have to make Hajj or fast a year', kaffarah of yamin will suffice him."This is also the view of Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى.

f: What if a man made a nazr to disobey Allaah?
b: He may not perform the sin because of the nazr. Instead he should pay kaffarah as in violated oaths.

f: A man made nazr to give his wealth in charity. What does he have to give?
b: He has to give whatever wealth category in which Zakah is compulsory upon him.

f: A man vows to give in charity whatever he owns. What must he give?
b: He must give whatever he owns but may retain an amount needed to maintain himself and his dependants until he can earn more money. Once he has earned more he must give an amount equivalent to the amount he had retained.

f: What is the Kaffarah for breaking an oath?
b:
Allaah has explained it in the Quraan as follows, "Allaah will not punish you for unintentional oaths, but will punish you for deliberate oaths. Its Kaffarah is that you feed ten poor people of the average food you feed your family, or clothe them, or freeing a slave. He who does not find, should fast three days. That is the Kaffarah of when you make oaths [you do not fulfil]. Guard your oaths. Thus Allaah explains your signs that you may be grateful." [al-Maidah:89]

Thus one has a choice between feeding ten poor people of the average food one feeds one's family, or clothing them, or freeing a slave. If one is unable to do any of these, then one must fast three consecutive days.

f: If one wishes to feed, how should it be done?
b: Feed ten poor people lunch and supper so that they are satiated; or give each of them half Sa' of wheat or a full Sa' of barley or dates.

f: Is the Kaffarah fulfilled if he gave each the value of a half Sa' of wheat or a full Sa' of barley or dates?
b: Yes.

f: How would he clothe them? [i.e. as Kaffarah]
b:
Give each of the ten poor at least that which wherein Salah would be valid.121 

121 According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى a trouser will not be enough as the wearer is still considered uncovered.

f: Which slave will suffice as Kaffarah?
b: A healthy, intact slave must be freed as described in kaffarah of Zhihar.

f: You have mentioned that if he is incapable of paying the any of the above three [i.e. feeding poor people, clothing them or freeing a slave as kaffarah], he must fast three consecutive days. The Quraan does not stipulate that it be consecutive. What is your proof for that?
b: According to the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى it is, "... fasting of three consecutive days..."

f: A man made an oath and wished to break it. He first paid the kaffarah and then broke the oath. Is he still liable?
b: Yes, he is liable to pay it a second time after breaking the oath.

f: What is da'wa literally and in Shari'ah?
b: Etymologically it is on the scale of fa'la. It means to attribute something to oneself. In Shari'ah it refers to attribution of something to oneself at the time of a dispute. In grammar it is used on the scale of ifti'al.

f: Who is the mudda'i [claimaint]?
b: The party which cannot be forced to continue the dispute is abandonded.

f: Who is the mudda'a 'alayhi [defendant]?
b: The party which can be forced to continue the dispute [at court].

f: If a man makes a claim against another, will the court accept his mere claim?
b: No, the mudda'i must mention something about the type and quantity of the goods. If it is a specific item that he claims, then the mudda'a 'alayhi must present it at court where the mudda'i will point at it and make his claim. If the object is not present then the mudda'i will mention its value. If it is land he claims, he will define its boundaries and mention that it is in the hands of the mudda'a 'alayhi and that he is claiming it. If it is a right which the mudda'a 'alayhi must fulfil then he will mention it and say, "I am claiming this from him."

f: What will the judge do once the claim is established?
b: The judge will then question the mudda'a 'alayhi. If he confesses, then the judge will rule according to the mudda'i's claim. If he denies the claim, the judge will ask the mudda'i to produce evidence. If he can present the evidence and witnesses he will receive the ruling in his favour. If he is unable to present evidence, and demands an oath-taking, the judge will first make him take an oath. If the mudda'a 'alayhi takes an oath to the contrary the judge will refuse the claim. If the mudda'a 'alayhi refuses to take the oath the judge will rule in the mudda'i's favour. It is appropriate for the judge to first say, "I shall present the oath-taking to you thrice. If you take it, well and good. If you refuse to, I shall rule against you according to what he claims." If he then refuses after the presentations, the judge will rule against him.

f: The judge demands that the mudda'i present his evidence. He replies, "I have evidence, but I want you to take an oath from the mudda'a 'alayhi about it." Can the judge accept his request?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he may not demand the oath when he has evidence.

f: The mudda'a 'alayhi refused to take the oath. Will the mudda'i have to take the oath again?
b: No.

f: Are there any matters about which the denier will not take an oath about?
b: The denier will not take an oath on the following claims - marriage, retracting a divorce, Fayy, Ila, slavery, being Ummul Walad, lineage, Wala, Hudud, Li'an.

f: Two men claimed the same item which is in the hands of a third party. Each claims to be the owner and presents evidence to that effect. What will the judge do?
b: He will allocate it to both of them.

f: What is the ruling if two men both claim to be married to the same woman and produce evidence to that effect?
b: He will accept neither of their evidence and will seek the woman's verification.

f: If two men both claim that they had bought a specific slave from a third party, and they produce evidence, what will the judge do?
b: Each may accept half the slave in exchange for half the price, or leave it. If the judge had ruled accordingly and one of the two says, "I do not want half a slave. I want to rescind the sale." then the other may not take the entire slave. If both claimants define a date of sale, then the slave is for whichever claimed the earlier date. If neither can produce a date but the slave is already in the possession of one of them, then the possessor keeps the slave.

f: One man claims to have bought from a third party and another claims that that was a gift to him from the third party. Both have taken possession from the third party. Neither can produce a date of sale or evidence. Who keeps the goods?
b: The one claiming a sale.

f: A man claims that he bought an item from another. A woman claims instead that he had married her for that as dowry. Both produce evidence. What is the ruling?
b: Both claims are equal. None will be preferred over the other.

f: The one claims an item is collateral from Zayd and the other that it is a gift from Zayd. They take possession and both produce evidence. What is the ruling?
b: The claim of collateral will be given preference.

f: If two parties who have not taken possession, make a general claim of ownership and produce different dates of ownership, whose claim will be accepted?
b: The one with the earlier date.

f: If both claim to have bought it from a third party and both produce different dates, whose claim will be accepted?
b: The one with the earlier date.

f: If both claim to have bought it from a third party and both produce the same date, whose claim will be accepted?
b:
Both's claims will be equally valid. Neither will be preferred over the other.122 

122 I.e. they will share it 50-50 [Sharhul Kanz]

f: One claimant does not have the item in his possession. The other claimaint does. The first produces a date of ownership and the second produces an earlier date. Whose claim will be preferred?
b: The one with the earlier date.

f: Two men both claim to own a beast and produce evidence that they owned it from its bith. The one has it in his possession and the other does not. Whose claim will be preferred?
b: The one who has it in his possession.

f: Two men both claim to own a cloth and produce evidence that they owned it from its time of embroiding. The one has it in his possession and the other does not. Whose claim will be preferred?
b: The one who has it in his possession is preferred in cloths which are only embroided once. Similarly any item whose cause of ownership occurs only once is treated the same in the above scenario.

f: The one who does not have possession produces evidence of general ownership. The one who has it in his possession produces evidence that he bought it from him. What is the ruling?
b: The one who has it keeps it.

f: Two men each claim to have bought an item from each other and produce evidence to that effect. They have no dates. What is the ruling?
b: The court will not decide between them. Both evidences will be rejected.

f: One claimant produces two witnesses and the other produces four. Will the first be preferred?
b: No, both are still equal.

f: A man claims Qisas [retaliation] but the mudda'a 'alayhi denies it. How will this case be decided?
b: The mudda'a 'alayhi will be made to take an oath. If he refuses and the retaliation is for something besides life, he will be retaliated against. If it is in a case of life, then he will be detained until he either confesses or takes the oath. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he must pay Arsh in both cases.

f: The mudda'i says, "I have evidence in the city which I shall present InshaAllaah." What should the judge do?
b: The judge will order the defendant to give a kafil for his life for three days. if he does so, well and good, or failing which he will order the mudda'i to follow him, unless he is a traveller. In that case he will follow him for the duration of the court's session.

f: A man claims an item from another. The mudda'a 'alayhi says, "This item a third party left as Wadi'ah/Rahn by me/I usurped it from a third party." What is the ruling?
b: If the mudda'a 'alayhi can produce evidence to that effect then the dispute between them will no longer be entertained.

f: If the mudda'a 'alayhi however says, "I bought it from a third party", does the claim of the mudda'i remain?
b:
Yes.123 

123 Because the mudda'a 'alayhi has in effect acknowledged that the claimaint has ownership in the item.

f: A man claims, "He stole that item from me", and produces evidence for that. The mudda'a 'alayhi says, "He left it as Wadi'ah by me", and produces evidence for that. Is the case dropped by the defendant's evidence?
b: No.

f: A man has an item in his possession and claims that a certain person left it as Wadi'ah in his care. Another man claims that he bought it from the same man. What is the ruling?
b: The case between them is dropped if there is no evidence.

f: A house is in the possession of a man. A second man claims that the entire house is his. A third man claims that half the house is his. Both produce evidence. What is the ruling?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the second man gets three-quarters and the third man gets a quarter. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the second gets two-third and the third gets a third.

f: If the house is instead in the hands of the two claimants, with with their claims as above? [i.e. one man claims that the entire house is his, and the other man claims that half the house is his, and both produce evidence]
b: Half will be ruled for the claimant of the entire house by way of a court order, and the other half will be said to be his without a court order.

f: Two men claim an animal. Both produce evidence that the animal was born in their possession. They also produce dates. In whose favour will the court rule?
b: The one whose date corresponds with the age of the animal. If that's indeterminate then it will be shared between them.

f: What is the ruling if one disputant is mounted on the beast and the other grabbing the bridle? [i.e. both claim the animal]
b: The rider's claim will be given preference.

f: Two men claim a beast of burden. The one has a load on the beast and the other only has his claim. Whose claim is preferred?
b: The owner of the load.

f: Two men claim a shirt. One is wearing it and the other is grabbing onto the sleeve. Whose claim will be preferred?
b: The one wearing it.

f: How are disputes regarding price and commodity between buyers and sellers settled?
b:
There are various scenarios, with different rulings:
When the seller claims a higher price than the buyer admits to, or the buyer claims a greater quantity of the commodity that the seller admits to; whichever produces evidence will have the ruling in his favour.
If both produce evidence, then the ruling will be according to the greater amount.
If neither can produce evidence then the buyer will be told, "Either accept the price the seller claims or the sale is cancelled." The seller will be told,  "Either accept the quantity the buyer claims or the sale is cancelled." If neither wishes to concede, then each will have to take an oath concerning the other's claim. The buyer will begin taking the oath. Once both have taken their oaths, the court will rescind the sale. If one of them refuses to take the oath, the court will rule in favour of the other's claim.
If the dispute is about the time given for payment, or Shartul Khiyar then there is no mutual oath taking. The word of the one who denies the time given or the option of rescinding will be accepted, but he must take an oath.
If the commodity perishes and they dispute the price, then they will not take oaths according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. The price which the buyer claims will be accepted. According to Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى both will take oaths and the sale will be cancelled based on the market value of the commodity.
If one of two slaves perished, and they dispute the price, they will not take oaths according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى, unless the seller agrees to give up his claim on the perished slave. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى, both will take oaths. The sale with reference to the surviving sale is cancelled and the perished slave is valued at market price.

f: How are disputes between the spouses regarding dowry settled?
b:
There are different scenarios as follows:
The husband claims that the dowry is 1,000 and the wife claims that it is 2,000. The claim of whoever can produce evidence will be accepted.
If both produce evidence, then the wife's word will be taken.
If neither has evidence, then they will take oaths according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. The marriage will not be cancelled. The ruling will be based on Mahr al-Mithl. If that is equal or less than the amount the husband stated, then the ruling will be according to his claim. If it is equal or more than what she said, then the ruling will be according to her claim. If Mahr al-Mithl is more than her amount and less than her amount then the ruling will be Mahr al-Mithl.

f: The couple disagree on household commodities. How will the dispute be settled?
b:
What is appropriate for men124 is for the husband and what is appropriate for women125 is for the wife. What is appropriate for both is for the man. This is if they dispute and both are still living. If one has died and the dispute is with the heirs, then what is appropriate for men and women is for the surviving one of the two. This is all according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the woman is given that which a woman like her prepares with, and the remainder goes to the husband under oath.

124 Such as turbans, horses, bows and weapons. 
125 Such as silken clothing.

f: How are disputes between the claims of the hirer and the hired resolved?
b:
There are several scenarios here as well:
If they dispute about the fee before the fulfilment of what was agreed upon, then both will take oaths and cancel the agreement.
If they disagree after the fulfilment then they will not take mutual oaths. The hirer's word will be taken under oath.
If they disagree after partial fulfilment, then both will take oaths and the remainder of the contract is cancelled. The past fulfilment will be according to the word of the hirer under oath.

f: The owner and the Mukatab dispute the amount payable for the Kitabah. Whose word is accepted?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى they will not both be put to oath. The Mukatab's word will be accepted under oath. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى they will both be put to oath and the Kitabah cancelled.

f: A man sold a slave-girl. She gave birth whilst in the buyer's possession. The seller claims the child as his own. Will his claim be accepted?
b: If she gave birth within six months of her sale, the child is the seller's and she becomes his Ummul Walad. The sale is rescinded.

f: Whose child is it if the buyer also claims the child at the same time or after the seller if the child was born within six months of the sale? [i.e. a man sold a slave-girl and she gave birth whilst in the buyer's possession]
b: It is still the seller's.

f: And if the child was born after six months of the day of her sale? [i.e. a man sold a slave-girl and she gave birth whilst in the buyer's possession, and both the seller and buyer claim the child as their own]
b: If it was born after six months and less than two years from the date of sale, the seller's claim will not be accepted unless the buyer verifies it.

f: The child was born less than six months and died. The seller still claims its lineage after death. Will his claim be accepted? [i.e. a man sold a slave-girl whom give birth whilst in the buyer's possession and the seller claims the child as his own]
b: Neither the child's lineage nor the mother being his Ummul Walad will be accepted.

f: The slave-girl gave birth in less than six months and dies. The seller claims the child. [i.e. he sold her and she gave birth whilst in the buyer's possession]. Is the lineage recognised?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the seller will take the child and return the full price. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he will only return the proportion of the child.

f: A slave-girl gave birth to twins. Her owner claims only one of them. Is the lineage of the other negated?
b: No, the lineage of both is attributed to him.

f: How is the mudda'a 'alayhi put to oath?
b:
There are several details:
A Muslim may not be put to oath except in the name of Allaah. The oath may be emphasised with His Attributes. An oath may not be made severe by demanding a specific time or place.
A Jew will take an oath in the name of "God who revealed the Torah to Moses عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ."
A Christian will take an oath in the name of "God who revealed the Gospel to Jesus عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ."
A Fire-worshipper will take an oath in the name of "God who created fire."
Oaths will not be taken in their houses of worship.

f: Scenarios of oath taking
b:
Someone claims to have bought that man's slave for 1000. The seller disputed him and they were put to oath. He will say, "By Allaah, there is no established sale with you in this slave", and not "You did not sell."
A man accused of usurpation will say, "By Allaah I am not obligated to return this item, not to return its price." He will not say, "By Allaah I did not usurp it."
Concerning marriage the oath will be, "By Allaah, there is no established marriage between us at present."
The oath accepted in divorce is, "By Allaah, she has never been irrevocably divorced from me at any time." He will not say, "By Allaah, I did not divorce her."

f: What is the status of Arsh in Shari'ah?
b:
It is Fard for the witnesses to testify, in order that rights are obtained and not lost. They have no right to hide their Arsh when the owner of the right seeks it. Allaah says, "The witnesses should not refuse when called to testify." He also says, "Do not hide Arsh. He who hides it has indeed a sinful heart." This is with regards to rights.

Regarding Hudud, the witness may choose between exposing and hiding his Arsh. Hiding is preferred in matters regarding theft of wealth. In that case he should say, "He took the wealth", and not "He stole the wealth."

f: Are there degrees of Arsh?
b:
Yes:
Arsh of Zina requires four male witnesses. The Arsh of females will not be accepted.
Qisas and the remaining Hudud require two males. The Arsh of females will not be accepted.
Other rights require two male, or a male and two female witnesses, whether in a case of wealth or not e.g. marriage, divorce, agency and bequests.
The Arsh of one female is accepted in matters men may not investigate e.g. birth, virginity and defects in women.

f: Are there conditions for the acceptance of Arsh?
b: Yes, in all these the witness must be 'adil [just] and must use the words, "I testify." If he says, "I know/I am certain", then the Arsh is not accepted.

f: Will apparent 'adalah of the witness be accepted or must his public and private life be investigated?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى a Muslim is accepted as 'adil on face-value except in matters of Hudud and Qisas. In these cases he must be investigated just as the allegations of the disputants are investigated. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى a public and secret investigation must be held.

f: Are there people who's Arsh is not accepted?
b:
Yes, the Arsh of the following is not accepted:
A blind person.
Slave.
One lashed for slander, even if he has repented.
One may not testify for one's father or grandfather, or son or grandson.
A spouse may not testify for the other.
An owner may not testify for his freed-slave or Mukatab.
A partner may not testify in that which he shares with the partner.
Transsexual.
Professional mourner.
Songstress.
An addict who drinks besides wine.
One who plays with birds.
One who sings to people.
One involved in major sins, particularly those associated with a Hadd.
One who enters the bath without a lower garment.
A consumer of usury.
One who gambles with backgammon and chess.
One who perpretrates demeaning acts such as urinating in the road and eating while walking.
He who vilifies the pious predecessors.
A Kafir from the lands of the Kuffar may not testify against a Kafir living under Islaam.
Someone who has enmity against another for wordly reasons may not testify against him.

f: Whose Arsh is accepted?
b:
They are as follows:
A man may testify for his brother and paternal uncle.
The Arsh of deviant sects is accepted126 except for the Khattabiyah.127 
A Zimmi may testify against a Zimmi.128 
A sinner whose good outweighs his evil, as long as he avoids major sins.
One with a cut penis, one castrated and one born out of wedlock may testify.
Hermaphrodite.
A Zimmi may testify against a Mustamin Harbi [Kafir who has obtained safety to enter the lands of Islaam] just as a Muslim may testify against both of them.
NOTE:

Arsh which accords with the claim is accepted. If they conflict it is rejected.
According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى regard is given if the testimonies of the two witnesses agree in word and meaning.129 
126 As long as their deviance is not such that they have become Kafir [az-Zayla'i in Sharhul Kanz]

127 Rafidi followers of Abul Khattab Muhammad bin Wahb al-Adja'. This man of al-Kufah claimed that 'Ali رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ is the greatets god and Ja'far as-Sadiq رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ the lesser god. Governor 'Isa bin Musa executed him by crucifixion.

128 Even if their religions differ i.e. amongst Christians, Jews and Magians who pay Jizyah are protected by the Islamic State.

129 According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى only the meaning is paid attention to.

f: The witnesses give contradictory Arsh e.g. one testifies "1000" and the other "2000". How is this resolved?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى both testimonies are rejected. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى, "1000" is accepted.

f: One witness testified "1000", and the other "1500". The mudda'i claims 1500. What is the ruling?
b: Both testimonies will be accepted as 1000.

f: Both witnesses testified to 1000, but one added, "He did however pay 500 of that." What is the ruling?
b: Both testimonies will be taken as 1000. The payment of 500 will be ignored unless the other also testifies to it. It is appropriate that if the witness does know that, that he does not testify to the 1000 until the mudda'i admits to receiving the 500.

f: Two witnesses testified that Zayd was killed on the Day of Nahr at Makkah. Another two testified that he was killed on the Day of Nahr at al-Kufah. They all testify at the same time. What will the court decide?
b: Both testimonies will be rejected.

f: The first pair testified [i.e. Two witnesses testified that Zayd was killed on the Day of Nahr at Makkah. Another two testified that he was killed on the Day of Nahr at al-Kufah] and the judge ruled accordingly. The next pair then arrives. Will the ruling be rescinded?
b: No, the second Arsh will not be accepted after a decision has been given on the first Arsh.

f: Can a witness testify to what he did not himself see?
b:
It is not permissible. However, if a reliable person has informed him of the following then he may convey it:
lineage,
death,
marriage,
intercourse,
and appointment of a judge.

f: Does Shari'ah recognise Arsh upon Arsh? What does it entail?
b:
A witness can give two forms of Arsh. The first is that by which a ruling can be established in itself. These include sale, hire, marriage, confession, usurpation, murder and a decision of a judge. If he hears or sees these matters he may testify to it if he does not make a secondary witness to it. He will say, "I testify that he sold..." and will not say, "I have been made witness ..."

The second is it does not establish a ruling in itself. This is Arsh upon Arsh. If he merely hears a witness testifying to something he cannot testify to it unless the primary witness makes him a secondary witness to the Arsh. Similarly if someone hears a primary witness making a secondary witness to a Arsh, the hearer cannot testify. Arsh upon Arsh is permissible in every right which does not become forfeit due to doubt. It is not accepted in Hudud and Qisas. The Arsh of two witnesses form two witnesses is acceptable, but not the Arsh of one from one.

f: Describe the procedure of making a secondary witness.
b: The primary witness will say to the secondary witness, for example, "Be witness to my Arsh that I testify that so-and-so confessed to me about that, and made me a witness against him." It is permissible if he omits, "He made me a witness against himself."

f: How will the secondary witness then testify? [i.e. in the procedure of making a secondary witness: The primary witness will say to the secondary witness, for example, "Be witness to my Arsh that I testify that so-and-so confessed to me about that, and made me a witness against him."]
b: He will say, "I testify that so-and-so confessed to him concerning ... and he then said to me, 'Testify according to my Arsh that ...' hence I testify to that."

f: Are there further conditions for the acceptance of secondary Arsh?
b: The secondary witness may only testify if the primary witness died; or has gone away the distance of three days' journey or more; or is too ill to attend the court.

f: What is the ruling of the secondary witnesses regarding the primary witnesses as 'adil?
b: If they regard them so it is permissible. If they remain silent about their 'adalah then it is also permissible but the judge will examine their state.

f: When the secondary witnesses intended to testify, the primary witnesses refuted their Arsh. Will the Arsh of the secondary witnesses still be accepted?
b: No.

f: What does the judge do when witnesses retract their Arsh?
b:
There are details to this which you should pay attention to:
If the witnesses retract their Arsh before the court rules on it, then their Arsh is forfeit and they have no liability.
If the judge had ruled that the mudda'a 'alayhi had to pay money based on their Arsh, and they thereafter retract, the decision is cancelled and they are liable to compensate the mudda'a 'alayhi for his loss.
If one of the two retracts then he is liable for half.
Three witnesses testified to a money case. One witness retracts. he does not owe anything. If however two retract, then the two must jointly compensate him for half the amount.
A man and two women testified. If a woman retracts then she is liable for a quarter of the amount. If both women retract then they are liable for half.
A man and ten women testified. If eight women retract then there is no liability upon them. If a ninth woman retracts, then the retracting women owe a quarter. If the man and women all retract then the man owes a sixth and the women five-sixths according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he owes half the women half.
Two witnesses testified that a woman married with Mahrul Mithl or more. If they retract then they are not liable. If they testified to less than Mahrul Mithl and then retracted, they are not liable for the deficiency.
Two witnesses testified that a man married with Mahrul Mithl or less. If they retract then they are not liable. If they testified to more than Mahrul Mithl and then retracted, they are liable for the excess.
If they testify that a commodity was sold at market value or more and then they retract, they are not liable. If they testified to less than market value they are liable for the loss.
They testified that a man divorced his wife before intercourse. If they retract they are liable for half the dowry. If they retracted after intercourse there is no liability.
They testified that a man freed his slave. If they retract they are liable for the value of the slave.
They testified to Qisas. The mudda'a alayhi was executed. They then retracted. They are liable for Diyah not Qisas. 
When secondary witnesses retract they are liable.
If the primary witnesses retract and say, "We did not authorise any secondary witnesses", then they are not liable. If they admit "We authorised them to testify but committed an error", then they are liable.
If the secondary witnesses claim that the primary witnesses lied or are mistaken, these claims will be ignored.
Four witnesses testified to Zina. Two witnesses testified that the perpretrator has Ihsan i.e. he will be stoned and not lashed. If these two witnesses retract after the stoning they are not liable.
When those who have declared the witnesses reliable retract they are liable.
Two witnesses testify that an oath was taken. Another two testify that there was a condition as well. They then retract. Liability is only on the witnesses to the oath.

f: Sundry regulations
b:
The judge will not entertain claims of the defendant that the witnesses be rejected [after having made his own investigations] nor negative Arsh [unless it is relevant to the case e.g. he has no other heir besides this man] and he will not rule according to that.
According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى a false witness will be exposed in the market and not physically punished. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he will be beaten and imprisoned.
The witness is not allowed to read one's letter and testify except when he knows the testimony.

f: Is it permissible to join the judicial system?
b:
There is no harm in it if one can fulfil one's duty with justice. It is Makruh for one who fears that he will be weak in fulfilling the legal duties or that he will not be able to be impartial. It is not appropriate to desire or seek a judicial post. A judicial appointment is not valid if the appointee does not fulfil the prerequisites of Arsh130 and that he be capable of Ijtihad131.

130 Sanity, adulthood, freedom, Islam and justice.
131 This condition is one of preference [not obligatory] - al-Hidayah

f: When a judge is appointed, what does a judge do with those prisoners whom the previous judge had detained?
b: The register of the previous judge is given to him. He will examine the cases of the prisoners. Those who confess will continue their sentences. As for those who plead innocent the word of the previous judge will not be accepted without evidence. Even if there is no evidence, the new judge will not hasten to release them. He will make an announcement and examine the case just as he will, regarding Wadi'ah and Awqaf. He will then act according to the evidence at hand or he who has them in his possession admits to them. The mere word of the previous judge will not be accepted unless the one who holds them admits that the previous judge had handed them to him, in which case his word will be accepted.

f: Mention some of the characteristics the judge will adopt during his tenure.
b: He will sit openly for passing judgement in the Masjid. He may not accept gifts except from Mahram blood relatives or from such people with whom he used to have a relationship of exchanging gifts before being appointed. He may not accept invitations, except those which are general. He must attend funerals and visit the sick. He may not host one party of disputants and exclude the other. When both parties attend court, he will treat them equally in seating and in giving them attention. He will not speak secretly to one of them. He will not pass hints to him. He will not lead him on in presenting his proofs.

f: Will the judge detain the mudda'a 'alayhi if found guilty?
b: If the mudda'i demands his right the judge should not hasten to detain the mudda'a 'alayhi. He should order him to pay what he owes. If he refuses the judge will detain him for any liability which was incurred by acquiring wealth in his hands such as the price of goods or loans; as well as for any debt incurred by transaction, such as deferred dowry and Kafalah. He may not be detained for other liabilities if he says he is poor.

f: Will his mere claim of being poor be accepted or will his condition be investigated?
b: If his creditor can prove that he has wealth he will be detained for two to three months. Thereafter he will again be questioned. If no wealth is revealed he will be released. His creditors will not be prevented from approaching him.

f: Can a man be imprisoned for not paying his wife's maintenance?
b: Yes.

f: Can a father be imprisoned for the debts of his son?
b: Only if he refused to pay the Wajib maintenance of his child.

f: The ruler appointed a female as a judge of a district. Is the appointment valid?
b: Yes, except in matters of Hudud and Qisas.

f: Can sentence be passed on someone who is absent?
b: No, unless a representative is present.

f: If the decision of one judge is taken to another, can he implement the decision?
b: He may, unless the decision conflicts with the Quraan, Sunnah or Consesus of the 'Ulama or is without proof.

f: Can the judge appoint a deputy in his absence?
b: No.

f: What is the status of a judge's ruling concerning his parents, children and wives?
b: It is void.

f: Two men have a dispute. They appoint a third party as arbitrator between them. They accept his decision. Is this permissible?
b:
It is permissible if the arbitrator has the attributes of decisionmaking. Thus the following may not arbitrate:
a Kafir,
slave,
Zimmi,
one lashed for slander,
an open sinner,
and a minor.

f: They appointed an aribitrator. One or both of them wish to withdraw from the arbitration. Is this permissible?
b: They can withdraw before a decision has been passed. Once a decision is passed it is binding.

f: The arbitration decision was referred to the judge. Can he implement it?
b: If in accord with his views, or else he can annul it.

f: Can the arbitrator examine evidence and pronounce a decision if a party refuses to take an oath?
b: Yes.

f: Two men appointed an arbitrator regarding an accidental murder. The arbitrator ruled that the 'Aqilah must pay Diyah. Will his decision be implemented.
b: No.

f: If a judge writes to another, will the letter be accepted?
b: It is accepted in matters of rights if it was witnessed to in his presence. It is not accepted in Hudud and Qisas. If the witnesses testify against the party which is present, he may rule accordingly and write his decision. If they testified and the party is not present, he may not give a ruling but will write the Arsh for the addressed judge to make a ruling. It is Wajib for him to first read out the letter to the witnesses that they may know its contents. He will then seal it and hand it to the witnesses.

f: Will the addressed judge [i.e. if a judge writes to another] accept the letter when he receives it without further evidence?
b:
He may not accept it without the Arsh of two men or a man and two women, nor may he accept it without the disputant being present. When the witnesses hand the letter to him, he must examine the seal.
The witnesses must testify, "It is the letter of Judge so-and-so, he handed it to us during high court session, he read it to us and sealed it." The addressed judge will then open it and read it to the disputant. He will implement its contents.

f: A house, property etc. is jointly owned. The partners require that it be partitioned. Who will do it?
b: It is appropriate for the ruler to appoint a Qasim [partitioner]. He will receive a state salary and will perform to partitioning service to the public for free.

f: How will he operate [i.e. a Qasim (partitioner)] if the public treasury cannot support him?
b: He will render his service for fee payable by the partners. The Qasim must be just, trustworthy and knowledgeable in partitioning. The judge will not force a single Qasim upon the people, nor will he allow those in that profession to collaborate in partnership.

f: Do the partners pay equal fees? [i.e. the partners that require partition from a Qasim (partitioner)]
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the fee is divided equally amongst each partner. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى the fee is split according to each one's share.

f: The partners request that the judge arrange for their house or property to be partitioned. They claim that they jointly inherited it. Will the judge order the partition just on their word or must he demand evidence?
b:
According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى he will not divide it until they produce evidence of the death and the amount of heirs.

According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى their word is accepted. This is in regards land. As regards other joint wealth, all agree that their word that they inherited it will be accepted.

f: Besides inheritance, what if they claim that they bought the land or claim ownership without specifying how they came to possess it?
b: it will be divided according to their claim.

f: Two heirs present evidence to the judge concerning the death and amount of heirs. They have the house in their hands and request a partition. There is however another absent heir. Will the judge agree to the partition based on the request of the present heirs?
b: Yes, he will appoint an agent to take possession of the share of the absent heir. This is if it is a jointly inherited house. If they bought it, it may not be partitioned in the absence of any partner, even if the others present proof of purchase.

f: A group inherits property. One of them is absent. He has the entire or part of the property in his possession. Those present seek partition. Will it be divided?
b: No.

f: Only one partner comes and seeks partition. Will the judge comply?
b: If the shared substance is such that each partner will benefit from his share, then partition can occur at the request of one partner. If however one will benefit and the other be harmed due to the minimal nature of his share, partition can occur at the request of the major holder nad not at the request of the other.

f: If both partners will be harmed by partition?
b: It will only be divided if both partners agree to it.

f: What is the ruling of dividing commodities?
b: It is a single kind of good it can be divided at the request of any partner. If a mixture of several kinds then it cannot be divided except through mutual consent.

f: What is the ruling of dividing slaves and jewels?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى they may not be divided. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammed رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى jewels can be divided, not slaves.

f: Can baths and mills be divided?
b: Only if there is mutual consent.

f: Several houses are jointly owned in the same city, how will they be divided?
b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى each house will be separately divided. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى and Imaam Muhammedd رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى if it be more convenient for them, each may take his share in whole houses.

f: How will partition be done if they share a house and land, or house and shop?
b: Each will be separately divided.

f: How does partition take place?
b: It is appropriate for the Qasim to draw what he is going to divide. He should settle their shares and measure it. He will arrange the buildings in such a way that each partner has his own access to the road and water and that each share thus is independent of the other. The shares will then be allotted by means of lots. Monetary compensation will not be part of the partition unless the partners mutually agree.

f: After the partition, the one partner still had a waterway or pathway in the property of the other. The judge had not stipulated the right to use them. How will this be resolved?
b: If possible, move the path from his share, because he cannot use the path or flow water in the land of the other. If this is not possible then the partition is annulled due to the mixture.
